children.translated_text: <s>Pāśupatasūtra</s>, 1

children.text: athātaḥ paśupateḥ pāśupataṃ yogavidhiṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ || PS_1.1 ||
children.translated_text: Now, from here, we shall explain the <s>Pāśupata</s> (relating to <s>Paśupati</s>) method of <s>yoga</s> (spiritual discipline) of <s>Paśupati</s> (Lord of Beings). || PS 1.1 ||

children.text: * hitārtham akhilaṃ yena sṛṣṭaṃ brahmādikaṃ jagat / praṇamya taṃ paśupatiṃ śirasā sadasaspatim / arthātiśayasampannaṃ jñānātiśayam uttamam / pañcārthaṃ kriyate bhāṣyaṃ kauṇḍinyenānupūrvaśaḥ // PSBh_1.1:1

children.translated_text: * He says: the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed Lord) will teach the five topics. // PSBh 1.1:2
* What then is the first <s>sūtra</s> (aphorism)? // PSBh 1.1:3

children.text: * atrocyate athātaḥ paśupateḥ pāśupataṃ yogavidhiṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ iti // PSBh_1.1:4
children.translated_text: * To this it is said: 'Now, from here, we shall explain the <s>Pāśupata yoga</s> method of <s>Paśupati</s>.' // PSBh 1.1:4
* This first <s>sūtra</s> is uttered at the beginning of the treatise. // PSBh 1.1:5
* After that, the word-analysis (<s>padavigraha</s>) is performed. // PSBh 1.1:6
* 'We shall explain the method of <s>yoga</s> that is useful for that.' // PSBh 1.1:7
* The <s>sūtra</s> consists of eight words. // PSBh 1.1:8

children.text: * tatra atha ataḥ iti dve pade naipātike // PSBh_1.1:9
children.translated_text: * Among them, 'atha' (now) and 'ataḥ' (from here) are two indeclinable words. // PSBh 1.1:9

children.text: * paśupater ity etat padaṃ parigrahārthenoccāryate // PSBh_1.1:10
children.translated_text: * The word '<s>paśupateḥ</s>' (of <s>Paśupati</s>) is uttered for the purpose of [indicating] possession. // PSBh 1.1:10
* '<s>Pāśupatam</s>' is a secondary derivative (<s>taddhita</s>). // PSBh 1.1:11
* '<s>Yogavidhim</s>' is a compound (<s>sāmāsika</s>). // PSBh 1.1:12

children.text: * vi āṅ iti dve pade / khyāsyāma ity ākhyātikam // PSBh_1.1:13
children.translated_text: * 'Vi' and 'ā' are two prefixes; 'khyāsyāmaḥ' is a verbal form. // PSBh 1.1:13

children.text: * āha kiṃ prayojanaṃ padavigrahaḥ kriyate // PSBh_1.1:14
children.translated_text: * He asks: What is the purpose of performing the word-analysis? // PSBh 1.1:14
* To that it is said: For the purpose of establishing the meaning. // PSBh 1.1:15
* Why is there non-establishment of meaning with regard to the words? // PSBh 1.1:16
* Because the words here have separate meanings. // PSBh 1.1:17
* Since this is so, he says: // PSBh 1.1:18

children.text: * yathā vivṛtagātro' pi śirasi prāvṛto naraḥ / nābhivyaktiṃ vrajaty evaṃ sūtraṃ vigrahavarjitam // PSBh_1.1:19
children.translated_text: * 'Just as a man whose body is uncovered but whose head is veiled does not become manifest — so too a <s>sūtra</s> without word-analysis [remains obscure].' // PSBh 1.1:19
* Thus the word-analysis is performed for the purpose of establishing the meaning. // PSBh 1.1:20

children.text: * āha uktaḥ padavigrahaḥ prayojanaṃ ca // PSBh_1.1:21
children.translated_text: * He says: The word-analysis and its purpose have been stated. // PSBh 1.1:21

children.text: * idaṃ tu vācyam atha śāstrādiḥ kaḥ iti // PSBh_1.1:22
children.translated_text: * But this must be stated: What is the beginning of the treatise? // PSBh 1.1:22

children.text: * atrocyate athātaḥ paśupater ity eṣa tāvac chāstrādiḥ // PSBh_1.1:23
children.translated_text: * To this it is said: 'Now, from here, of <s>Paśupati</s>' — this much is the beginning of the treatise. // PSBh 1.1:23

children.text: * tatra śāstraṃ tantraṃ grantho vidyā ca // PSBh_1.1:24
children.translated_text: * There, <s>śāstra</s> (treatise), <s>tantra</s> (doctrine), <s>grantha</s> (text), and <s>vidyā</s> (science) [are synonyms]. // PSBh 1.1:24
* Because it is the means of comprehending both the text and its meaning. // PSBh 1.1:25
* The extent [of the teaching] is the scripture beginning with the word 'atha' and ending with [the name] <s>Śiva</s>. // PSBh 1.1:26

children.text: * saṃkhyā pañcādhyāyāḥ pañca brahmāṇi adhikaraṇaṃ ca // PSBh_1.1:27
children.translated_text: * The enumeration [consists of] five chapters, five <s>Brahmans</s> (sacred formulas), and one <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topic). // PSBh 1.1:27
* From the words 'atha' and 'ataḥ,' the explanation, the teaching of bathing, sleeping, etc., the [roles of] the student and the teacher are established. // PSBh 1.1:28

children.text: * kaivalyagatānām api duḥkhitvadarśanāt kāryakāraṇapratyakṣadarśī vipratvād upāyopeyapratyakṣadarśitvāc ca praśnaprativaktā aiśvaryāvasthaś caiva muktatvān mano'manaḥsaṃsthaś ca kāmitvād ataḥ sarvācāryaviśiṣṭo 'yam ācārya iti // PSBh_1.1:29
children.translated_text: * Because even those who have attained <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation) are seen to be subject to suffering; because he directly perceives cause and effect; because of being a <s>vipra</s> (sage); because of directly perceiving means and ends; because he is the answerer of questions; because he is in the state of sovereignty; because he is liberated; because his mind transcends the ordinary mind; and because of his desiring nature — therefore this teacher is superior to all other teachers. // PSBh 1.1:29

children.text: * tathā brāhmaṇagrahaṇāt strīpratiṣedhād indriyajayopadeśāc ca uktaṃ hi / bādhiryam āndhyam aghratvaṃ mūkatā jaḍatā tathā / unmādaḥ kauṇyaṃ kuṣṭhitvaṃ klaibyaṃ gudāvartapaṅgutā // PSBh_1.1:30
children.translated_text: * Likewise, from the specification of 'a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>,' from the prohibition of women, and from the teaching of sense-control — for it has been said: 'Deafness, blindness, lack of smell, muteness, dullness, madness, lameness, leprosy, impotence, anal disorder, and limping' — // PSBh 1.1:30
* A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who is free from [all] these defects and has keen senses is [a qualified] student. // PSBh 1.1:31
* And this student is distinguished from others. // PSBh 1.1:32

children.text: * tathā devādibhyaś ca krīḍādharmitvāt krīḍānimittā īśvarapravṛttiḥ // PSBh_1.1:33
children.translated_text: * Likewise, in contrast to gods and others, because [the Lord's] nature is play, <s>Īśvara</s>'s (the Lord's) activity has play as its cause. // PSBh 1.1:33
* And the teacher's activity in speaking the teaching is for the purpose of grace. // PSBh 1.1:34

* Likewise, from the teaching of worship, injunction, faith, desire for <s>Śivatva</s> (the state of <s>Śiva</s>), the student who seeks the end of suffering is impelled to approach [the teacher]. // PSBh 1.1:35
* But not for the sake of <s>dharma</s> (duty), <s>artha</s> (wealth), <s>kāma</s> (pleasure), or <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation). // PSBh 1.1:36

children.text: * tathā kāmitvād indrakauśikādibhyaś cācāryo divyo niratiśayakrīḍaiśvaryasvābhāvyād ity arthaḥ // PSBh_1.1:37
children.translated_text: * Likewise, because of his desiring nature, the teacher is divine compared to <s>Indra</s>, <s>Kauśika</s>, and others, due to the inherent nature of unsurpassed play and sovereignty — this is the meaning. // PSBh 1.1:37

children.text: * codanopasadanasaṃskāravaśyādiduḥkhair abhibhūtatvāc cādivyā indrakauśikādyāḥ śiṣyā iti // PSBh_1.1:38
children.translated_text: * And <s>Indra</s>, <s>Kauśika</s>, and others are non-divine students, because they are overcome by sufferings such as injunction, approach, purificatory rites, and subjection. // PSBh 1.1:38

children.text: * tathā śiṣṭaprāmāṇyāt kāmitvād ajātatvāc ca manuṣyarūpī bhagavān brāhmaṇakāyam āsthāya kāyāvataraṇe avatīrṇa iti // PSBh_1.1:39
children.translated_text: * Likewise, due to the authority of the learned, due to his desiring nature, and due to being unborn, the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed Lord), assuming a human form and entering a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> body, descended in bodily incarnation. // PSBh 1.1:39

children.text:
* tathā padbhyām ujjayinīṃ prāptaḥ / kasmāt / śiṣṭaprāmāṇat cihnadarśanaśravaṇāc ca / atyāśramaprasiddhaṃ liṅgamāsthāya pravacanam uktavān bhasmasnānaśayanānusnānanirmālyaikavāsograhaṇād adhikaraṇaprasiddhyarthaṃ ca svaśāstrokte āyatane śiṣyasambandhārthaṃ śucau deśe bhasmavedyāmuṣitaḥ / ato rudrapracoditaḥ kuśikabhagavān abhyāgatyācārye paripūrṇaparitṛptyādyutkarṣalakṣaṇāni viparītāni cātmani dṛṣṭvā pādāv upasaṃgṛhya nyāyena jātiṃ gotraṃ śrutam anṛṇatvaṃ ca nivedayitvā kṛtakṣaṇam ācāryaṃ kāle vaidyavad avasthitam āturavad avasthitaḥ śiṣyaḥ pṛṣṭavān bhagavan kim eteṣām ādhyātmikādhibhautikādhidaivikānāṃ sarvaduḥkhānām aikāntiko 'tyantiko vyapoho 'sty uta neti / athoktaparigrahādhikāralipsāsu parāpadeśenopadeśe sacchiṣyasādhakapāṭhaprasiddhyarthaṃ kāraṇapadārthādhigamārthaṃ cātmani parāpadeśaṃ kṛtvā bhagavān evoktavān atheti / atra pūrvaprakṛtāpekṣāyām athaśabdaḥ / katham / śiṣyeṇodīritaṃ pūrvaṃ praśnam apekṣyoktavān atheti / evam ayam athaśabdaḥ pṛṣṭaprativacanārtho 'sti / sa duḥkhānta ity arthaḥ / āha kiṃ parīkṣitāya śiṣyāya duḥkhāntaḥ pratijñātaḥ utāparīkṣitāyeti / ucyate parīkṣitāya / yasmād āha iti / atra ataḥśabdaḥ śiṣyaguṇavacane / yasmād ayaṃ brahmāvartadeśajaḥ kulajaḥ paṭvindriyo vividiṣādisampannaḥ śiṣyaḥ / pūrvaṃ cātrārthato 'taḥ śabdo draṣṭavyaḥ / atha sa duḥkhāntaḥ kutaḥ prāpyate kena vābhyupāyeneti / tad ucyate paśupateḥ / prasādād iti vākyaśeṣaḥ / atra paśūnāṃ patiḥ // PSBh_1.1:40
* paśupatiḥ / atra paśavo nāma siddheśvaravarjaṃ sarve cetanāvantaḥ / kāryakaraṇāñjanā nirañjanāś ca paśavaḥ / āha kiṃ teṣāṃ paśutvam / ucyate anaiśvaryaṃ bandhaḥ / kāraṇaśaktisannirodhalakṣaṇam asvātantryam anaiśvaryaṃ bandho 'nāḍiḥ / bandhaguṇa ity upacaryate / tat kathaṃlakṣaṇam iti cet / tad ucyate paśyanāt pāśanāc ca paśavaḥ / tatra pāśā nāma kāryakaraṇākhyāḥ kalāḥ / tāś ca kalā upariṣṭād vakṣyāmaḥ / tābhiḥ pāśitāḥ baddhāḥ saṃniruddhāḥ śabdādiviṣayaparavaśāś ca bhūtvāvatiṣṭhante ity ato 'vagamyate 'svātantryam anaiśvaryaṃ bandhaḥ / kāryakaraṇarahitasya paśutvaṃ nivartata iti cet / tad ucyate saṃhṛtānām api punaḥ punaḥ saṃbandhagrahaṇāc chāstre / kiṃ cānyat / paśyanāc ca paśavaḥ / yasmād vibhutve 'pi citsamavetatve 'pi ca śarīramātram eva paśyanty upalabhanti ca na bahirddhāni / kāryakaraṇarahitāś ca na kāryakaraṇaṃ pratipadyate tyajanti vā / dharmādharmaprakāśadeśakālacodanādyapekṣitatvāc ca / ataḥ suṣṭhūktaṃ paśyanāt pāśanāc ca paśavaḥ / yasmād uktaṃ sāṃkhyayogena ye muktāḥ sāṃkhyayogeśvarāś ca ye / brahmādayas tiryagantāḥ sarve te paśavaḥ smṛtāḥ // PSBh_1.1:41
* patiḥ kasmāt / āpti pāti ca tān paśūn ity ataḥ patir bhavati / tān kenāpnoti kena rakṣati / tato vibhuśaktyā / yasmāt tatrāpi śaktim asyānantāṃ nātivartante / vipratvāc cāsyānantā jñānaśaktiḥ aparimitā / tayā aparimitayā aparimitān eva pratyakṣān paśūn āpnotīti patiḥ / tathā pālayatīti prabhuśaktiḥ / kasmāt / tacchandāt teṣāṃ pravṛttinivṛttiḥ sthitir iṣṭāniṣṭasthānaśarīrendriyaviṣayādiprāptir bhavati / tatparidṛṣṭānāṃ tatpracoditānāṃ cety arthaḥ / evaṃ // PSBh_1.1:42
* paśupater iti kāryakāraṇayoḥ prasādasya coddeśaḥ / tasmāt prasādāt sa duḥkhāntaḥ prāpyate / na tu jñānavairāgyadharmaiśvāryatyāgamātrād ity arthaḥ / āha kutrasthasya kadā kīdṛśasya vā sa bhagavān prasīdatīti / ucyate yadānena tu tat prāptaṃ bhavati / āha kiṃ tad iti / ucyate pāśupatam atra paśupatinoktaṃ parigṛhītaṃ paśupatim adhikṛtya cārabhyata iti pāśupatam / yathā vaiṣṇavaṃ mānasam iti / kiṃ tad iti / ucyate yogam / atrātmeśvarasaṃyogo yogaḥ / sa punaḥ puruṣasyādhyayanādinaimittikatvād anyatarakarmajaḥ sthāṇuśyenavat / codanādhyayanādivacanād meṣavad ubhayakarmajaḥ / yasmāt sati vibhutve anadhikārakṛtatvād viyogasya / viyuktasyaiva ca saṃyoga upadiśyate / viṣayaraktaviraktavat kriyāyoge / iha tu samādhilakṣaṇe yoge saṃniyama iti / āha kiṃ parijñānamātrād eva tadyogaḥ prāpyate / ucyate / yasmād āha tatprāptau vidhiṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ / atra yogasya vidhiḥ yogavidhir iti ṣaṣṭhītatpuruṣasamāsaḥ / atra sūkṣmasthūlasabāhyābhyantarasalakṣaṇavilakṣaṇakriyāsu vidhisaṃjñā yajñavidhivat / na tu senāvanādivat / kasmāt / kriyāṇāṃ kṣaṇikānāṃ samudāyāsambhavāt / yady evaṃ vidhiḥ kasmāt / vidhāyakatvād vidhiḥ / upāyopeyabhāvāc ca / vidhim iti karma / eva saduḥkhāntaḥ kāryaṃ kāraṇaṃ yogo vidhir iti pañcaiva padārthāḥ samāsata uddiṣṭāḥ / te vyākhyeyāḥ / vyākhyānam eteṣāṃ vistaravibhāgaviśeṣopasaṃhāranigamanāni / tasmād anyad vyākhyeyam anyad vyākhyānam / yasmād āha vyākhyāsyāmaḥ / atra viḥ vistare vibhāge viśeṣe ca bhavati / tatra vistara iti pratyakṣānu // PSBh_1.1:43
* mānāptavacanam iti pramāṇāny abhidhīyante / tatra pratyakṣaṃ dvividham indriyapratyakṣam ātmapratyakṣaṃ ca / indriyapratyakṣam indriyārthāḥ śabdasparśarūparasagandhaghaṭāhāḥ vyākhyānatāpamūtrapurīṣamāṃsalavaṇaprāṇāyāmaiḥ siddham / ātmapratyakṣaṃ tadupahārakṛtsnatapoduḥkhāntādi vacanāt siddham / yathā prasthena mito vrīhiḥ prasthaḥ / paramārthatas tv indriyārthasambandhavyañjakasāmagryaṃ dharmādharmaprakāśadeśakālacodanādyanugṛhītaṃ sat pramāṇam utpadyate / ātmapratyakṣaṃ tu cittāntaḥkaraṇasambandhasāmagryam / anumānam api pratyakṣapūrvakaṃ cittātmāntaḥkaraṇasambandhasāmagryaṃ ca dharmādharmaprakāśadeśakālacodanādismṛtihetukam utpattyanugrahatirobhāvakālādi / taiś cottarasṛṣṭikartṛtvam anumīyate kāraṇasya / ato notsūtram / tac ca dvividhaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ sāmānyatodṛṣṭaṃ ca / tatra dṛṣṭam api dvividhaṃ pūrvavaccheṣavac ca / tatra pūrvadṛṣṭo 'yaṃ ṣaḍaṅgulīyakaḥ sa eveti pūrvavat / viṣāṇādimātradarśanād gaur iti śeṣavat / sāmānyatodṛṣṭam apīha gatipūrvikāṃ deśāntaraprāptiṃ dṛṣṭvā cāsyādityādigatiprasiddhiḥ / traikālye 'py arthādhigame nimittaṃ pramāṇam / āgamo nāma ā maheśvarād gurupāramparyāgataṃ śāstram / āgamo 'laukikādivyavahārahetur ācakṣitaḥ smṛtaḥ / rudraḥ provāca vacanāt siddhiḥ / eṣv evopamānārthāpattisambhavābhāvaitihyapratibhādīnāṃ vyākhyāyamānānām antarbhāvaḥ / evam etāni trīṇi pramāṇāni / pramāpayitā bhagavāṃś codakaḥ / pramātā puruṣaḥ / prameyāḥ kāryakāraṇādayaḥ pañca padārthāḥ / pramitiḥ saṃvit / saṃvit saṃcintanaṃ sambodho vidyābhivyaktir ity arthaḥ / uddeśanirdeśādhigamāc ca vir vistare bhavati / vibhāgo nāma padapadārthasūtraprakaraṇādhyāyādyasaṃkaraḥ / viśeṣo // PSBh_1.1:44
* nāma sādhyasādhanavyatirekaḥ / āṅ iti vyākhyāmaryādāyāṃ bhavati / padāt padaṃ sūtrāt sūtraṃ prakaraṇāt prakaraṇam adhyāyād adhyāyam ā bodhād ā parisamāpter iti maryādāvasthasyaiva ca vakṣyāmaḥ / khyā prakathane / pratītāpratītābhiḥ saṃjñābhiḥ vedādivihitābhivyatirekeṇa ca vyākhyāsyāmaḥ / syā ity eṣye kāle / yāvad ayam ācāryo gṛhasthādibhyo 'bhyāgataṃ pūrvam ataḥśabdāt parīkṣitaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ vratopavāsādyaṃ mahādevasya dakṣiṇasyāṃ mūrtai sadyojātādisaṃskṛtena bhasmanā saṃskaroti utpattiliṅgavyāvṛttiṃ kṛtvā mantraśrāvaṇaṃ ca karoti tāvad eṣyaḥ kālaḥ kriyate / ma iti pratijñāyāṃ bhavati / utthānādigaṇe samyagvvāvasthitasya vyākhyeyavyākhyānayor bhagavān eva kramaśo vaktā / sthūlopāyapūrvakatvāt sūkṣmavidheyādhigamasya pūrvāśramaniyamapratiṣedhārtham atyāśramayamaniyamaprasiddhyarthaṃ ca vidhiḥ prathamaṃ vyākhyāyate / ity atrāyaṃ padārthopanyāsaḥ parisamāpta iti // PSBh_1.1:45
* atrāha pratipannāṃśo yathāvidhi prathamaṃ vyākhyāyate / idam idānīṃ cintyam / athāsya kaś cādiḥ kiṃ madhyaṃ ko 'ntaḥ katyaṅgo vā vidhir iti / tad ucyate bhasmanādyo nindāmadhyo mūḍhāntaś ca vidhiḥ / sa ca tryaṅgo dānayajanatapoṅga iti / tat katham avagamyate yasmād idam ārabhyate // PSBh_1.1:46
children.translated_text: * Likewise, he reached <s>Ujjayinī</s> on foot. Why? Because of the authority of the learned and because of seeing and hearing the signs. Having adopted the mark that is well-known as beyond the [four] <s>āśramas</s>, he uttered the teaching. By bathing in ash, sleeping, re-bathing, wearing a single garment of discarded offerings, and for the purpose of establishing jurisdiction — in a sacred place prescribed by his own scripture, for the purpose of connecting with disciples, on a clean ground, he dwelt on an ash-altar. Therefore, impelled by <s>Rudra</s>, the blessed <s>Kuśika</s>, having approached, seeing in the teacher the distinguishing marks of complete fullness, complete satisfaction, and other excellences — and their opposites in himself — grasped his feet. Having duly announced his birth, lineage, learning, and freedom from debts, the disciple, stationed like a patient, asked the teacher who was stationed like a physician at the right moment: 'Blessed One, is there a complete, absolute removal of all these sufferings — <s>ādhyātmika</s> (pertaining to the self), <s>ādhibhautika</s> (pertaining to beings), and <s>ādhidaivika</s> (pertaining to the gods) — or not?' Then, for the purpose of establishing the recitation by a worthy disciple-practitioner through indirect teaching regarding acceptance and authority over what has been stated, and for the purpose of comprehending the category of cause — having made the indirect reference to himself — the Blessed One himself said 'now' (<s>atha</s>). Here the word <s>atha</s> refers to what was previously commenced. How? Having regard to the question previously raised by the disciple, he said <s>atha</s>. Thus this word <s>atha</s> has the meaning of a reply to a question. Its meaning is: 'that is the end of suffering.' One asks: 'Is the end of suffering promised to an examined disciple or to an unexamined one?' The answer is: to an examined one. Because he says <s>ataḥ</s> ('therefore'). Here the word <s>ataḥ</s> refers to the qualities of the disciple. Because this disciple is born in the <s>Brahmāvarta</s> region, of good family, of sharp senses, endowed with the desire to know, and so forth. And previously here the word <s>ataḥ</s> should be understood in relation to the meaning. Now, that end of suffering — from where is it obtained, and by what means? The answer is: from <s>Paśupati</s>. 'By [his] grace' completes the sentence. Here, the lord of <s>paśus</s> (bound souls) [PSBh 1.1:40] is <s>Paśupati</s>. Here, <s>paśus</s> means all conscious beings except the perfected lords (<s>siddheśvara</s>). Those endowed with effects and instruments, and those free from coloring — [all] are <s>paśus</s>. One asks: what is their <s>paśu</s>-nature? The answer is: lack of sovereignty is bondage. The obstruction of the power of the cause, characterized by non-independence, is lack of sovereignty, bondage, absence of sovereignty. It is figuratively called 'the quality of bondage.' If one asks what its characteristic is, the answer is: they are <s>paśus</s> because of seeing (<s>paśyanā</s>) and because of being bound (<s>pāśana</s>). There, the bonds (<s>pāśas</s>) are the faculties called effects and instruments. We shall explain those faculties below. Being bound, fettered, obstructed by them, and being subject to external objects such as sound — from this, non-independence, lack of sovereignty, and bondage are understood. If one objects that <s>paśu</s>-nature ceases for one devoid of effects and instruments — the answer is: because in the scripture, even after withdrawal, there is repeated connection and grasping. And what else? Because of seeing (<s>paśyanā</s>), they are <s>paśus</s>. Because even in their all-pervading state, even in their state of being conjoined with consciousness, they see and perceive only the mere body, not external things. And being devoid of effects and instruments, they neither acquire effects and instruments nor abandon them — because of dependence on <s>dharma</s>, <s>adharma</s>, light, place, time, injunction, and so forth. Therefore it is well said: they are <s>paśus</s> because of seeing and being bound. As it is stated: 'Those who are liberated by <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and <s>Yoga</s>, and those who are lords of <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and <s>Yoga</s> — from <s>Brahmā</s> down to animals, all of them are remembered as <s>paśus</s>.' [PSBh 1.1:41] Why is he the Lord (<s>pati</s>)? Because he reaches and protects those <s>paśus</s>, therefore he is the Lord. By what does he reach them, by what does he protect them? By his all-pervading power. Because even there they do not surpass his infinite power. And because of his supreme nature, his infinite power of knowledge is unlimited. By that unlimited [power] he reaches the unlimited <s>paśus</s> directly — thus he is the Lord. Likewise, because he governs, there is [his] sovereign power. Why? Because by his will there is their activity and cessation, their stability, their obtaining of desired and undesired places, bodies, senses, objects, and so forth. This means: of those who are seen by him and impelled by him. Thus [PSBh 1.1:42] '<s>Paśupati</s>' — [this word] designates both the cause and the effect of [his] grace. From that grace, that end of suffering is obtained — not merely from knowledge, dispassion, <s>dharma</s>, sovereignty, and renunciation alone; this is the meaning. One asks: when and in what condition does that Blessed One become gracious to whom? The answer is: when this [the following] has been obtained by him. One asks: what is that? The answer is: <s>Pāśupata</s> — what is spoken by <s>Paśupati</s>, what is accepted [from him], and what is commenced with reference to <s>Paśupati</s> — that is <s>Pāśupata</s>. Just as <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> or <s>Mānasa</s>. What is that? The answer is: <s>yoga</s>. Here, the union of the self with the Lord is <s>yoga</s>. That [yoga], being occasioned by the person's study and other [practices], is born from one [kind of] action, like the hawk of <s>Sthāṇu</s>. Because of the statement of injunction and study, it is born from both kinds of action, like a ram. Because, given all-pervasiveness, separation is not made by any special qualification; and union is taught for one who is indeed separated — like the attached and detached regarding sense objects, in the yoga of action. But here, regarding <s>yoga</s> characterized by <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), it is restraint (<s>saṃniyama</s>). One asks: is that yoga obtained merely by knowledge? The answer is: because he says 'we shall explain the method (<s>vidhi</s>) for attaining that.' Here, the method of yoga is a <s>ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa</s> compound meaning 'the method of yoga.' Here, in subtle, gross, external, internal, with-characteristic, and without-characteristic actions, the designation <s>vidhi</s> (method) [is used] as in sacrificial procedure — but not as in an army march and such. Why? Because of the impossibility of an aggregate of momentary actions. If so, why [call it] <s>vidhi</s>? Because it is prescriptive, [it is called] <s>vidhi</s>. And because of the relationship of means and end. <s>Vidhi</s> is the object [of explanation]. Thus, the end of suffering, the effect, the cause, yoga, and method — these five categories are briefly enumerated. They are to be explained. The explanation of these consists of detailed exposition, division, specification, recapitulation, and conclusion. Therefore what is to be explained is one thing, and the explanation is another. Because he says 'we shall explain.' Here the prefix <s>vi</s> occurs in [the senses of] detail, division, and specification. There, 'detail' means: direct perception, infer- [PSBh 1.1:43] -ence, and authoritative testimony — these are called the means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇas</s>). There, direct perception is twofold: sense-perception and self-perception. Sense-perception [concerns] sense-objects — sound, touch, form, taste, smell, pot, etc. — established through explanation, heating, urine, feces, flesh, salt, and <s>prāṇāyāma</s>. Self-perception is established from the statement regarding that offering, complete austerity, end of suffering, etc. Just as grain measured by a measure is [called] a measure. But in ultimate reality, when the totality of the connection between sense and object, assisted by <s>dharma</s>, <s>adharma</s>, light, place, time, injunction, etc., is present, valid knowledge arises. Self-perception, however, is the totality of the connection of mind, self, and internal organ. Inference too is preceded by perception and is the totality of the connection of mind, self, and internal organ — caused by <s>dharma</s>, <s>adharma</s>, light, place, time, injunction, memory, etc. — [concerning] arising, assistance, disappearance, time, etc. And by these, the authorship of subsequent creation by the cause is inferred. Therefore it is not without a thread [of reasoning]. And that [inference] is twofold: based on what is seen and based on what is generally seen. Of these, the seen is also twofold: <s>pūrvavat</s> (based on the prior) and <s>śeṣavat</s> (based on the remainder). There, <s>pūrvavat</s>: 'this one with six fingers was seen before, he is the same one.' <s>Śeṣavat</s>: from seeing merely horns etc., [one infers] 'it is a cow.' The generally seen too: having seen here that reaching another place is preceded by movement, the movement of the sun etc. is established. A means of valid knowledge is a basis for understanding objects in all three times. <s>Āgama</s> (scripture) means the teaching that has come down through the succession of teachers from <s>Maheśvara</s>. Scripture is declared to be the cause of extraordinary and divine usage; from <s>Rudra</s>'s utterance comes success. Within these [three pramāṇas], analogy, presumption, probability, absence, tradition, intuition, and others are included when explained. Thus these are the three means of valid knowledge. The one who causes valid knowledge is the Blessed Lord, the impeller. The knower is the <s>puruṣa</s> (person). The knowable objects are the five categories beginning with effect and cause. The resultant knowledge (<s>pramiti</s>) is awareness (<s>saṃvit</s>). <s>Saṃvit</s> means reflection, awakening, manifestation of knowledge — this is the meaning. Through enumeration, detailed specification, and comprehension, the prefix <s>vi</s> is [used] in the sense of detail. Division (<s>vibhāga</s>) means the non-confusion of word, meaning, <s>sūtra</s>, section, and chapter. Specification [PSBh 1.1:44] means the distinction between what is to be accomplished and the means of accomplishment. The prefix <s>ā</s> is used to indicate the limit of explanation. From word to word, from <s>sūtra</s> to <s>sūtra</s>, from section to section, from chapter to chapter — up to awakening, up to completion — we shall explain in each established limit. <s>Khyā</s> [means] 'to declare.' We shall explain by means of known and unknown designations, and by distinction from what is prescribed in the <s>Vedas</s> and so forth. <s>Syā</s> [indicates] future tense. The time that elapses is this: until this teacher, having first examined — by the word <s>ataḥ</s> — a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who has come from householders and others, who has observed vows, fasting, etc., consecrates him with ash purified by the mantras <s>Sadyojāta</s> etc. on the southern form of <s>Mahādeva</s>, makes the distinction of the mark of origination, and performs the hearing of mantras. The prefix <s>ma</s> occurs in [the sense of] promise. For one who is properly established in the group beginning with rising, the Blessed One himself is the speaker of what is to be explained and the explanation, in due order. Because the comprehension of subtle prescriptions is preceded by gross means, the method is explained first — for the purpose of prohibiting the observances of the previous <s>āśrama</s>, and for the purpose of establishing the observances and restraints beyond the [four] <s>āśramas</s>. Thus here this presentation of the categories is completed. [PSBh 1.1:45] Here it is stated: the portion that has been undertaken is explained first according to the method. Now this should be considered: what is its beginning, what is its middle, what is its end, and how many limbs does the method have? The answer is: the method begins with ash, has censure as its middle, and <s>mūḍha</s> (the 'deluded' practice) as its end. And it has three limbs: giving (<s>dāna</s>), worship (<s>yajana</s>), and austerity (<s>tapas</s>). How is this understood? Because this [next sūtra] is commenced: [PSBh 1.1:46]

* Having bowed with the head to that <s>Paśupati</s> (Lord of Beings), lord of the assembly, by whom the entire world beginning with <s>Brahmā</s> was created for the benefit [of all]; this commentary on the five topics (<s>pañcārtha</s>), endowed with supreme excellence of meaning and supreme excellence of knowledge, is composed by <s>Kauṇḍinya</s> in proper order. // PSBh 1.1:1
One should bathe with ash three times a day. [PS 1.2]

children.text: * atra bhasma vāmadravyaṃ yad agnīndhanasaṃyogān niṣpannam // PSBh_1.2:1
children.translated_text: * Here, ash is the secondary substance that is produced from the combination of fire and fuel. [PSBh 1.2:1]

children.text: * tat parakṛtaṃ pārthivaṃ bhuktaṃ dīptimat // PSBh_1.2:2
children.translated_text: * That [ash] should be made by another, earthy, used [in fire rituals], and luminous. [PSBh 1.2:2]
* The collection of ash should be done by begging from villages and such, just like alms (<s>bhaikṣya</s>). [PSBh 1.2:3]

children.text: * snānaśayanānusnānakṛtyabandhutvān niṣparigrahatvād ahiṃsakatvād utkṛṣṭam eva śuci prabhūtaṃ grāhyaṃ sādhanatvāt // PSBh_1.2:4
children.translated_text: * Because of the connection with the duties of bathing, sleeping, and re-bathing, because of non-possessiveness, and because of non-violence — one should take only the best, pure, and abundant [ash], as it is the means [of practice]. [PSBh 1.2:4]
* In the absence [of the best], even a small amount should be taken. [PSBh 1.2:5]
* A container such as a gourd, hide, cloth, etc. is well-known here [for storing ash]. [PSBh 1.2:6]

children.text: * āha kiṃ tena bhasmanā kartavyam // PSBh_1.2:7
children.translated_text: * One asks: what should be done with that ash? [PSBh 1.2:7]

children.text: * tad ucyate bhasmaneti tṛtīyā karaṇārthe kartuḥ kriyām ādiśati yathā vāśyā takṣaṇaṃ buddhyā pidhānam // PSBh_1.2:8
children.translated_text: * The answer is: 'with ash' — the instrumental case indicates the instrument; it directs the action of the agent, just as an adze [directs] carpentry, or intelligence [directs] covering. [PSBh 1.2:8]

children.text: * āha atha kasmin kāle sā kriyā kartavyeti // PSBh_1.2:9
children.translated_text: * One asks: at what time should that action be performed? [PSBh 1.2:9]
* Three times a day (<s>triṣavaṇam</s>). [PSBh 1.2:10]
* [This is] a <s>dvigu</s> compound. [PSBh 1.2:11]
* 'Three' is a numeral. // PSBh 1.2:12
* '<s>Savana</s>' (pressing/libation time) is a designation of time. // PSBh 1.2:13

* The morning junction (<s>pūrvasaṃdhyā</s>), the midday junction (<s>madhyāhnasaṃdhyā</s>), and the evening junction (<s>aparasaṃdhyā</s>) — these are the three junctions (<s>saṃdhyātraya</s>). // PSBh 1.2:14

children.text: * triṣavaṇaṃ trisaṃdhyaṃ trikālam ity arthaḥ // PSBh_1.2:15
children.translated_text: * '<s>Triṣavaṇam</s>' (three libation-times), '<s>trisaṃdhyam</s>' (three junctions), and '<s>trikālam</s>' (three times) — this is the meaning. // PSBh 1.2:15

children.text: * āha triṣavaṇaṃ kim anena kartavyam // PSBh_1.2:16
children.translated_text: * He asks: What is to be done at the three libation-times (<s>triṣavaṇam</s>)? // PSBh 1.2:16
* To that it is said: one should bathe (<s>snāyīta</s>). // PSBh 1.2:17

children.text: * atra snānaṃ śaucakāryeṇa śarīreṣv āgantukānāṃ snehatvaglepamalagandhādīnāṃ bhasmanāpakarṣaṇaṃ kartavyam // PSBh_1.2:18
children.translated_text: * Here, bathing (<s>snāna</s>) for the purpose of purification (<s>śauca</s>) means that the removal of adventitious [impurities] such as oil, skin, excretions, dirt, odor, and so forth from the body is to be accomplished with ash (<s>bhasman</s>). // PSBh 1.2:18
* But bathing is the application of the substance of ash to the body. // PSBh 1.2:19

children.text: * paramārthatas tu snānādi puṇyaphalasaṃyogadharmātmavacanād ātmaśaucam evaitat // PSBh_1.2:20
children.translated_text: * In the ultimate sense, however, bathing and the like, since [the word <s>snāna</s>] speaks of the nature of the self (<s>ātman</s>) as conjoined with the merit-fruit — this is indeed purification of the self (<s>ātmaśauca</s>). // PSBh 1.2:20

* Solely because of statements such as 'one whose sins are destroyed by the unstained [nature of] bathing and the like,' the purification of the self is explained by means of the designation of effect and cause. // PSBh 1.2:21

children.text: * ita ity etad ājñāyāṃ niyoge ca // PSBh_1.2:22
children.translated_text: * The suffix '-<s>ita</s>' is used in the sense of command and injunction. // PSBh 1.2:22

children.text: * niyogatvān nigataṃ niyatatvān nigama ity arthaḥ // PSBh_1.2:23
children.translated_text: * Because of being an injunction (<s>niyoga</s>), it is fixed (<s>nigata</s>); because of being definite (<s>niyata</s>), it is a precept (<s>nigama</s>) — this is the meaning. // PSBh 1.2:23
* Why? // PSBh 1.2:24

* Because it is established in each respective system (<s>tantra</s>); because of being non-violent (<s>ahiṃsaka</s>); and because of being the cause of the highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>). // PSBh 1.2:25

children.text: * bhasmanā sneyaṃ na cādbhir viparītatvād ity arthaḥ // PSBh_1.2:26
children.translated_text: * One should bathe with ash, and not with water, because of the opposite [effect] — this is the meaning. // PSBh 1.2:26

children.text: * kiṃ snānam evaivaṃ bhasmanā kartavyam // PSBh_1.2:27
children.translated_text: * Should bathing alone be done with ash in this manner? // PSBh 1.2:27
* It is said: // PSBh 1.2:28
* Because he states: // PSBh 1.2:29
One should lie in ash. || PS 1.3 ||
* Here, ash (<s>bhasman</s>) is the same [as mentioned before]. // PSBh 1.3:1
* Its etymology has been stated previously. // PSBh 1.3:2
* 'In ash' (<s>bhasmani</s>) indicates proximity through contact. // PSBh 1.3:3
* '<s>Śaya</s>' (lying) is a designation for resting (<s>upaśama</s>) and repose (<s>viśrāma</s>). // PSBh 1.3:4

children.text: * ita ity etad ājñāyāṃ niyoge ca // PSBh_1.3:5
children.translated_text: * The suffix '-<s>ita</s>' is used in the sense of command and injunction. // PSBh 1.3:5

children.text: * bhasmany eva rātrau svaptavyaṃ nānyatrety arthaḥ // PSBh_1.3:6
children.translated_text: * One should sleep at night only in ash, not elsewhere — this is the meaning. // PSBh 1.3:6

children.text: * uktaṃ hi / yathā mṛgā mṛtyubhayasya bhītā udvignavāsā na labhanti nidrām / evaṃ yatir dhyānaparo mahātmā saṃsārabhīto na labheta nidrām // PSBh_1.3:7

children.translated_text: * Moreover, because of desiring distinction (<s>viśeṣa</s>). // PSBh 1.3:8
* And this <s>brāhmaṇa</s> is one who desires distinction. // PSBh 1.3:9

children.text: * uktaṃ hi / na viśeṣārthināṃ nidrā ciraṃ netreṣu tiṣṭhati / hayānām iva jātyānām ardharātrārdhaśāyinām // PSBh_1.3:10
children.translated_text: * For it has been said: 'Sleep does not long remain in the eyes of those who desire distinction, just as [it does not remain long] in the eyes of thoroughbred horses, who sleep only half the night.' // PSBh 1.3:10

children.text: * tasmāt parivṛṣṭe bhūpradeśe divā parigrahaṃ kṛtvā bhasmāstīryādhyayanādhyāpanadhyānābhiniviṣṭena pravacanacintanābhiniveśaiś ca śrāntena bāhūpadhānena sadyojātādisaṃskṛte bhasmani rātrau svaptavyam ity arthaḥ // PSBh_1.3:11
children.translated_text: * Therefore, having selected an open ground during the day, having spread ash prepared with [the mantra] '<s>Sadyojāta</s>' and the like, being absorbed in study (<s>adhyayana</s>), teaching (<s>adhyāpana</s>), and meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), and exhausted by absorption in reflection on the scripture (<s>pravacanacintanā</s>), one should sleep at night with one's arm as a pillow, on the ash consecrated with '<s>Sadyojāta</s>' and the like — this is the meaning. // PSBh 1.3:11
* If one asks: For what purpose? // PSBh 1.3:12

children.text: * ucyate tapo'rthaṃ bhūpradeśe śaucārthaṃ viśrāmārthaṃ vā // PSBh_1.3:13
children.translated_text: * It is said: For the purpose of austerity (<s>tapas</s>), on open ground; for the purpose of purity (<s>śauca</s>); or for the purpose of rest (<s>viśrāma</s>). // PSBh 1.3:13

children.text: * samaviṣamanimnonnatāyāṃ bhūmau yāmaṃ yāmadvayaṃ vā svaptavyam ity arthaḥ // PSBh_1.3:14
children.translated_text: * On ground that is level or uneven, low or elevated, one should sleep for one or two watches (<s>yāma</s>) — this is the meaning. // PSBh 1.3:14

children.text: * āha kiṃ snānaṃ śayanaṃ ca bhasmanā prayojanadvayam evātra kartavyam utānyad api // PSBh_1.3:15
children.translated_text: * He asks: Are only these two purposes — bathing and sleeping with ash — to be accomplished here, or is there something else as well? // PSBh 1.3:15

children.text: * savanāntasthasyāsyāśaucakaṃ prāptasya nirghātakaṃ kim iti // PSBh_1.3:16
children.translated_text: * For one situated at the end of a <s>savana</s> (libation-time), who has incurred impurity — what is the means of removing it? // PSBh 1.3:16
* To that it is said: // PSBh 1.3:17

* For it has been said: 'Just as deer, frightened by the fear of death, dwelling in agitation, do not obtain sleep — so too the ascetic (<s>yati</s>), great-souled one devoted to meditation, terrified of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence), should not obtain sleep.' // PSBh 1.3:7
Subsequent bathing (<s>anusnāna</s>). || PS 1.4 ||
* Like bathing with <s>mantras</s> and the like. // PSBh 1.4:1

children.text: * atra anu iti pṛṣṭhakarmakriyāyāṃ bhavati // PSBh_1.4:2
children.translated_text: * Here, '<s>anu</s>' (after/following) is used in the sense of a subsequent action. // PSBh 1.4:2
* Like a subsequent drink (<s>anupāna</s>) or following along (<s>anugamana</s>). // PSBh 1.4:3
* But bathing is indeed the application of the substance of ash. // PSBh 1.4:4

children.text: * savanatraye snānasyāntareṣu bhuktocchiṣṭakṣutaniṣṭhīvitamūtrapurīṣotsargādinimittakam aśaucakam abhisamīkṣya tad anusnānaṃ kartavyam // PSBh_1.4:5
children.translated_text: * In the intervals between the three libation-times, having recognized the impurity caused by eating, leftover food, sneezing, spitting, urination, defecation, and the like, one should perform subsequent bathing (<s>anusnāna</s>). // PSBh 1.4:5

children.text: * kim artham iti cet śaucārthaṃ liṅgābhivyaktyarthaṃ ca // PSBh_1.4:6
children.translated_text: * If one asks: For what purpose? For the purpose of purity (<s>śauca</s>) and for the purpose of manifesting the mark (<s>liṅga</s>). // PSBh 1.4:6
* 'One should bathe' — this is the meaning. // PSBh 1.4:7
* He asks: Is ash alone the cause of manifesting the mark (<s>liṅga</s>)? // PSBh 1.4:8

children.text: * bhaktivivṛddhau vā apratiṣiddhasya sādhanaṃ kim iti // PSBh_1.4:9
children.translated_text: * Or is there some other means, not prohibited, for the increase of devotion (<s>bhakti</s>)? // PSBh 1.4:9
* To that it is said: // PSBh 1.4:10
Remnant offerings (<s>nirmālya</s>). || PS 1.5 ||
* Here, like ash, <s>nirmālya</s> (remnant offerings) is well known in worldly usage and so forth. // PSBh 1.5:1
* '<s>Nir</s>' denotes that which has been released (<s>nirmukta</s>). // PSBh 1.5:2
* '<s>Mālya</s>' is a synonym for a collection of flowers (<s>puṣpasamūha</s>). // PSBh 1.5:3

children.text: * tat parakṛtaṃ kāraṇamūrtyāropitāvatāritaṃ niṣparigrahaṃ padmotpalādyam // PSBh_1.5:4
children.translated_text: * That is: flowers such as lotus, <s>utpala</s>, and others, made by another, placed upon and taken down from the form of the deity (<s>kāraṇamūrti</s>), and ownerless (<s>niṣparigraha</s>). // PSBh 1.5:4

children.text: * bhaktivivṛddhyarthaṃ liṅgābhivyaktyarthaṃ ca tad dhāryam ity arthaḥ // PSBh_1.5:5
children.translated_text: * For the purpose of increasing devotion (<s>bhakti</s>) and for the purpose of manifesting the mark (<s>liṅga</s>), that [<s>nirmālya</s>] should be worn — this is the meaning. // PSBh 1.5:5

children.text: * āha bhasmanirmālyena tasya liṅgaṃ vyaktaṃ bhavatīti kva siddham // PSBh_1.5:6
children.translated_text: * He asks: Where is it established that his mark (<s>liṅga</s>) becomes manifest through ash and <s>nirmālya</s> (remnant offerings)? // PSBh 1.5:6
* To that it is said: here [in the scripture]. // PSBh 1.5:7
* Because he states: // PSBh 1.5:8
One who bears the mark (<s>liṅgadhārī</s>). || PS 1.6 ||

children.text: * atra yathānyeṣām api varṇāśramiṇām āśramaprativibhāgakarāṇi liṅgāni bhavanti // PSBh_1.6:1
children.translated_text: * Here, just as other members of the social orders (<s>varṇāśramins</s>) also have marks (<s>liṅgas</s>) that distinguish their respective life-stages (<s>āśramas</s>). // PSBh 1.6:1

children.text: * tatra gṛhasthasya tāvad vāsas trayaṃ vaiṇavī yaṣṭiḥ sodakaṃ ca kamaṇḍalu sottaroṣṭhavapanaṃ yajñopavītādi liṅgam // PSBh_1.6:2
children.translated_text: * Among them, the householder (<s>gṛhastha</s>), to begin with, has as his mark three garments, a bamboo staff, a water-vessel (<s>kamaṇḍalu</s>) with water, shaving [only] the upper lip, the sacred thread (<s>yajñopavīta</s>), and so on. // PSBh 1.6:2

* Likewise, the celibate student (<s>brahmacārin</s>) also has as his mark a staff, water-vessel, <s>muñja</s>-grass girdle (<s>mauñjīmekhalā</s>), sacred thread, black antelope skin, and so on. // PSBh 1.6:3
* Likewise, the forest-dweller (<s>vānaprastha</s>) also has as his mark the wearing of <s>karīra</s> [bark], bark-garments, matted locks, and a bunch of <s>kuśa</s>-grass, and so on. // PSBh 1.6:4
* Likewise, the mendicant (<s>bhikṣu</s>) has as his mark the triple staff (<s>tridaṇḍa</s>), shaved head, water-vessel, ochre garments, water-purifier, ground-purifier, and so on. // PSBh 1.6:5

children.text: * evam ihāpi yad etat pāśupatayogādhikaraṇaṃ liṅgam ity āśramaprativibhāgakaraṃ bhasmasnānaśayanānusnānanirmālyaikavāsādiniṣpannaṃ svaśarīralīnaṃ pāśupatam iti laukikādijñānajanakaṃ tat // PSBh_1.6:6
children.translated_text: * Thus, here too, this mark (<s>liṅga</s>) which pertains to the discipline of <s>Pāśupata yoga</s>, which distinguishes the life-stage, which is produced from bathing with ash, sleeping [in ash], subsequent bathing, <s>nirmālya</s>, a single garment, and so on — [this mark is] inherent in one's own body, is known as '<s>Pāśupata</s>,' and generates knowledge in worldly [observers] and others — that is [the mark]. // PSBh 1.6:6
* Because of being inherent (<s>līyana</s>) and because of marking (<s>liṅgana</s>), it is called a mark (<s>liṅga</s>). // PSBh 1.6:7
* One who wears that [mark] becomes a mark-bearer (<s>liṅgadhārī</s>). // PSBh 1.6:8
* Like one who bears a staff (<s>daṇḍadhārin</s>) — this is the meaning. // PSBh 1.6:9

children.text: * āha athaite snānaśayanānusnānādayo 'rthāḥ kva kartavyāḥ // PSBh_1.6:10
children.translated_text: * He asks: Where should these activities — bathing, sleeping, subsequent bathing, and the like — be performed by one dwelling in that temple? // PSBh 1.6:10
* Or from where should <s>nirmālya</s> (remnant offerings) be obtained? // PSBh 1.6:11
* Or where should one stationed [in practice] wear it? // PSBh 1.6:12
* Or where should one who has adopted the mark reside? // PSBh 1.6:13
* To that it is said: In a sanctuary (<s>āyatana</s>). // PSBh 1.6:14
* Because he states: // PSBh 1.6:15
One who dwells in a sanctuary (<s>āyatanavāsī</s>). || PS 1.7 ||
* Now, like ash and <s>nirmālya</s>, the sanctuary (<s>āyatana</s>) is well known in worldly usage and so forth. // PSBh 1.7:1
* The prefix '<s>ā</s>' is used in the sense of a boundary (<s>maryādā</s>). // PSBh 1.7:2

children.text: * yasmād ete gṛhasthādayaḥ prayataniyataśucisādhvācārāḥ svasvamaryādayopatiṣṭhante yajanti ca śāntikapauṣṭikādibhiḥ kriyābhir iti // PSBh_1.7:3
children.translated_text: * Because these — householders and others — being devoted, regulated, pure, and of good conduct, attend upon [the Lord] according to their respective boundaries and worship with rites such as <s>śāntika</s> (pacificatory), <s>pauṣṭika</s> (prosperity-giving), and so on. // PSBh 1.7:3
* Because of worshipping (<s>yajana</s>), it is called a sanctuary (<s>āyatana</s>). // PSBh 1.7:4

children.text: * tasmin parakṛta āyatane vastavyam iti vāsī ity āyatanaṃ ca parigṛhṇāti // PSBh_1.7:5
children.translated_text: * One should dwell in that sanctuary built by another — thus 'dweller' (<s>vāsī</s>), and one also takes possession of the sanctuary. // PSBh 1.7:5

children.text: * bhūpradeśe ākāśe vṛkṣamūle bahiḥ prādakṣiṇyena vā yatra kvacit prativasan śiṣṭamaryādayā āyatanavāsī bhavati // PSBh_1.7:6
children.translated_text: * On open ground, in the open air, at the root of a tree, outside, by circumambulating — wherever one dwells in accordance with the established convention of the learned, one becomes a sanctuary-dweller (<s>āyatanavāsī</s>). // PSBh 1.7:6
* One should dwell like a sandbank-dweller — this is the meaning. // PSBh 1.7:7
* And the attainment of merit-fruit comes to him quickly. // PSBh 1.7:8

children.text: * uktaṃ hi / grāme vā yadi vāraṇye puṇyasthānaṃ hi śūlinaḥ // PSBh_1.7:9
* āvāso dharmatṛptānāṃ siddhikṣetraṃ hi tat param // PSBh_1.7:10
children.translated_text: * the dwelling of those satisfied in <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) — that indeed is the supreme field of perfection (<s>siddhikṣetra</s>).' // PSBh 1.7:10

children.text: * āha tasminn āyatane prativasatā kāḥ kriyāḥ kartavyāḥ // PSBh_1.7:11
children.translated_text: * He asks: What activities are to be performed by one dwelling in that sanctuary? // PSBh 1.7:11
* Are they [only] bathing and the like, or plastering and the like? // PSBh 1.7:12

children.text: * āhosvid dṛṣṭā asyānyā vaiśeṣikyaḥ kriyāḥ kartavyāḥ // PSBh_1.7:13
children.translated_text: * Or are there other special activities (<s>vaiśeṣikī kriyāḥ</s>) that are to be performed? // PSBh 1.7:13

children.text: * yathā cānyā vaiśeṣikyaḥ kriyāḥ kartavyāḥ prayojanaṃ ca vakṣyāmaḥ - // PSBh_1.7:14
children.translated_text: * And what other special activities are to be performed, and their purpose — we shall explain: // PSBh 1.7:14
* For it has been said: 'Whether in a village or in a forest, the sacred place of the Trident-bearer (<s>Śūlin</s>) — // PSBh 1.7:9
One should worship with laughter, song, dance, the bellowing sound (<s>ḍuṃḍuṃkāra</s>), obeisance (<s>namaskāra</s>), recitation (<s>japya</s>), and offering (<s>upahāra</s>). || PS 1.8 ||

children.text: * atha triṣu snānakāleṣu sadyojātādisaṃskṛtena bhasmanā japatā snātvā japataivāyatanam abhigantavyam // PSBh_1.8:1
children.translated_text: * Now, at the three bathing-times, having bathed with ash consecrated with '<s>Sadyojāta</s>' and the like while reciting, one should approach the sanctuary while [continuing to] recite. // PSBh 1.8:1

children.text: * abhigamya ca yat pūrvaṃ japati tat pratyāhārārthaṃ japyam oṃ oṃ oṃ // PSBh_1.8:2
children.translated_text: * And having approached, what one first recites — that is the recitation for the purpose of withdrawal (<s>pratyāhāra</s>): <s>Oṃ Oṃ Oṃ</s>. // PSBh 1.8:2

children.text: * hasitādīni tu kṛtvā yat paścāj japati tanniyamārthaṃ japyam // PSBh_1.8:3
children.translated_text: * But having performed laughter and the like, what one recites afterward — that is the recitation for the purpose of regulation (<s>niyama</s>). // PSBh 1.8:3

children.text: * tad atra hasitaṃ nāma yad etat kaṇṭhauṣṭhapuṭavisphūrjanam aṭṭahāsaḥ kriyate taddhasitam // PSBh_1.8:4
children.translated_text: * Here, 'laughter' (<s>hasita</s>) means the following: the bursting open of the throat and lips, the loud laughter (<s>aṭṭahāsa</s>) that is performed — that is laughter. // PSBh 1.8:4

children.text: * gītam api gāndharvaśāstrasamayānabhiṣvaṅgeṇa yatra bhagavato maheśvarasya sabhāyāṃ gauṇadravyajakarmajāni nāmāni cintyante tat // PSBh_1.8:5
children.translated_text: * Song (<s>gīta</s>) too — without attachment to the conventions of the science of music (<s>gāndharvaśāstra</s>) — is that in which the names of the Blessed Lord <s>Maheśvara</s> (Great Lord) in his assembly are contemplated, [names] that are secondary (<s>gauṇa</s>), material (<s>dravyaja</s>), and action-born (<s>karmaja</s>). // PSBh 1.8:5

children.text: * saṃskṛtaṃ prākṛtaṃ parakṛtam ātmakṛtaṃ vā yad gīyate tad geyam // PSBh_1.8:6
children.translated_text: * Whether the song is in Sanskrit (<s>saṃskṛta</s>), Prākrit (<s>prākṛta</s>), composed by another (<s>parakṛta</s>), or self-composed (<s>ātmakṛta</s>) — whatever is sung, that is the song. // PSBh 1.8:6

children.text: * nṛttam api nāṭyaśāstrasamayānabhiṣvaṅgeṇa hastapādādīnām utkṣepaṇam avakṣepaṇam ākuñcanaṃ prasāraṇaṃ calanam anavasthānam // PSBh_1.8:7
children.translated_text: * Dance (<s>nṛtta</s>) too — without attachment to the conventions of the science of dramaturgy (<s>nāṭyaśāstra</s>) — is the raising, lowering, bending, extending, moving, and instability of the hands, feet, and other [limbs]. // PSBh 1.8:7

children.text: * nigamakāle niyamārthaṃ geyasahakṛtaṃ nṛttaṃ prayoktavyam // PSBh_1.8:8
children.translated_text: * At the concluding time, for the purpose of regulation, dance accompanied by song should be performed. // PSBh 1.8:8

children.text: * ḍuṃḍuṃkāro nāma ya eṣa jihvāgratālusaṃyogān niṣpadyate puṇyo vṛṣanādasadṛśaḥ saḥ // PSBh_1.8:9
children.translated_text: * The bellowing sound (<s>ḍuṃḍuṃkāra</s>) is that which is produced from the contact of the tip of the tongue with the palate — auspicious, resembling the bellow of a bull (<s>vṛṣanāda</s>). // PSBh 1.8:9
* The making of '<s>ḍuṃḍuṃ</s>' is the <s>ḍuṃḍuṃkāra</s>. // PSBh 1.8:10
* The word '<s>kāra</s>' serves to determine that the <s>ḍuṃḍuṃkāra</s> is an integral part (<s>aṅga</s>) of the offering (<s>upahāra</s>). // PSBh 1.8:11
* '<s>Nama</s>' (obeisance) means the following: // PSBh 1.8:12
* It should not be done with the lips, nor should it be done in a whisper (<s>upāṃśu</s>). // PSBh 1.8:13
* But mental salutation (<s>mānasa namaskaraṇa</s>) is obeisance (<s>namaskāra</s>). // PSBh 1.8:14

children.text: * kāraśabdo vācikopāṃśupratiṣedhārthaṃ mānasopahārāṅgāvadhāraṇārthaṃ cety arthaḥ // PSBh_1.8:15
children.translated_text: * The word '<s>kāra</s>' serves to prohibit vocal and whispered [obeisance] and to determine that mental [obeisance] is an integral part of the offering — this is the meaning. // PSBh 1.8:15

children.text: * japyaṃ nāma sadyojātādiṣv akṣarapaṅktyāṃ manasā bhāvasya saṃcāravicāraḥ // PSBh_1.8:16
children.translated_text: * Recitation (<s>japya</s>) means the mental traversal and investigation (<s>saṃcāravicāra</s>) of meaning (<s>bhāva</s>) within the syllabic sequences of '<s>Sadyojāta</s>' and the like. // PSBh 1.8:16
* That is the recitation (<s>japya</s>). // PSBh 1.8:17

children.text: * upeti viśeṣaṇe kriyopasaṃhāre samastatve ca // PSBh_1.8:18
children.translated_text: * '<s>Upa</s>' (toward) is used in the senses of qualification, conclusion of an action, and completeness. // PSBh 1.8:18

children.text: * upaharaṇād upahāro vrataṃ niyama ity arthaḥ // PSBh_1.8:19
children.translated_text: * Because of offering (<s>upaharaṇa</s>), the offering (<s>upahāra</s>) [means] observance (<s>vrata</s>) and regulation (<s>niyama</s>) — this is the meaning. // PSBh 1.8:19

children.text: * upahriyate nivedyate niyogamātrakartṛtvāt sādhakenety upahāraḥ // PSBh_1.8:20
children.translated_text: * It is offered (<s>upahriyate</s>), presented (<s>nivedyate</s>), by the practitioner (<s>sādhaka</s>) who acts only as [an instrument of] injunction — [this is called] offering (<s>upahāra</s>). // PSBh 1.8:20
* One should attend (<s>upatiṣṭhet</s>). // PSBh 1.8:21
* Here '<s>upa</s>' (toward) is used in the sense of assent (<s>abhyupagama</s>). // PSBh 1.8:22
* By one who has assented, who is established in the rule (<s>vidhistha</s>), who is bowed and humble — this is the meaning. // PSBh 1.8:23

children.text: * tiṣṭhed ity aikāgryaṃ pratyāhārābhāvasthitim evādhikurute // PSBh_1.8:24
children.translated_text: * 'One should stand' (<s>tiṣṭhet</s>) enjoins one-pointed concentration (<s>aikāgrya</s>), the state of abiding in withdrawal (<s>pratyāhāra</s>). // PSBh 1.8:24

children.text: * sarvakaraṇānāṃ vṛttau pratyāhāraṃ kṛtvā kāyikavācikamānasikābhiḥ kriyābhir upahāraṃ kṛtvā bhṛtyavad upahāreṇa stheyam // PSBh_1.8:25
children.translated_text: * Having withdrawn all the senses from their activities, having made the offering through bodily, vocal, and mental actions, one should stand like a servant with the offering. // PSBh 1.8:25

children.text: * apasavyaṃ ca pradakṣiṇam upariṣṭād vakṣyāmaḥ // PSBh_1.8:26
children.translated_text: * And the leftward circumambulation (<s>apasavya pradakṣiṇa</s>) we shall explain further on. // PSBh 1.8:26
* He asks: Whose <s>nirmālya</s> (remnant offerings) should be worn? // PSBh 1.8:27
* Or in whose sanctuary should one dwell? // PSBh 1.8:28
* Or where should one attend [in worship]? // PSBh 1.8:29
* To that it is said: // PSBh 1.8:30
Of <s>Mahādeva</s> (the Great God), [before] the south-facing image (<s>dakṣiṇāmūrti</s>). || PS 1.9 ||
* Here, 'great' (<s>mahān</s>) is used in the sense of surpassing excellence. // PSBh 1.9:1

children.text: * sarvakṣetrajñānām abhyadhika utkṛṣṭo vyatiriktaś ca bhavatīty abhyadhikaḥ // PSBh_1.9:2
children.translated_text: * He who surpasses, excels, and transcends all <s>kṣetrajñas</s> (knowers of the field / individual souls) is called 'surpassing' (<s>abhyadhika</s>). // PSBh 1.9:2
* He is a seer (<s>ṛṣi</s>), a sage (<s>vipra</s>), and a sovereign lord (<s>adhipati</s>). // PSBh 1.9:3
* The eternal auspiciousness (<s>sadāśivatva</s>) and surpassing excellence we shall explain [later]. // PSBh 1.9:4

children.text: * atra deva iti divu krīḍāyām // PSBh_1.9:5
children.translated_text: * Here, '<s>deva</s>' (god) — from the root '<s>divu</s>' meaning 'play' (<s>krīḍā</s>). // PSBh 1.9:5
* Because [the Lord's activity] has play as its nature. // PSBh 1.9:6
* Just as fire has heat [as its nature]. // PSBh 1.9:7

children.text: * krīḍāvān eva bhagavān vidyākalāpaśusaṃjñakaṃ trividham api kāryam utpādayati anugṛhṇāti tirobhāvayati ca // PSBh_1.9:8
children.translated_text: * The playful <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed Lord) himself produces, sustains, and causes the disappearance of the threefold effect designated as knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>), art (<s>kalā</s>), and individual soul (<s>paśu</s>). // PSBh 1.9:8

children.text: * uktaṃ hi / apracodyaḥ pracodyais tu kāmakārakaraḥ prabhuḥ / krīḍate bhagavān lokair bālaḥ krīḍanakair iva // PSBh_1.9:9

children.translated_text: * 'Of the god' (<s>devasya</s>) — this is a genitive [case ending]. // PSBh 1.9:10
* The relationship [between god and devotee] is that of master and servant (<s>svasvāmibhāva</s>). // PSBh 1.9:11
* He undertakes [worship] precisely for the purpose of [divine] possession (<s>parigraha</s>). // PSBh 1.9:12
* Here, 'southern' (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>) refers to the directional distinction. // PSBh 1.9:13
* The sun divides the directions. // PSBh 1.9:14
* And the directions distinguish the [divine] form (<s>mūrti</s>). // PSBh 1.9:15

children.text: * mūrtināma yad etad devasya dakṣiṇe pārśve sthitenodaṅmukhenopānte yad rūpam upalabhyate vṛṣadhvajaśūlapāṇinandimahākālordhvaliṅgādilakṣaṇaṃ yad vā laukikāḥ pratipadyante mahādevasyāyatanam iti tatropastheyam // PSBh_1.9:16
children.translated_text: * As for 'form' — that form which is perceived on the southern side of the god, standing facing north at the edge, characterized by the bull-bannered one (<s>Vṛṣadhvaja</s>), the trident-bearer (<s>Śūlapāṇi</s>), <s>Nandin</s>, <s>Mahākāla</s>, the upright <s>liṅga</s>, and so forth, or whatever the worldly people understand as 'the temple of <s>Mahādeva</s>' — there one should present oneself for worship. // PSBh 1.9:16
* By the specification of 'the southern form' (<s>dakṣiṇāmūrti</s>), the eastern, northern, and western forms are excluded. // PSBh 1.9:17
* And because of the restriction to [a particular] form, in the absence of [that] form, the restriction lapses. // PSBh 1.9:18

children.text: * bhaikṣyānupayogān nirghātānām uktatvāc cety arthaḥ // PSBh_1.9:19
children.translated_text: * Because there is no use for alms-food, and because the striking practices (<s>nirghāta</s>) have [already] been stated — this is the meaning. // PSBh 1.9:19

children.text: * vidhir ity upadiṣṭānām arthānāṃ bhasmasnānopadeśād apsu snānādīnāṃ pratiṣedhaḥ // PSBh_1.9:20
children.translated_text: * 'Injunction' (<s>vidhi</s>) — from the teaching of bathing in ash (<s>bhasmasnāna</s>) among the prescribed matters, bathing in water and similar [practices] are prohibited. // PSBh 1.9:20
* From the teaching of lying on ash (<s>bhasmaśayana</s>), lying on [comfortable] objects and similar [practices] are prohibited. // PSBh 1.9:21

children.text: * āyatane vasaty arthopadeśāc cheṣavasaty arthapratiṣedhaḥ // PSBh_1.9:22
children.translated_text: * From the teaching that one should dwell at a temple (<s>āyatana</s>), dwelling in other places is prohibited. // PSBh 1.9:22
* From the teaching of laughter and similar [practices], other types of offerings are prohibited. // PSBh 1.9:23
* From the teaching of [using] offerings already used (<s>nirmālya</s>), fresh garlands are prohibited. // PSBh 1.9:24
* From the teaching of ash, used garlands, and the <s>liṅga</s>, other [religious] marks are prohibited. // PSBh 1.9:25
* By the specification of <s>Mahādeva</s>, devotion to other deities is prohibited. // PSBh 1.9:26
* By the specification of the southern form (<s>dakṣiṇāmūrti</s>), the eastern, western forms are prohibited. // PSBh 1.9:27

children.text: * evaṃ dakṣiṇāmūrtir ity ukte asya brāhmaṇasya pūrvaprasiddhā niyamā niyamaiḥ pratiṣidhyante // PSBh_1.9:28
children.translated_text: * Thus, when the 'southern form' (<s>dakṣiṇāmūrti</s>) is specified, the previously established observances (<s>niyama</s>) of this <s>brāhmaṇa</s> are superseded by [new] observances. // PSBh 1.9:28
* Like a peg [replaced] by a counter-peg, or like old water [replaced] by new water. // PSBh 1.9:29
* Here this section on ash (<s>bhasmaprakaraṇa</s>) is concluded. // PSBh 1.9:30

children.text: * āha niyamābhidhānād eva hi saṃśayaḥ // PSBh_1.9:31
children.translated_text: * He raises [an objection]: From the very statement of observances (<s>niyama</s>), indeed, a doubt [arises]. // PSBh 1.9:31
* Where there are restraints (<s>yama</s>), there [must also be] observances (<s>niyama</s>). // PSBh 1.9:32
* For these two are indeed a pair (<s>mithuna</s>). // PSBh 1.9:33
* Therefore there is no doubt. // PSBh 1.9:34

children.text: * yamā asmin tantre ke cintyante // PSBh_1.9:35
children.translated_text: * What restraints (<s>yama</s>) are considered in this system (<s>tantra</s>)? // PSBh 1.9:35

children.text: * ucyate prasiddhā yamāḥ ahiṃsādaya iti // PSBh_1.9:36
children.translated_text: * It is said: The well-known restraints (<s>yama</s>) are non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>) and so forth. // PSBh 1.9:36
* But here, [it differs] from [the systems of] others. // PSBh 1.9:37

children.text:
* ahiṃsā brahmacaryaṃ ca satyāsaṃvyavahārakau / asteyam iti pañcaite yamā vai saṃprakīrtitāḥ // PSBh_1.9:38
* akrodho guruśuśrūṣā śaucam āhāralāghavam / apramādaś ca pañcaite niyamāḥ saṃprakīrtitāḥ // PSBh_1.9:39
children.translated_text: * '<s>Ahiṃsā</s> (non-violence), <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy), <s>satya</s> (truthfulness), <s>asaṃvyavahāra</s> (non-worldly-dealings), and <s>asteya</s> (non-stealing) — these five are declared to be the restraints (<s>yama</s>). Non-anger (<s>akrodha</s>), service to the teacher (<s>guruśuśrūṣā</s>), purity (<s>śauca</s>), moderation in food (<s>āhāralāghava</s>), and vigilance (<s>apramāda</s>) — these five are declared to be the observances (<s>niyama</s>).' // PSBh 1.9:38-39
* It is not so for us [in this system]. // PSBh 1.9:40
* Why? // PSBh 1.9:41
* Because the cessation of observances (<s>niyama</s>) is observed. // PSBh 1.9:42

children.text: * asmin hi tantre kālāntaritā niyamā nivartante // PSBh_1.9:43
children.translated_text: * For in this system, observances cease after a [specified] period of time. // PSBh 1.9:43

children.text: * katham ā dehapātād yamānāṃ na nivṛttir asti // PSBh_1.9:44
children.translated_text: * How [can it be that] the restraints (<s>yama</s>) do not cease until the fall of the body [i.e., death]? // PSBh 1.9:44
* Why? // PSBh 1.9:45
* Because of the fault of violence (<s>hiṃsā</s>) and so forth. // PSBh 1.9:46

children.text: * tasmād ahiṃsādyā daśa sarve te yamāḥ pratyavagantavyaḥ // PSBh_1.9:47
children.translated_text: * Therefore, non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>) and the [other] ten — all of them should be understood as restraints (<s>yama</s>). // PSBh 1.9:47

children.text: * āha yady evaṃ nigamanivṛttau bhraṣṭaniyamasya patanaprasaṅgaḥ // PSBh_1.9:48
children.translated_text: * He objects: If so, when the observances cease, there is the danger of falling for one whose observances have been abandoned. // PSBh 1.9:48
* It is said: Because the purpose has been accomplished, there is no danger of falling. // PSBh 1.9:49
* Moreover, because of the primacy of the restraints (<s>yama</s>). // PSBh 1.9:50

children.text: * uktaṃ hi patati niyamavān yameṣv asakto na tu yamavān niyamālaso 'vasīdet // PSBh_1.9:51
children.translated_text: * For it has been said: 'One who has observances but is unattached to the restraints falls; but one who has restraints does not sink down, [even if] lax in observances.' // PSBh 1.9:51

children.text: * iti yamaniyamau samīkṣya buddhyā yamabahuleṣv atisaṃdadhīta buddhim // PSBh_1.9:52
children.translated_text: * 'Therefore, having examined the restraints and observances with intelligence, one should fix one's mind on [the system] where restraints predominate.' // PSBh 1.9:52
* Therefore there is no danger of falling. // PSBh 1.9:53
* Hence the well-known restraints (<s>yama</s>) are non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>) and so forth. // PSBh 1.9:54

children.text: * āha kiṃ prasiddhā iti kṛtvā gṛhyante āhosvic chakyam eteṣāṃ yamānāṃ sarvajñoktaśāstrataḥ sadbhāvo vaktum // PSBh_1.9:55
children.translated_text: * He asks: Are they accepted because they are well-known, or is it possible to establish the existence of these restraints from a treatise spoken by an omniscient one? // PSBh 1.9:55

children.text: * ucyate yady anyatra prasiddhā iti kva // PSBh_1.9:56
children.translated_text: * It is said: If they are well-known elsewhere, then where? // PSBh 1.9:56
* On that matter, one should reflect. // PSBh 1.9:57
* Why? // PSBh 1.9:58
* Because [their] teaching has been made [in the sūtra]. // PSBh 1.9:59
* Since it has been stated from the <s>sūtra</s> as 'done' (<s>kṛta</s>) in this [passage]. // PSBh 1.9:60

children.text: * kṛtāpratiṣedhā kṛtsnā hiṃsā tantre pratiṣiddhā draṣṭavyetyarthaḥ // PSBh_1.9:61
children.translated_text: * 'Done' means the prohibition is complete — all violence (<s>hiṃsā</s>) is to be seen as prohibited in this system — this is the meaning. // PSBh 1.9:61

children.text: * sā ca hiṃsā trividhā bhavati // PSBh_1.9:62
children.translated_text: * And that violence (<s>hiṃsā</s>) is threefold. // PSBh 1.9:62
* [Namely:] causing suffering (<s>duḥkhotpādana</s>), breaking eggs (<s>aṇḍabheda</s>), and releasing life-breath (<s>prāṇanirmocana</s>). // PSBh 1.9:63

children.text: * tatra duḥkhotpādanaṃ nāma krośanatarjanatāḍananirbhartsanādibahubhedo'pi caturvidhasyāpi bhūtagrāmasya manovākkāyakarmabhir abhidroho na kartavyaḥ // PSBh_1.9:64
children.translated_text: * There, 'causing suffering' means — though it takes many forms such as scolding, threatening, striking, and reviling — one should not commit hostility (<s>abhidroha</s>) against any of the four classes of living beings through actions of mind, speech, or body. // PSBh 1.9:64
* Thus non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>) applies to these creatures. // PSBh 1.9:65

children.text: * aṇḍabhedo nāma dāhatāpadhūmoparodhaparihārārtham agnikaraṇādānasampradānapratinidhānasaṃdhukṣaṇādīni na kuryāt naiva kārayet // PSBh_1.9:66
children.translated_text: * 'Breaking eggs' (<s>aṇḍabheda</s>) means: for the purpose of avoiding burning, scorching, smoking, and enclosure [of living beings], one should not make, take, give, deposit, or kindle fire and the like, nor should one cause [others] to do so. // PSBh 1.9:66

children.text: * tathā prāṇanirmocanaṃ nāma vastraśikyabhasmādhārabhaikṣyabhājanādīni muhurmuhur vivecayitavyāni // PSBh_1.9:67
children.translated_text: * Likewise, 'releasing life-breath' (<s>prāṇanirmocana</s>) means: cloth, hanging vessel, ash-container, alms-bowl, and the like should be inspected again and again. // PSBh 1.9:67
* Why? // PSBh 1.9:68

children.text: * prāṇino hi sūkṣmacāriṇaḥ kṣiprameva vilayaṃ prayānti // PSBh_1.9:69
children.translated_text: * For living beings that move about minutely perish very quickly. // PSBh 1.9:69

children.text: * tasmāt sūkṣmair aṅgapavitraiḥ pakṣmacāmaratālavṛntair vastrāntarair vā muhurmuhur vigranthodakena vā // PSBh_1.9:70
children.translated_text: * Therefore, with fine body-purifiers — eyelash [brushes], fly-whisks, palm-leaf fans, or cloth edges — [one should clean them] again and again, or by straining water. // PSBh 1.9:70

children.text: * hariteṣu tṛṇeṣu na saṃsikte bhūpradeśe bhavati // PSBh_1.9:71
children.translated_text: * [One should dwell] on green grass, not on ground that has been sprinkled [with water]. // PSBh 1.9:71

children.text: * vasantagrīṣmahaimāntikān aṣṭau māsān bhikṣur vicakramet // PSBh_1.9:72
children.translated_text: * For the eight months of spring, summer, and winter, the mendicant (<s>bhikṣu</s>) should wander about. // PSBh 1.9:72

children.text: * dayārthaṃ sarvabhūtānām ekatra varṣāsu vaset // PSBh_1.9:73
children.translated_text: * Out of compassion for all beings, he should stay in one place during the rains. // PSBh 1.9:73

children.text:
* varṣābhedaṃ tu yaḥ kuryād brāhmaṇo yogadīkṣitaḥ / prājāpatyena kṛcchreṇa tataḥ pāpāt pramucyate // PSBh_1.9:74
* śārīraṃ dṛśyate yatra bhayaṃ kasyāṃcid āpadi / durdine rāṣṭrabhaṅge vā varṣāsvapi vyatikramet // PSBh_1.9:75
* nāsūryaṃ ca vrajenmārgaṃ nādṛṣṭāṃ bhūmim ākramet / paripūnābhiradbhiśca nityaṃ kuryāt prayojanam // PSBh_1.9:76
* saṃvatsarakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ matsyabandhasya yad bhavet / ekāhāt tadavāpnoti apūtajalasaṃgrahī // PSBh_1.9:77
* dṛṣṭipūtaṃ nyaset pādaṃ vastrapūtaṃ jalaṃ pibet / satyapūtāṃ vaded vācaṃ manaḥpūtaṃ samācaret // PSBh_1.9:78
* hiṃsakāstu nivartante brahmatvamapi ye gatāḥ / tasmādapūtamudakaṃ nopayuñjīta yogavit // PSBh_1.9:79
* atha naṣṭe pavitre ca gṛhṇīyāt triṣu vai sakṛt / nadīprasravaṇe caiva gṛhastheṣu ca sādhuṣu // PSBh_1.9:80
* kāṇḍāni yāni gṛhyante kandāścaiva prarohiṇaḥ / bījāni caiva pakvāni sarvāṇyetāni varjayet // PSBh_1.9:81
* yadā na kuryād drohaṃ ca sarvabhūteṣu dāruṇam / karmaṇā manasā vācā brahma saṃpadyate tadā // PSBh_1.9:82
* yo na hiṃsati bhūtāni sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca / ātmānamiva sarvāṇi so 'mṛtatvāya kalpate // PSBh_1.9:83
* na yajñadānairna tapo'gnihotrairna brahmacaryair na ca satyavākyaiḥ / na vedavidyādhyayanair vratairvā prāpyaṃ phalaṃ yady ahiṃsakasya // PSBh_1.9:84
* yo dadyāt kāñcanaṃ meruṃ kṛtsnāṃ caiva vasuṃdharām / samudraṃ ratnapūrṇaṃ vā na tulyaṃ syādahiṃsayā // PSBh_1.9:85
children.translated_text: * 'But a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> consecrated for <s>yoga</s> who would break the rain-retreat — he is freed from that sin through the <s>Prājāpatya</s> penance (<s>kṛcchra</s>). Where physical danger is seen in some calamity, in bad weather or in the destruction of the kingdom, he may transgress even during the rains. One should not travel a path [not seen by] the sun, nor should one tread on ground unseen; one should always attend to one's needs with water that is fully [filtered]. Whatever sin a fish-catcher incurs in a year, that [same sin] one who collects impure water obtains in a single day. One should place one's foot only where purified by sight, drink water purified by cloth, speak speech purified by truth, and practice what is purified by mind. Even those who have attained the state of <s>Brahmā</s> fall if they commit violence; therefore the one who knows <s>yoga</s> should not use impure water. And when the filter is lost, one may take [water] three times — from a river, a spring, and from virtuous householders. Stalks that are plucked, and sprouting tubers, and ripe seeds — all these should be avoided. When one does no cruelty to any beings, whether stationary or moving, by action, mind, or speech — then one attains <s>Brahman</s>. One who does not harm beings, stationary or moving, regarding all as oneself — such a one is fit for immortality. Not by sacrifices and gifts, not by austerity and fire-offerings, not by celibacy or truthful words, not by study of the <s>Vedas</s> or vows — the fruit that belongs to one who is non-violent cannot be obtained [by any of these]. Were one to give golden [Mount] <s>Meru</s>, the entire earth, or the ocean filled with gems — it would not equal non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>).' // PSBh 1.9:74-85
* Thus non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>) is established in this system. // PSBh 1.9:86

children.text: * tathā brahmacaryaṃ ca tantre siddham // PSBh_1.9:87
children.translated_text: * Likewise, celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>) too is established in this system. // PSBh 1.9:87
* Why? // PSBh 1.9:88

children.text: * strīpratiṣedhāt indriyajayopadeśāc ca trayodaśakasya karaṇasyānutsargo brahmacaryamityuktam // PSBh_1.9:89
children.translated_text: * Because of the prohibition of women, and because of the teaching of sense-control — the non-release of the thirteen-fold instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) is stated to be celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>). // PSBh 1.9:89
* Especially with regard to the tongue and the sexual organ. // PSBh 1.9:90
* Here he asks: What is the purpose of the specific mention? // PSBh 1.9:91

children.text: * trayodaśakasya karaṇasyānutsargo brahmacaryamityuktvā jihvopasthayor viśeṣagrahaṇaṃ kiṃprayojanaṃ kriyate // PSBh_1.9:92
children.translated_text: * Having stated that the non-release of the thirteen-fold instrument is celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>), what purpose is served by specifically mentioning the tongue and the sexual organ? // PSBh 1.9:92
* It is said: Because of [their] primacy. // PSBh 1.9:93
* Because the activity of the others is rooted in those [two]. // PSBh 1.9:94
* For the activity of the other [senses] is rooted in those [two]. // PSBh 1.9:95
* How? // PSBh 1.9:96

children.text: * jihvendriyaviṣaye upasthendriyaviṣaye vā saktaḥ trayodaśabhiḥ pravartate // PSBh_1.9:97
children.translated_text: * One who is attached to the object of the tongue-sense or to the object of the genital organ operates with [all] thirteen [senses]. // PSBh 1.9:97
* Therefore it is stated: 'Especially with regard to the tongue and the sexual organ.' // PSBh 1.9:98

children.text: * jihvopasthanimittaṃ hi patanaṃ sarvadehinām / tasmād amitravat paśyej jihvopasthaṃ hi mānavaḥ // PSBh_1.9:99
children.translated_text: * 'For the fall of all embodied beings is caused by the tongue and the sexual organ; therefore a man should regard the tongue and the sexual organ as enemies.' // PSBh 1.9:99

children.text: * athavā manaḥpūrvakatvāt sarvavṛttīnāṃ tannigrahāt sarvavṛttīnāṃ nigrahaḥ kṛto bhavati // PSBh_1.9:100
children.translated_text: * Alternatively, since all activities are preceded by the mind, through the restraint of that [mind], the restraint of all activities is accomplished. // PSBh 1.9:100

children.text:
* uktaṃ hi / mano hi mūlaṃ sarveṣāmindriyāṇāṃ pravartane / śubhāśubhāsvavasthāsu tac ca me suvyavasthitam // PSBh_1.9:101
* punarapyuktam / indriyaiḥ prasṛtair duḥkhamindriyair nibhṛtaiḥ sukham / tasmād indriyarūpebhyo yac chedātmānamātmanā // PSBh_1.9:102
* indriyāṇi hi tat sarvaṃ yat svarganarakāv ubhau / nigṛhītavisṛṣṭāni svargāya narakāya ca // PSBh_1.9:103
* ato janma ato duḥkhamato mṛtyubhayaṃ tathā / indriyāṇāṃ prasaṅgād vai tasmādetān jayāmahe // PSBh_1.9:104
* indriyāṇāṃ prasaṅgena doṣam ṛcchatyasaṃśayam / saṃniyamya tu tānyeva tataḥ siddhiṃ niyacchati // PSBh_1.9:105
* rajjureṣā nibandhāya yā strīṣu ramate matiḥ / chittvaināṃ kṛtino yānti naināṃ tyajati duṣkṛtī // PSBh_1.9:106
* strīhetornirgamo grāmāt strīkṛte krayavikrayaḥ / striyo mūlamanarthānāṃ naināṃ prājñaḥ pariṣvajet // PSBh_1.9:107
* viṣamagnirasirbāṇaḥ sphuṭaṃ kṛtvā vibhīṣikā / māyā rūpavatī hy eṣā yāṃ striyaṃ manyate janaḥ // PSBh_1.9:108
* amedhyapūrṇe kṛmijantusaṃkule svabhāvadurgandha aśauca adhruve / kaḍebare mūtrapurīṣabhājane ramanti mūrkhā na ramanti paṇḍitāḥ // PSBh_1.9:109
* mādyatīti striyaṃ dṛṣṭvā surāṃ pītvā na mādyati / tasmād dṛṣṭimadāṃ nārīṃ dūrataḥ parivarjayet // PSBh_1.9:110
* adhomukhenādaṃṣṭreṇa jaghanāntaracāriṇā / sarvaśāstrācikitsyena jagad daṣṭaṃ bhagāhinā // PSBh_1.9:111
* lomaśena kurūpeṇa durgandhena kucarmaṇā / hariṇīpadamātreṇa sarvam andhīkṛtaṃ jagat // PSBh_1.9:112
* dīptāṅgārasamā nārī ghṛtakumbhasamaḥ pumān / ye prasaktā vilīnāste ye sthitāste divaṃ gatāḥ // PSBh_1.9:113
* yathāgniredhaḥsaṃvṛddho mahājyotiḥ prakāśate / tathendriyanirodhena svātmajyotiḥ prakāśate // PSBh_1.9:114
* brahmacarye sthitaṃ dhairyaṃ brahmacarye sthitaṃ tapaḥ / ye sthitā brahmacaryeṇa brāhmaṇā divi te sthitāḥ // PSBh_1.9:115
* kṣīraṃ pibanti madhu te pibanti somaṃ pibantyamṛtena sārdham / mṛtyoḥ purastādamarā bhavanti ye brāhmaṇā brahmacaryaṃ caranti // PSBh_1.9:116
children.translated_text:
* For it has been said: "The mind indeed is the root of all the senses in their activity, in auspicious and inauspicious states, and that [mind] of mine is well-established." PSBh_1.9:101
* And again it has been said: "From senses that are let loose comes suffering; from senses that are restrained comes happiness; therefore one should cut oneself off from the objects of the senses by one's own self." PSBh_1.9:102
* "The senses indeed are all that constitutes both heaven and hell; when restrained, [they lead] to heaven, and when released, to hell." PSBh_1.9:103
* "From these [senses] comes birth, from these comes suffering, and likewise from these comes the fear of death; it is indeed due to the attachment of the senses, therefore let us conquer them." PSBh_1.9:104
* "Through attachment of the senses one incurs fault without doubt; but by restraining those very [senses], one then attains <s>siddhi</s> (perfection)." PSBh_1.9:105
* "That inclination which delights in women is a rope for bondage; the meritorious cut it and go forth, but the wicked one does not abandon it." PSBh_1.9:106
* "It is for the sake of women that one leaves the village, for the sake of women that buying and selling [occurs]; women are the root of all misfortunes — a wise man should not embrace them." PSBh_1.9:107
* "Poison, fire, sword, arrow — having made [these] manifest as terrors — this woman whom people regard is indeed <s>māyā</s> (illusion) in a beautiful form." PSBh_1.9:108
* "In this body filled with impurity, swarming with worms and creatures, foul-smelling by nature, impure, impermanent — in this corpse that is a vessel of urine and excrement, fools delight, but the wise do not." PSBh_1.9:109
* "One becomes intoxicated upon seeing a woman, [yet] does not become intoxicated upon drinking liquor; therefore one should avoid from afar a woman who intoxicates through sight." PSBh_1.9:110
* "By the downward-facing, fangless [serpent] that moves between the thighs — by the vagina-serpent incurable by all <s>śāstras</s> (scriptures) — the world has been bitten." PSBh_1.9:111
* "By that which is hairy, ugly, foul-smelling, with bad skin, merely the size of a doe's footprint — the entire world has been blinded." PSBh_1.9:112
* "A woman is like a blazing ember; a man is like a pot of ghee; those who are attached are dissolved, [but] those who stand firm have gone to heaven." PSBh_1.9:113
* "Just as fire, nourished with fuel, shines with great radiance, so through the restraint of the senses, the light of one's own <s>ātman</s> (self) shines forth." PSBh_1.9:114
* "In <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy) is established firmness; in <s>brahmacarya</s> is established <s>tapas</s> (austerity); those <s>brāhmaṇas</s> who are established in <s>brahmacarya</s> — they are established in heaven." PSBh_1.9:115
* "They drink milk, they drink honey, they drink <s>Soma</s> together with the immortal nectar; they become immortal before [the face of] death — those <s>brāhmaṇas</s> who practice <s>brahmacarya</s>." PSBh_1.9:116
* Thus <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy) is established in the system. PSBh_1.9:117
* Likewise, <s>satya</s> (truthfulness) is established in the system. PSBh_1.9:118
* And that is of two kinds. PSBh_1.9:119

children.text: * tadyathā paridṛṣṭārthabhūtārthaṃ vacanaṃ vāksatyaṃ ceti // PSBh_1.9:120
children.translated_text: * Namely: speech whose content has been directly observed and is factual is [one kind of] truth, and truth of speech [is the other]. PSBh_1.9:120

children.text: * tatra paridṛṣṭārthabhūtārthaṃ vacanaṃ satyaṃ tantre siddham // PSBh_1.9:121
children.translated_text: * Of these, speech whose content has been directly observed and is factual — [that kind of] truth is established in the system. PSBh_1.9:121
* Why? PSBh_1.9:122
* Because of the teaching of explanation, and because of the teaching of the learned. PSBh_1.9:123
* Likewise, truth of speech also is established in the system. PSBh_1.9:124
* Why? PSBh_1.9:125
* Because of the teaching of the purification of speech. PSBh_1.9:126
* Here, when one speaks what is stated in one's own <s>śāstra</s> (scripture), even what is [technically] untrue becomes truth. PSBh_1.9:127
* Why? PSBh_1.9:128
* Because it produces purification and increase [of merit]. PSBh_1.9:129

children.text:
* yasmādāha / svargamanṛtena gacchati dayārthamuktena sarvabhūtānām / satyenāpi na gacchati satāṃ vināśārthamuktena // PSBh_1.9:130
* punastvāha / gobrāhmaṇārthe 'vacanaṃ himasti na strīṣu rājan na vivāhakāle / prāṇātyaye sarvadhanāpahāre pañcānṛtānyāhurapātakāni // PSBh_1.9:131
* satyaṃ brūyāt priyaṃ brūyān na brūyāt satyamapriyam / priyaṃ ca nānṛtaṃ brūyādeṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ // PSBh_1.9:132
children.translated_text:
* Since he says: "One goes to heaven by an untruth spoken out of compassion for all beings; but one does not go [to heaven] even by truth, when it is spoken for the destruction of good people." PSBh_1.9:130
* And again he says: "A false statement for the sake of cows and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> does not harm, nor [falsehood spoken] regarding women, O king, nor at the time of marriage, nor when life is in danger, nor when all wealth is being seized — these five untruths, they say, are not sins." PSBh_1.9:131
* "One should speak what is true; one should speak what is pleasant; one should not speak what is true but unpleasant; and one should not speak what is pleasant but untrue — this is the eternal <s>dharma</s>." PSBh_1.9:132

children.text: * yathā hi teṣāmeva bhūtānāṃ hitamanṛtamapi satyamāpadyate evamihāpyasmākaṃ svaśāstroktaṃ bhāṣatāmanṛtamapi satyamāpadyate // PSBh_1.9:133
children.translated_text: * Just as for those very beings, even an untruth that is beneficial becomes truth, so here too for us, when we speak what is stated in our own <s>śāstra</s>, even what is [technically] untrue becomes truth. PSBh_1.9:133
* Why? PSBh_1.9:134
* Because it is prescribed by injunction. PSBh_1.9:135
* Thus this too is established therein. PSBh_1.9:136
* Likewise, <s>asaṃvyavahāra</s> (non-worldly-dealings) is established in the system. PSBh_1.9:137
* Why? PSBh_1.9:138
* Because of the teaching [to behave as one who is] unmanifest, [as if] a ghost, mad, or bewildered. PSBh_1.9:139

children.text: * neha loke avyaktapretonmattamūḍhāḥ saṃvyavahāraṃ kurvanti yasmād ato'trāsaṃvyavahārastantre siddhaḥ // PSBh_1.9:140
children.translated_text: * In this world, those who are unmanifest, ghost-like, mad, or bewildered do not engage in worldly dealings; therefore <s>asaṃvyavahāra</s> (non-worldly-dealings) is established in the system. PSBh_1.9:140
* And worldly dealings are again of two kinds. PSBh_1.9:141
* Namely: dealings of buying and selling, and dealings with the royal court. PSBh_1.9:142

children.text: * ata ekatareṇāpyatrādhikṛtasyātmapīḍā parapīḍā cāvarjanīye bhavataḥ // PSBh_1.9:143
children.translated_text: * Hence, for one who is initiated [in this system], even by either one of these, self-affliction and affliction of others become unavoidable. PSBh_1.9:143

children.text: * tatra yadyātmānaṃ pīḍayati tenehaiva loke duḥkhī bhavati // PSBh_1.9:144
