children.translated_text: * In that regard, if one afflicts oneself, then one becomes miserable in this very world. PSBh_1.9:144

children.text: * syāt paraṃ pīḍayati tatrāpyasyādharmo duḥkhādiphalaḥ pracīyate // PSBh_1.9:145
children.translated_text: * Should one afflict another, in that case too <s>adharma</s> (demerit) bearing fruit as suffering and so on accumulates for him. PSBh_1.9:145
* Thereby one experiences intense suffering in the next world. PSBh_1.9:146
* Therefore, worldly dealings should be avoided in both ways. PSBh_1.9:147

children.text:
* bhavati hy api / yaśca pāpaṃ prakurute yaśca pāpaṃ praśaṃsati / sahāyaścopabhoktā ca sarve te samakarmiṇaḥ // PSBh_1.9:148
* uktaṃ hi / vikraye tu mahān doṣo vikrayāt patate yataḥ / eṣa eva kraye doṣastasmāt taṃ parivarjayet // PSBh_1.9:149
* pracchannaṃ kurute pāpaṃ na me jānāti kaścana / mucyate janavādebhyastasmāt pāpān na mucyate // PSBh_1.9:150
* punarapyuktam / ādityacandrāv anilo'nalaśca dyaur bhūmir āpo hṛdayaṃ yamaśca / ahaśca rātriśca ubhe ca saṃdhye dharmo hi jānāti narasya vṛttam // PSBh_1.9:151
* nārambhaśīlo na ca dambhaśīlaḥ śāstropadiṣṭāni karotyadīnaḥ / yameṣu yukto niyameṣu caiva munir bhavaty eṣv ajaro'maraśca // PSBh_1.9:152
children.translated_text:
* For it is also said: "He who commits sin, he who praises sin, the accomplice, and the one who enjoys [its fruits] — all these are equal in their <s>karma</s>." PSBh_1.9:148
* For it has been said: "In selling there is great fault, since through selling one falls; the same fault exists in buying — therefore one should avoid it." PSBh_1.9:149
* "One commits sin in secret [thinking] 'no one knows about me'; one may escape the censure of people, but one does not escape from sin." PSBh_1.9:150
* And again it has been said: "<s>Āditya</s> (the Sun), <s>Candra</s> (the Moon), the wind, fire, the sky, the earth, the waters, the heart, <s>Yama</s>, and day and night and both twilights — <s>Dharma</s> indeed knows the conduct of a man." PSBh_1.9:151
* "One who is not given to [worldly] undertakings, nor given to hypocrisy, who performs what is taught in the <s>śāstras</s> without dejection, who is devoted to the <s>yamas</s> (restraints) and the <s>niyamas</s> (observances) — such a sage becomes ageless and immortal." PSBh_1.9:152
* Likewise, <s>asteya</s> (non-stealing) is established in the system. PSBh_1.9:153
* Why? PSBh_1.9:154
* Because of the teaching of non-possession of clothing, and because of the prohibition against [eating] food that has not been [freely] offered. PSBh_1.9:155

children.text: * iha vidyamānasyāpyekasya vāsaso malavad avasthitasyāvāsopadeśāt parigrahaparityāga upadiśyate // PSBh_1.9:156
children.translated_text: * Here, through the teaching of non-possession of clothing, the renunciation of possessions is taught — [such that] even a single garment that exists remains in a soiled condition. PSBh_1.9:156
* And what else? PSBh_1.9:157
* Because the use of food, drink, and other things that have been discarded [by others] is observed. PSBh_1.9:158
* Therefore <s>asteya</s> (non-stealing) is established in the system. PSBh_1.9:159
* And stealing is again of six kinds. PSBh_1.9:160

children.text: * tatra adattādānam anatisṛṣṭagrahaṇam anabhimatagrahaṇam anadhikārapratigrahaḥ anupālambhaḥ aniveditopayogaśceti // PSBh_1.9:161
children.translated_text: * Of these: taking what is not given, seizing what has not been granted, taking what is not desired [by the owner to be taken], accepting what one has no authority [to accept], deception, and using without informing — [these are the six]. PSBh_1.9:161
* Taking what has not been given is <s>adattādāna</s> (taking the ungiven). PSBh_1.9:162
* <s>Anatisṛṣṭagrahaṇa</s> (seizing what has not been granted) means the appropriation of the wealth of children, the mad, the careless, the aged, and the weak. PSBh_1.9:163
* <s>Anabhimatagrahaṇa</s> (taking what is not desired) means the appropriation of property not intended [to be taken] from insects, bees, birds, moths, and the like. PSBh_1.9:164

children.text: * anadhikārapratigraho nāma iha śāstre anabhyanujñātānām arthānāṃ gobhūhiraṇyadvipadacatuṣpadādīnāṃ grahaṇam // PSBh_1.9:165
children.translated_text: * <s>Anadhikārapratigraha</s> (accepting without authority) means the acceptance of things not sanctioned in this <s>śāstra</s> — cows, land, gold, bipeds, quadrupeds, and the like. PSBh_1.9:165

children.text: * anupālambho nāma kuhakakalkanaḍambhavismāpanavardhāpanādibhir upāyaiḥ parebhyo hiraṇyāc chādanopayogaḥ // PSBh_1.9:166
children.translated_text: * <s>Anupālambha</s> (deception) means the use of gold, clothing, and other goods [obtained] from others by means of trickery, fraud, deceit, dazzlement, flattery, and similar stratagems. PSBh_1.9:166

children.text: * aniveditopayogo nāma bhakṣyabhojyalehyapeyacoṣyādīnām anyatamaṃ yatkiṃcid gurave 'niveditam upayuṅkte sa ucyate aniveditopayoga iti // PSBh_1.9:167
children.translated_text: * <s>Aniveditopayoga</s> (using without informing) means when one consumes any among things to be eaten, to be chewed, to be licked, to be drunk, to be sucked, and so forth, without having informed [one's] <s>guru</s> (teacher) — that is called using without informing. PSBh_1.9:167
* Thus stealing is of six kinds. PSBh_1.9:168

children.text: * asya ṣaḍvidhasyāpi steyasya parivarjanam asteyamāhurācāryāḥ // PSBh_1.9:169
children.translated_text: * The avoidance of this sixfold stealing, the <s>ācāryas</s> (teachers) call <s>asteya</s> (non-stealing). PSBh_1.9:169

children.text:
* bhavati hy api / yadetad dhanamityāhuḥ prāṇā hy ete bahiścarāḥ / sa tasya harate prāṇān yo yasya harate dhanam // PSBh_1.9:170
* uktaṃ hi / sarvasvaparimoṣṭā ca jīvitāntakaraśca yaḥ / dvāv etau samakarmāṇau tasmāt steyaṃ vivarjayet // PSBh_1.9:171
* na stenasya paro loko nāyaṃ loko durātmanaḥ / śaṅkitaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ drohātmā pāpa eva saḥ // PSBh_1.9:172
* mṛdamāpastathā yānaṃ pattraṃ puṣpaṃ phalānyapi / asaṃvṛtāni gṛhṇīyāt pavitrārthīha kāryavān // PSBh_1.9:173
* nadyaśca vāpyaḥ kūpāśca taṭākāni sarāṃsi ca / asaṃvṛtāni gṛhṇīyāt prājāpatyena karmaṇā // PSBh_1.9:174
children.translated_text:
* For it is also said: "What they call wealth — these are indeed one's life-breaths moving outside; he who steals another's wealth steals his life-breaths." PSBh_1.9:170
* For it has been said: "One who robs another of all possessions and one who takes another's life — these two are equal in their <s>karma</s>; therefore one should renounce stealing." PSBh_1.9:171
* "For a thief there is no next world, nor is this world [agreeable] for the wicked-souled one; suspected by all beings, hostile in spirit — he is nothing but evil." PSBh_1.9:172
* "One who has duties to perform and seeks purity may take things that are unenclosed: earth, water, a vehicle, leaves, flowers, and fruits." PSBh_1.9:173
* "Rivers, reservoirs, wells, tanks, and lakes — one may use those that are unenclosed, by the rite of <s>Prajāpati</s>." PSBh_1.9:174
* Thus <s>asteya</s> (non-stealing) is established in the system. PSBh_1.9:175
* <s>Akrodha</s> (non-anger) is established in the system. PSBh_1.9:176
* Why? PSBh_1.9:177
* Because of the prohibition regarding <s>śūdras</s>, and because of the teaching on excessive austerity. PSBh_1.9:178

children.text: * ihādhyātmikādhibhautikādhidaivikānāṃ sarvadvaṃdvānāṃ manasi śarīre ca upanipatitānāṃ sahiṣṇutvam apratīkāraśceti yasmāt kṛto 'trākrodhas tantre siddhaḥ // PSBh_1.9:179
children.translated_text: * Here, since the patient endurance of all pairs of opposites — <s>ādhyātmika</s> (pertaining to the self), <s>ādhibhautika</s> (pertaining to beings), and <s>ādhidaivika</s> (pertaining to the gods) — when they befall the mind and body, and non-retaliation [are taught], therefore <s>akrodha</s> (non-anger) is established in the system. PSBh_1.9:179
* And anger is again of four kinds. PSBh_1.9:180

children.text: * tadyathā bhāvalakṣaṇaḥ karmalakṣaṇaḥ vaikalyakaraḥ udvegakaraśceti // PSBh_1.9:181
children.translated_text: * Namely: characterized by emotional states, characterized by action, causing injury, and causing agitation. PSBh_1.9:181

children.text: * tatra bhāvalakṣaṇo nāma saḥ yatrāsūyādveṣamadamānamātsaryādayo bhāvāḥ pravartante // PSBh_1.9:182
children.translated_text: * Of these, that which is characterized by emotional states is where states such as envy, hatred, intoxication, pride, jealousy, and the like arise. PSBh_1.9:182

children.text: * karmalakṣaṇo nāma yatra kalahavairasaṃpraharaṇādyā bhāvāḥ pravartante // PSBh_1.9:183
children.translated_text: * That which is characterized by action is where states such as quarrel, enmity, combat, and the like arise. PSBh_1.9:183

children.text: * vaikalyakaro nāma yatra pāṇipādanāsākṣyaṅgulipraharaṇādayo bhāvāḥ pravartante // PSBh_1.9:184
children.translated_text: * That which causes injury is where states such as striking with hands, feet, nose, eyes, fingers, weapons, and the like arise. PSBh_1.9:184

children.text: * udvegakaro nāma yatra svātmānaṃ parātmānaṃ vā prāṇair viyojayati // PSBh_1.9:185
children.translated_text: * That which causes agitation is where one separates oneself or another from [their] life-breaths. PSBh_1.9:185
* Thus anger is of four kinds. PSBh_1.9:186

children.text: * asya caturvidhasyāpi krodhasya parivarjanam akrodhamāhurācāryāḥ // PSBh_1.9:187
children.translated_text: * The avoidance of this fourfold anger, the <s>ācāryas</s> (teachers) call <s>akrodha</s> (non-anger). PSBh_1.9:187

children.text: * tasmād deśajātikulakarmasambandhanindāyāṃ karaṇakriyāyāṃ kāryanindāyām āhāranindāyāṃ vādhikṛtena krodho na kartavyaḥ // PSBh_1.9:188
children.translated_text: * Therefore, the initiated one should not give rise to anger when [there is] censure of [one's] region, birth, family, actions, or associations, when [there is] censure of [one's] practices and rituals, when [there is] censure of [one's] duties, or when [there is] censure of [one's] food. PSBh_1.9:188
* Of these, first there is censure of one's region. PSBh_1.9:189

children.text: * tadyathā yatra bhavān jātastatra deśe brāhmaṇā eva na santīti yadi kaścidadhikṣepaṃ kuryāt tatra krodho na kartavyaḥ // PSBh_1.9:190
children.translated_text: * For example: if someone should reproach [one] saying, "In the region where you were born, there are no <s>brāhmaṇas</s> at all" — in that case, anger should not be produced. PSBh_1.9:190

children.text: * tatraitat syād evamabhihite tīvraduḥkhaṃ mānasamabhivyajyate // PSBh_1.9:191
children.translated_text: * In that regard, one might [object]: "When [one is] addressed thus, intense mental suffering manifests." PSBh_1.9:191
* "How will anger not arise in that case?" PSBh_1.9:192
* It is said: it will not arise. PSBh_1.9:193
* Why? PSBh_1.9:194
* Because of the power of analytical contemplation. PSBh_1.9:195

children.text: * iha manuṣyaloke deśo'yaṃ nāma mātāpitṛhetukaḥ aupacayikaḥ kāryapiṇḍaḥ śarīrākhyaḥ // PSBh_1.9:196
children.translated_text: * In this human world, what is called 'region' is this body — caused by mother and father, produced by accumulation [of <s>karma</s>], a product-aggregate, designated as 'body.' PSBh_1.9:196
* He [the self] is [merely] born from that [body]. PSBh_1.9:197
The <s>kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field), however, is conscious, all-pervading, and pure.
And the difference between him and us is unknown.
You might say this regarding a matter that has not been observed.

children.text: * ataḥ krodhanimittāsaṃbhavāt parisaṃkhyānasāmarthyena krodho na kāryaḥ // PSBh_1.9:201
children.translated_text: Therefore, since the cause for anger does not arise, by the power of reasoning (<s>parisaṃkhyāna</s>), anger should not be produced.
The same should be understood with respect to the remaining [afflictions] as well.

children.text:
* bhavati hy api / śṛṅgavān nakhavān daṃṣṭrī vikṛto rudhirāśanaḥ / rākṣaso vā piśāco vā krodhiṣṇur jāyate naraḥ // PSBh_1.9:203
* punaścāha / kaṅkagṛdhrasṛgāleṣu daṃśeṣu maśakeṣu ca / pannageṣu ca jāyante narāḥ krodhaparāyaṇāḥ // PSBh_1.9:204
* vidviṣṭaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ bahvamitro 'lpabāndhavaḥ / krūradharmā durācāraḥ krodhiṣṇur jāyate naraḥ // PSBh_1.9:205
* kruddhaḥ karoti pāpāni kruddhaḥ pāpāni bhāṣate / kruddho bhavati nirlajjastasmāt krodhaṃ vivarjayet // PSBh_1.9:206
* tathā coktam / yat krodhano japati yac ca juhoti yadvā yadvā tapastapyati yad dadāti tatsarvam / vaivasvato harati pūrtamamuṣya sarvaṃ mithyā śrutaṃ bhavati tasya śamo'pi tasya // PSBh_1.9:207
* dhanyāste puruṣavyāghrā ye buddhyā krodhamutthitam / śamayanti mahātmāno dīptamagnimivāmbhasā // PSBh_1.9:208
* yato rūpaṃ tato jñānaṃ yato jñānaṃ tatastapaḥ / yatastapastataḥ siddhiryataḥ siddhistataḥ kṣamā // PSBh_1.9:209
* kṣamā sarvaparaṃ mitraṃ krodhaḥ sarvaparo ripuḥ / kṣamāvatāmayaṃ lokaḥ paro lokaḥ kṣamāvatām // PSBh_1.9:210
children.translated_text: For it is also said: "Horned, clawed, fanged, deformed, feeding on blood — as a <s>Rākṣasa</s> or a <s>Piśāca</s>, or as a wrathful human is one reborn." And again it says: "Among herons, vultures, jackals, biting insects, mosquitoes, and serpents are reborn those men who are devoted to anger." "Hated by all beings, having many enemies and few kinsmen, of cruel conduct and evil behavior — as such a wrathful person is reborn." "An angry man commits sins, an angry man speaks sinful words, an angry man becomes shameless — therefore one should abandon anger." And thus it is said: "Whatever an angry man recites, whatever he offers in oblation, whatever austerity he performs, whatever he gives — all that <s>Vaivasvata</s> (Yama) takes away; all his merit becomes false, and even his tranquility is lost." "Blessed are those tigers among men who, with wisdom, extinguish anger once it has arisen, as great souls extinguish a blazing fire with water." "From beauty comes knowledge, from knowledge comes austerity, from austerity comes accomplishment, from accomplishment comes forbearance." "Forbearance (<s>kṣamā</s>) is the supreme friend, anger is the supreme enemy; this world belongs to the forbearing, and the next world also belongs to the forbearing."

children.text: * etasmāt kāraṇāt kṣantavyam ity evamakrodhastantre siddhaḥ // PSBh_1.9:211
children.translated_text: For this reason, one should practice forbearance — thus <s>akrodha</s> (non-anger) is established in the doctrine.
Likewise, <s>guruśuśrūṣā</s> (service to the teacher) is established in the doctrine.
Why?
Because of the instruction regarding exposition (<s>vyākhyāna</s>) and the instruction from the learned.

children.text: * iha coktaṃ vidhiṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ iti // PSBh_1.9:215
children.translated_text: And here it has been stated: "We shall expound the rule (<s>vidhi</s>)."
Here, the particle <s>āṇ</s> is used in the sense of a binding injunction (<s>maryādā</s>).
The particle <s>ma</s> occurs in the sense of a solemn declaration (<s>pratijñā</s>).
"It depends on me."
"It rests in me."

children.text: * yadi ceṣṭe vatsyasi yadi ceṣṭe sthāsyasi tataste vakṣyāmaḥ // PSBh_1.9:220
children.translated_text: "If you will abide in what is desired, if you will remain in what is desired, then we shall tell you."
There, the word <s>iṣṭa</s> ("desired") refers to the eightfold <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate discipline) as the binding injunction.

children.text: * tadyathā utthānapratyutthānābhivādanagurukāryahitakārī anuttarottaravādī pūrvotthāyī jaghanyasaṃveśī preṣitāpreṣitasarvakāryakṛtajñaḥ sarvaniveditātmā dakṣo dākṣiṇyānuraktaḥ snānodvartanasaṃvāhanādibhiḥ kriyāviśeṣaiḥ chāyevānugato nityamidaṃ kṛtam idaṃ kariṣye kiṃ karavāṇīti bhūtvā gurave 'harahar vartitavyam // PSBh_1.9:222
children.translated_text: That is as follows: one who performs rising, rising in greeting, salutation, the teacher's tasks, and beneficial acts; who does not speak back with a superior retort; who rises first and retires last; who is grateful for all tasks whether commanded or uncommanded; who dedicates his entire self [to the teacher]; who is skillful, devoted to courtesy; who follows like a shadow always through special services such as bathing, anointing, and massaging — having become one who says "this has been done, this I shall do, what shall I do?" — one should conduct oneself thus toward the teacher day after day.

children.text: * yastu vidyāṃ guroradhikṛtya bahubhyaḥ samprayacchati anenāsya vidyāyā dānena guravaḥ śuśrūṣitā bhavanti // PSBh_1.9:223
children.translated_text: But one who, having received knowledge from the teacher, imparts it to many — by this gift of knowledge, the teachers are thereby served.

children.text: * kṣīṇe ca brahmacarye niyataṃ guruṣu yad gauravaṃ tad brahmacaryam // PSBh_1.9:224
children.translated_text: And when the period of <s>brahmacarya</s> has ended, the reverence that is maintained toward teachers — that itself is <s>brahmacarya</s>.

children.text:
* bhavati hy api / gururdevo guruḥ svāmī gururmātā guruḥ pitā / yasyaivaṃ niścito bhāvaḥ śreyastasya na dūrataḥ // PSBh_1.9:225
* agnisūryendutārābhiścākṣuṣo 'rthaḥ prakāśate / bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ bhaviṣyaṃ ca guruvākyaiḥ prakāśate // PSBh_1.9:226
* deśakairgamyate'dhvānaṃ deśakairgamyate'rṇavaḥ / deśakairgamyate svargo gururmokṣasya deśakaḥ // PSBh_1.9:227
* amṛtasya pradātāraṃ yo guruṃ hy avamanyate / ṣaṣṭivarṣasahasrāṇi narakaṃ paryupāsate // PSBh_1.9:228
* guroryatra parīvādo nindā yatra pravartate / karṇau tatra pidhātavyau gantavyaṃ vā tato'nyataḥ // PSBh_1.9:229
* ācāryaṃ pūjayed yastu sarvāvasthaṃ hi nityaśaḥ / pūjitastena bhavati śivo vai nātra saṃśayaḥ // PSBh_1.9:230
* ācāryamūrtimāsthāya śivo jñānaṃ prayacchati / tasmād vai nāvamantavya ācāryaḥ śreya icchatā // PSBh_1.9:231
* granthārthaviduṣe nityaṃ yogamārgānudarśine / sarvārthenāpi kartavyaḥ paritoṣo vijānatā // PSBh_1.9:232
* ṛcaṃ vā yadi vārdharcaṃ pādaṃ vā yadi vākṣaram / sakāśād yasya gṛhṇīyān niyataṃ tatra gauravam // PSBh_1.9:233
* liṅgakartrī yathā mātā śāstrakartā yathā pitā / prabodhakṛd gurusteṣāṃ tadevāyatanaṃ mahat // PSBh_1.9:234
children.translated_text: For it is also said: "The teacher is God, the teacher is the lord, the teacher is the mother, the teacher is the father — for one whose conviction is thus established, well-being is not far away." "By fire, sun, moon, and stars, visible objects are illuminated; but the past, present, and future are illuminated by the words of the teacher." "By a guide one traverses a road, by a guide one crosses the ocean, by a guide one reaches heaven — the teacher is the guide to <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation)." "One who disrespects the teacher, the bestower of the immortal — that person dwells in hell for sixty thousand years." "Where there is slander of the teacher, where criticism takes place, there one should cover one's ears, or else go elsewhere." "One who always worships the <s>ācārya</s> (preceptor) in all circumstances — <s>Śiva</s> is indeed pleased by that; there is no doubt about this." "Assuming the form of the <s>ācārya</s>, <s>Śiva</s> bestows knowledge; therefore, the <s>ācārya</s> should never be disrespected by one who desires well-being." "To one who knows the meaning of the texts, who always shows the path of <s>yoga</s> — by all means should the discerning one render satisfaction to him." "From whomever one learns even a single verse, or half a verse, or a quarter, or even a syllable — toward that person reverence is obligatory." "As the mother is the maker of the body, as the father is the maker of sacred knowledge, so the teacher is the awakener — that is their great abode."
Thus, <s>guruśuśrūṣā</s> (service to the teacher) is established in the doctrine.
Likewise, <s>śauca</s> (purity) is established in the doctrine.
Why?
Because of the instruction regarding bathing with ash (<s>bhasmasnāna</s>).
And that purity is threefold.

children.text: * tad yathā gātraśaucaṃ bhāvaśaucam ātmaśaucaṃ ceti // PSBh_1.9:240
children.translated_text: That is as follows: purity of the body (<s>gātraśauca</s>), purity of disposition (<s>bhāvaśauca</s>), and purity of the self (<s>ātmaśauca</s>).

children.text: * tatra bhasmasnānopadeśāt prasiddhaṃ bhasmanā gātraśaucam // PSBh_1.9:241
children.translated_text: Of these, from the instruction regarding bathing with ash, purity of the body through <s>bhasman</s> (ash) is well-established.

children.text: * āha yaduktaṃ prasiddhaṃ bhasmanā gātraśaucamiti etadevāyuktam // PSBh_1.9:242
children.translated_text: One objects: "What has been stated — that purity of the body through ash is well-established — this itself is improper."
Why?
Because of contradiction between the earlier and later [statements].

children.text: * iha purastāduktaṃ prasiddhā yamā ahiṃsādayo bhavanti // PSBh_1.9:245
children.translated_text: Here it was stated earlier that the <s>yamas</s> (restraints) such as <s>ahiṃsā</s> (non-violence) and so forth are well-established.

children.text: * yadiha bhūyo'pi aprasiddhaṃ bhasmanā gātraśaucamityabhidhīyate // PSBh_1.9:246
children.translated_text: If here again bodily purity through ash is stated as something not [already] well-established,
then the earlier and later statements do not agree with each other.
And there would be a contradiction.
This is the fault — therefore, because of contradiction between the earlier and later [statements].

children.text: * tatra yaduktaṃ prasiddhaṃ bhasmanā gātraśaucamityetadayuktam // PSBh_1.9:250
children.translated_text: In that regard, what was stated — that purity of the body through ash is well-established — that is improper.
The reply is: this is not a fault.
Why?
Because it is seen to be well-established [elsewhere].
Elsewhere too, purity of the body through ash is well-established.

children.text:
* evaṃ hy āha / saṃsargajāśca ye doṣā ye cānye pitṛmātṛjāḥ / annapānakṛtāścaiva saṃkarā dehamāśritāḥ / sarvāṃstān dahate bhasma asthimajjāgatānapi // PSBh_1.9:255
* punaścāha / keśakīṭopapannāni duṣṭānnāni ca yāni vai / bhasmanā spṛṣṭamātrāṇi bhojyāny āhur manīṣiṇaḥ // PSBh_1.9:256
* punarapyuktam / madyaṃ pītvā gurudārāṃśca gatvā steyaṃ kṛtvā brahmahatyāṃ ca kṛtvā / bhasmoddhvasto bhasmarāśau śayāno rudrādhyāyī mucyate pātakebhyaḥ // PSBh_1.9:257
* yaḥ snānam ācaren nityamāgneyaṃ saṃyatendriyaḥ / kulaikaviṃśamuddhṛtya sa gacchet paramāṃ gatim // PSBh_1.9:258
children.translated_text: For thus it is said: "Those impurities born of association, those arising from father and mother, those caused by food and drink, and the mixtures residing in the body — ash burns all of them, even those lodged in the bones and marrow." And again it says: "Foods that are contaminated with hair and insects, and those that are spoiled — when merely touched by ash, they become fit for eating, say the wise." And further it is said: "Having drunk liquor, having gone to the wife of the teacher, having committed theft, and having committed the slaying of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> — one who is covered with ash, who lies on a heap of ash, who recites the <s>Rudrādhyāya</s>, is freed from sins." "One who always performs the fire-bath (<s>āgneya snāna</s>) with restrained senses — having uplifted twenty-one generations of his family, he attains the supreme destination."
Thus, elsewhere too, purity of the body through ash is well-established.

children.text: * tasmād yuktaṃ vaktuṃ prasiddhā yamā ahiṃsādaya iti // PSBh_1.9:260
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is proper to say that the <s>yamas</s> such as <s>ahiṃsā</s> and so forth are well-established.

children.text: * tathopasparśanaprāṇāyāmajapyaiḥ akaluṣamatirbhavatīti bhāvaśaucaṃ tantre siddham // PSBh_1.9:261
children.translated_text: Likewise, <s>bhāvaśauca</s> (purity of disposition) is established in the doctrine, since through <s>upasparśana</s> (ritual touching of water), <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control), and <s>japya</s> (recitation), one becomes free from mental impurity.

children.text:
* bhāvamantargataṃ duṣṭaṃ na snānamapakarṣati / bhāvaśuddhiḥ parā śuddhiḥ śeṣaṃ śṛṅgāramārjanam // PSBh_1.9:262
* mṛttikānāṃ sahasreṇa jalakumbhaśatena ca / na śudhyanti durātmānaḥ pāpopahatacetasaḥ // PSBh_1.9:263
* satyaṃ śaucaṃ tapaḥ śaucaṃ śaucamindriyanigrahaḥ / sarvabhūtadayā śaucam adbhiḥ śaucaṃ tu pañcamam // PSBh_1.9:264
* śaucameva paraṃ teṣāṃ yeṣāṃ notpadyate spṛhā / pratigrahe tathārambhe indriyāṇāṃ ca gocare // PSBh_1.9:265
* yasmādāha / sarvasvamapi yo dadyāt kaluṣeṇāntarātmanā / na tena dharmabhāg bhavati bhāva evātra kāraṇam // PSBh_1.9:266
* yathā yathā hi puruṣaḥ kalyāṇīṃ kurute matim / tathā tathāsya sidhyanti sarvārthā nātra saṃśayaḥ // PSBh_1.9:267
children.translated_text: "Bathing does not remove the inner, corrupted disposition; purity of disposition is the highest purity — the rest is mere cosmetic cleansing." "With thousands of clods of earth and hundreds of water-pots, wicked souls whose minds are stained by sin are not purified." "Truth is purity, austerity is purity, restraint of the senses is purity, compassion for all beings is purity — purification by water is but the fifth." "Purity is truly supreme for those in whom no craving arises regarding receiving gifts, undertaking actions, or the objects of the senses." As it says: "Even one who gives away all his possessions, but with a tainted inner self — he does not partake of <s>dharma</s>; for the disposition alone is the cause here." "As a person cultivates a wholesome mind, so do all his aims succeed — there is no doubt about this."
Thus, <s>bhāvaśauca</s> (purity of disposition) is established in the doctrine.
Likewise, <s>ātmaśauca</s> (purity of the self) is established in the doctrine.
Why?

children.text: * yasmād avamānaparibhavaparivādādyair apahatapāpmā bhavati ityātmaśaucaṃ tantre siddham // PSBh_1.9:271
children.translated_text: Because through dishonor, humiliation, slander, and the like, one becomes freed from sin (<s>apahatapāpmā</s>) — thus <s>ātmaśauca</s> (purity of the self) is established in the doctrine.

children.text: * yasmād anyair apyuktaṃ / kṛtsnāṃ mahīṃ paryaṭataḥ saśailavanakānanām / apamānāt paraṃ nāsti sādhanaṃ manurabravīt // PSBh_1.9:272
children.translated_text: As others too have said: "For one who wanders over the entire earth with its mountains, forests, and groves — <s>Manu</s> declared that there is no greater means [of purification] than dishonor."
Thus, <s>śauca</s> (purity) is established in the doctrine.
Likewise, <s>āhāralāghava</s> (lightness of diet) is established in the doctrine.
Why? Because of the instruction regarding food obtained through <s>bhaikṣa</s> (begging alms), what is discarded, and what is obtained by chance.

children.text: * svalpamapi anupāyato'rjitamalaghu prabhūtamapi upāyato'rjitaṃ laghveva draṣṭavyam // PSBh_1.9:276
children.translated_text: Even a small amount acquired by improper means is not light; even a large amount acquired by proper means should be regarded as light indeed.

children.text:
* uktaṃ hi / carenmādhukarīṃ vṛttiṃ valmīkanicayopamām / akruddhaś cāprahṛṣṭaś ca tapastaddhi sanātanam // PSBh_1.9:277
* yaścaret sarvabhojyeṣu bhaikṣyaṃ ca vyavahārataḥ / bhuñjīta pratigṛhṇīyāt praśastānāṃ svakarmasu // PSBh_1.9:278
* cāturvarṇyaṃ cared bhaikṣyaṃ patitāṃstu vivarjayet / payaścāpaśca bhaikṣyaṃ ca samametan na saṃśayaḥ // PSBh_1.9:279
* bhaikṣyaśeṣaṃ tu yo bhikṣuryadi kiṃcit samutsṛjet / grāse grāse tu kartavyāḥ prāṇāyāmāstrayastrayaḥ // PSBh_1.9:280
* saṃnidhānaṃ na kurvīta sarvāvastho'pi yogavit / saṃnidhānakṛtairdoṣairyatiḥ saṃjāyate kṛmiḥ // PSBh_1.9:281
* mādhukaram asaṃkalpaṃ prākpravṛttamayācitam / tattatkālopapannaṃ ca bhaikṣyaṃ pañcavidhaṃ smṛtam // PSBh_1.9:282
* gṛhād gṛhaṃ paryaṭaṃstu na gṛhaṃ parivarjayet / parasya vacanaṃ śrutvā duṣṭaveśma vivarjayet // PSBh_1.9:283
* aduṣṭāpatitaṃ sādhuṃ bhikṣuko yo vyatikramet / sa tasya sukṛtaṃ dattvā duṣkṛtaṃ pratipadyate // PSBh_1.9:284
* tathaiva ca gṛhasthasya nirāśo bhikṣuko vrajet / sa tasyeṣṭaṃ ca pūrtaṃ ca bhikṣurādāya gacchati // PSBh_1.9:285
* akṛte vaiśvadeve tu bhikṣuke gṛhamāgate / uddhṛtya vaiśvadevārthaṃ bhikṣukaṃ tu visarjayet // PSBh_1.9:286
* vaiśvadevakṛtān doṣān śakto bhikṣurvyapohitum / nahi bhikṣukṛtān doṣān vaiśvadevo vyapohati // PSBh_1.9:287
* daśāhaṃ dvādaśāhaṃ vā yatra bhikṣā na labhyate / tad gṛhaṃ varjayed bhikṣurūṣarāṇīva karṣakaḥ // PSBh_1.9:288
* caturakṣarasaṃyuktāṃ bhikṣāṃ tu samudāharet / eṣa pravrajināṃ dharmaḥ śeṣastu krayavikrayaḥ // PSBh_1.9:289
* na hasen na cābhiprekṣet bhikṣāmicchaṃstu bhikṣukaḥ / godohamātraṃ saṃtiṣṭhen nopatiṣṭhet kadācana // PSBh_1.9:290
* jarāmaraṇagarbhebhyo bhītasya narakādapi / bhayāt kṣapayate yasmāt tasmād bhaikṣyamiti smṛtam // PSBh_1.9:291
* dadhibhakṣāḥ payobhakṣā ye 'nye yāvakabhakṣiṇaḥ / sarve te bhaikṣyabhakṣasya kalāṃ nārhanti ṣoḍaśīm // PSBh_1.9:292
* taptakāñcanavarṇena gavāṃ mūtreṇa yāvakam / pibed dvādaśa varṣāṇi na tad bhaikṣyasamaṃ bhavet // PSBh_1.9:293
* māsi māsi kuśāgreṇa yaḥ pibet somamagrajaḥ / bhaikṣyaṃ cāvyavahāreṇa tulyaṃ bhavati vā na vā // PSBh_1.9:294
* bhaikṣyamannaṃ paraṃ śreyo bhaikṣyamannaṃ paraṃ śuci / bhaikṣyaṃ hi vratināṃ śreṣṭhaṃ bhaikṣyameva parā gatiḥ // PSBh_1.9:295
* yadyaj jalaṃ nirdhamaneṣv apeyaṃ nadīgataṃ tat punareva peyam / tathānnapānaṃ vidhipūrvamāgataṃ dvijātipātrāntaritaṃ na duṣyati // PSBh_1.9:296
* lavaṇamalavaṇaṃ vā snigdham asnehikaṃ vā saharasavirasaṃ vā śuṣkamannaṃ dravaṃ vā / yadi iha niravadyaṃ bhuñjate bhaikṣyamannaṃ sa khalu bhavati bhikṣurbhikṣudharmādaluptaḥ // PSBh_1.9:297
children.translated_text: * For it has been said: 'One should practice the bee-like mode of living, comparable to collecting from an anthill; neither angry nor elated — for that is the eternal austerity.' [PSBh 1.9:277] 'One who would partake of alms among all [kinds of] food, in the course of worldly conduct — one may eat and accept from those of good repute in their own occupations.' [PSBh 1.9:278] 'One should beg alms from all four <s>varṇas</s> (classes) but should avoid the fallen. Milk, water, and alms — these are equal; there is no doubt.' [PSBh 1.9:279] 'If a mendicant discards even a small remainder of alms-food, three <s>prāṇāyāmas</s> (breath-controls) should be performed for each morsel.' [PSBh 1.9:280] 'One who knows <s>yoga</s> should not store [food] in any condition. By the faults born of storing, the ascetic becomes a worm.' [PSBh 1.9:281] 'The bee-like, without premeditation, received before [asking], unbegged, obtained at the appropriate time — alms are remembered as fivefold.' [PSBh 1.9:282] 'Wandering from house to house, one should not skip any house. Having heard the word of another, one should avoid a corrupt dwelling.' [PSBh 1.9:283] 'A mendicant who passes by an uncorrupted, unfallen, virtuous [householder] — he gives away his own merit and receives [that person's] sin.' [PSBh 1.9:284] 'Likewise, a mendicant should leave without hope from a householder's [home]. The mendicant who departs takes away [that householder's] sacrificial and meritorious works.' [PSBh 1.9:285] 'When the <s>vaiśvadeva</s> (offering to all gods) has not yet been performed and a mendicant arrives at the house, one should set aside the portion for the <s>vaiśvadeva</s> and then dismiss the mendicant.' [PSBh 1.9:286] 'The mendicant is able to remove the faults incurred by [the interruption of] the <s>vaiśvadeva</s>, but the <s>vaiśvadeva</s> does not remove the faults incurred [from turning away] a mendicant.' [PSBh 1.9:287] 'A house where alms are not obtained for ten or twelve days — the mendicant should avoid that house, as a farmer [avoids] saline ground.' [PSBh 1.9:288] 'One should utter the request for alms with four syllables ["bhavati bhikṣāṃ dehi"]. This is the <s>dharma</s> of renunciants; anything else is buying and selling.' [PSBh 1.9:289] 'A mendicant desiring alms should neither laugh nor stare. One should stand for the time of milking a cow, and never sit down.' [PSBh 1.9:290] 'Because it destroys [suffering] out of fear — fear of old age, death, the womb, and hell — therefore it is remembered as <s>bhaikṣya</s> (alms-food).' [PSBh 1.9:291] 'Those who eat curds, those who drink milk, and others who eat barley gruel — none of them are worth a sixteenth part of one who eats alms-food.' [PSBh 1.9:292] 'Even if one were to drink barley gruel with cow's urine of molten-gold color for twelve years, it would not equal alms-food.' [PSBh 1.9:293] 'One who would drink <s>Soma</s> month after month with the tip of <s>kuśa</s> grass, first-born — whether that equals alms-food taken without worldly commerce, or not.' [PSBh 1.9:294] 'Alms-food is the supreme welfare; alms-food is the supreme purity. Alms-food is the best for those who observe vows; alms-food alone is the highest goal.' [PSBh 1.9:295] 'Whatever water is undrinkable at irrigation channels becomes drinkable again when it reaches a river. Likewise, food and drink that has come through proper procedure, having passed through the vessel of a twice-born, is not polluted.' [PSBh 1.9:296] 'Whether salty or unsalted, oily or without oil, with flavor or tasteless, dry food or liquid — if here one eats blameless alms-food, that one is truly a mendicant, undiminished in the <s>dharma</s> of mendicants.' [PSBh 1.9:297]

children.text: * tathotsṛṣṭaṃ yathālabdhaṃ ca tatraivāvasaraprāptatvāt pratitantrasiddhāntasiddhaṃ sūtrato 'rthanirdeśaṃ kariṣyāmaḥ // PSBh_1.9:298
children.translated_text: * Likewise, what has been released and obtained as it comes — since the occasion has arrived right there, we shall make the explanation of meaning from the <s>sūtra</s>, as established by the doctrine of each system. [PSBh 1.9:298]
* Thus lightness in food (<s>āhāralāghava</s>) is established in this system. [PSBh 1.9:299]
* Likewise, vigilance (<s>apramāda</s>) is established in this system. [PSBh 1.9:300]
* Because of the teaching of vigilance, and because of the teaching of recitation (<s>japya</s>). [PSBh 1.9:302]

children.text: * iha nityaṃ yameṣv apramattenopasthitasmṛtinā bhavitavyam // PSBh_1.9:303
children.translated_text: * Here, one must always be vigilant with present mindfulness regarding the restraints (<s>yamas</s>). [PSBh 1.9:303]

children.text:
* uktaṃ hi / apramādo damastyāgo brāhmaṇasya hayāḥ smṛtāḥ / śīlaraśmisamāyuktair dheyātmā mānase rathe // PSBh_1.9:304
* taṃ brahmarathamāruhya garbhajanmajarāyutān / chindan mṛtyubhayān pāśān brahmabhūto'vatiṣṭhate // PSBh_1.9:305
children.translated_text: * For it has been said: 'Vigilance, self-control, and renunciation are remembered as the horses of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. Yoked with the reins of good conduct, one should drive the self in the chariot of the mind.' [PSBh 1.9:304] 'Having mounted that chariot of <s>Brahman</s>, cutting the bonds of death's fear — [bonds] accompanied by womb, birth, and old age — one becomes <s>Brahman</s> and stands [firm].' [PSBh 1.9:305]
* Thus vigilance (<s>apramāda</s>) is established in this system. [PSBh 1.9:306]
* Thus the well-known restraints (<s>yamas</s>) are non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>) and so forth. [PSBh 1.9:307]

children.text: * āha aviśeṣadoṣān na prasiddhā yamāḥ // PSBh_1.9:308
children.translated_text: * He objects: the restraints are not established, because of the fault of non-distinction. [PSBh 1.9:308]
* Here, others too have non-violence and such as the means of <s>dharma</s>. [PSBh 1.9:309]
* And in this scripture too, they are the same. [PSBh 1.9:310]
* Therefore, there is no distinction even in the conclusions regarding what is to be accomplished and the means of accomplishment. [PSBh 1.9:311]
* The answer is: no. [PSBh 1.9:312]
* Because of over-extension (<s>atiprasaṅga</s>) and non-exclusiveness (<s>anekānta</s>). [PSBh 1.9:313]

children.text: * yadi dharmasādhanāstitvamātrasādharmyād ahiṃsādīnāṃ tyāgaḥ kriyate tasmāt kāryakāraṇakṣetrajñadharmādharmasukhaduḥkhasaṃsārapadārthādayo 'pi tyājyāḥ // PSBh_1.9:314
children.translated_text: * If non-violence and such are to be abandoned merely because of the similarity of being means of <s>dharma</s> [shared with other systems], then the categories of effect, cause, knower of the field (<s>kṣetrajña</s>), <s>dharma</s>, <s>adharma</s>, pleasure, suffering, <s>saṃsāra</s>, and so forth would also have to be abandoned. [PSBh 1.9:314]
* But [one might say] it is not so — [then there is] non-exclusiveness. [PSBh 1.9:315]
* Moreover, if [non-violence etc.] were abandoned, there would be the unwanted consequence that violence and such would become means of <s>dharma</s>. [PSBh 1.9:316]

* Moreover, through excessive giving, excessive worship, excessive austerity, excessive going forth, and non-return — [these show that] the method contains the restraints (<s>yama</s>) and observances (<s>niyama</s>) within itself, and this is established. [PSBh 1.9:317]
* And because of the qualification of the observances (<s>niyama</s>), there is no non-distinction. [PSBh 1.9:318]

children.text: * tasmād yuktamuktaṃ prasiddhā yamā ahiṃsādaya iti // PSBh_1.9:319
children.translated_text: * Therefore it is rightly said: the well-known restraints are non-violence and so forth. [PSBh 1.9:319]
* Hence it is said: 'of the southern form of <s>Mahādeva</s>.' [PSBh 1.9:320]
* Here this section on restraints (<s>yama</s>) is completed. [PSBh 1.9:321]

children.text: * āha tasminn āyatane prativasataḥ kā mātrā // PSBh_1.9:322
children.translated_text: * He asks: what is the measure [of possessions] for one dwelling in that sacred place? [PSBh 1.9:322]
* Should it be stated as for a householder and such? [PSBh 1.9:323]
* The answer is: no. [PSBh 1.9:324]
* Because [the sūtra] states: [PSBh 1.9:325]
* For it has been said: 'Unprompted, yet prompting [all], acting of his own will, the sovereign Lord — the <s>Bhagavān</s> plays with the worlds as a child [plays] with toys.' // PSBh 1.9:9
Having a single garment. [PS 1.10]
* Here, 'one' (<s>eka</s>) is a number. [PSBh 1.10:1]
* '<s>Vāsas</s>' is used in the sense of covering. [PSBh 1.10:2]

children.text: * tasya vāsaḥ pañcavidham aṇḍajaṃ voḍajaṃ vālajaṃ valkalajaṃ carmajaṃ vā // PSBh_1.10:3
children.translated_text: * His garment is of five kinds: born from an egg [i.e., silk], born from a womb [i.e., wool], born from hair, born from bark, or born from hide. [PSBh 1.10:3]

children.text: * yat kuśalenābhyupāyenopapadyate tad ekapaṭalam anekapaṭalaṃ vā grāmyādibhyo niṣparigrahaṃ kaupīnapracchādanamātraṃ lajjāpratīkārārthaṃ caikaṃ vāso grāhyam // PSBh_1.10:4
children.translated_text: * Whatever is obtained by skillful means — whether single-layered or multi-layered — [taken] without possessiveness from villages and such, being merely a covering for a loincloth (<s>kaupīna</s>), for the purpose of averting shame — that single garment should be taken. [PSBh 1.10:4]

children.text:
* asyaiva ca sūtrasya sāmarthyāt sarvadravyaparityāge kṛte ekavāsomātraparigrahaḥ saṃskartavyaḥ śiṣyaḥ / āha lajjāvinivṛttir asya kadā bhavatīti / ucyate jñānākaluṣābhyām / atra yadā prāptajñānaḥ kṣīṇakaluṣaś ca bhavati tadā tasya lajjānivṛttiḥ // PSBh_1.10:5
* āha kiṃ vinivṛttāyām api lajjāyāṃ niyatam evaikaṃ vāso grāhyam āhosvid aniyatam iti / ucyate aniyatam yasmād āha // PSBh_1.10:6
children.translated_text: * And by the force of this very <s>sūtra</s>, having renounced all possessions, the disciple is to be consecrated with the possession of only a single garment. He asks: when does the cessation of his shame occur? The answer is: through knowledge and the absence of impurity. Here, when one has attained knowledge and one's impurity has been exhausted, then one's shame ceases. [PSBh 1.10:5] He asks: even when shame has ceased, must one necessarily take a single garment, or is it optional? The answer is: it is optional, because [the sūtra] states: [PSBh 1.10:6]
Or without a garment. [PS 1.11]

children.text:
* atra akāro vāsaḥpratiṣedhe vartate / avāsasā nagnena yathā jātena niṣparigraheṇa bhavitavyam / āha avāsastve kiṃ te prayojanam / tad vācyam ekavāsastvavat / tad ucyate niṣparigrahārtham amaṅgalakhyāpanārthaṃ ceti prayojanadvayaṃ draṣṭavyam / vāśabdaḥ śaktyaśaktyor vicāraṇe / yady aśaktas tadā anagnenaikavāsasā bhāvyam / yadi śaktas tadā avāsasā nagnena yathājātena niṣparigraheṇa bhavitavyam ity arthaḥ / na tu vā vikalpe / vikalpārthāsaṃbhavād ity arthaḥ // PSBh_1.11:1
* āha tasminn āyatane prativasatā kim ā dehapātād anirgacchataiva stheyaṃ dhyānaikaniṣṭhena śilāvad āhosvid dṛṣṭo 'syāyatanān nirgamaḥ bhasmabhaikṣyodakārjanādinimittaṃ grāmādipraveśo vā / ucyate dṛṣṭaḥ / yasmāt // PSBh_1.11:2
children.translated_text: * Here the prefix 'a-' serves to negate the garment. One should be without a garment, naked, as one was born, without possessions. He asks: what is the purpose of being without a garment? That should be stated, like the purpose of having a single garment. The answer is: two purposes should be seen — for the sake of non-possessiveness and for the sake of proclaiming inauspiciousness. The word <s>vā</s> ('or') is for the examination of ability and inability. If unable, then one should be unclothed with a single garment. If able, then one should be without a garment, naked, as one was born, without possessions — this is the meaning. But <s>vā</s> is not for [expressing] an option [between equals]. Because the meaning of [mere] option is impossible — this is the meaning. [PSBh 1.11:1] He asks: while dwelling in that sacred place, should one remain without ever leaving, devoted solely to meditation, like a rock, until the fall of the body? Or is departure from this sacred place observed — for the purpose of collecting ash, alms, water, etc., or entering villages and such? The answer is: it is observed. Because: [PSBh 1.11:2]
One should not look at urine and feces. [PS 1.12]

children.text: * atra mūtraṃ ca purīṣaṃ ca mūtrapurīṣam / cārthe dvaṃdvasamāsaḥ atra mūtraṃ nāma yad etad udaraparyuṣitaṃ niḥsarati bahiḥ sravati tan mūtram // PSBh_1.12:1

children.translated_text: * From 'releasing' (<s>mocana</s>), [it is called] urine (<s>mūtra</s>). [PSBh 1.12:2]

children.text: * mūtratvābhisambandhāddhi mūtraṃ lokādiprasiddham ity arthaḥ // PSBh_1.12:3
children.translated_text: * Because of its connection with the nature of urine, urine is well-known in common usage — this is the meaning. [PSBh 1.12:3]

children.text: * purīṣaṃ nāma yad etat pītakhāditāvalīḍhānām āhāraviśeṣāṇām ādhyātmikena agninā paripakvam apānena skhalati tat purīṣam // PSBh_1.12:4
children.translated_text: * Feces (<s>purīṣa</s>) means that which, among the various foods that have been drunk, eaten, and licked, is cooked by the internal fire and expelled by the downward breath (<s>apāna</s>) — that is feces. [PSBh 1.12:4]

children.text: * purān nirgatatvāt purīṣatvābhisambandhād vā purīṣaṃ lokādiprasiddham ity arthaḥ // PSBh_1.12:5
children.translated_text: * Because it comes out from the body (<s>pura</s>), or because of its connection with the nature of feces, <s>purīṣa</s> is well-known in common usage — this is the meaning. [PSBh 1.12:5]
* The negative particle <s>na</s> serves to prohibit seeing. [PSBh 1.12:6]
* The meaning is: one should not look [at them]. [PSBh 1.12:7]

children.text: * ava iti apavarjanaṃ nāma pratiṣedhe jātigrahaṇendriyāntarapratiṣedhe cety arthaḥ // PSBh_1.12:8
children.translated_text: * <s>Ava</s> means 'exclusion' — [used] in prohibition, and by the mention of the class [i.e., seeing], it also prohibits the other senses — this is the meaning. [PSBh 1.12:8]
* <s>Īkṣa</s> [is the root meaning] 'to see.' [PSBh 1.12:9]

children.text: * yad etan nijaṃ buddhīndriyaṃ cakṣur anena cakṣuṣā anayā buddhyā manuṣyādīnāṃ mūtrapurīṣaṃ na draṣṭavyam // PSBh_1.12:10
children.translated_text: * With this eye — one's own cognitive sense-organ, the eye — with this faculty of intellect, one should not look at the urine and feces of humans and such. [PSBh 1.12:10]

children.text: * na tu gavādīnām ity arthaḥ // PSBh_1.12:11
children.translated_text: * But not [the urine and feces] of cows and such — this is the meaning. [PSBh 1.12:11]

children.text: * āha kiṃ mūtrapurīṣasaṃdarśanamātram evāsya pratiṣidhyate // PSBh_1.12:12
children.translated_text: * He asks: is only the mere seeing of urine and feces prohibited for him? [PSBh 1.12:12]
* The answer is: no. [PSBh 1.12:13]
* Because [the sūtra] states: [PSBh 1.12:14]

* Here, urine and feces — <s>mūtrapurīṣam</s> — is a <s>dvandva</s> compound with the meaning of 'and.' Here, urine means that which, having remained in the belly, exits and flows out. That is urine. [PSBh 1.12:1]
One should not speak to women and <s>śūdras</s>. [PS 1.13]

children.text: * atra strī ca śūdraś ca strīśūdram // PSBh_1.13:1
children.translated_text: * Here, a woman and a <s>śūdra</s> — <s>strīśūdram</s>. [PSBh 1.13:1]
* [This is] a <s>dvandva</s> compound with the meaning of 'and.' [PSBh 1.13:2]

children.text: * atra strī nāma seyaṃ lokaprasiddhā stanajaghanakeśavatī hāvabhāvavilāsayuktā puruṣabhāvasvabhāvikā divyā mānuṣā atiratirasā viṣayamūrtir iti kṛtvā pratiṣidhyate // PSBh_1.13:3
children.translated_text: * Here, a woman means she who is well-known in the world, possessing breasts, hips, and hair, endowed with coquetry, amorous gestures, and charm, whose nature inclines toward men — whether divine or human, exceedingly delightful — the embodiment of sense objects; considering this, [speaking to her] is prohibited. [PSBh 1.13:3]

children.text: * anubhāṣaṇapūrvikā cāsyāḥ prāptir bhaviṣyatītyataḥ strī nābhibhāṣitavyety arthaḥ // PSBh_1.13:4
children.translated_text: * And since approach to her would be preceded by conversation, therefore the meaning is: one should not speak to a woman. [PSBh 1.13:4]
* A <s>śūdra</s> means one who is well-known in the world and tradition as the servant of the three [higher] <s>varṇas</s>. [PSBh 1.13:5]
* From 'grieving' (<s>śocana</s>) and from 'harming' (<s>drohaṇa</s>) — [he is called] a <s>śūdra</s>. [PSBh 1.13:6]

children.text: * sa khalv adayālur iti kṛtvā pratiṣidhyate // PSBh_1.13:7
children.translated_text: * He indeed, being merciless — considering this, [speaking to him] is prohibited. [PSBh 1.13:7]
* For what purpose? [PSBh 1.13:8]

children.text: * tenākruṣṭaś cābhihataś ca vā kruddhas tadvadhārthaṃ pravartate ato jātijñānatapaḥśrutahānir bhavati // PSBh_1.13:9
children.translated_text: * Being abused or struck by him, [the practitioner], becoming angry, would proceed to kill him — and thereby there would be loss of birth [merit], knowledge, austerity, and learning. [PSBh 1.13:9]
* And when [the practice of] indication [of dishonor] is indicated, in the absence of dishonor and such, there is absence of both indication and growth [of merit]. [PSBh 1.13:10]
* We shall explain the fault-specification of this in the <s>sūtra</s> on freedom from impurity (<s>akaluṣa</s>). [PSBh 1.13:11]
* The negative particle <s>na</s> serves to prohibit speaking. [PSBh 1.13:12]
* The meaning is: one should not speak [to them]. [PSBh 1.13:13]
* The prefix <s>abhi</s> [means] engagement, connection. [PSBh 1.13:14]

children.text: * pratiṣedhe jātigrahaṇe cetarapratiṣedhe cety arthaḥ // PSBh_1.13:15
children.translated_text: * In prohibition, and by the mention of the class [i.e., speaking], it also prohibits the other [forms of communication] — this is the meaning. [PSBh 1.13:15]
* <s>Bhāṣa</s> [is the root used] in articulate speech. [PSBh 1.13:16]

children.text: * yad etat karmendriyaṃ vāg anayā vāṇyā iti // PSBh_1.13:17
children.translated_text: * That which is the action-organ of speech — by this voice, [one should not speak] — thus. [PSBh 1.13:17]

children.text: * ataḥ strīśūdraṃ nābhibhāṣitavyam ity arthaḥ // PSBh_1.13:18
children.translated_text: * Therefore, the meaning is: one should not speak to women and <s>śūdras</s>. [PSBh 1.13:18]

children.text: * āha nāvekṣen nābhibhāṣed ity ukte 'tha kim anena sādhakenāndhamūkavad avasthātavyam iti // PSBh_1.13:19
children.translated_text: * He asks: When it is stated 'one should not look at, one should not speak to,' does this practitioner then have to remain like a deaf-mute? // PSBh 1.13:19
* It is said: No. // PSBh 1.13:20
* Since he says: // PSBh 1.13:21
If one should look at, if one should speak to — || PS 1.14 ||

children.text: * atra yadi yadi ity āśaṅkāyām // PSBh_1.14:1
children.translated_text: * Here 'if... if...' [expresses] apprehension. // PSBh 1.14:1

children.text: * nābhibhāṣed iti vacanān niṣiddhe 'py arthe gurvartham ātmārthaṃ vā bhasmabhaikṣyodakārjanādinimittaṃ grāmādīn praviṣṭasya viṇmūtrayoḥ strīśūdrayoś ca darśanam abhibhāṣaṇaṃ ca bhaviṣyatīti kṛtvā // PSBh_1.14:2
children.translated_text: * Even though 'one should not speak to' has been stated as a prohibition, when [the practitioner] has entered villages and the like for the purpose of the teacher or for his own purpose — such as obtaining ash, alms-food, or water — the seeing of excrement and urine, of women and <s>śūdras</s>, and speaking [to them] will [inevitably] occur; considering this — // PSBh 1.14:2

children.text: * ata etad uktaṃ sarvajñena bhagavatā yady avekṣed yady abhibhāṣed iti // PSBh_1.14:3
children.translated_text: * Therefore this is stated by the omniscient <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'If one should look at, if one should speak to.' // PSBh 1.14:3
* It will necessarily happen — this is the meaning. // PSBh 1.14:4

children.text: * āha dṛṣṭe cābhibhāṣite copahatena nirghātanaṃ kiṃ kartavyam // PSBh_1.14:5
children.translated_text: * He asks: When one has looked at and spoken to [such things], what purificatory practice (<s>nirghātana</s>) should be performed by the contaminated one? // PSBh 1.14:5
* To that it is said: Touching [with ash] (<s>upasparśana</s>). // PSBh 1.14:6
* Since — // PSBh 1.14:7
Having touched [with ash] — || PS 1.15 ||
* Here 'upa' (near) indicates acceptance. // PSBh 1.15:1
* Through acceptance, [one becomes] one whose mind is purified of impurity — this is the meaning. // PSBh 1.15:2
* 'Touching' (<s>spṛśya</s>) means precisely the application of the ash substance to the body. // PSBh 1.15:3
* '<s>Upaspṛśya</s>' (having touched) is a synonym for bathing (<s>snāna</s>). // PSBh 1.15:4
* Like touching water while clothed. // PSBh 1.15:5

children.text: * sa ca bhasmanā kartavyaḥ nādbhiḥ // PSBh_1.15:6
children.translated_text: * And that [bathing] should be done with ash, not with water. // PSBh 1.15:6
* Why? // PSBh 1.15:7
* Because it would contradict the earlier and later [teachings]. // PSBh 1.15:8
* And because bathing [in water] is not applicable. // PSBh 1.15:9
* '<s>Upaspṛśya</s>' (having touched) is the completion [of the purification]. // PSBh 1.15:10

children.text: * āha upaspṛśya yadi kaluṣaṃ na kṣīṇaṃ syāt tato nirghātanaṃ kiṃ kartavyam // PSBh_1.15:11
children.translated_text: * He asks: If after touching [with ash] the impurity is not destroyed, then what purificatory practice should be performed? // PSBh 1.15:11

children.text: * tad ucyate sākāṅkṣatvān niṣṭhāśabdasya prāṇāyāmaḥ kartavyaḥ // PSBh_1.15:12
children.translated_text: * To that it is said: Because the word indicating completion has a further expectation, <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath-control) should be performed. // PSBh 1.15:12
* Since he says: // PSBh 1.15:13
Having performed <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath-control) — || PS 1.16 ||

children.text: * atra prāṇo nāma ya eṣa mukhanāsikābhyāṃ niḥsarati vāyur eṣa prāṇaḥ // PSBh_1.16:1
children.translated_text: * Here, <s>prāṇa</s> (life-breath) is that air which exits through the mouth and nostrils — this is <s>prāṇa</s>. // PSBh 1.16:1

children.text: * tasya āyāmo nigraho nirodhaḥ sa prāṇāyāmaḥ // PSBh_1.16:2
children.translated_text: * Its <s>āyāma</s> (extension) is restraint, suppression — that is <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath-control). // PSBh 1.16:2
* And it should be understood as an activity of the person (<s>puruṣa</s>). // PSBh 1.16:3
* Why? // PSBh 1.16:4
* Because <s>prāṇāyāma</s> too is preceded by knowledge, desire, and effort. // PSBh 1.16:5
* One exhalation, or two exhalations; // PSBh 1.16:6

children.text: * tathā viṃśatimātraś caturviṃśatimātras triṃśanmātro vā // PSBh_1.16:7
children.translated_text: * Likewise, of twenty <s>mātrās</s> (measures), or twenty-four <s>mātrās</s>, or thirty <s>mātrās</s>. // PSBh 1.16:7
* A <s>mātrā</s> (measure), however, is the duration of a blink of the eye. // PSBh 1.16:8
* It should be performed according to one's ability and strength. // PSBh 1.16:9

children.text: * tasmād upaspṛśya padmakasvastikopasthāñjalikārdhacandrapīṭhakadaṇḍāyatasarvatobhadrādīnām anyatamenāsanabandhena prāṅmukha udaṅmukho vā upaviśyaitāny aṅgāni kṛtvā grīvām unnāmya pūraṇapūrvako vā recakapūrvako vā tāvat kartavyo yāvan nigṛhītā vāyavo dhyānībhūtaś ca bhavati // PSBh_1.16:10
children.translated_text: * Therefore, having touched [with ash], sitting facing east or north with one of the posture-bindings (<s>āsanabandha</s>) such as <s>padmaka</s> (lotus), <s>svastika</s>, <s>upasthāñjali</s>, <s>ardhacandrapīṭhaka</s> (half-moon seat), <s>daṇḍāyata</s> (staff-extended), <s>sarvatobhadra</s> (auspicious-on-all-sides), and the like, and having performed these limbs [of the practice], raising the neck, [the practitioner should perform prāṇāyāma] beginning either with inhalation (<s>pūraka</s>) or with exhalation (<s>recaka</s>), continuing until the vital airs are restrained and one becomes absorbed in meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>). // PSBh 1.16:10

children.text: * tatra dhyānībhūto nāma yadā dantivad antaḥśarīraṃ pūrṇaṃ bhavati // PSBh_1.16:11
children.translated_text: * There, 'absorbed in meditation' means when, like an elephant, the interior of the body becomes full [of air]. // PSBh 1.16:11

children.text: * nigṛhītānāṃ tu lakṣaṇaṃ yadā kūrmavad antaḥśarīre ucchvāsapratyucchvāsā vartante svacchendriyaś ca bhavati tadā mantavyā nigṛhītā vāyava iti // PSBh_1.16:12
children.translated_text: * The sign of the [vital airs] being restrained: when, like a tortoise, the inhalation and exhalation occur within the body and the senses become clear — then one should consider the vital airs to be restrained. // PSBh 1.16:12

children.text: * tataḥ śanaiḥ śanair moktavyā nāsikayā yathotpalapattram api nāsāpuṭasthaṃ na kampayati // PSBh_1.16:13
children.translated_text: * Then one should release them slowly, slowly through the nostrils, so that even a lotus petal placed at the nostril does not tremble. // PSBh 1.16:13

children.text: * tad atra praśnākrāntau krameṇākramitavyaḥ antarbhāve 'ntare vāyavo bhāvayitavyāḥ // PSBh_1.16:14
children.translated_text: * In this matter, when the sequence of questions arises, [the practitioner] should proceed step by step; in internalization (<s>antarbhāva</s>), the vital airs should be cultivated internally. // PSBh 1.16:14
* 'An' [is the root meaning] 'to breathe.' // PSBh 1.16:15
* The [prefix] 'ā' governs the sequence of posture-binding, firm [holding], restraint, destruction of impurity, release, and so forth. // PSBh 1.16:16
* 'Yam' [is the root meaning] 'to restrain.' // PSBh 1.16:17
* [The vital airs] are to be restrained. // PSBh 1.16:18
* 'Ḍukṛñ' [is the root meaning] 'to do'; it should be understood [accordingly]. // PSBh 1.16:19
* 'Tvā' indicates the completion of an action. // PSBh 1.16:20
* With a break — this is the meaning. // PSBh 1.16:21

children.text: * āha atha kṛte prāṇāyāme yadi kaluṣaṃ na kṣīṇaṃ syāt tato 'nena kiṃ kartavyam // PSBh_1.16:22
children.translated_text: * He asks: Now, when <s>prāṇāyāma</s> has been performed, if the impurity is not destroyed, then what should the practitioner do? // PSBh 1.16:22
* To that it is said: Recitation (<s>japya</s>). // PSBh 1.16:23
* Since he says: // PSBh 1.16:24

children.text: raudrīṃ gāyatrīṃ bahurūpīṃ vā japet || PS_1.17 ||
children.translated_text: One should recite the <s>Raudrī Gāyatrī</s> or the <s>Bahurūpī</s> — || PS 1.17 ||

children.text: * atra tvāśabdasāmarthyād gamyate prāṇasaṃyamena samaṃ japyaṃ kartavyam // PSBh_1.17:1
children.translated_text: * Here, from the force of the [gerundive suffix] 'tvā,' it is understood that the recitation should be done simultaneously with breath-control. // PSBh 1.17:1
* Like the touching [with ash]. // PSBh 1.17:2

children.text: * tasmād atra raudrī nāma tatpuruṣā // PSBh_1.17:3
children.translated_text: * Therefore, here, the <s>Raudrī</s> is a <s>tatpuruṣa</s> [compound]. // PSBh 1.17:3
* And why [is it called] <s>Raudrī</s>? // PSBh 1.17:4
* Because it brings one into the presence of <s>Rudra</s>, it is <s>Raudrī</s>. // PSBh 1.17:5

children.text: * rudro vāsyāṃ cintyate rudraprāpakatvād vā raudrī // PSBh_1.17:6
children.translated_text: * Or, <s>Rudra</s> is meditated upon through it, or because it leads to <s>Rudra</s>, it is <s>Raudrī</s>. // PSBh 1.17:6

children.text: * āha sadyojātādibahuprakārā tatra kā sā raudrī // PSBh_1.17:7
children.translated_text: * He asks: Since there are many types such as <s>Sadyojāta</s> and so forth, which one is that <s>Raudrī</s>? // PSBh 1.17:7
* To that it is said: The <s>Gāyatrī</s>. // PSBh 1.17:8

children.text: * atra yā raudrī sā gāyatrī // PSBh_1.17:9
children.translated_text: * Here, that which is <s>Raudrī</s> is the <s>Gāyatrī</s>. // PSBh 1.17:9
* And why [is it called] <s>Gāyatrī</s>? // PSBh 1.17:10
* 'Being sung, it protects the singer' — thus [it is called <s>Gāyatrī</s>]. // PSBh 1.17:11

children.text: * gāyatre vā chandasi vartata iti gāyatrī // PSBh_1.17:12
children.translated_text: * Or, because it occurs in the <s>Gāyatra</s> meter, it is <s>Gāyatrī</s>. // PSBh 1.17:12
* Here, by the specification of '<s>Raudrī</s>,' the Vedic and other <s>Gāyatrīs</s> are excluded. // PSBh 1.17:13

children.text: * iha tu gāyatrīgrahaṇāt sadyojātādīnāṃ pratiṣedhaḥ // PSBh_1.17:14
children.translated_text: * But here, by the specification of '<s>Gāyatrī</s>,' <s>Sadyojāta</s> and the other [Rudra mantras] are excluded. // PSBh 1.17:14
* '<s>Gāyatrīm</s>' is the object [of the verb 'recite']. // PSBh 1.17:15
* '<s>Bahurūpī</s>' is [the mantra called] <s>Aghorā</s>. // PSBh 1.17:16
* And why [is it called] <s>Bahurūpī</s> (having many forms)? // PSBh 1.17:17

children.text: * bahurūpasyoktaparigraheṣv ākāreṣu vartata iti bahurūpī // PSBh_1.17:18
children.translated_text: * Because the one of many forms (<s>Bahurūpa</s>) abides in the accepted forms — therefore [it is called] <s>Bahurūpī</s>. // PSBh 1.17:18

children.text: * bahurūpo vā asyāṃ cintyata iti bahurūpaprāpakatvād bahurūpī // PSBh_1.17:19
children.translated_text: * Or, the one of many forms is meditated upon through it, or because it leads to the one of many forms — [it is called] <s>Bahurūpī</s>. // PSBh 1.17:19
* '<s>Bahurūpīm</s>' is the object [of the verb 'recite']. // PSBh 1.17:20
* 'Or' (<s>vā</s>) indicates an option. // PSBh 1.17:21

children.text: * ubhayor api brahmatvam ubhayor api tulyārthasādhakatvam ubhe api maheśvaraparigṛhīte ity ata ekām anekāṃ vā upaspṛśya japed iti mānasī kriyety arthaḥ // PSBh_1.17:22
children.translated_text: * Both [mantras] lead to the state of <s>Brahman</s>, both accomplish the same purpose, both are accepted by <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord); therefore, having touched [with ash], one should recite one or many — [this is] a mental activity; this is the meaning. // PSBh 1.17:22
* He asks: For one who has undertaken touching [with ash], <s>prāṇāyāma</s>, and recitation — what is the result of the task? // PSBh 1.17:23
* To that it is said: Freedom from impurity (<s>akaluṣatva</s>). // PSBh 1.17:24
* Since he says: // PSBh 1.17:25
Of one whose mind is free from impurity (<s>akaluṣamati</s>) — || PS 1.18 ||
* Thus. // PSBh 1.18:1

children.text: * atra akaluṣā yasya matiḥ so 'yam akaluṣamatiḥ // PSBh_1.18:2
children.translated_text: * Here, one whose mind (<s>mati</s>) is free from impurity (<s>akaluṣa</s>) — this is [the compound] <s>akaluṣamati</s>. // PSBh 1.18:2
* [It is] a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound. // PSBh 1.18:3
* Here, the prefix 'a' negates impurity. // PSBh 1.18:4
* The impurity referred to here is specifically the impurity of mental states (<s>bhāvakāluṣya</s>). // PSBh 1.18:5
* How is this understood? // PSBh 1.18:6
* Because it has been previously established. // PSBh 1.18:7
* And here, earlier it was stated: // PSBh 1.18:8

children.text: * nāvekṣen nābhibhāṣed ity ukte arthāpannaṃ dṛṣṭe cābhibhāṣite ca dveṣecchākrodhā utpadyante // PSBh_1.18:9
children.translated_text: * When it was said 'one should not look at, one should not speak to,' it is implied that upon seeing and speaking to [impure things], aversion, desire, and anger arise. // PSBh 1.18:9
* And these, once arisen, manifest in the mind. // PSBh 1.18:10
* Like seeing a mole or mark and the like. // PSBh 1.18:11

children.text: * abhivyakteś cocyate kaluṣito 'haṃ vyāhato 'haṃ malinīkṛto 'ham iti // PSBh_1.18:12
children.translated_text: * And because of this manifestation, one says: 'I am contaminated, I am afflicted, I am defiled.' // PSBh 1.18:12
* Therefore, because aversion, desire, and anger are the causes [of impurity], the prohibition of [seeing] urine, excrement, women, and <s>śūdras</s> is made. // PSBh 1.18:13

children.text: * yadā tv ete dveṣādayo bhāvā bījakṣaye sati notpadyante tadā paraṃ bhāvaśaucaṃ pratyavagantavyam // PSBh_1.18:14
children.translated_text: * But when these states such as aversion and the like do not arise because the seed [of impurity] has been destroyed, then one should understand the supreme purity of mental states (<s>bhāvaśauca</s>). // PSBh 1.18:14
* 'Of one whose mind is impure' (<s>kaluṣamati</s>) — // PSBh 1.18:15
* And the impurity is caused by [external] conditions (<s>naimittika</s>). // PSBh 1.18:16

children.text: * na ca nimittānityatvān naimittikaṃ nityaṃ bhavati // PSBh_1.18:17
children.translated_text: * And since the conditions are impermanent, the conditional [impurity] is not permanent. // PSBh 1.18:17
* Like a sprout when the seed is destroyed. // PSBh 1.18:18

children.text: * na ca yatraiva kaluṣam utpadyate tatraivopasparśanādīni kartavyāni // PSBh_1.18:19
children.translated_text: * And the touching [with ash] and other [purifications] are not to be performed at the very place where the impurity arises. // PSBh 1.18:19
* Rather, they should be performed at the temple (<s>āyatana</s>). // PSBh 1.18:20

children.text: * athāpi kaluṣam utpannaṃ pradhvastaṃ syāt tathāpi tadarthaṃ na kartavyāni // PSBh_1.18:21
children.translated_text: * Moreover, even if the arisen impurity has been destroyed, still the [purificatory practices] should not be performed for that purpose [alone]. // PSBh 1.18:21

children.text: * yadā tu tad avasthitaṃ sambhavati śirorogādivat tadā kartavyāni // PSBh_1.18:22
children.translated_text: * But when [the impurity] persists and recurs, like a headache and the like, then they should be performed. // PSBh 1.18:22

children.text: * atra matir iti buddhir ity anarthāntaram // PSBh_1.18:23
children.translated_text: * Here, 'mind' (<s>mati</s>) and 'intellect' (<s>buddhi</s>) are not different in meaning. // PSBh 1.18:23

children.text: * atrāpi karaṇavyapadeśenātmaśaucaṃ vyākhyāyata ity arthaḥ // PSBh_1.18:24
children.translated_text: * Here too, the purity of the self (<s>ātman</s>) is explained by means of the designation of the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) — this is the meaning. // PSBh 1.18:24

children.text: * āha akaluṣamatinā sādhakena kiṃ kartavyam // PSBh_1.18:25
children.translated_text: * He asks: What should the practitioner whose mind is free from impurity do? // PSBh 1.18:25
* To that it is said: He should practice (<s>caritavya</s>). // PSBh 1.18:26
* Since he says: // PSBh 1.18:27
Of one who practices — || PS 1.19 ||

children.text: * atra carataḥ iti dharmārjanam adhikurute // PSBh_1.19:1
children.translated_text: * Here, 'of one who practices' governs the acquisition of merit (<s>dharmārjana</s>). // PSBh 1.19:1

children.text: * bhaikṣyacaraṇavat tapaś caritavyaṃ vihartavyaṃ tapaso 'rjanaṃ kartavyaṃ na stheyam ity arthaḥ // PSBh_1.19:2
children.translated_text: * Like going for alms-food, austerity should be practiced, one should move about, the acquisition of austerity should be done, one should not remain stationary — this is the meaning. // PSBh 1.19:2
* 'Carata' is in the present tense. // PSBh 1.19:3

children.text: * akaluṣamateś carato vā asya kā kāryaniṣpattiḥ // PSBh_1.19:4
children.translated_text: * Of one whose mind is free from impurity and who practices — or, what is the result of the task for this one? // PSBh 1.19:4
* To that it is said: // PSBh 1.19:5
Then <s>yoga</s> (union) commences for him — || PS 1.20 ||
* Here, 'then' (<s>tataḥ</s>) refers to the practice. // PSBh 1.19:1

children.text: * tataḥ caryābhiniveśād anantaraṃ tajjanyadharmād ity arthaḥ // PSBh_1.20:2
children.translated_text: * Then, immediately after dedication to practice, from the merit born thereof — this is the meaning. // PSBh 1.20:2
* 'Of him' (<s>asya</s>) designates the practitioner. // PSBh 1.20:3

children.text: * yo 'yam akaluṣamatiś carati tasyety arthaḥ // PSBh_1.20:4
children.translated_text: * Of this one who, with purified mind, practices — this is the meaning. // PSBh 1.20:4
* He asks: What happens? // PSBh 1.20:5
* To that it is said: <s>Yoga</s> commences. // PSBh 1.20:6

children.text: * adhyayanadhyānādilakṣaṇaḥ kriyāyogaś carataḥ pravartata ity arthaḥ // PSBh_1.20:7
children.translated_text: * The <s>kriyāyoga</s> (yoga of action) characterized by study, meditation, and the like commences for the one who practices — this is the meaning. // PSBh 1.20:7
* Here, <s>yoga</s> should be understood as the union of the self (<s>ātman</s>) with the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>). // PSBh 1.20:8

children.text: * pra iti ādikarmaṇi ārambhe bhavati // PSBh_1.20:9
children.translated_text: * 'Pra' indicates the initial action, the beginning. // PSBh 1.20:9

children.text: * yadā akaluṣamatiś carati tadā pravartata ity arthāt // PSBh_1.20:10
children.translated_text: * When one of purified mind practices, then [yoga] commences — this is implied. // PSBh 1.20:10
* There, from what does [yoga] commence? // PSBh 1.20:11
* From the sense-objects. // PSBh 1.20:12
* That which commences for one whose mind has been withdrawn [from objects] — that is <s>yoga</s>. // PSBh 1.20:13
* How does it commence? // PSBh 1.20:14
* Gradually. // PSBh 1.20:15
* By what means does it commence? // PSBh 1.20:16
* It commences through austerity (<s>tapas</s>). // PSBh 1.20:17
* For whom does it commence? // PSBh 1.20:18
* For the self (<s>ātman</s>), the practitioner. // PSBh 1.20:19
* In what does it commence? // PSBh 1.20:20

children.text: * yo 'yam ātmany ātmabhāvaḥ sa maheśvare pravartata ity arthaḥ // PSBh_1.20:21
children.translated_text: * That selfhood which belongs to the self — that commences in <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord); this is the meaning. // PSBh 1.20:21

children.text: * evaṃ yasmād dravyāvasthānakāladeśakriyāprayogoccāvacaprayojanayamaniyamavṛttivasatyarthaprāṇāyāmapratyāhāranimittapratiṣedhasaṃśayanirghātanaśaucaniyogaphalopāyāś ca vyākhyātāḥ ato 'trāyatanaprakaraṇaṃ samāptam // PSBh_1.20:22
children.translated_text: * Thus, since substance, condition, time, place, activity, method, high-and-low purpose, restraints (<s>yama</s>), observances (<s>niyama</s>), conduct, dwelling, purpose, <s>prāṇāyāma</s>, withdrawal of the senses (<s>pratyāhāra</s>), cause, prohibition, doubt, purificatory striking (<s>nirghātana</s>), purification, prescription, result, and means have been explained — therefore the section on the temple (<s>āyatanaprakaraṇa</s>) is concluded. // PSBh 1.20:22
* Here he asks: Is the system (<s>tantra</s>) complete with [the attainment of] its purpose? // PSBh 1.20:23
* It is said: No. // PSBh 1.20:24
* It culminates in <s>yoga</s>. // PSBh 1.20:25

children.text: * yasmād āha yuktottare saty api padārthavailakṣaṇye raṅgapatākādivacchiṣyapralobhanārtham idam ārabhyate // PSBh_1.20:26
children.translated_text: * Since he says: Even though the higher [teaching] is connected with <s>yoga</s> and there is a distinction of topics, this [next section] is begun for the purpose of attracting disciples, like a stage-curtain or banner. // PSBh 1.20:26
Seeing, hearing, thinking, and discerning also commence for him — || PS 1.21 ||

children.text: * atra dūraṃ nāma yad etad darśanādyaṃ vikaraṇāntaṃ māheśvaram aiśvaryam anena kadācit prāptapūrvakaṃ tasmiṃs tatprāptau ca // PSBh_1.21:1
children.translated_text: * Here, 'distance' (<s>dūra</s>) means the following: this sovereignty (<s>aiśvarya</s>) of <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord), beginning with seeing (<s>darśana</s>) and ending with dissolution (<s>vikaraṇa</s>), was never previously attained by him — and [refers to] its attainment. // PSBh 1.21:1
* With regard to seeing and the rest, the word 'distant' should be understood here in a technical sense. // PSBh 1.21:2
* And the attainment of that [sovereignty] comes from the practice of <s>yoga</s>. // PSBh 1.21:3

children.text: * āha yady evaṃ sūtrato 'bhidhīyantāṃ darśanādayaḥ // PSBh_1.21:4
children.translated_text: * He asks: If so, let seeing and the rest be described from the <s>sūtra</s>. // PSBh 1.21:4
* They are [now] described. // PSBh 1.21:5

children.text: * darśanam ity atrāpi ca nastrikaṃ cintyate // PSBh_1.21:6
children.translated_text: * Regarding 'seeing' (<s>darśana</s>) — here too the threefold analysis (<s>nastrika</s>) is to be considered. // PSBh 1.21:6
* The seer (<s>draṣṭā</s>), the seeing (<s>darśana</s>), and the seen (<s>dṛśya</s>). // PSBh 1.21:7
* Here, the seer is the perfected one (<s>siddha</s>). // PSBh 1.21:8
* Seeing (<s>darśana</s>) is his perfection (<s>siddhi</s>), [which is] knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>). // PSBh 1.21:9
* The objects to be seen are forms (<s>rūpa</s>). // PSBh 1.21:10

children.text: * tat kṛtsneṣu viṣayeṣu samāsavistaravibhāgaviśeṣataś ca darśanaṃ pravartata ity arthaḥ // PSBh_1.21:11
children.translated_text: * That [seeing] operates with regard to all objects, in summary, in detail, by division, and in particular — this is the meaning. // PSBh 1.21:11

children.text: * tathā śravaṇam ity atrāpi nastrikaṃ cintyante // PSBh_1.21:12
children.translated_text: * Likewise, regarding 'hearing' (<s>śravaṇa</s>) — here too the threefold analysis is to be considered. // PSBh 1.21:12
* The hearer (<s>śrotā</s>), the hearing (<s>śravaṇa</s>), and the audible (<s>śravya</s>). // PSBh 1.21:13
* There, the hearer is the perfected one (<s>siddha</s>). // PSBh 1.21:14
* Hearing (<s>śravaṇa</s>) is his perfection (<s>siddhi</s>), [which is] knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>). // PSBh 1.21:15
* The audible objects are sounds (<s>śabda</s>). // PSBh 1.21:16

children.text: * tad asya siddhasya śrāvyeṣv artheṣu samāsavistaravibhāgaviśeṣataś ca śravaṇaṃ pravartata ity arthaḥ // PSBh_1.21:17
children.translated_text: * That [hearing] of this perfected one operates with regard to audible objects, in summary, in detail, by division, and in particular — this is the meaning. // PSBh 1.21:17

children.text: * tathā mananam ity atrāpi ca nastrikaṃ cintyate // PSBh_1.21:18
children.translated_text: * Likewise, regarding 'thinking' (<s>manana</s>) — here too the threefold analysis is to be considered. // PSBh 1.21:18
* The thinker (<s>mantā</s>), the thinking (<s>manana</s>), and the thinkable (<s>mantavya</s>). // PSBh 1.21:19
* Here, the thinker is the perfected one (<s>siddha</s>). // PSBh 1.21:20
* Thinking (<s>manana</s>) is his perfection (<s>siddhi</s>), [which is] knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>). // PSBh 1.21:21
* The thinkable objects are the minds of others (<s>paracitta</s>). // PSBh 1.21:22

children.text: * devamanuṣyatiryagyonīnāṃ dharmārthakāmamokṣacittānāṃ mantā bhavatīty arthaḥ // PSBh_1.21:23
children.translated_text: * He becomes the knower of the minds of gods, humans, and animals, [their minds directed toward] <s>dharma</s> (duty), <s>artha</s> (wealth), <s>kāma</s> (pleasure), and <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) — this is the meaning. // PSBh 1.21:23

children.text: * tathā vijñānam ity atrāpi nastrikaṃ cintyante // PSBh_1.21:24
children.translated_text: * Likewise, regarding 'discernment' (<s>vijñāna</s>) — here too the threefold analysis is to be considered. // PSBh 1.21:24
* The discerner (<s>vijñātā</s>), the discernment (<s>vijñāna</s>), and the discernible (<s>vijñeya</s>). // PSBh 1.21:25
* There, the discerner is the perfected one (<s>siddha</s>). // PSBh 1.21:26
* Discernment (<s>vijñāna</s>) is his perfection (<s>siddhi</s>), [which is] knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>). // PSBh 1.21:27
* The discernible objects are the mental modifications (<s>vṛtti</s>). // PSBh 1.21:28

children.text: * asya siddhasya pravartante svataḥ prādurbhavantīty arthaḥ // PSBh_1.21:29
children.translated_text: * For this perfected one, they arise spontaneously, manifesting of their own accord — this is the meaning. // PSBh 1.21:29
* Does he have [such] knowledge or not? // PSBh 1.21:30
* It is said: He does. // PSBh 1.21:31
* Because he states: // PSBh 1.21:32
Omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>). || PS 1.22 ||

children.text: * atrokteṣu dṛśyaśravyādiṣu ca aśeṣeṣu siddheśvarapaśvādiṣu nirviśeṣavācī sarvaśabdo draṣṭavyaḥ // PSBh_1.22:1
children.translated_text: * Here, with regard to the aforementioned visible, audible, and other [objects], as well as all [beings] without exception — perfected ones (<s>siddha</s>), the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>), bound souls (<s>paśu</s>), and so on — the word 'all' (<s>sarva</s>) should be understood as a comprehensive term without distinction. // PSBh 1.22:1

children.text: * jñatā ity atrāpi ca nas trikaṃ cintyate // PSBh_1.22:2
children.translated_text: * Regarding '<s>jñatā</s>' (knowledge) — here too the threefold analysis is to be considered. // PSBh 1.22:2
* The knower (<s>jñātā</s>), the knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), and the knowable (<s>jñeya</s>). // PSBh 1.22:3

children.text: * tatra jñātā siddhaḥ jñānam asya siddhir jñānam // PSBh_1.22:4
children.translated_text: * There, the knower is the perfected one (<s>siddha</s>); knowledge is his perfection (<s>siddhi</s>), [which is] knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>). // PSBh 1.22:4

children.text: * jñeyaṃ kāryaṃ kāraṇaṃ siddhāś ceti // PSBh_1.22:5
children.translated_text: * The knowable comprises effects (<s>kārya</s>), causes (<s>kāraṇa</s>), and the perfected ones (<s>siddha</s>). // PSBh 1.22:5

children.text: * tasmād ekā jñānaśaktir aparimitena jñeyenānekenānekadhopacaryate // PSBh_1.22:6
children.translated_text: * Therefore, a single power of knowledge is employed in manifold ways by the unlimited and manifold knowable. // PSBh 1.22:6

children.text: * sphaṭikādityavac cāsya sarvataḥ pravartata ity arthaḥ // PSBh_1.22:7
children.translated_text: * And like a crystal and the sun, it operates in all directions — this is the meaning. // PSBh 1.22:7

children.text: * āha kim ayaṃ siddho jñānamātrasaṃtuṣṭaḥ paṅguvad uta kriyāśaktir apy asti neti // PSBh_1.22:8
children.translated_text: * He asks: Is this perfected one content with knowledge alone, like a lame person, or does he also possess the power of action (<s>kriyāśakti</s>) or not? // PSBh 1.22:8
* It is said: He does. // PSBh 1.22:9
* Because he states: // PSBh 1.22:10
Speed of mind (<s>manojavitvam</s>). || PS 1.23 ||
* Here, the power of omniscience has been stated as adventitious (<s>āgantuka</s>). // PSBh 1.23:1

children.text: * na tu ṛṣitvavipratvavad ity arthaḥ // PSBh_1.23:2
children.translated_text: * But not [intrinsic] like [the Lord's own] seerhood (<s>ṛṣitva</s>) and sagehood (<s>vipratva</s>) — this is the meaning. // PSBh 1.23:2

children.text: * yasmāt atra manojavavad ity evaṃ prāpte samānopamānatvān manojavitvam ity uktam // PSBh_1.23:3
children.translated_text: * Because here, when it is understood as 'like the speed of mind' (<s>manojavavat</s>), on account of the analogy being equivalent, it is stated as 'having the speed of mind' (<s>manojavitvam</s>). // PSBh 1.23:3
* Like the speed of mind (<s>manojavavat</s>). // PSBh 1.23:4
* He asks: // PSBh 1.23:5
* What is the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>? // PSBh 1.23:6

children.text: * ucyate yādṛṅ manaso javitvam āśukāritvam īdṛśam asya siddhasya kartṛtve śīghratvam // PSBh_1.23:7
children.translated_text: * It is said: Just as the mind has swiftness (<s>javitva</s>) and quickness of action — such is the rapidity of this perfected one in his agency (<s>kartṛtva</s>). // PSBh 1.23:7

children.text: * na cāsya prajāpativat taponimittatvād bhāvottarā pravṛttiḥ // PSBh_1.23:8
children.translated_text: * And his activity is not subsequent to [mere] intention, as is the case with <s>Prajāpati</s>, because [his activity] does not have austerity (<s>tapas</s>) as its cause. // PSBh 1.23:8

children.text: * kiṃtu bhāvasya balīyastvāt pravṛtter utpannasvabhāvaḥ karomīti kṛtam eva bhavati // PSBh_1.23:9
children.translated_text: * Rather, because of the superior strength of his intention (<s>bhāva</s>), his activity being of an inherently arising nature — [the moment he thinks] 'I shall create,' it is already created. // PSBh 1.23:9
* Or [the moment he thinks] 'I shall destroy,' it is already destroyed. // PSBh 1.23:10
* Because his vision and action are unobstructed (<s>apratīghāta</s>). // PSBh 1.23:12

children.text: * tvam iti bhāvanirdeśād gamyate vittam asya śaktiḥ sāmarthyam // PSBh_1.23:13
children.translated_text: * From the word '<s>tvam</s>' (you/nature), indicating nature (<s>bhāva</s>), it is understood that his capacity (<s>vitta</s>), power (<s>śakti</s>), and capability (<s>sāmarthya</s>) [are indicated]. // PSBh 1.23:13
* Such is his sovereignty (<s>aiśvarya</s>) — this is the meaning. // PSBh 1.23:14

children.text: * āha kim asya siddhasya kartavyaṃ karaṇaṃ kuto vā karoti // PSBh_1.23:15
children.translated_text: * He asks: What is this perfected one's instrument of action (<s>karaṇa</s>), and from where does he act? // PSBh 1.23:15
* To that it is said: // PSBh 1.23:16
The ability to assume any form at will (<s>kāmarūpitvam</s>). || PS 1.24 ||

children.text: * kāmarūpī ity atrāpi ca nas trikaṃ cintyate // PSBh_1.24:1
children.translated_text: * Regarding 'one whose form is [determined by] desire' (<s>kāmarūpin</s>) — here too the threefold analysis is to be considered. // PSBh 1.24:1
* The desirer (<s>kāmin</s>), the desire (<s>kāma</s>), and the desired (<s>kāmya</s>). // PSBh 1.24:2
* There, the desirer is the perfected one (<s>siddha</s>). // PSBh 1.24:3
* Desire (<s>kāma</s>) is his will (<s>icchā</s>). // PSBh 1.24:4
* The desired [objects] are forms (<s>rūpa</s>). // PSBh 1.24:5
* How [does this work]? // PSBh 1.24:6
* The root '<s>kamu</s>' is used in the sense of wishing (<s>icchā</s>). // PSBh 1.24:7

children.text: * rūpāṇi yāvanti yādṛśāni cecchati tāvanti tādṛśāni ca karoti // PSBh_1.24:8
children.translated_text: * However many forms and of whatever kind he desires, that many and of that kind he creates. // PSBh 1.24:8
* And the instruments for creating forms — earth (<s>pṛthivī</s>) and the other [elements] — are dependent on himself. // PSBh 1.24:9

children.text: * vibhutvāc ca karaṇānāṃ yatra yatra rūpāṇy abhinirvartayati tatra tatra cāsya buddhyādīnāṃ karaṇānāṃ vṛttilābho bhavati // PSBh_1.24:10
children.translated_text: * And because of the all-pervasiveness (<s>vibhutva</s>) of the instruments, wherever he manifests forms, there the activity of his instruments — intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) and the others — obtains its function. // PSBh 1.24:10
* By analogy with the eye and the other [senses]. // PSBh 1.24:11
* [Objection:] He is not the presider (<s>adhiṣṭhātā</s>) [over those forms]. // PSBh 1.24:12
* That is not so. // PSBh 1.24:13
* Because he states '<s>rūpin</s>' (one who possesses forms). // PSBh 1.24:15
* Here, he presides over forms — therefore [he is called] '<s>rūpin</s>' (form-possessor). // PSBh 1.24:16
* Like one who possesses a staff (<s>daṇḍin</s>). // PSBh 1.24:17

children.text: * rūpivacanāc ca sarveṣām eva rūpāṇāṃ yugapad evādhiṣṭhātā bhavati // PSBh_1.24:18
children.translated_text: * And because of the statement '<s>rūpin</s>,' he is the simultaneous presider over all forms whatsoever. // PSBh 1.24:18
* Because of all-pervasiveness (<s>vibhutva</s>), he is undifferentiated from <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord). // PSBh 1.24:19
