* And this is understood from the teaching of union with <s>Rudra</s> (<s>rudrasāyujya</s>). // PSBh 1.24:20

children.text: * tvam iti bhāvanirdeśād gamyate vittam asya śaktiḥ sāmarthyam // PSBh_1.24:21
children.translated_text: * From the word '<s>tvam</s>' (you/nature), indicating nature (<s>bhāva</s>), it is understood that his capacity (<s>vitta</s>), power (<s>śakti</s>), and capability (<s>sāmarthya</s>) [are indicated]. // PSBh 1.24:21
* Such is his sovereignty (<s>aiśvarya</s>) — this is the meaning. // PSBh 1.24:22

children.text: * āha parimiteṣu kṛtyeṣu aśaktidarśanāt saṃdehaḥ // PSBh_1.24:23
children.translated_text: * He objects: Since inability is observed in limited tasks, there is doubt. // PSBh 1.24:23

children.text: * atha kim ayaṃ siddhas teṣāṃ svakṛtānāṃ rūpāṇāṃ saṃhāre śaktaḥ uta viśvāmitravad aśaktaḥ iti // PSBh_1.24:24
children.translated_text: * Is this perfected one capable of withdrawing those forms he has created, or is he incapable like <s>Viśvāmitra</s>? // PSBh 1.24:24
* It is said: // PSBh 1.24:25
* Because he states: // PSBh 1.24:26
Without instruments (<s>vikaraṇa</s>). || PS 1.25 ||
* Here, '<s>vi</s>' is used in the sense of destruction, [indicating] being without instruments (<s>vinākaraṇa</s>). // PSBh 1.25:1
* He becomes without instruments (<s>vikaraṇa</s>). // PSBh 1.25:2
* Like 'arrowless' (<s>viśikha</s>) or 'chariotless' (<s>viratha</s>). // PSBh 1.25:3
* By the negation of instruments, the negation of effects is accomplished. // PSBh 1.25:4
* Why? // PSBh 1.25:5

children.text: * viśiṣṭatvād grāhakatvāt sūkṣmatvāc ca karaṇānām // PSBh_1.25:6
children.translated_text: * Because the instruments are of a distinguished, apprehending, and subtle nature. // PSBh 1.25:6
* Therefore, '<s>vikaraṇa</s>' (without instruments) means <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation/liberation). // PSBh 1.25:7

children.text: * āha aviśeṣād iha sāṃkhyayogādīnām api sahaiśvaryeṇa kāryakaraṇatyāgaṃ kṛtvā kaivalyaniṣṭhā // PSBh_1.25:8
children.translated_text: * He objects: Without distinction from the <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, <s>Yoga</s>, and other [systems], which also, together with sovereignty, having abandoned effects and instruments, are established in <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation). // PSBh 1.25:8
* And [the same holds] in this treatise as well. // PSBh 1.25:9
* How then is there no distinction? // PSBh 1.25:10

children.text: * atha matiḥ niratiśaye mokṣe nāsti vaiṣamyaṃ tathāpy atidānādibhiḥ sādhyasādhananiṣṭhāto 'tha viśeṣaḥ ucyate // PSBh_1.25:11
children.translated_text: * Now, if the view is that there is no inequality in unsurpassed liberation, even so, a distinction exists through the establishment of the means-and-end [relationship], through excessive generosity and the like. It is said: // PSBh 1.25:11
* There is no non-distinction. // PSBh 1.25:12
* Because he states: // PSBh 1.25:13
And [the state of] possessing qualities (<s>dharmitvam</s>). || PS 1.26 ||
* Here, he becomes a possessor of qualities (<s>dharmin</s>) through the quality-nature (<s>guṇadharma</s>). // PSBh 1.26:1

children.text: * yad etad darśanādyaṃ vikaraṇāntaṃ māheśvaram aiśvaryam asyeśaprasādāt svaguṇasaṃvṛttaṃ tenāyaṃ guṇadharmeṇa dharmī bhavati // PSBh_1.26:2
children.translated_text: * This sovereignty of <s>Maheśvara</s>, beginning with seeing (<s>darśana</s>) and ending with dissolution (<s>vikaraṇa</s>), having arisen from his own qualities through the grace of the Lord (<s>Īśa</s>) — by that quality-nature, he becomes a possessor of qualities (<s>dharmin</s>). // PSBh 1.26:2
* From what [do we know this]? // PSBh 1.26:3
* It is understood from the word '<s>tvam</s>' (you/nature), indicating nature (<s>bhāva</s>). // PSBh 1.26:4

children.text: * ṛte 'pi kāryakaraṇe jñātā kartā ca bhavati // PSBh_1.26:5
children.translated_text: * Even apart from effects and instruments, he is both a knower and an agent (<s>kartā</s>). // PSBh 1.26:5

children.text: * tataś ca kaivalyādyāḥ sarvaniṣṭhā viśeṣitā bhavanti // PSBh_1.26:6
children.translated_text: * And thereby, all [states of] establishment beginning with <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation) are distinguished. // PSBh 1.26:6
* The word '<s>ca</s>' (and) here serves to indicate the cumulation of the powers of knowledge and action. // PSBh 1.26:7

children.text: * evam atrāsya siddhasya kāmarūpivikaraṇavacanāt svakṛteṣu rūpeṣu prabhutvaṃ vibhutvaṃ guṇadharmitvaṃ ca vyākhyātam // PSBh_1.26:8
children.translated_text: * Thus, here, for this perfected one, from the statements about assuming forms at will (<s>kāmarūpin</s>) and being without instruments (<s>vikaraṇa</s>), his lordship (<s>prabhutva</s>), all-pervasiveness (<s>vibhutva</s>), and possession of qualities (<s>guṇadharmitva</s>) over his self-created forms have been explained. // PSBh 1.26:8

children.text: * etad yuktottare prasādād guṇāḥ pravartanta ity arthaḥ // PSBh_1.26:9
children.translated_text: * This, combined with the preceding [discussion], means that through [divine] grace, the qualities arise — this is the meaning. // PSBh 1.26:9

children.text: * atredam ādhikārikam aiśvaryaprakaraṇaṃ parisamāptam iti // PSBh_1.26:10
children.translated_text: * Here, this technical section on sovereignty (<s>aiśvarya</s>) is concluded. // PSBh 1.26:10

children.text: * āha kiṃ parakṛteṣv api devamanuṣyatiryagyonirūpeṣv asya siddhasya prabhutvaṃ vibhutvaṃ cāsti neti // PSBh_1.26:11
children.translated_text: * He asks: Does this perfected one also possess lordship (<s>prabhutva</s>) and all-pervasiveness (<s>vibhutva</s>) over forms created by others — those of gods, humans, and animals — or not? // PSBh 1.26:11
* It is said: He does. // PSBh 1.26:12
* Because he states: // PSBh 1.26:13
And all become subject to him. || PS 1.27 ||

children.text: * atra sarve niravaśeṣāḥ paśudharmāṇa ity arthaḥ // PSBh_1.27:1
children.translated_text: * Here, 'all' means without remainder — all entities possessing the nature of bound souls (<s>paśu</s>) — this is the meaning. // PSBh 1.27:1
* The word '<s>ca</s>' (and) serves to combine the self-created and other-created forms. // PSBh 1.27:2

children.text: * parakṛteṣv api devādirūpeṣu prabhutvaṃ vibhutvaṃ cāstīti // PSBh_1.27:3
children.translated_text: * Over other-created forms — those of gods and others as well — he has lordship (<s>prabhutva</s>) and all-pervasiveness (<s>vibhutva</s>). // PSBh 1.27:3
* 'His' (<s>asya</s>) means 'of the perfected one' (<s>siddha</s>) — this is the meaning. // PSBh 1.27:4
* 'Subject' (<s>vaśya</s>) means 'obedient' (<s>vidheya</s>). // PSBh 1.27:5
* And they become under his control (<s>vaśavartin</s>) — this is the meaning. // PSBh 1.27:6
* 'They become' (<s>bhavanti</s>) — this is a statement of [actual] fact, beyond doubt. // PSBh 1.27:7

children.text: * āha kim ayaṃ siddhas teṣāṃ kadācid vaśyo bhavati neti // PSBh_1.27:8
children.translated_text: * He asks: Does this perfected one ever become subject to them or not? // PSBh 1.27:8
* It is said: No. // PSBh 1.27:9
* Because he states: // PSBh 1.27:10
And he becomes unsubjugable by all (<s>sarveṣām avaśya</s>). || PS 1.28 ||
* Here too, the word 'all' (<s>sarva</s>) applies only to the bound souls (<s>paśu</s>). // PSBh 1.28:1
* 'Of all' (<s>sarveṣām</s>) is used in the sense of comprehensive inclusion. // PSBh 1.28:2
* The word '<s>ca</s>' (and) is used in the sense of surpassing excellence. // PSBh 1.28:3

children.text: * abhyadhika utkṛṣṭo vyatiriktaś ca bhavatīty arthaḥ // PSBh_1.28:4
children.translated_text: * He becomes surpassing (<s>abhyadhika</s>), supreme (<s>utkṛṣṭa</s>), and transcendent (<s>vyatirikta</s>) — this is the meaning. // PSBh 1.28:4
* Regarding '<s>avaśya</s>' (unsubjugable): // PSBh 1.28:5
* The prefix '<s>a</s>' negates any subjugation (<s>vaśyatva</s>) that may have existed previously. // PSBh 1.28:6
* 'He becomes' (<s>bhavati</s>) — this is a statement of [actual] fact, beyond doubt. // PSBh 1.28:7

children.text: * yadā guṇair yuktaḥ prāptaiśvaryaḥ siddhas tadā sarveṣāṃ śakter avaśyo bhavatīty arthaḥ // PSBh_1.28:8
children.translated_text: * When the perfected one is endowed with qualities and has attained sovereignty (<s>aiśvarya</s>), then he becomes unsubjugable by the power of all [others] — this is the meaning. // PSBh 1.28:8

children.text: * āha kiṃ svaśaktyādhyākrāntā vaśyā bhavanti āhosvid dharmamaryādāṃ rakṣanti guruśiṣyavat // PSBh_1.28:9
children.translated_text: * He asks: Do they become subject because they are overpowered by his power, or do they preserve the boundary of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), like a teacher and a student? // PSBh 1.28:9
* The student, though capable, is not overpowered by the teacher [but follows willingly]. // PSBh 1.28:10
* Because he states: // PSBh 1.28:11
And he enters all. || PS 1.29 ||

children.text: * atrāpi sarvaśabdaḥ paśuṣv eva niravaśeṣavācī draṣṭavyaḥ // PSBh_1.29:1
children.translated_text: * Here too, the word 'all' (<s>sarva</s>) should be understood as a comprehensive term applying only to the bound souls (<s>paśu</s>). // PSBh 1.29:1
* The word '<s>ca</s>' (and) combines [this] with what was stated before. // PSBh 1.29:2

children.text: * na kevalam asya te vaśyāḥ kiṃ tv āveśyāś ceti // PSBh_1.29:3
children.translated_text: * Not only are they subject to him, but they can also be entered (<s>āveśya</s>) [by him]. // PSBh 1.29:3

children.text: * atra āṅ iti āveśanamaryādām adhikurute // PSBh_1.29:4
children.translated_text: * Here, the prefix '<s>ā</s>' governs the boundary of entering (<s>āveśanamaryādā</s>). // PSBh 1.29:4
* '<s>Viśa</s>' [is used] in the sense of entering (<s>praveśana</s>). // PSBh 1.29:5

children.text: * sa tasya jñānakriyayor vibhutve 'pi śaktisaṃyogād āviśya pratyayalopaṃ kartuṃ samartho bhavatītyarthaḥ // PSBh_1.29:6
children.translated_text: * He, despite the all-pervasiveness of his knowledge and action, through the conjunction of [his] power, having entered [another being], is capable of causing the destruction of [that being's] cognition — this is the meaning. // PSBh 1.29:6

children.text: * āha kim ayaṃ siddhas teṣāṃ kadācid āveśyo bhavati neti // PSBh_1.29:7
children.translated_text: * He asks: Does this perfected one ever become enterable by them or not? // PSBh 1.29:7
* It is said: No. // PSBh 1.29:8
* Because he states: // PSBh 1.29:9
And he becomes unenterable by all (<s>sarveṣām anāveśya</s>). || PS 1.30 ||
* Here too the word 'all' (<s>sarva</s>) refers only to the <s>paśus</s> (bound souls). [PSBh 1.30:1]
* 'Of all' — in the sense of encompassing the lesser. [PSBh 1.30:2]
* And the word <s>ca</s> ('and') is in the sense of superiority. [PSBh 1.30:3]

children.text: * abhyadhika utkṛṣṭo vyatiriktaś ca bhavatītyarthaḥ // PSBh_1.30:4
children.translated_text: * The meaning is: he becomes superior, excellent, and surpassing. [PSBh 1.30:4]
* 'Not to be entered' (<s>anāveśya</s>) — [PSBh 1.30:5]
* The prefix 'a-' negates the former state of being subject to entry. [PSBh 1.30:6]
* He becomes one whose nature cannot be entered. [PSBh 1.30:7]

children.text: * na vyādhiśeṣavad avasthānam bhavati iti bhūtārthavādo niḥsaṃśayam // PSBh_1.30:8
children.translated_text: * There is no lingering like the remnant of a disease — this is a statement of fact, beyond doubt. [PSBh 1.30:8]

children.text: * yadā guṇair yuktaḥ prāptaiśvaryaḥ siddhas tadā sarveṣāṃ cānāveśyo bhavatīty arthaḥ // PSBh_1.30:9
children.translated_text: * When endowed with [these] qualities, having attained sovereignty, [and become] perfected — then he becomes not to be entered by all; this is the meaning. [PSBh 1.30:9]

children.text: * āha kim āveśanamātra eva śakto yakṣarakṣaḥpiśācādivad uta prāṇair api viprayogaṃ yātanābhiś ca saṃyogaṃ kartuṃ śakto bhavatīti // PSBh_1.30:10
children.translated_text: * He asks: is he capable only of entering [others], like <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, <s>piśācas</s>, and such? Or is he also capable of separating [beings] from their life-breaths and subjecting [them] to torments? [PSBh 1.30:10]
* The answer is: he is capable. [PSBh 1.30:11]
* Because [the sūtra] states: [PSBh 1.30:12]
And all become subject to his killing. [PS 1.31]

children.text: * atrāpi sarvaśabdaḥ paśuṣv eva niravaśeṣavācī draṣṭavyaḥ // PSBh_1.31:1
children.translated_text: * Here too the word 'all' should be seen as referring exhaustively only to the <s>paśus</s>. [PSBh 1.31:1]
* The word <s>ca</s> is in the sense of accumulation. [PSBh 1.31:2]

children.text: * na kevalam asya te vaśyāḥ āveśyāś ca kiṃtu vadhyāś ceti // PSBh_1.31:3
children.translated_text: * Not only are they subject to his control and entry, but also subject to his killing. [PSBh 1.31:3]
* 'His' (<s>asya</s>) — in reference to the perfected one. [PSBh 1.31:4]
* 'Subject to killing' (<s>vadhya</s>) — [PSBh 1.31:5]
* <s>Vadha</s> [means] separation from life-breaths and [subjection to] torment. [PSBh 1.31:6]

children.text: * prāṇair api viprayogaṃ yātanābhiś ca saṃyogaṃ kartuṃ samartho bhavatītyarthaḥ // PSBh_1.31:7
children.translated_text: * The meaning is: he becomes capable of separating [beings] from their life-breaths and subjecting [them] to torments. [PSBh 1.31:7]
* 'They become' — this is a statement of fact, beyond doubt. [PSBh 1.31:8]

children.text: * yadā guṇair yuktaḥ prāptaiśvaryaḥ siddhas tadā sarve cāsya vadhyā bhavantītyarthaḥ // PSBh_1.31:9
children.translated_text: * When endowed with [these] qualities, having attained sovereignty, [and become] perfected — then all become subject to his killing; this is the meaning. [PSBh 1.31:9]

children.text: * āha kim ayaṃ siddhas teṣāṃ kadācid vadhyo bhavati neti // PSBh_1.31:10
children.translated_text: * He asks: does this perfected one ever become subject to killing by them, or not? [PSBh 1.31:10]
* The answer is: no. [PSBh 1.31:11]
* Because [the sūtra] states: [PSBh 1.31:12]
And he becomes not subject to killing by all. [PS 1.32]
* Here too the word 'all' refers only to the <s>paśus</s>. [PSBh 1.32:1]
* 'Of all' — in the sense of encompassing the lesser. [PSBh 1.32:2]
* And the word <s>ca</s> is in the sense of superiority. [PSBh 1.32:3]

children.text: * abhyadhikaḥ utkṛṣṭo vyatiriktaś ca bhavatītyarthaḥ // PSBh_1.32:4
children.translated_text: * The meaning is: he becomes superior, excellent, and surpassing. [PSBh 1.32:4]
* 'Not subject to killing' (<s>avadhya</s>) — [PSBh 1.32:5]
* The prefix 'a-' negates the former state of being subject to killing. [PSBh 1.32:6]

children.text: * yadā guṇair yuktaḥ prāptaiśvaryaḥ siddhas tadā sarveṣāṃ cāvadhyo bhavatītyarthaḥ // PSBh_1.32:7
children.translated_text: * When endowed with [these] qualities, having attained sovereignty, [and become] perfected — then he becomes not subject to killing by all; this is the meaning. [PSBh 1.32:7]

children.text: * evaṃ parakṛteṣvapi devādiśarīreṣu rūpeṣu prabhutvaṃ vibhutvaṃ ca vyākhyātam // PSBh_1.32:8
children.translated_text: * Thus, sovereignty and all-pervasiveness have been explained with regard to bodies and forms of gods and others that are created by another. [PSBh 1.32:8]
* Here this section of six <s>sūtras</s> is completed. [PSBh 1.32:9]

children.text: * āha kim asya siddhasyaitadaiśvaryaṃ nityam āhosvit pārthivāpyataijasavāyavyavyomamānasāhaṃkārikamahadātmakādivad anityam iti // PSBh_1.32:10
children.translated_text: * He asks: is this sovereignty of the perfected one eternal, or is it impermanent like [the sovereignty] of the earthy, watery, fiery, airy, spatial, mental, egoic, and those of the nature of the great [principle] and the self? [PSBh 1.32:10]
* The answer is: it is eternal. [PSBh 1.32:11]
* Because [the sūtra] states: [PSBh 1.32:12]
Fearless. [PS 1.33]

children.text: * atra akṣayādivacanavirodhād adhītaś caratīti pāṭhānupapattiḥ // PSBh_1.33:1
children.translated_text: * Here, because of the contradiction with the statements about imperishability and so forth, the reading 'one who has studied and practices' (<s>adhītaś carati</s>) is not tenable. [PSBh 1.33:1]

children.text: * tasmād atītānāgatavartamānakālabhayaṃ na vidyata ity ato 'bhītaḥ // PSBh_1.33:2
children.translated_text: * Therefore, since there is no fear regarding past, future, or present time, he is 'fearless' (<s>abhīta</s>). [PSBh 1.33:2]

children.text: * āha abhītānām api brahmādīnāṃ saṃhāre kṣayaḥ śrūyate // PSBh_1.33:3
children.translated_text: * He objects: even for fearless ones like <s>Brahmā</s> and others, destruction is heard of at the time of cosmic dissolution. [PSBh 1.33:3]
* Therefore, [sovereignty] is not eternal merely because of fearlessness. [PSBh 1.33:4]
* Or what is the characteristic of being fearless? [PSBh 1.33:5]
* That is stated: [PSBh 1.33:6]
Imperishable. [PS 1.34]
* Here the prefix 'a-' serves to negate destruction. [PSBh 1.34:1]

children.text: * atra kṣayo nāma sati puruṣanityatve pūrvam asya brāhmaṇasya tais tair aiśvaryair apakarṣaḥ // PSBh_1.34:2
children.translated_text: * Here, destruction (<s>kṣaya</s>) means: given the eternality of the <s>puruṣa</s> (person), the diminishment of this <s>brāhmaṇa</s>'s various sovereignties as before. [PSBh 1.34:2]
* The connection with [principles] such as the egoic, the great, and the self is impermanent. [PSBh 1.34:3]

children.text: * ayaṃ tu anena nityena māheśvareṇaiśvaryeṇa yogāt puruṣaḥ akṣayaḥ ity upacaryate // PSBh_1.34:4
children.translated_text: * But this person, because of his connection with this eternal sovereignty of <s>Maheśvara</s>, is figuratively called 'imperishable' (<s>akṣaya</s>). [PSBh 1.34:4]
* Like a royal treasury, like the property of a householder. [PSBh 1.34:5]

children.text: * āha īśvarāṇām api yayātiprabhṛtīnāṃ jarābhibhavanād atha kim ayaṃ jīryate neti // PSBh_1.34:6
children.translated_text: * He objects: even for sovereigns like <s>Yayāti</s> and others, since old age overcomes them — does this one grow old or not? [PSBh 1.34:6]
* Or what is the characteristic of being imperishable? [PSBh 1.34:7]
* That is stated: [PSBh 1.34:8]
Without old age. [PS 1.35]
* Here the prefix 'a-' negates old age. [PSBh 1.35:1]

children.text: * atra jarā nāma palitaskhalityādilakṣaṇā kāryasya dṛkkriyāśaktihāniś ca karaṇānām // PSBh_1.35:2
children.translated_text: * Here, old age means [the condition] characterized by grey hair, baldness, and so forth — the loss of the power of sight and action of the effect [body] and of the instruments [senses]. [PSBh 1.35:2]
* Why? [PSBh 1.35:3]

children.text: * tatphalabhoktṛtvād ayaṃ jīryata ity upacaryate // PSBh_1.35:4
children.translated_text: * Because he is the experiencer of its fruits, he is figuratively said to 'grow old.' [PSBh 1.35:4]

children.text: * idānīṃ tu kāmitvād vikaraṇadharmitvāc ca nāstītyataḥ ajara ityucyate // PSBh_1.35:5
children.translated_text: * But now, because he possesses the power of will (<s>kāmitva</s>) and the quality of [having instruments that are] free from decay (<s>vikaraṇadharmin</s>), [old age] does not exist — therefore he is called 'without old age' (<s>ajara</s>). [PSBh 1.35:5]

children.text: * āha ajarāṇām api devādīnāṃ saṃhārād arvāṅ mṛtyur dṛśyate // PSBh_1.35:6
children.translated_text: * He objects: even for the ageless ones such as gods, death is seen [to occur] before the cosmic dissolution. [PSBh 1.35:6]

children.text: * atha kim asya mṛtyur vidyate neti // PSBh_1.35:7
children.translated_text: * So does death exist for this one, or not? [PSBh 1.35:7]
* Or what is the characteristic of being without old age? [PSBh 1.35:8]
* That is stated: [PSBh 1.35:9]
Immortal. [PS 1.36]
* Here the prefix 'a-' serves to negate death. [PSBh 1.36:1]
* The root <s>mṛ</s> means 'abandonment of life-breath.' [PSBh 1.36:2]
* Here, the cessation of the functioning of the <s>prāṇa</s> (life-breath) and so forth is called death. [PSBh 1.36:3]
* Why? [PSBh 1.36:4]
* Because he is the experiencer of its fruits. [PSBh 1.36:5]

children.text: * so 'sya kāmitvād vikaraṇadharmitvāc ca nāstītyataḥ // PSBh_1.36:6
children.translated_text: * That [death] does not exist for him, because he possesses the power of will and the quality of [having instruments] free from decay — therefore [PSBh 1.36:6]
* he is called 'immortal' (<s>amara</s>). [PSBh 1.36:7]
* Therefore, from the statements about fearlessness, imperishability, and so forth, it is established that sovereignty is eternal. [PSBh 1.36:8]
* He says: [PSBh 1.36:9]
And everywhere he has unobstructed movement. [PS 1.37]

children.text: * sarvatra abhipretārtheṣu pravartamānasya maheśvareṇāpi apratibandhadharmitvam apratīghātaḥ // PSBh_1.37:1
children.translated_text: * Everywhere — for one who proceeds in desired matters, there is the quality of non-obstruction, non-opposition, even by <s>Maheśvara</s>. [PSBh 1.37:1]

children.text: ity etair guṇair yukto bhagavato mahādevasya mahāgaṇapatir bhavati || PS_1.38 ||
children.translated_text: Endowed with these qualities, he becomes the great chief of <s>gaṇas</s> of the Blessed <s>Mahādeva</s>. [PS 1.38]

children.text: * ity etaiḥ pūrvoktaiḥ avaśyatvānāveśyatvāvadhyatvābhītatvākṣayatvājaratvāmaratvāpratīghātatvākhyaiḥ aṣṭabhir guṇaiḥ siddhilakṣaṇair yukto bhagavato mahādevasya mahāgaṇapatir bhavati // PSBh_1.38:1
children.translated_text: * 'With these' — with the previously mentioned eight qualities whose names are: controllability, non-enterability, invulnerability, fearlessness, imperishability, agelessness, immortality, and unobstructedness — which are the marks of perfection (<s>siddhi</s>) — being endowed [with these], he becomes the great chief of <s>gaṇas</s> (<s>mahāgaṇapati</s>) of the Blessed <s>Mahādeva</s>. [PSBh 1.38:1]
* Superiority over all <s>paśus</s>, and greatness from the excellence of sovereignty. [PSBh 1.38:2]
* The <s>gaṇas</s> are <s>Nandin</s>, <s>Mahākāla</s>, and others. [PSBh 1.38:3]
* Lordship (<s>patitva</s>) is being the master of all affairs of <s>paśus</s> and such. [PSBh 1.38:4]

children.text: * evam adhyāyaparisamāptiṃ kṛtvā yuktaṃ vaktum // PSBh_1.38:5
children.translated_text: * Having thus completed the chapter, it is proper to state: [PSBh 1.38:5]
Here one should recite this <s>Brahman</s> [mantra]. [PS 1.39]

children.text: * bṛhac ca tebhyaḥ sarvabrahmabhyaḥ svayaṃ bhavati // PSBh_1.39:1
children.translated_text: * It is great (<s>bṛhat</s>), and it arises spontaneously from all those <s>Brahmans</s>. [PSBh 1.39:1]
* 'One should recite' (<s>japet</s>) — this is a mental action. [PSBh 1.39:2]
* The recitation (<s>japya</s>) should be understood. [PSBh 1.39:3]

children.text: * uktam āha japayajñastu yajñānāṃ viśiṣṭo daśabhirguṇaiḥ // PSBh_1.39:4
children.translated_text: * It has been stated: 'The sacrifice of recitation (<s>japayajña</s>) is superior to [other] sacrifices by ten times.' [PSBh 1.39:4]

children.text: * upāṃśu syācchataguṇaḥ sāhasro mānasaḥ smṛtaḥ // PSBh_1.39:5
children.translated_text: * 'The whispered [recitation] is a hundredfold; the mental [recitation] is remembered as a thousandfold.' [PSBh 1.39:5]
* Therefore one should recite with the mind alone. [PSBh 1.39:6]
* If [one asks] for what purpose? [PSBh 1.39:7]

children.text: * taducyate adharmavyucchittyarthaṃ dharmasya cābhivṛddhyarthaṃ tasya cākuśalebhyo vyāvartanārthaṃ brahmaṇyanavaratapadapaṅktyām upanibandhanārthaṃ cetyarthaḥ // PSBh_1.39:8
children.translated_text: * The answer is: for the purpose of destroying <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness), for the growth of <s>dharma</s>, for turning him away from unwholesome [acts], and for binding [the mind] to the unceasing succession of syllables of <s>Brahman</s> — this is the meaning. [PSBh 1.39:8]
* He asks: what then is that <s>Brahman</s>? [PSBh 1.39:9]
* The answer here is: [the mantra beginning with] <s>Sadyojāta</s> and so forth. [PSBh 1.39:10]
* Or alternatively, there is a distant connection between <s>Brahman</s> and the chapters here. [PSBh 1.39:11]
* When '<s>Paśupati</s>' was stated, a doubt [arose]. [PSBh 1.39:13]

children.text: * kiṃnarapatisurapatiprajāpatiprabhṛtivad asyaiśvaryaṃ kṛtam anityam āgantukaṃ vā // PSBh_1.39:14
children.translated_text: * Is his sovereignty created, impermanent, or adventitious — like that of a lord of <s>kinnaras</s>, lord of gods, <s>Prajāpati</s>, and such? [PSBh 1.39:14]

children.text: * kiṃ cāsya janma mṛtyur vā vidyate neti // PSBh_1.39:15
children.translated_text: * And does birth or death exist for him, or not? [PSBh 1.39:15]
* The answer is: no. [PSBh 1.39:16]
* Because [the sūtra] states: [PSBh 1.39:17]
I take refuge in the Instantly-born (<s>Sadyojāta</s>). [PS 1.40]

children.text: * atra sadyaḥ ity asmin pade 'rthadvayaṃ cintyate // PSBh_1.40:1
children.translated_text: * Here, in the word <s>sadyaḥ</s>, a twofold meaning is considered. [PSBh 1.40:1]
* <s>Sat</s> (existing) and <s>ādya</s> (primordial). [PSBh 1.40:2]
* Like 'reaching' and 'protecting' [in the etymology of <s>pati</s>]. [PSBh 1.40:3]
* Here <s>sat</s> is in the sense of eternality. [PSBh 1.40:4]
* Why? [PSBh 1.40:5]
* Because of the absence of a cause of destruction. [PSBh 1.40:6]

children.text: * nityaṃ dhruvam avināśi patyuḥ patitvaṃ nānyeṣām ity ato'bhidhīyate sad iti // PSBh_1.40:7
children.translated_text: * Eternal, firm, indestructible is the lordship of the Lord — not of others; therefore he is designated as <s>sat</s> (existing). [PSBh 1.40:7]

children.text: * āha kim ayam ādimattve sati nityo mokṣavat // PSBh_1.40:8
children.translated_text: * He asks: is he eternal while having a beginning, like <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation)? [PSBh 1.40:8]
* The answer is: no. [PSBh 1.40:9]
* Because [the sūtra] says <s>ādya</s> (primordial). [PSBh 1.40:10]
* Because a cause distinct from him [PSBh 1.40:11]

children.text: * hetor asaṃbhavād ādyaman āgantukaṃ patyuḥ patitvaṃ nānyeṣām ityarthaḥ // PSBh_1.40:12
children.translated_text: * is impossible — the lordship of the Lord is primordial, not adventitious, and not [the lordship] of others; this is the meaning. [PSBh 1.40:12]

children.text: * āha kiṃ nityānāditve sati puruṣavaj jāyate // PSBh_1.40:13
children.translated_text: * He asks: being eternal and without beginning, is he born like a <s>puruṣa</s>? [PSBh 1.40:13]
* The answer is: no. [PSBh 1.40:14]
* Because [the sūtra] says <s>ajāta</s> (unborn). [PSBh 1.40:15]
* Here the prefix 'a-' negates birth and death. [PSBh 1.40:16]
* The Blessed One is free from birth and death, stainless (<s>nirañjana</s>). [PSBh 1.40:17]
* Because there is no obtaining of the functioning [associated with the staining of] coloring agents. [PSBh 1.40:19]
* Freedom from self-conceit is not [a quality] of others — therefore. [PSBh 1.40:20]
* '<s>Ajātam</s>' (the unborn) is the object [of the verb]. [PSBh 1.40:21]

children.text: * āha athaitat sattvam ādyatvam ajātatvaṃ ca guṇaṃ kāraṇe jñātvā sādhakena kiṃ kartavyam // PSBh_1.40:22
children.translated_text: * He asks: now, having known this existence (<s>sattva</s>), primordiality (<s>ādyatva</s>), and unbornness (<s>ajātatva</s>) as qualities in the cause — what should the practitioner (<s>sādhaka</s>) do? [PSBh 1.40:22]
* The answer is: one should take refuge (<s>prapattavya</s>). [PSBh 1.40:23]
* Because [the sūtra] says <s>prapadyāmi</s> ('I take refuge'). [PSBh 1.40:24]
* This is stated from the standpoint of the practitioner. [PSBh 1.40:25]

children.text: * yathā agne vratapate vrataṃ cariṣyāmi iti // PSBh_1.40:26
children.translated_text: * Just as [one says]: 'O <s>Agni</s>, lord of vows, I shall observe the vow.' [PSBh 1.40:26]

children.text: * atra praśabdaḥ kāraṇāntareṣu sattvādyatvājātatvapratiṣedhārtho bhṛśārthaś ca // PSBh_1.40:27
children.translated_text: * Here the prefix <s>pra</s> serves to negate existence, primordiality, and unbornness in other causes, and also has an intensive meaning. [PSBh 1.40:27]

children.text: * tasmāt sarvabhāvānabhiṣvaṅgeṇa tad eva kāraṇaṃ prapattavyam // PSBh_1.40:28
children.translated_text: * Therefore, with non-attachment to all [other] existences, one should take refuge in that cause alone. [PSBh 1.40:28]
* The meaning is: one should go to [it as] a shelter. [PSBh 1.40:29]

children.text: * āha atra prapannaḥ kiṃ kariṣyati // PSBh_1.40:30
children.translated_text: * He asks: having taken refuge here, what will he do? [PSBh 1.40:30]
* Or what will he give? [PSBh 1.40:31]

children.text: * tad ucyate pūjāṃ kariṣyaty ātmānaṃ ca dāsyati // PSBh_1.40:32
children.translated_text: * The answer is: he will perform worship, and he will give himself. [PSBh 1.40:32]
* As it is stated: [PSBh 1.40:33]
Homage indeed to <s>Sadyojāta</s> (the Instantly-born). [PS 1.41]

children.text: * āha sattvam ādyatvam ajātatvaṃ ca pūrvoktam // PSBh_1.41:1
children.translated_text: * He says: existence, primordiality, and unbornness have been stated previously. [PSBh 1.41:1]
* '<s>Sadyojātāya</s>' — [this is] a dative case. [PSBh 1.41:2]
* The word <s>vai</s> is in the sense of honoring/affirming. [PSBh 1.41:3]

children.text: * sattvam ādyatvam ajātatvaṃ ca dharmān saṃbhāvya bravīti sadyo'jātāya vai namaḥ // PSBh_1.41:4
children.translated_text: * Having honored the qualities of existence, primordiality, and unbornness, he says: 'Homage indeed to <s>Sadyojāta</s>.' [PSBh 1.41:4]

children.text: * nama ity ātmapradāne pūjāyāṃ ca // PSBh_1.41:5
children.translated_text: * '<s>Namas</s>' (homage) is in the sense of self-offering and worship. [PSBh 1.41:5]

children.text: * namaskāreṇātmānaṃ prayacchati pūjāṃ ca prayuṅkta ity arthaḥ // PSBh_1.41:6
children.translated_text: * By the act of homage, he offers himself and performs worship — this is the meaning. [PSBh 1.41:6]

children.text: * āha kiṃ prayojanam ātmānaṃ maheśvarāya prayacchati // PSBh_1.41:7
children.translated_text: * He asks: for what purpose does he offer himself to <s>Maheśvara</s>? [PSBh 1.41:7]
* Does he [<s>Maheśvara</s>] have suffering? [PSBh 1.41:8]
* Or what does he seek from <s>Maheśvara</s>? [PSBh 1.41:9]

children.text: * kiṃ vā svayam utpāditānugṛhītatirobhāvitānāṃ paśūnāṃ patiḥ uta parairiti // PSBh_1.41:10
children.translated_text: * Is he the lord of <s>paśus</s> that are produced, sustained, and dissolved by himself, or by others? [PSBh 1.41:10]
* The answer is: by himself. [PSBh 1.41:11]
* Because [the sūtra] states: [PSBh 1.41:12]
In existence, in existence, not in excessive existence. [PS 1.42]

children.text: * atra bhave bhave iti vīpsā // PSBh_1.42:1
children.translated_text: * Here, 'in existence after existence' (<s>bhave bhave</s>) is a distributive repetition (<s>vīpsā</s>). // PSBh 1.42:1

children.text: * bhava iti vidyākalāpaśūnāṃ samastānāṃ grahaṇam // PSBh_1.42:2
children.translated_text: * '<s>Bhava</s>' (existence) is the collective designation of <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), <s>kalā</s> (art), and <s>paśus</s> (individual souls). // PSBh 1.42:2
* Why [is it called] <s>bhava</s>? // PSBh 1.42:3
* Because it is produced by [the Lord's] act of bringing-into-being and nurturing (<s>bhavanabhāvana</s>). // PSBh 1.42:4

children.text: * yasmād devamanuṣyatiryaktvena bhāvayati ca tānīśvaraḥ // PSBh_1.42:5
children.translated_text: * Because the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>) nurtures them in the form of gods, humans, and animals. // PSBh 1.42:5

* Because of producing and nurturing <s>dharma</s> (virtue), <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion), <s>aiśvarya</s> (sovereignty), and [their opposites] <s>adharma</s> (vice), <s>ajñāna</s> (ignorance), <s>avairāgya</s> (attachment), and <s>anaiśvarya</s> (lack of sovereignty) — [it is called] <s>bhava</s>. // PSBh 1.42:6

children.text: * tasya bhūyobhūya utpattyanugrahatirobhāvaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā // PSBh_1.42:7
children.translated_text: * Having seen his repeated production, sustenance, and disappearance — // PSBh 1.42:7

children.text: * vīpsāyāḥ utpattāv utpattāv anugrahe'nugrahe tirobhāve tirobhāve cety arthaḥ // PSBh_1.42:8
children.translated_text: * The distributive repetition means: at each production, at each act of sustenance, at each disappearance — this is the meaning. // PSBh 1.42:8
* 'Not in [further] existence' (<s>nātibhave</s>) — // PSBh 1.42:9
* The negative particle (<s>na</s>) negates the state of being an effect. // PSBh 1.42:10
* 'May I not exist in further existences' — this is the meaning. // PSBh 1.42:11

children.text: * āha kiṃ bhavād viyogamātram evaikaṃ mṛgayate // PSBh_1.42:12
children.translated_text: * He asks: Does [the practitioner] seek merely separation from existence alone? // PSBh 1.42:12
* To that it is said: No. // PSBh 1.42:13
* Since he says: // PSBh 1.42:14
Favor me! || PS 1.43 ||
* Here, '<s>bhaja</s>' (favor) indicates grace (<s>anugraha</s>). // PSBh 1.43:1
* 'Sva' designates the cause. // PSBh 1.43:2
* 'Mām' (me) designates the self. // PSBh 1.43:3

children.text: * bhajasva māṃ trāyasva mām anugṛhṇīṣva māmityarthaḥ // PSBh_1.43:4
children.translated_text: * 'Favor me, protect me, bestow grace upon me' — this is the meaning. // PSBh 1.43:4
* He asks: Whom does he address? // PSBh 1.43:5
* To whom does he take refuge? // PSBh 1.43:6
* To whom does he make obeisance? // PSBh 1.43:7

children.text: * kas taṃ puruṣaṃ bhavān mokṣayati // PSBh_1.43:8
children.translated_text: * Who is that person that liberates him? // PSBh 1.43:8

children.text: * kaṃ vā bravīti bhajasva māmiti // PSBh_1.43:9
children.translated_text: * Or, to whom does he say 'Favor me'? // PSBh 1.43:9
* To that it is said: Since he says — // PSBh 1.43:10
The source of existence (<s>bhavodbhava</s>) — || PS 1.44 ||

children.text: * atra bhava iti vidyākalāpaśūnāmeva grahaṇam // PSBh_1.44:1
children.translated_text: * Here, '<s>bhava</s>' is the collective designation of <s>vidyā</s>, <s>kalā</s>, and <s>paśus</s> alone. // PSBh 1.44:1

children.text: * tasyotpattikartā bhagavān ityato bhavodbhava iti // PSBh_1.44:2
children.translated_text: * He who is the agent of their production is the <s>Bhagavān</s>; therefore [he is called] <s>bhavodbhava</s> (source of existence). // PSBh 1.44:2

children.text: * atrotpādakānugrāhakatirobhāvakadharmi kāraṇam utpādyānugrāhyatirobhāvyadharmi kāryam ityetat kāryakāraṇayor lakṣaṇam // PSBh_1.44:3
children.translated_text: * Here, the cause (<s>kāraṇa</s>) possesses the properties of producing, sustaining, and causing to disappear; the effect (<s>kārya</s>) possesses the properties of being produced, sustained, and caused to disappear — this is the definition of cause and effect. // PSBh 1.44:3

children.text: * etasmin kāraṇe prapattyādi kramopayogi draṣṭavyam // PSBh_1.44:4
children.translated_text: * In this cause, taking refuge and the like should be understood as applicable in sequence. // PSBh 1.44:4

children.text: * evamatra bhagavatkauṇḍinyakṛte pañcārthabhāṣye prathamo'dhyāyaḥ saha brahmaṇā granthato 'rthataśca parisamāpta iti // PSBh_1.44:5
children.translated_text: * Thus, here in the <s>Pañcārthabhāṣya</s> composed by the blessed <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>, the first chapter, together with the <s>Brahman</s> [section], is concluded in both text and meaning. // PSBh 1.44:5
<s>Pāśupatasūtra</s>, 2
<s>Vāma</s> (beautiful/eminent) — || PS 2.1 ||
* Among the names [of the Lord], [<s>Vāma</s> means] 'the best' — this is the meaning. // PSBh 2.1:1

children.text: * uktaṃ hi / puruṣadhvajaśṛṅgeṣu havirbhūṣaṇalakṣmasu / vāmaḥ śreṣṭheṣvavakreṣu navasvartheṣu kīrtitaḥ // PSBh_2.1:2

children.translated_text: * He asks: What is the cause of his activity of producing and the like, or what is its purpose? // PSBh 2.1:3
* To that it is said: // PSBh 2.1:4

* For it has been said: 'Among persons, banners, horns, oblations, ornaments, auspicious marks, <s>Vāma</s> is declared [to mean] the best, the upright, and that which serves nine purposes.' // PSBh 2.1:2
Of the god (<s>deva</s>) — || PS 2.2 ||
* Thus. // PSBh 2.2:1

children.text: * atra deva iti divu krīḍāyām // PSBh_2.2:2
children.translated_text: * Here, '<s>deva</s>' (god) [derives from] '<s>div</s>' [meaning] 'to play.' // PSBh 2.2:2
* Because [his] nature is play, [his activity] is caused by play. // PSBh 2.2:3

children.text: * krīḍāvāneva sa bhagavān vidyākalāpaśusaṃjñakaṃ trividhamapi kāryam utpādayan anugṛhṇāti tirobhāvayati cety ato devaḥ // PSBh_2.2:4
children.translated_text: * That playful <s>Bhagavān</s>, producing, sustaining, and causing the disappearance of the threefold effect designated as <s>vidyā</s>, <s>kalā</s>, and <s>paśu</s> — therefore [he is called] <s>deva</s>. // PSBh 2.2:4
* And [his] activity should be understood as having production and the like as its fruits. // PSBh 2.2:5
* 'Of the god' (<s>devasya</s>) — the genitive case [indicates] having that property. // PSBh 2.2:6

children.text: * āha kiṃ nāmadvayamevātra kāraṇe vitanyate arthadvayameva vā āhosvid anyadapyasti neti // PSBh_2.2:7
children.translated_text: * He asks: Are only two names expounded here regarding the cause, or only two meanings, or is there yet something more? // PSBh 2.2:7
* It is said: There is. // PSBh 2.2:8
* Since he says: // PSBh 2.2:9
Of the eldest (<s>jyeṣṭha</s>) — || PS 2.3 ||
* Thus. // PSBh 2.3:1
* Here, [he is called] <s>jyeṣṭha</s> (eldest) because of [his] supremacy. // PSBh 2.3:2
* Superior to whom, or by what? // PSBh 2.3:3
* To that it is said: To the perfected ones (<s>siddha</s>), practitioners (<s>sādhaka</s>), and individual souls (<s>paśu</s>). // PSBh 2.3:4

children.text: * tadāyattatvāt siddhasādhakabhāvasya sarvapaśūnāṃ ca pravṛttinivṛttisthityādiphalānām ityato jyeṣṭhaḥ parataraḥ // PSBh_2.3:5
children.translated_text: * Because the state of being perfected or practitioner depends on him, and because the results such as activity, cessation, and stability of all individual souls [depend on him] — therefore [he is] <s>jyeṣṭha</s>, more supreme, // PSBh 2.3:5
* and the most supreme. // PSBh 2.3:6
* And his sovereignty is uncreated (<s>akṛtaka</s>). // PSBh 2.3:7

children.text: * uktaṃ hi / dṛkkriyālakṣaṇā śaktistattvadharmo'sya nityatā / śreṣṭho'taḥ sarvabhūteṣu tasmādeṣa paraḥ smṛtaḥ // PSBh_2.3:8

children.translated_text: * Thus, because of [his] supremacy, [he is called] <s>jyeṣṭha</s>. // PSBh 2.3:9
* Here too, 'of the eldest' (<s>jyeṣṭhasya</s>) — the genitive case [indicates] having that property. // PSBh 2.3:10

children.text: * āha kiṃ nāmatrayam evātra kāraṇe cintyate arthatrayameva vā āhosvid anyadapyasti neti // PSBh_2.3:11
children.translated_text: * He asks: Are only three names considered here regarding the cause, or only three meanings, or is there yet something more? // PSBh 2.3:11
* It is said: There is. // PSBh 2.3:12

* For it has been said: 'The power characterized by perception and action is his essential property, [and] its permanence [is his nature]. Therefore he is the most excellent among all beings; hence he is regarded as supreme.' // PSBh 2.3:8
<s>Rudra</s> — || PS 2.4 ||
* Thus. // PSBh 2.4:1

children.text: * atra rutasya bhayasya drāvaṇāt saṃyojanād rudraḥ tatra rutam abhilāpa ityanarthāntaram // PSBh_2.4:2
children.translated_text: * Here, [he is called] <s>Rudra</s> because he drives away (<s>drāvaṇa</s>) and conjoins (<s>saṃyojana</s>) fear (<s>bhaya</s>), which is [expressed as] crying (<s>ruta</s>); there, <s>ruta</s> means utterance (<s>abhilāpa</s>) — this is not a different meaning. // PSBh 2.4:2
* As for 'driving away' — // PSBh 2.4:3
* Fear is manifold. // PSBh 2.4:4

children.text: * uktaṃ hi / nānāvidhaiḥ kṛtairyasmād bhayaiśca vividhaistathā / saṃyojayati bhūtāni tasmād rudra iti smṛtaḥ // PSBh_2.4:5

children.translated_text: * Here too, the genitive case [indicates] having that property. // PSBh 2.4:6
* He asks: What is that? // PSBh 2.4:7
* Or, what is its nature? // PSBh 2.4:8
* It is said: // PSBh 2.4:9
* For it has been said: 'Because he conjoins beings with various and manifold fears through diverse actions — therefore he is known as <s>Rudra</s>.' // PSBh 2.4:5
Whose seat (<s>āsana</s>) is adorned (<s>kalita</s>) — || PS 2.5 ||

children.text: * atra trividhena kāryeṇa vidyākalāpaśusaṃjñakena tatraiva sthityutpattipralayān prāpnuvatā kalitaṃ śobhitaśabditaṃ nabhastārābhir ivetyarthaḥ // PSBh_2.5:1
children.translated_text: * Here, adorned (<s>kalita</s>) means embellished, resounding — by the threefold effect designated as <s>vidyā</s>, <s>kalā</s>, and <s>paśu</s>, which undergoes stability, production, and dissolution therein — like the sky [adorned] with stars; this is the meaning. // PSBh 2.5:1

children.text: * āha yadetat patyuḥ patitvaṃ śaktiḥ sāmarthyamaiśvaryaṃ svaguṇaḥ sadbhāvaḥ satattvaṃ tattvadharmaḥ tad āsanam // PSBh_2.5:2
children.translated_text: * He says: That which is the lordship, the power, the capability, the sovereignty, the own-quality, the existence, the true reality, the essential property of the Lord (<s>pati</s>) — that is [his] seat (<s>āsana</s>). // PSBh 2.5:2

children.text: * natu padmāsanavadupaveśanalakṣaṇam ityarthaḥ āsanaṃ kasmāt // PSBh_2.5:3
children.translated_text: * But it is not [a physical seat] characterized by sitting down, like the lotus-posture (<s>padmāsana</s>) — this is the meaning. Why [is it called] <s>āsana</s>? // PSBh 2.5:3
* He sits (<s>āste</s>) in it — [therefore it is] the seat (<s>āsana</s>). // PSBh 2.5:4
* Or, the effect is presided over (<s>adhyāsta</s>) by him — therefore [it is called] <s>āsana</s>; this is the meaning. // PSBh 2.5:5
* Therefore [it is] the seat. // PSBh 2.5:6

children.text: * ato'vyayo'mṛto bhagavān kāmataḥ svaśaktisthaṃ kāryaṃ svaśaktyā adhyāste // PSBh_2.5:7
children.translated_text: * Thus the imperishable, immortal <s>Bhagavān</s>, at will, presides over the effect that abides in his own power, by his own power. // PSBh 2.5:7
* Therefore, the effect and the cause [both] abide in the seat. // PSBh 2.5:8
* He objects: There would be the fault of confusion of the functions of effect and cause, like the [mixing of] milk of cows, sheep, and buffaloes. // PSBh 2.5:9
* That is not so. // PSBh 2.5:10
* Like the fingertip, form, and the like — there is no confusion. // PSBh 2.5:11
* And like the illumination of a lamp, the sun, and eye-rays — there is no confusion. // PSBh 2.5:12

children.text: * āha saṃkare aparicchedadoṣaḥ īśvarapuruṣavidyākalānāṃ mākṣikakoṭadravyavat // PSBh_2.5:13
children.translated_text: * He objects: In [the case of] confusion, there would be the fault of non-differentiation of the Lord, the person, <s>vidyā</s>, and <s>kalā</s> — like honey, lac, and [their constituent] substances. // PSBh 2.5:13

children.text: * taducyate ekottarotkarṣeṇa vyāpyavyāpakabhāvenāvasthitānāṃ tattvādīnāṃ nāparicchedadoṣaḥ sūtratvād vyāpakaṃ maheśvaratattvaṃ vyāpyaṃ puruṣādipañcaviṃśakam // PSBh_2.5:14
children.translated_text: * To that it is said: For the principles (<s>tattva</s>) and the rest, which are established in the relation of pervaded and pervader through progressive ascent, there is no fault of non-differentiation, because [of their relation] like a thread — the <s>Maheśvara</s> principle is the pervader, and the twenty-five [principles] beginning with <s>puruṣa</s> are the pervaded. // PSBh 2.5:14

children.text: * tathā ātmatvād vyāpakaṃ puruṣatattvaṃ vyāpyaṃ pradhānādicaturviṃśakam // PSBh_2.5:15
children.translated_text: * Likewise, because of selfhood, the <s>puruṣa</s> (person) principle is the pervader, and the twenty-four [principles] beginning with <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) are the pervaded. // PSBh 2.5:15

children.text: * tathā vyāpakaṃ pradhānaṃ vyāpyaṃ buddhyāditrayoviṃśakam // PSBh_2.5:16
children.translated_text: * Likewise, <s>pradhāna</s> is the pervader, and the twenty-three [principles] beginning with <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) are the pervaded. // PSBh 2.5:16

children.text: * vyāpikā bhavati buddhiḥ vyāpyam ahaṃkārādidvāviṃśakam // PSBh_2.5:17
children.translated_text: * <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect) is the pervader, and the twenty-two [principles] beginning with <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego) are the pervaded. // PSBh 2.5:17

children.text: * tathā vyāpako bhavatyahaṃkāraḥ vyāpyānyekādaśendriyāṇi daśavidhaṃ ca kāryam // PSBh_2.5:18
children.translated_text: * Likewise, <s>ahaṃkāra</s> is the pervader, and the eleven senses and the tenfold effect are the pervaded. // PSBh 2.5:18
* The eleven senses are the pervaders, and the five subtle elements (<s>bhūtasūkṣma</s>) — sound and the rest — are the pervaded. // PSBh 2.5:19

children.text: * tathā vyāpakāni pañcabhūtasūkṣmāṇi śabdādīni vyāpyāni ākāśādīni pañcamahābhūtāni // PSBh_2.5:20
children.translated_text: * Likewise, the five subtle elements — sound and the rest — are the pervaders, and the five great elements (<s>mahābhūta</s>) — space and the rest — are the pervaded. // PSBh 2.5:20
* Likewise, space (<s>ākāśa</s>) is the pervader, and the four elements beginning with wind are the pervaded. // PSBh 2.5:21

children.text: * tathā vyāpako bhavati vāyuḥ vyāpyaṃ tejaḥprabhṛti bhūtatrayam // PSBh_2.5:22
children.translated_text: * Likewise, wind (<s>vāyu</s>) is the pervader, and the three elements beginning with fire are the pervaded. // PSBh 2.5:22

children.text: * tathā vyāpakaṃ bhavati tejaḥ vyāpyam abādidvayam // PSBh_2.5:23
children.translated_text: * Likewise, fire (<s>tejas</s>) is the pervader, and the two — water and the rest — are the pervaded. // PSBh 2.5:23

children.text: * tathā vyāpikā bhavantyāpaḥ vyāpyā pṛthivī // PSBh_2.5:24
children.translated_text: * Likewise, water (<s>āpas</s>) is the pervader, and earth (<s>pṛthivī</s>) is the pervaded. // PSBh 2.5:24

children.text: * vyāpikā pṛthivī vyāpyāni bhūmyudakarasalakṣaṇāni kāryāṇi // PSBh_2.5:25
children.translated_text: * Earth is the pervader, and the effects characterized by land, water, and essence are the pervaded. // PSBh 2.5:25

children.text: * tathā vyāpakāni bhūmyudakarasalakṣaṇāni kāraṇāni vyāpyaṃ devamanuṣyatiryagyoni tṛṇauṣadhivṛkṣagulmalatāvanaspatyādikāryam anekavidham ato nāparicchedadoṣaḥ // PSBh_2.5:26
children.translated_text: * Likewise, the causes characterized by land, water, and essence are the pervaders, and the manifold effects — the wombs of gods, humans, and animals, grass, herbs, trees, shrubs, vines, and plants — are the pervaded. Therefore there is no fault of non-differentiation. // PSBh 2.5:26

children.text: * āha vṛttyasaṃkaragrahaṇe dṛṣṭāntābhāvād ayuktam taducyate haridrodakavad vyāpyaṃ vyāpakaṃ ca tadyathā haridrodake snigdhatvaśaityādidharmair apāṃ grahaṇaṃ gandhavarṇaghanakṣāratvādibhir haridrāyāḥ // PSBh_2.5:27
children.translated_text: * He objects: Because there is no illustration for the non-confusion of functions [when things are pervading each other], it is improper. To that it is said: Like turmeric-water — the pervaded and the pervader — just as in turmeric-water, the water is apprehended by [its] properties of oiliness, coldness, and the like, and the turmeric by [its properties of] odor, color, density, alkalinity, and the like — // PSBh 2.5:27
* Similarly, the Lord [is apprehended] by the arrangement of oceans, divine realms, stations, bodies, senses, objects, and the like, and by the conjunction of pleasure and pain. // PSBh 2.5:28
* So too for <s>puruṣa</s> (the individual soul). // PSBh 2.5:29

children.text: * īśvarasyāpi apariṇāmidharmitvāt sukhaduḥkhadātṛtvāc ca pradhānadharmādharmādīnāṃ grahaṇam // PSBh_2.5:30
children.translated_text: * For the Lord too, because of having the property of non-transformation, and because of being the giver of pleasure and pain — [there is] apprehension of <s>pradhāna</s>, <s>dharma</s>, <s>adharma</s>, and the rest. // PSBh 2.5:30

children.text: * tathā pradhānasya mānasasaṃkalpālocanagamanādibhiḥ karaṇagrāmasya viṣayāṇāṃ ca grahaṇam // PSBh_2.5:31
children.translated_text: * Likewise, for <s>pradhāna</s>, [there is] apprehension of the group of instruments (<s>karaṇagrāma</s>) and the objects by [their properties of] mental resolve, reflection, locomotion, and the like. // PSBh 2.5:31

children.text: * tathā dhṛtisaṃgrahapaktivyūhāvakāśadānādibhir dharmaiḥ pṛthivyādīnāṃ grahaṇamiti pradhānavādino manyante // PSBh_2.5:32
children.translated_text: * Likewise, the proponents of <s>pradhāna</s> hold that there is apprehension of earth and the rest by [their] properties of support, cohesion, digestion, arrangement, giving of space, and the like. // PSBh 2.5:32

children.text: * āha atheha tantre kathaṃ kāryakāraṇāvasthānam // PSBh_2.5:33
children.translated_text: * He asks: Now, in this system, how is the relation of effect and cause established? // PSBh 2.5:33
* That should be stated. // PSBh 2.5:34

children.text: * taducyate iha yasmād āha śarvasarvebhyaḥ iti vacanād yathāsambhavam // PSBh_2.5:35
children.translated_text: * To that it is said: Here, since it is stated '<s>Śarva</s> [rules over] all' — according to possibility. // PSBh 2.5:35

children.text: * sati vibhutve svavṛttyā kāryakāraṇayoḥ sarvagatatve'pi svavṛttyasaṃkaraḥ tasmād āsanasthaṃ kāryaṃ kāraṇaṃ ceti // PSBh_2.5:36
children.translated_text: * When omnipresence obtains, cause and effect, even while being all-pervading through their own functions, have no confusion of functions. Therefore, the effect and the cause [both] abide in the seat. // PSBh 2.5:36

children.text: * āha kiṃ tad āsanasthaṃ kāryam āsane nityam āhosvid anityamiti // PSBh_2.5:37
children.translated_text: * He asks: Is that effect which abides in the seat permanent in the seat, or impermanent? // PSBh 2.5:37
* It is said: The effect is permanent. // PSBh 2.5:38
* Why? // PSBh 2.5:39
* It belongs to the Lord (<s>pati</s>). // PSBh 2.5:40
* Because of the permanence of the Lord who is the cause, the lordship is permanent. // PSBh 2.5:41
* Here, from the statement beginning with '<s>Sadyojāta</s>' (Instantly Born), the protector is permanent. // PSBh 2.5:42
* And because of the permanence of the protector, the protected is also permanent. // PSBh 2.5:43
* Why? // PSBh 2.5:44

children.text: * na hy asati pālye pālaka ityeva // PSBh_2.5:45
children.translated_text: * For without the protected, there is simply no protector. // PSBh 2.5:45

children.text: * sati nityatve tānyeva paśvādīni saṃyojayati // PSBh_2.5:46
children.translated_text: * Since permanence obtains, he conjoins those very <s>paśus</s> (individual souls) and the rest. // PSBh 2.5:46
* Like walls made of clay and metal — from the illustration. // PSBh 2.5:47
* And the acquisition of function is called 'production' (<s>utpatti</s>). // PSBh 2.5:48

children.text: * sthitisthānaśarīrendriyaviṣayādyāyatanānāṃ parasparopakārāc cānugrahaḥ īśvaracodanānugrahaḥ viyojanaṃ vṛttilopaśca // PSBh_2.5:49
children.translated_text: * Sustenance (<s>anugraha</s>) [arises] from the mutual benefit of [the entities'] station, body, senses, objects, and other supports; it is the sustenance [arising from] the Lord's impulse. Separation and loss of function [constitute disappearance]. // PSBh 2.5:49
* Loss means non-existence. // PSBh 2.5:50

children.text: * tasmāt triṣvapi kāleṣu āsanasthaṃ kāryaṃ draṣṭavyam // PSBh_2.5:51
children.translated_text: * Therefore, in all three times, the effect should be understood as abiding in the seat. // PSBh 2.5:51
* Like a seed in the earth — this is the meaning. // PSBh 2.5:52

children.text: * āha kiṃ tat kāryaṃ bhagavān yugapadutpādayati kramaśo vā // PSBh_2.5:53
children.translated_text: * He asks: Does the <s>Bhagavān</s> produce that effect simultaneously or in sequence? // PSBh 2.5:53

children.text: * kiṃ vā karmāpekṣaḥ anapekṣo vā // PSBh_2.5:54
children.translated_text: * Or, does he act with regard to <s>karma</s> (deeds) or without regard [to them]? // PSBh 2.5:54
* To that it is said: As he wishes. // PSBh 2.5:55
* Since he says: // PSBh 2.5:56
They call [him] one whose desires encompass all (<s>sārvakāmika</s>) — || PS 2.6 ||
* Here, the word 'all' (<s>sarva</s>) should be understood as designating all effects beginning with <s>vidyā</s> without remainder. // PSBh 2.6:1
* In '<s>kāmika</s>' (relating to desire), three [forms] are to be considered: // PSBh 2.6:2

children.text: * kāmī kāmaḥ kāmyamiti ca tatra kāmī īśvaraḥ // PSBh_2.6:3
children.translated_text: * '<s>Kāmī</s>' (the desirer), '<s>kāma</s>' (the desire), and '<s>kāmya</s>' (the desired) — among these, the desirer is the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>). // PSBh 2.6:3
* His desire is [his] will (<s>icchā</s>). // PSBh 2.6:4
* The desired [object] is the effect such as knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>) and the like. // PSBh 2.6:5
* That [<s>Rudra</s>] produces [effects] either simultaneously or sequentially, as he wishes. // PSBh 2.6:6
* Why? // PSBh 2.6:7
* Because of his desiring nature (<s>kāmitva</s>). // PSBh 2.6:8
* And his independence from <s>karma</s> (action) is thereby established. // PSBh 2.6:9

children.text: * karmakāminaśca maheśvaramapekṣante na tu bhagavānīśvaraḥ karma puruṣaṃ vāpekṣate // PSBh_2.6:10
children.translated_text: * Those who desire [the fruits of] action depend on <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord), but the Blessed Lord <s>Īśvara</s> does not depend on action or on any person. // PSBh 2.6:10
* Therefore, the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>) is not dependent on <s>karma</s>. // PSBh 2.6:11
* The word '<s>iti</s>' serves the purpose of concluding the section, since the meanings have been etymologically explained. // PSBh 2.6:12
* He objects: The [Lord's] desiring nature (<s>kāmitva</s>) would create a difference from the true nature [of the <s>ātman</s>]. // PSBh 2.6:13

children.text: * kāryatvena vā pariṇāmitvam ātmano bandhamokṣaviparyayaṃ vā kuryāt // PSBh_2.6:14
children.translated_text: * Or, because of being an effect, it would entail the transformability of the self, or a reversal of bondage and liberation. // PSBh 2.6:14
* To that it is said — because he states '<s>āṅ</s>' (up to/within): // PSBh 2.6:15

children.text: * āṅ iti kāryakāraṇatvam ātmano muktānāṃ ca maryādā // PSBh_2.6:16
children.translated_text: * '<s>Āṅ</s>' indicates the limit (<s>maryādā</s>) of the cause-and-effect [relationship] for the self and for the liberated ones. // PSBh 2.6:16

children.text: * taducyate utpādyānugrāhyatirobhāvyakalpakatvābhāvakatvenāpariṇāmitvam ātmano muktānāṃ ca punarduḥkhair asaṃyojanam ityeṣā kāraṇamaryādā // PSBh_2.6:17
children.translated_text: * To that it is said: Since [<s>Rudra</s>] is the producer, benefactor, concealer, creator, and destroyer — the non-transformability of the self and of the liberated ones, and their non-re-conjunction with suffering — this is the boundary of causation. // PSBh 2.6:17
* And the boundary of effects is to be established. // PSBh 2.6:18
* To that it is said: The boundary of what is to be produced, benefited, concealed, created, and transformed. // PSBh 2.6:19
* And the presiding over other objections as well. // PSBh 2.6:20
* '<s>Cakṣiṅ</s>' [is used] in the sense of speaking. // PSBh 2.6:21
* It has been declared by the Blessed One, by <s>Rudra</s> himself, to the effects. // PSBh 2.6:22
* The power (<s>śakti</s>) of the Blessed Lord <s>Maheśvara</s> is eternal (<s>sanātanī</s>). // PSBh 2.6:23
* That effect such as knowledge and the like has been set in motion [by him] — this is the meaning. // PSBh 2.6:24
* Likewise, it has been said, i.e., described — this is the meaning. // PSBh 2.6:25
* Here, this technical section on cause and effect (<s>kāryakāraṇa</s>) is concluded. // PSBh 2.6:26

children.text: * kiṃ nāma kāmitvaṃ rudrakāmitvaṃ ca // PSBh_2.6:27
children.translated_text: * What exactly are the desiring nature [of the self] and the desiring nature of <s>Rudra</s>? // PSBh 2.6:27
* Is this [desiring nature] itself the great fortune (<s>mahābhāgya</s>) in the cause, or is there something else? // PSBh 2.6:28
* It is said: There is [something else]. // PSBh 2.6:29
* Because he states: // PSBh 2.6:30
And the inauspicious (<s>amaṅgala</s>) here becomes auspicious (<s>maṅgala</s>). || PS 2.7 ||

children.text: * amaṅgalam iti atra sādhanajātam adhikurute taduddeśena tu maṅgalavacananirdeśaṃ karoti // PSBh_2.7:1
children.translated_text: * 'Inauspicious' (<s>amaṅgala</s>) — here [the sūtra] takes up the entire class of practices (<s>sādhanajāta</s>), and by reference to that, it makes the teaching expressed by the word 'auspicious' (<s>maṅgala</s>). // PSBh 2.7:1
* The word '<s>ca</s>' (and) should be seen as introducing the statement about the qualities of the cause. // PSBh 2.7:2

children.text: * upakṣipyottaratra maṅgalaṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ ca vakṣyāmaḥ // PSBh_2.7:3
children.translated_text: * Having introduced [it], we shall explain further on about the auspicious and the circumambulation (<s>pradakṣiṇa</s>). // PSBh 2.7:3

children.text: * tasmādubhayaṃ rudre devāśca pitaraśca ityupariṣṭād vakṣyāmaḥ // PSBh_2.7:4
children.translated_text: * Therefore, both [aspects] in <s>Rudra</s> — 'gods and ancestors' — we shall explain further on. // PSBh 2.7:4

children.text: * atraśabde mūrtyadhiṣṭhātari manaḥsaṃjñe kāraṇe sakale upatiṣṭhatā apasavyasambandho draṣṭavyaḥ // PSBh_2.7:5
children.translated_text: * By the word 'here' (<s>atra</s>), one should see the connection with the leftward [circumambulation] in the context of the cause, the presider over the image (<s>mūrti</s>), designated by the term 'mind' (<s>manas</s>), which is complete. // PSBh 2.7:5

children.text: * maṅgalam ityatrāpi cāmaṅgale vaktavye maṅgalameva tad vakṣyāmaḥ // PSBh_2.7:6
children.translated_text: * Regarding 'auspicious' (<s>maṅgala</s>) — here too, though the inauspicious is being discussed, it is the auspicious itself that we shall explain. // PSBh 2.7:6

children.text: * tad ucyate atra amaṅgalaṃ nāma nagnatvāpasavyatvasambandho hasitādyaḥ sādhanavargaḥ // PSBh_2.7:7
children.translated_text: * To that it is said: Here, 'inauspicious' (<s>amaṅgala</s>) refers to the class of practices such as nakedness (<s>nagnatva</s>), the leftward connection (<s>apasavyatvasambandha</s>), laughter and the like. // PSBh 2.7:7
* That, here, by the power of the causal image (<s>kāraṇamūrti</s>), becomes auspicious (<s>maṅgala</s>). // PSBh 2.7:8
* Like a mountain, water, and a forest. // PSBh 2.7:9
* 'Auspicious' (<s>maṅgala</s>) means a practice (<s>sādhana</s>) that accomplishes <s>dharma</s>. // PSBh 2.7:10
* 'It becomes' (<s>bhavati</s>) — this is a statement of [actual] fact, beyond doubt. // PSBh 2.7:11
* The inauspicious, when performed before the causal image (<s>kāraṇamūrti</s>), becomes auspicious — this is the meaning. // PSBh 2.7:12

children.text: * āha kiṃ nagnatvam apasavyatvaṃ vā sādhanadvayamevocyate // PSBh_2.7:13
children.translated_text: * He asks: Are only nakedness and leftward [circumambulation] — these two practices — mentioned? // PSBh 2.7:13
* Because he states: // PSBh 2.7:15
And the leftward (<s>apasavya</s>) becomes the rightward circumambulation (<s>pradakṣiṇa</s>). || PS 2.8 ||
* And nakedness is also a practice — this is the meaning. // PSBh 2.8:1

children.text: * atrāmaṅgalanirdeśārthatvāt pratyāhāravad upahārasāmānyamātrakhyāpanāc ca pṛthagapasavyārambhaḥ // PSBh_2.8:2
children.translated_text: * Here, because of the purpose of indicating the inauspicious, and because of merely indicating the general [nature of] offering (<s>upahāra</s>) — like withdrawal (<s>pratyāhāra</s>) — the leftward [circumambulation] is separately commenced. // PSBh 2.8:2

children.text: * tasmādatra apasavyaṃ nāma yat savyād viparītam // PSBh_2.8:3
children.translated_text: * Therefore, here, 'leftward' (<s>apasavya</s>) means that which is opposite to the right (<s>savya</s>). // PSBh 2.8:3
* The word '<s>ca</s>' (and) is used in the sense of conjunction. // PSBh 2.8:4

children.text: * na kevalaṃ kāraṇamūrtisāmarthyād amaṅgalaṃ maṅgalamāpadyate apasavyaṃ ca pradakṣiṇamāpadyata ityarthaḥ // PSBh_2.8:5
children.translated_text: * Not only does the inauspicious become auspicious by the power of the causal image, but the leftward also becomes [equivalent to] the rightward circumambulation (<s>pradakṣiṇa</s>) — this is the meaning. // PSBh 2.8:5

children.text: * pradakṣiṇaṃ nāma yad anyeṣām apasavyaṃ tadiha pradakṣiṇaṃ dharmaniṣpādakaṃ bhavati // PSBh_2.8:6
children.translated_text: * 'Rightward circumambulation' (<s>pradakṣiṇa</s>) means: what is leftward (<s>apasavya</s>) for others, that here becomes the rightward circumambulation that accomplishes <s>dharma</s>. // PSBh 2.8:6

children.text: * nanu yat teṣāṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ kasmāt // PSBh_2.8:7
children.translated_text: * But what about the [conventional] rightward circumambulation of those [other systems] — why [is it rejected]? // PSBh 2.8:7
* Because of the fault of deviation from the rule (<s>utsūtra</s>) and the like — like non-bathing and the like — this is the meaning. // PSBh 2.8:8

children.text: * āha samastānāṃ kāraṇaguṇānāṃ tu vacanaṃ kimasti neti // PSBh_2.8:9
children.translated_text: * He asks: Is there a comprehensive statement about all the qualities of the cause, or not? // PSBh 2.8:9
* It is said: There is. // PSBh 2.8:10
* Because he states: // PSBh 2.8:11
Therefore, he should be worshipped in both ways. || PS 2.9 ||
* Thus. // PSBh 2.9:1
* Here, the word 'therefore' (<s>tasmāt</s>) refers to the statement about the qualities of the cause. // PSBh 2.9:2
* What are the qualities of the cause? // PSBh 2.9:3

children.text: * taducyate patitvasattvādyatvājātatvotpādakānugrāhakatirobhāvakatvatapāvāvede vāmadevajyeṣṭharudrakāmitvaṃ ca maṅgalāvāptiḥ pradakṣiṇāvāptiśca // PSBh_2.9:4
children.translated_text: * To that it is said: Lordship (<s>patitva</s>), existence (<s>sattva</s>), unborn nature (<s>ajātatva</s>), being the producer, benefactor, and concealer, <s>Tapas</s> (austerity), the two <s>Vedas</s>, and the desiring nature of <s>Vāmadeva</s>, <s>Jyeṣṭha</s>, and <s>Rudra</s> — and the attainment of the auspicious, and the attainment of the rightward circumambulation. // PSBh 2.9:4
* Having known these qualities of the cause — // PSBh 2.9:5
* therefore he says 'therefore' (<s>tasmāt</s>). // PSBh 2.9:6

children.text: * athaitat kāraṇaguṇavacanaṃ jñātvā sādhakena kiṃ kartavyam // PSBh_2.9:7
children.translated_text: * Now, having known this statement about the qualities of the cause, what should the practitioner (<s>sādhaka</s>) do? // PSBh 2.9:7
* To that it is said: He should be worshipped in both ways (<s>ubhayathā yaṣṭavyaḥ</s>). // PSBh 2.9:8
* Here, 'in both ways' (<s>ubhayathā</s>) means 'in two ways' (<s>dvidhā</s>) — this is the meaning. // PSBh 2.9:9
* Regarding 'he should be worshipped' (<s>yaṣṭavya</s>) — here too the threefold analysis (<s>nastrika</s>) is to be considered. // PSBh 2.9:10
* The worshipper (<s>yaṣṭā</s>), the worship (<s>yajana</s>), and the one to be worshipped (<s>yaṣṭavya</s>). // PSBh 2.9:11
* Here, the worshipper is the practitioner (<s>sādhaka</s>). // PSBh 2.9:12
* The one to be worshipped is the Blessed Lord <s>Maheśvara</s>. // PSBh 2.9:13
* The worship is contemplation (<s>bhāvanā</s>). // PSBh 2.9:14
* Worship [consists of] study (<s>adhyayana</s>), teaching (<s>adhyāpana</s>), remembrance (<s>smaraṇa</s>), and the like. // PSBh 2.9:15
* The fruit of that — eternal union with the deity (<s>devanityatā</s>), [which is] union (<s>sāyujya</s>) — we shall explain further on. // PSBh 2.9:16
* He objects: Since there is no specification, there is doubt. // PSBh 2.9:17
* How [exactly is it] 'in both ways'? // PSBh 2.9:18
* The twofold specification should be stated. // PSBh 2.9:19
* To that it is said: // PSBh 2.9:20
Like [the worship] of gods (<s>deva</s>) and like [the worship] of ancestors (<s>pitṛ</s>). || PS 2.10 ||
* How? // PSBh 2.10:1

children.text: * ucyate pūrvamasya brāhmaṇasya devayajane pitṛyajane cādhikāro'dhigataḥ // PSBh_2.10:2
children.translated_text: * It is said: Previously, this <s>brāhmaṇa</s> had the qualification for worshipping gods and worshipping ancestors. // PSBh 2.10:2

children.text: * tasmāt tebhyo devapitṛbhyo bhaktivyāvartanaṃ kṛtvā ubhayathāpi maheśvare bhāvam avasthāpya yajanaṃ kartavyaṃ nānyasya // PSBh_2.10:3
children.translated_text: * Therefore, having turned away the devotion from those gods and ancestors, and having established devotion in both ways in <s>Maheśvara</s>, the worship should be performed — and not for any other. // PSBh 2.10:3
* The word '<s>ca</s>' (and) is used in the sense of prohibition. // PSBh 2.10:4

children.text: * yat tat pūrvaṃ devapitṛṣu kārakatvaṃ saṃbhāvitaṃ tat teṣu na vidyate // PSBh_2.10:5
children.translated_text: * That agency which was formerly attributed to the gods and ancestors — that does not exist in them. // PSBh 2.10:5

children.text: * atasteṣāṃ yajanaṃ na kartavyam ityarthaḥ // PSBh_2.10:6
children.translated_text: * Therefore, worship of them should not be performed — this is the meaning. // PSBh 2.10:6

children.text: * āha yadyevaṃ tasmād ucyatāṃ devapit ṇāṃ ko doṣaḥ yasmāt te na yaṣṭavyāḥ // PSBh_2.10:7
children.translated_text: * He asks: If so, then let it be stated — what is the fault of the gods and ancestors, such that they should not be worshipped? // PSBh 2.10:7

children.text: * rudre vā ko guṇaḥ yasmāt sa eva yaṣṭavyaḥ // PSBh_2.10:8
children.translated_text: * Or what is the virtue of <s>Rudra</s>, such that he alone should be worshipped? // PSBh 2.10:8
* Let the specification be stated. // PSBh 2.10:9
* Like [the rejection of] non-bathing and the like. // PSBh 2.10:10
* To that it is said: // PSBh 2.10:11

children.text: ubhayaṃ tu rudre devāḥ pitaraśca || PS_2.11 ||
children.translated_text: But both [types] — gods and ancestors — [exist] in <s>Rudra</s>. || PS 2.11 ||
* There, 'both' means 'the two,' i.e., the totality — this is the meaning. // PSBh 2.11:1

children.text: * tuśabdo devapitṛṣu vaiśeṣikaṃ kāraṇatvaṃ vyāvartayati rudre iti kāraṇāpadeśam // PSBh_2.11:2
children.translated_text: * The word '<s>tu</s>' (but) removes the special causality [attributed] to gods and ancestors; 'in <s>Rudra</s>' indicates [him as] the cause. // PSBh 2.11:2
* The <s>Rudra</s>-nature of <s>Rudra</s> has been stated previously. // PSBh 2.11:3
* '<s>Rudra</s>' indicates a proximity pertaining to the domain [of his power]. // PSBh 2.11:4
* Here, power (<s>śakti</s>) and domain (<s>viṣaya</s>) are not different things. // PSBh 2.11:5

children.text: * te devapitaro rudraśaktyāṃ hāryadhāryakāryatvena vartante ādhīyante viṣaye vartanta ityarthaḥ // PSBh_2.11:6
children.translated_text: * Those gods and ancestors exist within the power of <s>Rudra</s> as [objects to be] carried, supported, and acted upon — they are placed within his domain — this is the meaning. // PSBh 2.11:6
* Gods and ancestors. // PSBh 2.11:7

children.text: * tatra devā iti ṛbhuṣu brahmādipiśācānteṣu manuṣyatiryagyonivarjaṃ sāmānyasaṃjñā // PSBh_2.11:8
children.translated_text: * There, 'gods' (<s>devāḥ</s>) is a general designation for [all beings] from <s>Ṛbhus</s> to <s>Brahmā</s> and ending with <s>piśācas</s> (spirits), excluding human and animal births. // PSBh 2.11:8
* As [established] by rule (<s>vidhi</s>). // PSBh 2.11:9

children.text: * pitara iti viśeṣasaṃjñā bhasmasnānādivad ityarthaḥ // PSBh_2.11:10
children.translated_text: * 'Ancestors' (<s>pitaraḥ</s>) is a specific designation — like bathing with ash and the like — this is the meaning. // PSBh 2.11:10
* And like '<s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Devadatta</s>' and similar [expressions of general and specific]. // PSBh 2.11:11

children.text: * atrāha sāmānyaviśeṣasaṃjñābhidhāne kiṃ prayojanamiti cet // PSBh_2.11:12
children.translated_text: * He asks here: What is the purpose of stating [both] the general and specific designations? // PSBh 2.11:12

children.text: * taducyate trividhasyāpi kāryasya rudre hāryadhāryakāryajñāpanārthaṃ kiṃca kālakriyāsvāhāsvadhāmantrānyatvadarśanād devapitṛyajanāpahṛtacittavyāvartanārthatvāc ca // PSBh_2.11:13
children.translated_text: * To that it is said: For the purpose of indicating that all three types of effects [exist] in <s>Rudra</s> as [objects to be] carried, supported, and effected; and furthermore, because the difference between times, rites, <s>svāhā</s>, <s>svadhā</s>, <s>mantras</s>, and other [elements] is observed — for the purpose of turning away the minds of those who are attracted to the worship of gods and ancestors. // PSBh 2.11:13
* Therefore, the explanation through both identity and difference is not faulty. // PSBh 2.11:14
* The word '<s>ca</s>' (and) is used in the sense of surpassing excellence. // PSBh 2.11:15

children.text: * devapitṛvat sattvasya trividhasyāpi kāryasyeśvare pratiṣṭhāprasavasaṃyogaviyogasukhamohabandhamokṣadātṛtvena ca sa eva paraṃ kāraṇaṃ samastatvenāpyate ityevaṃ caśabdo'bhyadhikatve draṣṭavyaḥ tasmād duḥkhāntārthinā te devapitaro na yaṣṭavyāḥ // PSBh_2.11:16
children.translated_text: * Just as with gods and ancestors, [so too] for the threefold existence (<s>sattva</s>), through the Lord's (<s>Īśvara</s>'s) being the giver of establishment, origination, conjunction, disjunction, happiness, delusion, bondage, and liberation [of all three types of effects] — he alone is the supreme cause, and he is approached as complete — thus the word '<s>ca</s>' should be seen in the sense of surpassing excellence. Therefore, the one who seeks the end of suffering should not worship those gods and ancestors. // PSBh 2.11:16

children.text: * tadarthe bhagavān maheśvaro yaṣṭavya ityarthaḥ // PSBh_2.11:17
children.translated_text: * For that purpose, the Blessed Lord <s>Maheśvara</s> should be worshipped — this is the meaning. // PSBh 2.11:17
* Here, this ancillary section on cause and effect is concluded. // PSBh 2.11:18

children.text: * ata uttarasya vidhiprakaraṇasya satyapi padārthavailakṣaṇye sādhyasādhanabhāvād yajanena saha sambandhaṃ kariṣyāmaḥ // PSBh_2.11:19
children.translated_text: * From here onward, though the section on rules (<s>vidhi</s>) has a different category of subject matter, we shall establish its connection with worship through the relationship of end and means. // PSBh 2.11:19

children.text: * iha purastāduktam ubhayathā yaṣṭavyaḥ devavat pitṛvac ca // PSBh_2.11:21
children.translated_text: * Here it was previously stated: 'He should be worshipped in both ways — like [the worship] of gods and like [the worship] of ancestors.' // PSBh 2.11:21

children.text: * yatra pūrvaṃ devapitṛbhyo vyāvartitayā bhaktyā maheśvaraṃ yajato'navagamāt svātmeśvarasaṃyogaṃ yogaṃ prāpsyasi tatphalaṃ vakṣyāmaḥ // PSBh_2.11:22
children.translated_text: * Where, having turned away devotion previously [directed] toward gods and ancestors, and while worshipping <s>Maheśvara</s> — since [the fruit] is not yet comprehended — 'you will attain <s>yoga</s>, the union of self and Lord, and we shall explain its fruit.' // PSBh 2.11:22

children.text: * yena ca balenopabṛṃhitasya tatraiva yajane udyogo'bhiniveśaśca bhaviṣyati tad balaṃ vakṣyāmaḥ // PSBh_2.11:23
children.translated_text: * And that strength by which, when one is fortified, there will be zeal and absorption in that very worship — we shall explain that strength. // PSBh 2.11:23
* And we shall explain the means for attaining that strength. // PSBh 2.11:24
* To that it is said: // PSBh 2.11:25
One who is joyful and non-negligent (<s>harṣāpramādī</s>). || PS 2.12 ||
* Thus. // PSBh 2.12:1
* Or alternatively, [this sūtra has] a different, remote connection. // PSBh 2.12:2

children.text: * yasmād ucyate yasya yenārthasambandho dūrasthasyāpi tena tadarthotpattiḥ samānā // PSBh_2.12:3
children.translated_text: * Because it is said: For one whose purpose is connected with something, even if remote, the arising of that purpose is the same. // PSBh 2.12:3

children.text: * ānantarye'pi asaṃbandho grahaṇakṣayādivan na tv atra amaṅgalādibhiḥ // PSBh_2.12:4
children.translated_text: * Even in proximity, there may be non-connection — as in the case of an eclipse and [its supposed] destruction — but not here with the inauspicious and the like. // PSBh 2.12:4
* Why? // PSBh 2.12:5
* Because there is no remainder [to be explained]. // PSBh 2.12:6
* Thus, here too, there is a remote connection. // PSBh 2.12:7
* Why? // PSBh 2.12:8

children.text: * iha purastāduktam akaluṣamateḥ carataḥ tato'sya yogaḥ pravartate // PSBh_2.12:9
children.translated_text: * Here it was previously stated: 'For one who practises with an untainted mind, thereupon <s>yoga</s> arises for him.' // PSBh 2.12:9

children.text: * atra kaluṣavyatirekeṇa ye 'nye yogavyāghātakarā hetavaḥ tān vakṣyāmaḥ // PSBh_2.12:10
children.translated_text: * Here, we shall explain the other causes that obstruct <s>yoga</s>, apart from taintedness (<s>kaluṣa</s>). // PSBh 2.12:10

children.text: * yathā caikā caritavyā yogaprāpikā iti vyākhyāsyāmaḥ // PSBh_2.12:11
children.translated_text: * And we shall explain how the [proper] conduct, which leads to the attainment of <s>yoga</s>, should be practised. // PSBh 2.12:11

children.text: * tathā caryāntareṇa tapasā yogaprāptiryathā bhavati tad balaṃ vakṣyāmaḥ // PSBh_2.12:12
children.translated_text: * Likewise, how the attainment of <s>yoga</s> comes about through another [kind of] conduct — through austerity (<s>tapas</s>) — we shall explain that strength. // PSBh 2.12:12
* And we shall explain the means for attaining that strength. // PSBh 2.12:13
* 'One who is joyful and non-negligent' (<s>harṣāpramādī</s>). // PSBh 2.12:14

children.text: * atra harṣo nāma divyeṣu viṣayeṣu vidhānajadharmaprakāśiteṣu prītituṣṭipramodāḥ // PSBh_2.12:15
children.translated_text: * Here, 'joy' (<s>harṣa</s>) means delight (<s>prīti</s>), satisfaction (<s>tuṣṭi</s>), and rapture (<s>pramoda</s>) with regard to divine objects (<s>viṣaya</s>) that are manifested through the <s>dharma</s> born of ritual observance (<s>vidhānaja</s>). // PSBh 2.12:15

children.text: * te tv iha prāptyādiva viśvāmitrādisvarūpā draṣṭavyāḥ // PSBh_2.12:16
children.translated_text: * But here, they should be regarded as having the nature of attainment and the like, like [the joy experienced by] <s>Viśvāmitra</s> and others. // PSBh 2.12:16
* Of what characteristics [is this joy]? // PSBh 2.12:17

children.text: * taducyate kāryakaraṇaviśuddhilakṣaṇāḥ tatra kāryaviśuddhis tāvad yadaitad devaśarīraṃ jvalantaṃ bhāsā dīpyantaṃ divi bhuvyantarikṣe ca rukmadaṇḍavad ucchritamātmānaṃ paśyati tadā divi aṇimā laghimā mahimā iti trayaḥ kāryaguṇā bhavanti // PSBh_2.12:18
children.translated_text: * That is explained: [the <s>harṣas</s> (joys)] are characterized by the purification of effect and instrument. There, first, the purification of effect is: when he sees this divine body, blazing, shining with radiance in heaven, earth, and the atmosphere, raised up like a golden staff — then in heaven, <s>aṇimā</s> (minuteness), <s>laghimā</s> (lightness), and <s>mahimā</s> (greatness) — these three qualities of effect arise. // PSBh 2.12:18
* And in the atmosphere, due to a particular <s>dharma</s> (merit). // PSBh 2.12:19

children.text: * tathā karaṇaviśuddhirapi garimādibhiḥ bāhyairantaḥ karaṇena ca dūraviṣayagrāhakatvālocanasaṃkalpādhyavasāyābhimānādayo bhavanti // PSBh_2.12:20
children.translated_text: * Likewise, the purification of instrument also [arises]: through <s>garimā</s> (heaviness) and the other external [powers], and through the inner instrument — the capacity to grasp distant objects, perception, volition, determination, self-awareness, and so forth arise. // PSBh 2.12:20
* Because of the statement about <s>dharma</s> (merit) and so forth. // PSBh 2.12:22

children.text: * apica prāptiḥ prākāmyam īśitvaṃ vaśitvaṃ ca yatra kāmāvasāyitvamiti pañca karaṇaguṇā bhavanti // PSBh_2.12:23
children.translated_text: * Moreover, <s>prāpti</s> (attainment), <s>prākāmya</s> (irresistible will), <s>īśitva</s> (lordship), <s>vaśitva</s> (subjugation), and <s>yatrakāmāvasāyitva</s> (fulfillment of all desires) — these five qualities of instrument arise. // PSBh 2.12:23

children.text: * ityevaṃ yadanyeṣām aṇimādyaṣṭaguṇaṃ catuḥṣaṣṭivikalpaṃ dharmakāryam aiśvaryaṃ tadiha śāstre harṣa iti saṃjñitam // PSBh_2.12:24
children.translated_text: * Thus, what for others is the eightfold power beginning with <s>aṇimā</s> (minuteness), having sixty-four subdivisions, the sovereignty that is an effect of <s>dharma</s> (merit) — that in this teaching is designated as <s>harṣa</s> (joy). // PSBh 2.12:24

children.text: * teṣu madam akurvan harṣāpramādī bhavati // PSBh_2.12:25
children.translated_text: * Not becoming intoxicated by those, he becomes one who is vigilant regarding <s>harṣa</s> (joy). // PSBh 2.12:25
* The meaning is: through the power of <s>dharma</s> (merit) and knowledge. // PSBh 2.12:26

children.text: * āha kutrasthasya te harṣā abhivyajyante kīdṛśasya vā // PSBh_2.12:27
children.translated_text: * [Objection:] In what state do these <s>harṣas</s> (joys) manifest for him, and of what kind [is he]? // PSBh 2.12:27
* That is explained: // PSBh 2.12:28
In each observance, in each observance. // PS 2.13 //

children.text: * atra caryāyāṃ caryāyām iti vīpsā // PSBh_2.13:1
children.translated_text: * Here, "in each observance, in each observance" is <s>vīpsā</s> (distributive repetition). // PSBh 2.13:1

children.text: * āha anirdeśādiha vīpsā ekavacanadvivacanabahuvacaneṣu bhavati // PSBh_2.13:2
children.translated_text: * [Objection:] Without specification, <s>vīpsā</s> (distributive repetition) here can occur in the singular, dual, and plural. // PSBh 2.13:2
* There, first, it occurs in the singular. // PSBh 2.13:3

children.text: * yasmāduktam / adya te rudhiraṃ tīvraṃ pibāmi puruṣādhama / vadedānīṃ susaṃrabdhaḥ punargauriti gaur iti // PSBh_2.13:4

children.translated_text: * Thus. // PSBh 2.13:5

children.text: * tathā dvivacane'pi bhavati / ubhau dhvajau vātamalau śuśubhāte rathe rathe / saṃrabdhau paramakruddhau yudhi ghnantau parasparam // PSBh_2.13:6
children.translated_text: * Likewise, it also occurs in the dual: "Both banners, wind-soiled, shone on each chariot, the two enraged and supremely furious, striking each other in battle." // PSBh 2.13:6
* Likewise, it also occurs in the plural. // PSBh 2.13:7

children.text: * yasmāduktam / puruṣe puruṣe buddhiḥ sā sā bhavati niścitā / tuṣyanti ca pṛthak sarve te manuṣyāstathā tathā // PSBh_2.13:8
children.translated_text: * Since it has been said: "In each man, each particular conviction of intellect arises; and all those men are separately satisfied in such and such a way." // PSBh 2.13:8
* Hence the doubt. // PSBh 2.13:9

children.text: * ataḥ kimekā cariḥ uta caridvayam uta caribahutvamiti // PSBh_2.13:10
children.translated_text: * Therefore: is it one observance, or a pair of observances, or a multiplicity of observances? // PSBh 2.13:10

children.text: * ucyate ekā cariḥ kriyābahutve'pi bhavati // PSBh_2.13:11
children.translated_text: * It is said: it is one observance, even when there is a multiplicity of actions. // PSBh 2.13:11
* As in the temple and in public. // PSBh 2.13:12

children.text: * tatrāyatane snānahasitādyāḥ loke ca krāthanaspandanādyāḥ vidhikriyāḥ ityevaṃ carikriyātattvaṃ dṛṣṭvā vīpsārthenābhihitaṃ caryāyāṃ caryāyāṃ kriyāyāmityarthaḥ // PSBh_2.13:13
children.translated_text: * There, in the temple, bathing, laughing, and so forth; and in public, <s>krāthana</s> (snoring), <s>spandana</s> (trembling), and so forth are the prescribed actions. Thus, having discerned the true nature of the actions of observance, it is stated with distributive meaning: "in each observance, in each observance" means "in each action" — this is the meaning. // PSBh 2.13:13

children.text: * tasmāt sakṛduccāritā vīpsā bahuvacane'pi bhavati // PSBh_2.13:14
children.translated_text: * Therefore, <s>vīpsā</s> (distributive repetition), though uttered once, also applies to the plural. // PSBh 2.13:14
* Like the offering to a tree. // PSBh 2.13:15

children.text: * kiṃca māhātmyamiti caryottarasambandhāt kathyate ekā cariḥ kriyābahutve bhavati // PSBh_2.13:16
children.translated_text: * Furthermore, since "greatness" is said in connection with what follows the observance, it is stated that it is one observance when there is a multiplicity of actions. // PSBh 2.13:16
* It has been said that the <s>harṣas</s> (joys) are characterized by purification of effect and instrument. // PSBh 2.13:17

children.text: * na ca vibhā kāryakaraṇaiśvaryābhiniveśaḥ śakyate kartumityato'vagamyate kāryakaraṇavataścarato mahimāno'bhivyajyanta ityarthaḥ // PSBh_2.13:18
