children.translated_text: * And since the attachment to the sovereignty of effect and instrument cannot be made manifest without them, it is understood from this that the powers of greatness manifest for the one who practices while possessing effect and instrument — this is the meaning. // PSBh 2.13:18
* [Objection:] What is the accomplishment of effect for one who practices vigilantly? // PSBh 2.13:19
* That is explained: // PSBh 2.13:20
* Since it has been said: "Today I shall drink your fierce blood, O worst of men! Speak now, enraged, again 'cow' and 'cow'!" // PSBh 2.13:4
He attains greatness. // PS 2.14 //
* <s>Māhātmya</s> (greatness) means: noble, as if not manifest. // PSBh 2.14:1

children.text: * taduta yasya sāṃnidhyād ayaṃ brāhmaṇaḥ paridṛṣṭārtho'pi bhūtvā duṣṭāśvatararathasthānīyair dehendriyādibhir apanīyate apahriyate tad amāhātmyam // PSBh_2.14:2
children.translated_text: * Now then, when in whose presence this <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, even though he has discerned the truth, is carried away, dragged off by the body, senses, and so forth — which are like a chariot with vicious mules — that is the absence of greatness. // PSBh 2.14:2
* That is the incapacity for engagement in prescribed practice, the power of <s>adharma</s> (demerit). // PSBh 2.14:3

children.text: * uktaṃ hi / hriyate buddhirmano'pi narasya dehendriyaiḥ / amūḍhasaṃjño durdāntair duṣṭāśvairiva sārathiḥ // PSBh_2.14:4

children.translated_text: * <s>Māhātmya</s> (greatness) is the opposite of that. // PSBh 2.14:5

children.text: * yasya sāṃnidhyād ayaṃ brāhmaṇaḥ snānaśayanānusnānādikrāthanaspandanādhyayanadhyānasmaraṇakaraṇasamartho bhavati parayā śraddhayā yuktas tanmāhātmyam // PSBh_2.14:6
children.translated_text: * When in whose presence this <s>brāhmaṇa</s> becomes capable of bathing, sleeping, post-bathing rites, <s>krāthana</s> (snoring), <s>spandana</s> (trembling), study, meditation, recollection, and action, endowed with supreme faith — that is <s>māhātmya</s> (greatness). // PSBh 2.14:6
* [Objection:] What is that? // PSBh 2.14:7

children.text: * ucyate yadetat prabhraṣṭasya tapaso vīryaṃ tapobalaṃ tapaḥśaktis tanmāhātmyam // PSBh_2.14:8
children.translated_text: * It is said: that which is the vigor of <s>tapas</s> (austerity) that has been cast forth, the power of <s>tapas</s>, the potency of <s>tapas</s> — that is <s>māhātmya</s> (greatness). // PSBh 2.14:8
* How is this known? // PSBh 2.14:9
* Because it is stated immediately after the observance. // PSBh 2.14:10

children.text: * yadanantaraṃ yadavāpnoti tata eva tad āsādayatītyarthaḥ // PSBh_2.14:11
children.translated_text: * What he attains immediately after — from that very [observance] he obtains it, this is the meaning. // PSBh 2.14:11
* [Objection:] Let the reading be "he attains." // PSBh 2.14:12
* It is said: it will belong to the one who has obtained [it]. // PSBh 2.14:13

children.text: * avaramya kṣaṇagatiprītiprāptyarthatvāt tena vidhicaraṇena rakṣate harṣaviśeṣāṇām abhiprītiviśeṣaṇam atigatisaṃstavanāvāptiś ca // PSBh_2.14:14
children.translated_text: * Having paused, because of the purpose of momentary progress, delight, and attainment, through that prescribed practice he protects the distinguishing characteristic of the special delight of the <s>harṣas</s> (joys), and there is the attainment of supreme progress and praise. // PSBh 2.14:14

children.text: * tasmān mantrabalavad dharmabalamevāsya māhātmyam avāpnotītyarthaḥ // PSBh_2.14:15
children.translated_text: * Therefore, like the power of a <s>mantra</s>, the power of <s>dharma</s> (merit) alone is his greatness — "he attains" means this. // PSBh 2.14:15
* [Objection:] What is the means? // PSBh 2.14:16

children.text: * kāni vā tāni dharmasādhanāni yair harṣotpattir māhātmyalābhaśca bhavati // PSBh_2.14:17
children.translated_text: * And what are those instruments of <s>dharma</s> (merit) by which the arising of <s>harṣa</s> (joy) and the attainment of <s>māhātmya</s> (greatness) occur? // PSBh 2.14:17
* Or, how many divisions of the actions of observance are there? // PSBh 2.14:18

children.text: * dānādīnāṃ vā pūrvoktānāṃ viśeṣaṇaṃ kimasti neti // PSBh_2.14:19
children.translated_text: * Or, is there any specification of the previously mentioned giving and so forth, or not? // PSBh 2.14:19
* It is said: there is. // PSBh 2.14:20
* Since he says: // PSBh 2.14:21

* For it has been said: "The intellect and even the mind of a man are carried away by the body and senses, undeluded though he be in awareness, like a charioteer by unruly, wicked horses." // PSBh 2.14:4
Supreme giving, supreme sacrifice. // PS 2.15 //
* Here, inferior gifts are cows, land, gold, precious metal, and so forth. // PSBh 2.15:1
* Why? // PSBh 2.15:2
* Because their fruits are not exclusive, not permanent, and have something superior; and because of the teaching of the wrong path. // PSBh 2.15:3
* Therefore, here the prefix "<s>ati</s>" (supreme) serves as a qualifier. // PSBh 2.15:4
* And <s>atidāna</s> (supreme giving) is the offering of oneself. // PSBh 2.15:5
* Why? // PSBh 2.15:6
* Because the self is the giver, there is no further purpose of giving beyond [giving oneself]. // PSBh 2.15:7
* Because it does not lead to [rebirth in a particular] place, body, senses, objects of experience, and so forth. // PSBh 2.15:8

children.text: * aikāntikātyantikarudrasamīpaprāpter ekāntenaivānāvṛttiphalatvād asādhāraṇaphalatvāc cātmapradānam atidānam // PSBh_2.15:9
children.translated_text: * Because of the exclusive and permanent attainment of proximity to <s>Rudra</s>, because exclusively its fruit is non-return, and because its fruit is unique — the offering of oneself is <s>atidāna</s> (supreme giving). // PSBh 2.15:9
* Likewise, inferior sacrifices are the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> and so forth. // PSBh 2.15:10

children.text: * saṃgrahapratigrahahiṃsādiyuktena śraveṇābhinirvṛttidarśanāt pattrīrātrijadevatādisādhāraṇaphalatvād anityasātiśayasaṃkīrṇaphalatvāc ca kuyajanāny agniṣṭomādīni // PSBh_2.15:12
children.translated_text: * Because [they involve] accumulation, acceptance, violence, and so forth; because their accomplishment is seen through audible recitation; because their fruits are shared in common with birds, night-creatures, and other deities; and because their fruits are impermanent, surpassable, and mixed — the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> and so forth are inferior sacrifices. // PSBh 2.15:12
* Therefore, here the prefix "<s>ati</s>" (supreme) serves as a qualifier. // PSBh 2.15:13

children.text: * atiyajanaṃ nāma yadāyatane loke vā // PSBh_2.15:14
children.translated_text: * <s>Atiyajana</s> (supreme sacrifice) is what is [performed] in the temple and in public. // PSBh 2.15:14

children.text: * tatrāyatane snānahasitādyā loke ca krāthanaspandanādyā vidhikriyā // PSBh_2.15:15
children.translated_text: * There, in the temple: bathing, laughing, and so forth; and in public: <s>krāthana</s> (snoring), <s>spandana</s> (trembling), and so forth are the prescribed actions. // PSBh 2.15:15

children.text: * saṃgrahapratigrahahiṃsādirahitena krameṇa svaśarīrasamutthābhiḥ kāyikavācikamānasikābhirijyate yasmāt // PSBh_2.15:17
children.translated_text: * Because through a method free from accumulation, acceptance, violence, and so forth, one worships with bodily, verbal, and mental [acts] arising from one's own body. // PSBh 2.15:17
* And therefore it is called <s>atiyajana</s> (supreme sacrifice). // PSBh 2.15:18

children.text: * āha kiṃ dānaṃ yajanaṃ ca sādhanadvayam evātrātiśabdena viśiṣṭaṃ kartavyamiti // PSBh_2.15:19
children.translated_text: * [Objection:] Are only giving and sacrifice — these two means — to be performed as qualified by the prefix "<s>ati</s>" (supreme)? // PSBh 2.15:19
* It is said: no. // PSBh 2.15:20
* Since he says: // PSBh 2.15:21
Supreme austerity is likewise practiced. // PS 2.16 //
* The prefix "<s>ati</s>" (supreme) serves as a qualifier. // PSBh 2.16:1

children.text: * nāyāntyādhyātmikādhibhautikādhidaivikās teṣāṃ svaśāstroktena krameṇa manasi saṃmatānāṃ matānām anupāyataḥ pratīkāram akurvatāṃ tapo niṣpadyate // PSBh_2.16:2
children.translated_text: * For those who do not overcome the <s>ādhyātmika</s> (personal), <s>ādhibhautika</s> (elemental), and <s>ādhidaivika</s> (divine) [afflictions], for those who, following the method prescribed in their own scripture, having assented in mind to accepted [practices], do not undertake a remedy without [proper] means — for them, <s>tapas</s> (austerity) is accomplished. // PSBh 2.16:2

children.text: * yatra tṛtīyāyām ātmasaṃyogān niṣpadyate tat tapa ityarthaḥ // PSBh_2.16:3
children.translated_text: * Where, in the third [stage], it is accomplished through connection with the self — that is <s>tapas</s> (austerity), this is the meaning. // PSBh 2.16:3
* Then how [does it apply] to the purpose of sleeping? // PSBh 2.16:4

children.text: * tathātitāpebhyo 'titapo niṣpadyate tathā dānayajanābhyām apīti // PSBh_2.16:5
children.translated_text: * Likewise, from supreme endurance, <s>atitapas</s> (supreme austerity) is accomplished; likewise also from giving and sacrifice. // PSBh 2.16:5
* The word "likewise" serves to summarize the three means. // PSBh 2.16:6

children.text: * yadā dadāti tadā yajati tapyati ca // PSBh_2.16:7
children.translated_text: * When he gives, he also sacrifices and practices austerity. // PSBh 2.16:7

children.text: * yadāpi yajati tadā dadāti tapyati ca // PSBh_2.16:8
children.translated_text: * And when he sacrifices, he also gives and practices austerity. // PSBh 2.16:8

children.text: * yadā tapyati tadā dadāti yajati ca // PSBh_2.16:9
children.translated_text: * When he practices austerity, he also gives and sacrifices. // PSBh 2.16:9
* Thus, beginning from the initiation of this <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, // PSBh 2.16:10

children.text: * ebhis tribhir upāyair gaṅgāsrotovad dharmasyāyo 'dharmasya vyayo bhavati tadātidānādiniṣpannena prakṛṣṭena tapasā asya brāhmaṇasya harṣotpattirmāhātmyalābhaśca sambhavatītyarthaḥ // PSBh_2.16:11
children.translated_text: * through these three means, like the current of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, there is an influx of <s>dharma</s> (merit) and an outflow of <s>adharma</s> (demerit). Then, through the excellent <s>tapas</s> (austerity) accomplished by <s>atidāna</s> (supreme giving) and so forth, the arising of <s>harṣa</s> (joy) and the attainment of <s>māhātmya</s> (greatness) become possible for this <s>brāhmaṇa</s> — this is the meaning. // PSBh 2.16:11

children.text: * āha atidānādiniṣpannena prakṛṣṭena tapasāsya brāhmaṇasya kā gatirbhavatīti // PSBh_2.16:12
children.translated_text: * [Objection:] What destiny does this <s>brāhmaṇa</s> obtain through the excellent <s>tapas</s> accomplished by <s>atidāna</s> (supreme giving) and so forth? // PSBh 2.16:12
* It is said: distinct from worldly prosperity and <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation), // PSBh 2.16:13
He leads [the practitioner] to the supreme destination. // PS 2.17 //
* Here, the prefix "<s>ati</s>" (supreme) serves as a qualifier. // PSBh 2.17:1
* The particle "<s>ā</s>" denotes a limit. // PSBh 2.17:2

children.text: * katham adhyayanadhyānādirahitamapi sādhakaṃ tapo'tigatiṃ gamayati tadabhyāso haratyenam iti vacanāt // PSBh_2.17:3
children.translated_text: * How does <s>tapas</s> (austerity) lead the practitioner to the supreme destination even when devoid of study, meditation, and so forth? Because of the statement: "its practice carries him [to the goal]." // PSBh 2.17:3
* <s>Atigati</s> (supreme destination) is a synonym for <s>yoga</s>. // PSBh 2.17:4
* How is this known? // PSBh 2.17:5
* Because it is an effect of <s>tapas</s> (austerity), like infinity and union with <s>Brahman</s>. // PSBh 2.17:6
* Because it is distinguished from the particular destinations of worldly prosperity and so forth in <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and <s>Yoga</s>, it stands above [them] — this is the meaning. // PSBh 2.17:7

children.text: * tasmāt tapasaḥ phalaṃ viśeṣārthamabhidhīyate yogo'tigatimiti // PSBh_2.17:8
children.translated_text: * Therefore, the fruit of <s>tapas</s> (austerity) is declared for the purpose of distinction: <s>yoga</s> is the <s>atigati</s> (supreme destination). // PSBh 2.17:8
* "<s>Atigati</s> (supreme destination)" is the object [of the verb]. // PSBh 2.17:9
* "He leads." // PSBh 2.17:10

children.text: * na tāvad gataḥ gamiṣyati kiṃtu gamayatītyarthaḥ // PSBh_2.17:11
children.translated_text: * He has not yet gone, nor will he [merely] go in the future, but rather "he leads" — this is the meaning. // PSBh 2.17:11

children.text: * āha atidānād yathāvat tapaso guṇavacanaṃ kimasti neti // PSBh_2.17:12
children.translated_text: * [Objection:] Is there a statement of the quality of <s>tapas</s> (austerity) according to <s>atidāna</s> (supreme giving), or not? // PSBh 2.17:12
* It is said: there is. // PSBh 2.17:13
* Since he says: // PSBh 2.17:14
Therefore. // PS 2.18 //
* Thus. // PSBh 2.18:1
* Here, the word "therefore" describes the quality of <s>tapas</s> (austerity). // PSBh 2.18:2

children.text: * tasmādatidānādiniṣpanno dharmo'tyāgatiṃ gamayate niratiśayāṃ prāpayati // PSBh_2.18:3
children.translated_text: * Therefore, the <s>dharma</s> (merit) accomplished through <s>atidāna</s> (supreme giving) and so forth leads to the <s>atigati</s> (supreme destination), causes one to attain that which has nothing superior. // PSBh 2.18:3
* Not to the attainment of [a particular] place, body, senses, objects of experience, and so forth. // PSBh 2.18:4
* Having seen that the attainment of proximity to <s>Rudra</s> is exclusive and permanent, and that exclusively its fruit is non-return, // PSBh 2.18:5
* therefore he says "therefore." // PSBh 2.18:6

children.text: * āha atyantatapaso guṇavacanaṃ jñātvā kāraṇaṃ ca sādhakena kiṃ kartavyam // PSBh_2.18:7
children.translated_text: * [Objection:] Having known the statement of the quality of supreme <s>tapas</s> (austerity) and its cause, what should the practitioner do? // PSBh 2.18:7
* That is explained: for that very purpose, // PSBh 2.18:8
One should practice austerity further. // PS 2.19 //

children.text: * atra bhūyaḥ punaḥsaṃdhāne draṣṭavyaḥ iṣṭāpūrtavat // PSBh_2.19:1
children.translated_text: * Here, the word "further" should be understood as [indicating] resumption, like <s>iṣṭāpūrta</s> (Vedic and meritorious rites). // PSBh 2.19:1
* How? // PSBh 2.19:2

children.text: * harṣeṣv abhisaktasya muhūrtamardhamuhūrtaṃ vā sādhanebhyo vyucchedaṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃdhāne bhūyaḥśabdo'bhihitaḥ // PSBh_2.19:3
children.translated_text: * Having seen that one who is attached to the <s>harṣas</s> (joys) undergoes interruption from the means of practice for a moment or half a moment, the word "further" is stated for the purpose of resumption. // PSBh 2.19:3
* Therefore, here <s>tapas</s> (austerity) is that very same [as before]. // PSBh 2.19:4
* Its etymology has been stated previously. // PSBh 2.19:5
* "One should practice" conveys accumulation [of merit]. // PSBh 2.19:6

children.text: * dharmānekasaṃśayānyatvāc ca apunarukto'yaṃ caraśabdo draṣṭavyaḥ // PSBh_2.19:7
children.translated_text: * Because <s>dharma</s> (merit) has many [aspects] and because of the [resolution of] doubt and otherness, this word "<s>cara</s>" (practice) should be understood as not being a mere repetition. // PSBh 2.19:7

children.text: * āha yadyevaṃ tasmāducyatāṃ harṣāṇāṃ ko doṣo'bhivyajyate // PSBh_2.19:8
children.translated_text: * He says: if so, then let it be stated — what fault of the pleasures is revealed? // PSBh_2.19:8

children.text: * māhātmyasya vā ko guṇaḥ yasmāt tad grāhyamiti // PSBh_2.19:9
children.translated_text: * Or what virtue of greatness is there, such that it should be accepted? // PSBh_2.19:9
* To that it is said: it produces greatness. // PSBh_2.19:10
* Because he says: // PSBh_2.19:11
But no other devotion than to <s>Śaṃkara</s>. || PS_2.20 ||
* This negative particle 'na' is for the prohibition of devotion to another. // PSBh_2.20:1
* <s>Bhakti</s> means <s>bhāvanā</s> (contemplation) — that is the meaning. // PSBh_2.20:2
* The particle 'tu' is for specification. // PSBh_2.20:3
* How so? // PSBh_2.20:4

children.text: * ye harṣeṣvabhisaktāḥ dūṣyataḥ taskaratvamāpannāḥ te viśeṣeṇa tu śaṃkarād dūrasthā bhavanti // PSBh_2.20:5
children.translated_text: * Those who are attached to pleasures are corrupted, having attained the state of thieves; they in particular are far removed from <s>Śaṃkara</s>. // PSBh_2.20:5
* Why <s>Śaṃkara</s>? // PSBh_2.20:6
* Because he is the maker of all happiness and <s>nirvāṇa</s> (final liberation), he is <s>Śaṃkara</s>. // PSBh_2.20:7
* 'In <s>Śaṃkara</s>' — this is a proximate connection (<s>aupaśleṣika saṃnidhāna</s>). // PSBh_2.20:8

children.text: * śaṃkare bhāvanā kartavyā nānyatrety arthaḥ // PSBh_2.20:9
children.translated_text: * Contemplation is to be directed toward <s>Śaṃkara</s>, not elsewhere — that is the meaning. // PSBh_2.20:9

children.text:
* uktaṃ hi / karmaṇā manasā vācā yad aślakṣṇaṃ niṣevate / tadabhyāso haratyenaṃ tasmāt kalyāṇamācaret // PSBh_2.20:10
* evamete mahātmānaḥ prāhur adhyātmacintakāḥ / yaccittas tanmayo bhāvo guhyametat sanātanam // PSBh_2.20:11
* gacchaṃs tiṣṭhan śayāno vā jāgrac caiva svapaṃstathā / śaṃkare bhāvanāṃ kuryād yadīcched yogamātmanaḥ // PSBh_2.20:12
* yasmāt kṣayānte trailokyaṃ śaṃkare yāti saṃkṣayam / tasmāt saṃvartako dhātā śaṃkarastvabhidhīyate // PSBh_2.20:13
* evaṃ śaṃkare bhāva upaśleṣitavyo nānyatrety arthaḥ // PSBh_2.20:14
children.translated_text: * Thus devotion is to be directed toward <s>Śaṃkara</s>, not elsewhere — that is the meaning. // PSBh_2.20:14

children.text: * evaṃ parisamāptiṃ kṛtvā yuktaṃ vaktum // PSBh_2.20:15
children.translated_text: * Having thus brought this to completion, it is proper to say: // PSBh_2.20:15

* For it has been said: 'Whatever unwholesome thing one pursues by action, mind, or speech — the practice of that carries one away; therefore one should practice what is auspicious.' // PSBh_2.20:10
* 'Thus these great souls, contemplators of the self, have declared: one becomes of the nature of that upon which the mind is fixed — this is the eternal secret.' // PSBh_2.20:11
* 'Whether going, standing, lying down, waking, or sleeping, one should direct contemplation toward <s>Śaṃkara</s>, if one desires <s>yoga</s> for oneself.' // PSBh_2.20:12
* 'Since at the end of dissolution the triple world goes to destruction in <s>Śaṃkara</s>, therefore the creator who brings about dissolution is called <s>Śaṃkara</s>.' // PSBh_2.20:13
Here one should recite this <s>brahman</s> (sacred formula). || PS_2.21 ||
* Thus: // PSBh_2.21:1
* Its meaning has been stated previously. // PSBh_2.21:2

children.text: * āha dharmapariṇāmakatvāt śaṃkaratvāt sukhada īśvaro'bhihitaḥ // PSBh_2.21:3
children.translated_text: * He says: because of being the transformer of <s>dharma</s> and because of being <s>Śaṃkara</s>, the Lord has been described as the giver of happiness. // PSBh_2.21:3

children.text: * athāntarasṛṣṭyāṃ sukhaduḥkhakāraṇaṃ kiṃ bhavati dharmādharmasattvarajovad uta neti // PSBh_2.21:4
children.translated_text: * Now, in the secondary creation, what is the cause of happiness and suffering — is it <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, <s>sattva</s> and <s>rajas</s>, or not? // PSBh_2.21:4

children.text: * ucyate atra ya upāyaḥ sukhadaḥ tathā vakṣyāmaḥ yathāvān yatra vyavasthite saṃsāragate kārye sa eva kāraṇaṃ param // PSBh_2.21:5
children.translated_text: * It is said: here we shall explain the means that gives happiness, just as it is, and where, when the effect involved in <s>saṃsāra</s> is established, that alone is the supreme cause. // PSBh_2.21:5

children.text: * nanu koryakalavan niradhikāras tathā vakṣyāmo vistaraśaś cāsmin brahmaṇi kāraṇaśaktiṃ vakṣyāmaḥ // PSBh_2.21:6
children.translated_text: * Indeed, like one without authority over the aggregate of effects, we shall explain thus, and we shall explain in detail the causal power in this <s>brahman</s>. // PSBh_2.21:6

children.text: * śaktiṃ ca jñātvā yathā sādhako'ṣṭabhir namaskārairātmānaṃ dadāti tathā vakṣyāmaḥ // PSBh_2.21:7
children.translated_text: * And having known the power, we shall explain how the practitioner offers himself through the eight <s>namaskāras</s> (salutations). // PSBh_2.21:7
* Therefore this is commenced. // PSBh_2.21:8

children.text: vāmadevāya namo jyeṣṭhāya namo rudrāya namaḥ || PS_2.22 ||
children.translated_text: Salutation to <s>Vāmadeva</s>, salutation to <s>Jyeṣṭha</s>, salutation to <s>Rudra</s>. || PS_2.22 ||
* Thus: // PSBh_2.22:1

children.text: * prayogānyatvāt prayojanānyatvāc cāpunaruktā vāmadevādiśabdā draṣṭavyāḥ // PSBh_2.22:2
children.translated_text: * Because of the difference in application and difference in purpose, the words <s>Vāmadeva</s> and the rest should be understood as not being repetitions. // PSBh_2.22:2

children.text: * atra vāmatvaṃ devatvaṃ jyeṣṭhatvaṃ rudratvaṃ ca pūrvoktam // PSBh_2.22:3
children.translated_text: * Here the qualities of being <s>Vāma</s> (beautiful/left), being a <s>deva</s> (deity), being <s>Jyeṣṭha</s> (eldest/foremost), and being <s>Rudra</s> have been stated previously. // PSBh_2.22:3
* '<s>Vāmadevāya</s>, <s>Jyeṣṭhāya</s>, <s>Rudrāya</s>' — these are in the dative case. // PSBh_2.22:4
* '<s>Namas</s>' is for self-offering and for worship. // PSBh_2.22:5
* And because of the difference in the conception (of the deity), all the salutations should be understood as not being repetitions. // PSBh_2.22:6

children.text: * āha kiṃ catuṣkamevātra kāraṇe cintyate // PSBh_2.22:7
children.translated_text: * He asks: is only a group of four contemplated here as the cause? // PSBh_2.22:7

children.text: * nāmacatuṣkāpadeśena vā nāmni namaskāro draṣṭavyaḥ // PSBh_2.22:8
children.translated_text: * Or should the salutation be understood as being to the name, by means of the designation of the group of four names? // PSBh_2.22:8
* It is said: no. // PSBh_2.22:9
* Because he says: // PSBh_2.22:10
Salutation to <s>Kāla</s> (Time). || PS_2.23 ||

children.text: * atra kāla ityeṣa maheśvaraparyāyaḥ kasmāt pūrvottarasūtrasāmarthyāt // PSBh_2.23:1
children.translated_text: * Here '<s>Kāla</s>' is a synonym of <s>Maheśvara</s>. Why? Because of the force of the preceding and following <s>sūtras</s>. // PSBh_2.23:1

children.text: * kālayate yasmāt kṣetrasādhiniṣṭhāni sthānāni kalādiśarīrendriyaviṣayādibhyo viyogeneti tataḥ kālaḥ // PSBh_2.23:2
children.translated_text: * Because he drives (<s>kālayate</s>) the stations established in the field-knowers (<s>kṣetrajñas</s>) away from <s>kalā</s> (parts) and the rest — body, senses, objects, and so forth — by separation, therefore he is <s>Kāla</s>. // PSBh_2.23:2
* For it has been said: // PSBh_2.23:3

children.text:
* brahmādibhūrjaparyantaṃ jagad etac carācaram / yataḥ kalayate rudraḥ kālarūpī tataḥ smṛtaḥ // PSBh_2.23:4
* kālyān kalayate yasmāt kalābhyaḥ kālaparyayāt / kalanāt kālanāc cāpi kāla ityabhidhīyate // PSBh_2.23:5

children.translated_text: * Thus <s>Kāla</s> is indeed the Blessed Lord. // PSBh_2.23:6
* The '<s>kālyāḥ</s>' are the <s>kṣetrajñas</s> (field-knowers, i.e. individual souls). // PSBh_2.23:7

children.text: * sthānāni tu brahmendradevapitrādivacanād brāhmaṃ prājāpatyaṃ saumyam aindraṃ gāndharvaṃ yākṣaṃ rākṣasaṃ paiśācamiti // PSBh_2.23:8
children.translated_text: * The 'stations' — from the mention of <s>Brahma</s>, <s>Indra</s>, gods, and ancestors — are: the <s>Brāhma</s> (of <s>Brahmā</s>), <s>Prājāpatya</s> (of <s>Prajāpati</s>), <s>Saumya</s> (of <s>Soma</s>), <s>Aindra</s> (of <s>Indra</s>), <s>Gāndharva</s> (of <s>Gandharvas</s>), <s>Yākṣa</s> (of <s>Yakṣas</s>), <s>Rākṣasa</s> (of <s>Rākṣasas</s>), and <s>Paiśāca</s> (of <s>Piśācas</s>). // PSBh_2.23:8

* Likewise, from the mention of brāhmaṇas, śūdras, cows, deer, and all beings and prepared food, etc., the inclusion of human, animal, deer, bird, reptile, plant, and other stations is understood. // PSBh_2.23:9
* Likewise the lords of <s>yoga</s> are included among the gods. // PSBh_2.23:10
* Because of the abundance of <s>dharma</s>. // PSBh_2.23:12
* Likewise the hell-beings are included among the animals. // PSBh_2.23:13
* Because of the abundance of <s>adharma</s> (demerit). // PSBh_2.23:15
* Thus, based on the stations, <s>saṃsāra</s> is figuratively spoken of as having fourteen divisions. // PSBh_2.23:16
* Among these, from the mention of <s>kalā</s> and the rest, <s>Maheśvara</s> is the instrumental cause. // PSBh_2.23:17
* Because in the previous and subsequent bodies there is merely the manifestation and disappearance of experience. // PSBh_2.23:19
* <s>Saṃsāra</s> should be understood as having a beginning. // PSBh_2.23:20

children.text: * tatphalabhoktṛtvāt kāryakaraṇayor anāditvād anādir akṛtābhyāgamād ityetad bhagavatyabhyadhikatvaṃ śeṣeṣu ca puruṣeṣu nyūnatvaṃ jñātvā yuktaṃ vaktuṃ kālāya namaḥ // PSBh_2.23:21
children.translated_text: * Because he is the experiencer of the fruits thereof; because the effect and instrument are beginningless; because it is beginningless; because there is no acquisition of what was not created — knowing this superiority in the Blessed Lord and inferiority in the remaining beings, it is proper to say: salutation to <s>Kāla</s>. // PSBh_2.23:21
* Here too, '<s>Kālāya</s>' is in the dative case. // PSBh_2.23:22
* '<s>Namas</s>' is for self-offering and for worship. // PSBh_2.23:23
* And because of the difference in the conception, this salutation should be understood as not being a repetition. // PSBh_2.23:24

children.text: * āha atha sthānaśarīrendriyaviṣayādīnāṃ kimeṣa bhagavān prabhuḥ kartā bhavati neti // PSBh_2.23:25
children.translated_text: * He asks: now, is this Blessed Lord the master and maker of the stations, bodies, senses, objects, and so forth, or not? // PSBh_2.23:25
* It is said: he is indeed the master and maker. // PSBh_2.23:26
* Because he says: // PSBh_2.23:27

* 'This entire world of moving and unmoving beings, from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a blade of grass — since <s>Rudra</s> drives it, he is known as having the form of <s>Kāla</s>.' // PSBh_2.23:4
* 'Since he drives the field-knowers, since he impels through the parts (<s>kalās</s>), through the revolution of Time, and because of impelling and destroying, he is called <s>Kāla</s>.' // PSBh_2.23:5
Salutation to <s>Kalavikaraṇa</s> (the Transformer of Parts). || PS_2.24 ||

children.text: * atra kalā nāma kāryakaraṇākhyāḥ kalāḥ // PSBh_2.24:1
children.translated_text: * Here, '<s>kalā</s>' refers to the <s>kalās</s> (parts/categories) known as effects and instruments. // PSBh_2.24:1
* Among these, those known as effects are: earth, water, fire, air, and space. // PSBh_2.24:2
* Space has sound as its quality. // PSBh_2.24:3

children.text: * śabdasparśaguṇo vāyustau ca rūpaṃ ca tejasi / te rasaśca jale jñeyāste ca gandhaḥ kṣitāv api // PSBh_2.24:4

children.translated_text: * Sound, touch, form, taste, and smell. // PSBh_2.24:5

children.text: * tathā karaṇākhyāḥ śrotraṃ tvak cakṣuḥ jihvā ghrāṇaṃ pādaḥ pāyuḥ upasthaḥ hastaḥ vāk manaḥ ahaṃkāraḥ buddhir iti // PSBh_2.24:6
children.translated_text: * Likewise, those known as instruments are: ear, skin, eye, tongue, nose, feet, anus, generative organ, hands, speech, mind, ego (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>), and intellect (<s>buddhi</s>). // PSBh_2.24:6
* The Blessed Lord <s>Īśvara</s> is the transformer of these. // PSBh_2.24:7
* Because his powers of perception and action are unobstructed. // PSBh_2.24:9

children.text: * vikaraṇatvaṃ nāma sthānaśarīrendriyaviṣayādisaṃniveśena vistaravibhāgaviśeṣataśca kāryakaraṇākhyābhiḥ kalābhir dharmajñānavairāgyaiśvaryādharmājñānāvairāgyānaiśvaryādibhiśca kṣetrajñasaṃyojanamityetad bhagavaty abhyadhikatvaṃ śeṣeṣu ca puruṣeṣu nyūnatvaṃ jñātvā yuktaṃ vaktuṃ kalavikaraṇāya namaḥ // PSBh_2.24:10
children.translated_text: * 'Transformership' means: the conjunction of the <s>kṣetrajñas</s> (field-knowers) with the <s>kalās</s> known as effects and instruments — through the arrangement of stations, bodies, senses, objects, and so forth, and through specific distinctions of extent and division — and with <s>dharma</s> (merit), <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion), <s>aiśvarya</s> (sovereignty), <s>adharma</s> (demerit), <s>ajñāna</s> (ignorance), <s>avairāgya</s> (non-dispassion), <s>anaiśvarya</s> (non-sovereignty), and the rest — knowing this superiority in the Blessed Lord and inferiority in the remaining beings, it is proper to say: salutation to <s>Kalavikaraṇa</s>. // PSBh_2.24:10

children.text: * atrāpi kalavikaraṇāya iti caturthī / nama ityātmapradāne pūjāyāṃ ca // PSBh_2.24:11
children.translated_text: * Here too, '<s>Kalavikaraṇāya</s>' is in the dative case. '<s>Namas</s>' is for self-offering and for worship. // PSBh_2.24:11
* And because of the difference in the conception, this word '<s>namaḥ</s>' should be understood as not being a repetition. // PSBh_2.24:12

children.text: * āha kālanavikaraṇatvād avāntarasṛṣṭyāṃ karmakṣaye vṛttilābhe cāpekṣate neti // PSBh_2.24:13
children.translated_text: * He asks: does he, because of being the impeller and transformer, depend on anything in the secondary creation, in the exhaustion of <s>karma</s>, and in the attainment of a livelihood, or not? // PSBh_2.24:13

children.text: * dharmajñānavairāgyaiśvaryādīnāṃ vā kimeṣa bhagavān prabhurbhavati neti // PSBh_2.24:14
children.translated_text: * Or is this Blessed Lord the master of <s>dharma</s>, <s>jñāna</s>, <s>vairāgya</s>, <s>aiśvarya</s>, and the rest, or not? // PSBh_2.24:14
* It is said: he is the master. // PSBh_2.24:15
* Because he says: // PSBh_2.24:16
* Air has the qualities of sound and touch; in fire there are those two plus form; in water, those plus taste are to be known; and in earth, those plus smell as well. // PSBh_2.24:4
Salutation to <s>Balapramathana</s> (the Destroyer of Powers). || PS_2.25 ||

children.text: * balaṃ nāma dharmajñānavairāgyaiśvaryādharmājñānāvairāgyānaiśvaryāṇi icchādveṣaprayatnādīni vidyāvargaḥ rūpāṇi // PSBh_2.25:1
children.translated_text: * '<s>Bala</s>' (power) refers to: <s>dharma</s> (merit), <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion), <s>aiśvarya</s> (sovereignty), <s>adharma</s> (demerit), <s>ajñāna</s> (ignorance), <s>avairāgya</s> (non-dispassion), <s>anaiśvarya</s> (non-sovereignty); desire, aversion, effort, and the rest; the <s>vidyā</s>-group (category of knowledge); and forms. // PSBh_2.25:1

children.text: * pra iti bhṛśārthe kāmitvākarṣaṇe ca // PSBh_2.25:2
children.translated_text: * The prefix 'pra' is used in the sense of intensity and forceful drawing. // PSBh_2.25:2
* 'Churning' (<s>mathana</s>) means the suppression of the activity of powers, like the churning of the ocean. // PSBh_2.25:3
* It is not that fire, knowledge, and the rest are weak. // PSBh_2.25:4

children.text: * yasmāduktam / na hy atejasvināśāya taijasāḥ prabhavanti vai / balānyatibalānyasya na bhave'tibalāni vai // PSBh_2.25:5
* ityevaṃ bhagavatyabhyadhikatvaṃ śeṣeṣu puruṣeṣu nyūnatvaṃ jñātvā yuktaṃ vaktuṃ balapramathanāya namaḥ // PSBh_2.25:6
children.translated_text: * Thus, knowing this superiority in the Blessed Lord and inferiority in the remaining beings, it is proper to say: salutation to <s>Balapramathana</s>. // PSBh_2.25:6
* Here too, '<s>Balapramathanāya</s>' is in the dative case. // PSBh_2.25:7
* '<s>Namas</s>' is for self-offering and for worship. // PSBh_2.25:8
* And because of the difference in the conception, this salutation should be understood as not being a repetition. // PSBh_2.25:9
* He asks: upon whom does he perform the impelling, transforming, and churning? // PSBh_2.25:10
* To that it is said: upon beings. // PSBh_2.25:11
* Because he says: // PSBh_2.25:12

* Because it has been said: 'Indeed, luminous things do not have the power to destroy one who is not luminous; his powers are exceedingly powerful, and they would not be exceedingly powerful in [ordinary] existence.' // PSBh_2.25:5
Salutation to <s>Sarvabhūtadamana</s> (the Subduer of All Beings). || PS_2.26 ||

children.text: * atra kalāvacane punaruktidoṣān na pṛthivyādiṣu sarvaśabdaḥ // PSBh_2.26:1
children.translated_text: * Here, because of the fault of repetition with the mention of <s>kalā</s> (parts), the word 'sarva' (all) does not refer to earth and the other elements. // PSBh_2.26:1

children.text: * kiṃ tu siddheśvaravarjaṃ cetaneṣveva sarvabhūtaśabdaḥ // PSBh_2.26:2
children.translated_text: * Rather, the word '<s>sarvabhūta</s>' (all beings) refers only to sentient beings, excluding the perfected lords (<s>siddheśvaras</s>). // PSBh_2.26:2
* He objects: the word '<s>sarvabhūta</s>' cannot refer to sentient beings, because the term '<s>bhūta</s>' does not apply to them. // PSBh_2.26:3
* To that it is said: [it is explained by] '<s>damanāya</s>' (for subduing). // PSBh_2.26:4
* '<s>Śam</s>' and '<s>dam</s>' are used in the sense of pacification. // PSBh_2.26:5

children.text: * devamanuṣyādīnāṃ sthānaśarīrendriyaviṣayādiṣu yā ratiḥ rañjanādhivāsanā tatsarvam antaradṛṣṭyā sarvamīśvarakṛtameva draṣṭavyamityetad bhagavatyabhyadhikatvaṃ śeṣeṣu ca puruṣeṣu nyūnatvaṃ jñātvā yuktaṃ vaktuṃ sarvabhūtadamanāya namaḥ // PSBh_2.26:6
children.translated_text: * The attachment and delight and habitual impression of gods, humans, and others toward stations, bodies, senses, objects, and so forth — all of that, by inner vision, should be seen as entirely the work of <s>Īśvara</s> — knowing this superiority in the Blessed Lord and inferiority in the remaining beings, it is proper to say: salutation to <s>Sarvabhūtadamana</s>. // PSBh_2.26:6
* Here too, '<s>Sarvabhūtadamanāya</s>' is in the dative case. // PSBh_2.26:7
* '<s>Namas</s>' is for self-offering and for worship. // PSBh_2.26:8
* And because of the difference in the conception, this salutation should be understood as not being a repetition. // PSBh_2.26:9

children.text: * āha kīdṛśe maheśvare kālanādiśaktirucyate kiṃ sakale niṣkale uta ubhayorapi // PSBh_2.26:10
children.translated_text: * He asks: in what kind of <s>Maheśvara</s> is the power of impelling and the rest said to reside — in the one with parts (<s>sakala</s>), in the one without parts (<s>niṣkala</s>), or in both? // PSBh_2.26:10
* It is said: in both. // PSBh_2.26:11
* Because he says: // PSBh_2.26:12
Salutation to <s>Mano'mana</s> (the Mind of the Mind / Beyond Mind). || PS_2.27 ||

children.text: * atra manaḥśabdenāntaḥkaraṇaṃ tattantratvād udāharaṇārthatvāc ca manograhaṇasya ubhayātmakatvāc ca manasaḥ sarvakaraṇagrahaṇānugrahaṇāc ca kāryagrahaṇamityataḥ kāryakaraṇādhiṣṭhātṛtvāc ca sakala ityupacaryate // PSBh_2.27:1
children.translated_text: * Here, by the word '<s>manas</s>' (mind) the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) is meant, because it is dependent on that, because the mention of mind serves as an illustration, because the mind has a twofold nature, and because the mention of mind implies the grasping and favoring of all instruments — therefore, because of being the presiding lord over effects and instruments, he is figuratively called '<s>sakala</s>' (with parts). // PSBh_2.27:1

children.text: * tathā caitādṛśamanasaḥ pratiṣedhādatra kāryakaraṇarahito niṣkalo bhagavān amana ityucyate // PSBh_2.27:2
children.translated_text: * Likewise, because of the negation of such a mind, the Blessed Lord, devoid of effects and instruments, without parts (<s>niṣkala</s>), is called '<s>amana</s>' (beyond mind). // PSBh_2.27:2
* Therefore, the beginningless power that favors both the one with parts and the other exists. // PSBh_2.27:3

children.text: * uktaṃ hi / apāṇipādodarapārśvajihvaḥ atīndriyo vyāpisvabhāvasiddhaḥ / paśyaty acakṣuḥ sa śṛṇotyakarṇo na cāstyabuddhaṃ na ca buddhirasti / sa vetti sarvaṃ na ca tasyāsti vettā tamāhuragryaṃ puruṣaṃ mahāntam // PSBh_2.27:4
* ityetad bhagavatyabhyadhikatvaṃ śeṣeṣu ca nyūnatvaṃ ca jñātvā yuktaṃ vaktuṃ mano'manāya namaḥ // PSBh_2.27:5
children.translated_text: * Thus, having known this superiority in the Blessed One and the inferiority in the rest, it is proper to say: 'Homage to the one whose mind is beyond mind (<s>mano'manā</s>).' [PSBh 2.27:5]
* '<s>Mano'manāya</s>' — [this is] a dative case. [PSBh 2.27:6]
* '<s>Namu</s>' (homage) is in the sense of self-offering and worship. [PSBh 2.27:7]

children.text: * sambhāvanānyatvāc cāpunaruktāḥ sarve namaḥśabdā draṣṭavyāḥ // PSBh_2.27:8
children.translated_text: * And because of the difference in the object of honor, all the words <s>namaḥ</s> (homage) should be understood as non-repetitive. [PSBh 2.27:8]

* For it has been said: 'Without hands, feet, belly, sides, or tongue; beyond the senses; pervading; self-established in nature; he sees without eyes, he hears without ears; there is nothing unknown to him, yet there is no knower of him — they call him the foremost, the great <s>Puruṣa</s>.' // PSBh_2.27:4
<s>Pāśupatasūtra</s>, [Chapter] 3
One whose mark is unmanifest. [PS 3.1]
* Thus: [PSBh 3.1:1]
* Here the prefix 'a-' negates the manifestness of the mark. [PSBh 3.1:2]

children.text: * avasitaprayojanaḥ pūrvoktair liṅgopakaraṇair anusnānanirmālyaikavāsādyaiḥ prayojanair vinivṛttair lokatas triṣu snānaṃ kurvannapi // PSBh_3.1:3
children.translated_text: * When the purpose has been accomplished, and the previously mentioned purposes of the marks and accessories — re-bathing, discarded offerings, single garment, and so forth — have ceased, even though he still performs the triple daily bathing from [the perspective of] the world, [PSBh 3.1:3]
* the marks of the six <s>āśramas</s> being imperceptible and the previously stated mark being unascertained — the practices should be performed in an unmanifest manner. [PSBh 3.1:4]

children.text: * āha kayā vā maryādayā kasmin vā kāle sā kriyā kartavyā // PSBh_3.1:5
children.translated_text: * He asks: by what rule and at what time should that practice be performed? [PSBh 3.1:5]
* That is stated: [PSBh 3.1:6]
One whose conduct is manifest. [PS 3.2]
* Here the word 'manifest' (<s>vyakta</s>) refers to daytime. [PSBh 3.2:1]
* 'Manifest' means clear, bright, luminous. [PSBh 3.2:2]
* The meaning is: during the day. [PSBh 3.2:3]
* The prefix <s>ā</s> indicates the limit of the accomplishment of dishonor and so forth. [PSBh 3.2:4]
* '<s>Cāra</s>' (conduct) is a designation for <s>krāthana</s> (snoring/groaning) and the rest. [PSBh 3.2:5]

children.text: * tān krāthanādīn sādhako naṭadavasthito raṅgaval laukikānadhijanya nāṭakavad ācārānācarati karoti prayuṅkta ityato'yaṃ vyaktācāraḥ // PSBh_3.2:6
children.translated_text: * The practitioner, situated like an actor, on a stage as it were, having learned these [behaviors] — <s>krāthana</s> and the rest — from worldly [observation], performs, executes, and employs them like a theatrical performance; therefore he is called one 'whose conduct is manifest.' [PSBh 3.2:6]

children.text: * āha avyaktaliṅgino vyaktācārasya kā kāryaniṣpattiḥ // PSBh_3.2:7
children.translated_text: * He asks: what is the result accomplished for one whose mark is unmanifest but whose conduct is manifest? [PSBh 3.2:7]
* The answer is: dishonor. [PSBh 3.2:8]
* Because [the sūtra] states: [PSBh 3.2:9]
Despised. [PS 3.3]
* Here <s>ava</s> [means] avoidance. [PSBh 3.3:1]

children.text: * mānena teṣāṃ liṅgācārajñānavidhiviparītapravṛttiṃ dṛṣṭvā sarvadoṣaduṣṭo'yamiti mānasādhenāvamāne yo janaḥ parivarjayatānyato 'yamabahumatatvaṃ prāpnoti // PSBh_3.3:2
children.translated_text: * When people, seeing his conduct contrary to the proper procedures of marks, conduct, and knowledge, [think] 'this one is corrupted by all faults' — through that mental disdain, the person who avoids [him] causes this one to attain the state of being disregarded. [PSBh 3.3:2]
* And it has been said: [PSBh 3.3:3]

children.text:
* amṛtasyeva lipseta naiva mānaṃ vicakṣaṇaḥ / viṣasyeva jugupseta sanmānasya sadā dvijaḥ // PSBh_3.3:4
* sukhaṃ hy avamataḥ śete sarvasaṅgavivarjitaḥ / doṣān parasya na dhyāyet tasya pāpaṃ sadā muniḥ // PSBh_3.3:5

children.translated_text: * He asks: among whom should one with an unmanifest mark, manifest conduct, be despised? [PSBh 3.3:6]
* That is stated: [PSBh 3.3:7]

* 'As if seeking nectar, the wise one should always seek dishonor; as if loathing poison, the twice-born should always [loathe] honor.' [PSBh 3.3:4] 'One who is despised sleeps happily, free from all attachments. The sage should not dwell on the faults of others — [for] the sin is always his [who does so].' [PSBh 3.3:5]
Among all beings. [PS 3.4]
* Here the expression 'all beings' should be understood as referring to those belonging to the <s>varṇas</s> (classes) and <s>āśramas</s> (stages of life). [PSBh 3.4:1]
* Why is it said 'among those of the <s>varṇas</s> and <s>āśramas</s>'? [PSBh 3.4:2]
* Because 'among beings' is said, not among gods, animals, <s>mlecchas</s>, and such. [PSBh 3.4:3]
* Why? [PSBh 3.4:4]
* Because it would contradict the giving and receiving of dishonor through manifest conduct. [PSBh 3.4:5]

children.text: * uktaṃ hi / dhanyo deśo yatra gāvaḥ prabhūtāḥ medhyaṃ cānnaṃ pārthivā dharmaśīlāḥ / puṇyā nadyaḥ sarvalokopabhogyās tāṃs tān deśānsiddhikāmo vrajeta // PSBh_3.4:6

children.translated_text: * 'Among beings' (<s>bhūteṣu</s>) indicates proximate presence. [PSBh 3.4:7]
* In the proximity of beings, in the vicinity of beings, in the presence of beings — this is the meaning. [PSBh 3.4:8]
* Through the explanation of proximity, the practice of this method [becomes possible] because the place of dishonor and so forth is made clearer. [PSBh 3.4:9]
* And because of the indication of practice 'among the <s>asuras</s>.' [PSBh 3.4:10]

children.text: * āha avamatena sarvabhūteṣu kiṃ kartavyam // PSBh_3.4:11
children.translated_text: * He asks: what should be done by one who is despised among all beings? [PSBh 3.4:11]
* The answer is: one should wander about. [PSBh 3.4:12]
* Because [the sūtra] states: [PSBh 3.4:13]

* For it has been said: 'Blessed is the land where cattle are abundant, food is pure, the rulers are righteous, the rivers are holy and enjoyed by all people — one who desires perfection should go to such lands.' [PSBh 3.4:6]
Being abused, one should wander about. [PS 3.5]
* Here <s>pari</s> [means] 'on all sides.' [PSBh 3.5:1]
* They are to be examined on all sides — this is the meaning. [PSBh 3.5:2]
* <s>Bhūya</s> means 'in many ways.' [PSBh 3.5:3]
* Being struck with sticks, fists, and such — that is <s>paribhava</s> (abuse). [PSBh 3.5:4]
* The meaning is: physical [abuse]. [PSBh 3.5:5]
* '<s>Māna</s>' refers to the practitioner's designation of the time and action. [PSBh 3.5:6]
* While being abused. [PSBh 3.5:7]

children.text: * sa paribhavo daridrapuruṣarājābhiṣeka iva draṣṭavyaḥ // PSBh_3.5:8
children.translated_text: * That abuse should be seen like the royal consecration of a poor man. [PSBh 3.5:8]
* One should be like a touchstone or like <s>Indra</s>'s post (<s>indrakīlaka</s>). [PSBh 3.5:9]
* 'One should wander' (<s>caret</s>) refers to acquiring. [PSBh 3.5:10]

children.text: * dharmārjane niyoge ca nindita iti garhitābhyākhyāne caritavyamityarthaḥ // PSBh_3.5:11
children.translated_text: * In the injunction for acquiring <s>dharma</s>, and when censured — in the state of being reviled — one should wander about; this is the meaning. [PSBh 3.5:11]

children.text: * āha avamatasya paribhūyamānasyācarataḥ kiṃ tāpaśāntireva uta śuddhir apyasti // PSBh_3.5:12
children.translated_text: * He asks: for one who is despised and abused while wandering about, is there only the quelling of torment, or is there also purification? [PSBh 3.5:12]
* The answer is: there is. [PSBh 3.5:13]
* Because [the sūtra] states: [PSBh 3.5:14]
One whose sins are destroyed. [PS 3.6]
* 'He becomes' is the completion of the sentence, understood from the context of the statement. [PSBh 3.6:1]

children.text: * atra apa varjane āghāte nāśe ca // PSBh_3.6:2
children.translated_text: * Here <s>apa</s> [is used in the senses of] removal, striking, and destruction. [PSBh 3.6:2]
* 'Destroyed' (<s>apahatā</s>) means destroyed by [transfer to] another — this is the meaning. [PSBh 3.6:3]
* The sins (<s>pāpmānas</s>) here are of two kinds: those characterized by pleasure and those characterized by suffering. [PSBh 3.6:4]

children.text: * tatra sukhalakṣaṇāḥ unmādaḥ madaḥ mohaḥ nidrā ālasyaṃ koṇatā aliṅgaḥ nityamasadvāditvaṃ bahubhojanamityevamādyāḥ // PSBh_3.6:5
children.translated_text: * Of these, those characterized by pleasure are: frenzy, intoxication, delusion, sleepiness, laziness, crookedness, being without a mark, always speaking untruthfully, overeating — and so forth. [PSBh 3.6:5]
* Likewise, those characterized by suffering are: headache, toothache, eye disease, and so forth. [PSBh 3.6:6]

children.text: * evamete pāpmāna ātmagatāḥ kāyakaraṇeṣv ādarśapratirūpakavadabhivyaktāḥ // PSBh_3.6:7
children.translated_text: * Thus these sins, residing in the self, are manifested in the body and instruments like reflections in a mirror. [PSBh 3.6:7]

children.text: * kṛtsnāḥ apahatāḥ pāpmānaḥ so 'yamapahatapāpmā bhavatītyarthaḥ // PSBh_3.6:8
children.translated_text: * All sins being destroyed — he becomes one whose sins are destroyed (<s>apahatapāpmā</s>); this is the meaning. [PSBh 3.6:8]

children.text: * āha kimavamānaḥ paribhavaśca kāyikaṃ mānasaṃ sādhanadvayamevāsya pāpakṣayaśuddhihetuḥ āhosvid vācikamapyasti neti // PSBh_3.6:9
children.translated_text: * He asks: are dishonor and abuse — the twofold means, physical and mental — the sole cause of his destruction of sin and purification? Or is there also a verbal [means]? [PSBh 3.6:9]
* The answer is: because [the sūtra] states: [PSBh 3.6:10]
From the reviling of others. [PS 3.7]

children.text: * atra parā nāma svaparasamayādhikṛtā ye avamānādibhiḥ saṃyojayanti teṣām // PSBh_3.7:1
children.translated_text: * Here, 'others' (<s>para</s>) means those who are established in their own and others' doctrines — those who subject [him] to dishonor and such. [PSBh 3.7:1]
* 'Of others' (<s>pareṣām</s>) — genitive plural. [PSBh 3.7:2]

children.text: * āha svaparavākyāvamānādibhiḥ śuddhirevāsya na tu vṛddhiḥ // PSBh_3.7:3
children.translated_text: * He objects: through the dishonor of one's own and others' words, there is only purification for him, but not growth [of merit]. [PSBh 3.7:3]

children.text: * sā ca sādhakasya phalābhidhānād atidānādiṣvityucyate na pūrvakṛtasukṛtadānavivakṣayā // PSBh_3.7:4
children.translated_text: * And that [growth], because of the statement of the fruit for the practitioner, is spoken of in connection with excessive giving and so forth — not with the intention of speaking about giving away previously accumulated merit. [PSBh 3.7:4]
* <s>Pari</s> is in the sense of 'on all sides.' [PSBh 3.7:5]
* <s>Vada</s> — speech, abuse. [PSBh 3.7:6]

children.text: * avyakto'yaṃ preto'yam unmatto'yaṃ mūḍho'yaṃ mūrkho'yaṃ nidrāviṣṭo vāyuruddho'yaṃ duṣkāmy asamyakkārī asamyagvādī ityevamugrairvacobhir abhighnantīti vādāḥ // PSBh_3.7:7
children.translated_text: * 'This one is unmanifest, this one is a ghost, this one is mad, this one is deluded, this one is a fool, this one is overcome by sleep, this one is possessed by wind, this one has evil desires, this one acts wrongly, this one speaks wrongly' — striking with such harsh words are the abuses (<s>vādas</s>). [PSBh 3.7:7]
* 'From the reviling' (<s>vādāt</s>) — this should be seen as an ablative of cause. [PSBh 3.7:8]

children.text: * tasmādavamānādibhiḥ parān saṃyojayatā svayamevātmā saṃyoktavyaḥ // PSBh_3.7:9
children.translated_text: * Therefore, by one who subjects others to dishonor and such, one should connect oneself [with those abuses] — [PSBh 3.7:9]
* otherwise one would be a mere <s>pāśa</s> (bond). [PSBh 3.7:10]
* Or there is doubt because of the indication of the class of sins. [PSBh 3.7:11]
* Whose effect are the sins? [PSBh 3.7:12]

children.text: * kathaṃ vā teṣāṃ kāryakaraṇeṣvabhivyaktānāṃ parasamutthairavamānādibhirnirghātanaṃ bhavati // PSBh_3.7:13
children.translated_text: * And how are those [sins], manifested in body and instruments, driven out by dishonor and such produced by others? [PSBh 3.7:13]
* That is stated: [PSBh 3.7:14]
* Because [the sūtra] states: [PSBh 3.7:15]
And he gives sin to them. [PS 3.8]
* Here, 'sin' (<s>pāpa</s>) is a synonym for <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness). [PSBh 3.8:1]

children.text: * tadyathā / āgo'parāgo musalaṃ duritaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ tarūn / pāpaṃ pāpmānaṃ vṛjinaṃ steyam // PSBh_3.8:2

children.translated_text: * these are words having the same meaning. [PSBh 3.8:3]
* And here [in the sūtra] 'sin' (<s>pāpa</s>) is used. [PSBh 3.8:4]
* And why [is it called] <s>pāpa</s>? [PSBh 3.8:5]
* Because of purifying, causing to fall, and binding — [it is called] <s>pāpa</s>. [PSBh 3.8:6]

children.text: * pāvayati yasmāt śirorogadantarogākṣirogādibhiḥ pātayati narakādiṣu pāsayati vāniṣṭābhiḥ kāryakaraṇākhyābhiḥ kalābhiriti // PSBh_3.8:7
children.translated_text: * Because it purifies [i.e., burns], because it causes to fall into hells and such through headache, toothache, eye disease, and so forth, and because it binds with the undesirable faculties called effects and instruments — [PSBh 3.8:7]
* therefore, because of purifying, causing to fall, and binding, [it is called] <s>pāpa</s>. [PSBh 3.8:8]

children.text: * evaṃca bījāṅkuravat pāpapāpmanāṃ hetuhetumattvopanayo draṣṭavyaḥ // PSBh_3.8:9
children.translated_text: * And thus, like seed and sprout, the relationship of cause and effect between sin (<s>pāpa</s>) and sinful afflictions (<s>pāpman</s>) should be understood. [PSBh 3.8:9]
* The sinful afflictions are born from the seed of sin — this is the meaning. [PSBh 3.8:10]
* 'To them' (<s>tebhyaḥ</s>) — [this] dative is in the sense of the recipient. [PSBh 3.8:11]

children.text: * atha evamavamānādibhiḥ saṃyojayanti tebhyo dadāti prayacchati saṃkrāmayatītyarthaḥ // PSBh_3.8:12
children.translated_text: * Thus, to those who subject [him] to dishonor and such, he gives, offers, transfers [his sin] — this is the meaning. [PSBh 3.8:12]

children.text: * āha kimavamānādibhiḥ śuddhirevāsya na tu vṛddhiriti // PSBh_3.8:13
children.translated_text: * He asks: through dishonor and such, is there only purification for him, but not growth [of merit]? [PSBh 3.8:13]
* The answer is: there is also growth. [PSBh 3.8:14]
* Because [the sūtra] states: [PSBh 3.8:15]
* As follows: guilt, offense, pestle, evil fortune, misdeed, wickedness, sin, sinful state, crookedness, theft — [PSBh 3.8:2]
And he takes the merit from them. [PS 3.9]
* Here <s>su</s> is in the sense of praise. [PSBh 3.9:1]
* '<s>Kṛta</s>' (done) is a synonym for <s>dharma</s>. [PSBh 3.9:2]
* The word <s>ca</s> is for the purpose of accumulation with purification, and for the purpose of the injunction of the preceding <s>dharma</s>. [PSBh 3.9:3]
* 'Of them' (<s>teṣām</s>) — [PSBh 3.9:4]
* of those who subject [him] to dishonor and such — this is the meaning. [PSBh 3.9:5]
* 'Of them' — the genitive case is for the purpose of indicating the taking of the entirety of what is not [yet] manifest. [PSBh 3.9:6]
* 'He takes' (<s>ādatte</s>) — [PSBh 3.9:7]
* <s>Ā</s> [is used] in the sense of grasping. [PSBh 3.9:8]

children.text: * svātmani karoti viṣamaṃ vā ihāturavadityarthaḥ // PSBh_3.9:9
children.translated_text: * He makes [it his] own, or [takes it] unevenly, like a sick person here — this is the meaning. [PSBh 3.9:9]

children.text: * āha atidānādyatitapovad avamānādisādhanaṃ guṇavacanaṃ kimasti neti // PSBh_3.9:10
children.translated_text: * He asks: is there a statement of the quality of the means [consisting of] dishonor and such, like [the statements about] excessive giving and excessive austerity, or not? [PSBh 3.9:10]
* The answer is: there is. [PSBh 3.9:11]
* Because [the sūtra] states: [PSBh 3.9:12]
Therefore. [PS 3.10]
* How? [PSBh 3.10:2]

children.text: * yasmādavamānādibhiḥ pāpapāpmanāṃ kṣaye śuddhiḥ sukṛtādāne ca vṛddhirbhavati // PSBh_3.10:3
children.translated_text: * Because through dishonor and such there is purification by the destruction of sin and sinful afflictions, and growth through the taking of merit. [PSBh 3.10:3]

children.text: * yasmāc ca tanniṣṭhālaukikaśarīrendriyaviṣayādiprāpakaḥ aikāntikātyantikarudrasamīpaprāptir ekāntenātyantikī bhavati // PSBh_3.10:4
children.translated_text: * And because [this practice], culminating in that [result], leads to extraordinary bodies, senses, objects, and so forth — the absolute and final proximity to <s>Rudra</s> becomes definitively and permanently [established]. [PSBh 3.10:4]
* Therefore he says 'therefore' (<s>tasmāt</s>). [PSBh 3.10:5]
* He asks: now, should only this practice of dishonor and such be performed? [PSBh 3.10:6]
* Or should one wander about only in the unmanifest state? [PSBh 3.10:7]
* The answer is: no. [PSBh 3.10:8]
* Because [the sūtra] states: [PSBh 3.10:9]
* Thus: here the word 'therefore' (<s>tasmāt</s>) is a statement of the quality of the means [consisting of] dishonor and such. [PSBh 3.10:1]
One should wander like a ghost. [PS 3.11]

children.text: * atra puruṣākhyaḥ pretaḥ na mṛtākhyaḥ // PSBh_3.11:1
children.translated_text: * Here 'ghost' (<s>preta</s>) means a [living] person, not a dead one. [PSBh 3.11:1]
* Why? [PSBh 3.11:2]
* Because of the teaching of conduct [for a living being]. [PSBh 3.11:3]
* <s>Vat</s> indicates a partial resemblance. [PSBh 3.11:4]

* One should be like a madman, like a poor person, like one who has bathed [but whose] limbs are smeared with dirt, bearing grown-out beard, nails, and body hair, devoid of all purificatory rites. [PSBh 3.11:5]
* From this arise the cutting off of <s>varṇa</s> (class) and <s>āśrama</s> (stage), and the enthusiasm of dispassion. [PSBh 3.11:6]
* And the accomplishment of purpose occurs — [namely] dishonor and so forth. [PSBh 3.11:7]
* 'One should wander' (<s>caret</s>) refers to a command. [PSBh 3.11:8]
* In the injunction for acquiring <s>dharma</s>. [PSBh 3.11:9]
* And because of the difference in context, this word <s>cara</s> (wander) should be understood as non-repetitive. [PSBh 3.11:10]
* He asks: what are the specific practices for one who thus wanders? [PSBh 3.11:11]
* And what is the result accomplished? [PSBh 3.11:12]
* Or what is the elaboration of the conducts? [PSBh 3.11:13]
* That is stated: [PSBh 3.11:14]
One should snore/groan, or — [PS 3.12]

children.text: * atra yadā prāptajñānaḥ kṣīṇakaluṣaśca kṛtābhyanujñaḥ tadā ācāryasakāśān niṣkramyāgatya pratyagāraṃ nagaraṃ vā praviśya yatra laukikānāṃ samūhastatra teṣāṃ nātidūre nātisaṃnikarṣe yatra ca teṣāṃ noparodho dṛṣṭinipātaśca bhavati tatra hastyaśvarathapadātīnāṃ panthānaṃ varjayitvopaviśya nidrāliṅgaśiraścalitajṛmbhikādīni prayoktavyāni // PSBh_3.12:1
children.translated_text: * Here, when [the practitioner] has attained knowledge, his impurity has been destroyed, and he has received permission [from the teacher], then departing from the teacher's presence, he should enter a village or town, and wherever there is a gathering of worldly people, not too far from them and not too near, where there is no obstruction [to them] but where their gaze may fall, avoiding the paths of elephants, horses, chariots, and infantry, he should sit down and employ [the signs of] sleep — such as drooping of the head, nodding, yawning, and the like. // PSBh 3.12:1
* There indeed, though not asleep, he should behave as if asleep. // PSBh 3.12:2

children.text: * tataḥ prāṇarecanasya vāyoḥ kaṇṭhadeśe purupuruśabdaḥ kartavyaḥ // PSBh_3.12:3
children.translated_text: * Then, with the exhaled breath, he should make a 'puru-puru' sound in the throat region. // PSBh 3.12:3

children.text: * tataste manasā vā vācā vā nidrāviṣṭo'yamiti laukikāḥ prapadyante paribhavanti ca // PSBh_3.12:4
children.translated_text: * Then the worldly people, mentally or verbally, conclude 'this one is overcome by sleep' and treat him with contempt. // PSBh 3.12:4

children.text: * anenānṛtābhiyogenāsya yat teṣāṃ sukṛtaṃ tadāgacchati // PSBh_3.12:5
children.translated_text: * Through this false attribution (<s>anṛtābhiyoga</s>), whatever merit is theirs comes to him. // PSBh 3.12:5

children.text: * asyāpi ca yat pāpaṃ tat tān prati // PSBh_3.12:6
children.translated_text: * And whatever sin is his goes to them. // PSBh 3.12:6
* Thus, 'snoring' (<s>krāthana</s>) is the practice. // PSBh 3.12:7

children.text: * ita ity abhiyajana ājñāyāṃ niyoge ca // PSBh_3.12:8
children.translated_text: * 'Ita' [indicates] the practice of acquiring [merit], in the sense of command and injunction. // PSBh 3.12:8
* The word 'or' (<s>vā</s>) should be understood as distinguishing between snoring, trembling, and the like. // PSBh 3.12:9

children.text: * āha avibhaktābhidhānādeva krāthanaspandanādīnāṃ vibhāgasiddhiḥ hasitādivat // PSBh_3.12:10
children.translated_text: * He says: From the undivided statement itself, the distinction of snoring, trembling, and the like is established — like laughing and the like. // PSBh 3.12:10
* Why is the future tense used? // PSBh 3.12:11

children.text: * ucyate pṛthagabhidhāne satyapi hasitagītanṛtyavat saṃdehaḥ // PSBh_3.12:12
children.translated_text: * It is said: Even though there is a separate statement, there is doubt, like laughing, singing, and dancing. // PSBh 3.12:12

children.text: * pṛthagabhidhāne satyapi hasitagītayoḥ pṛthak pṛthak prayogaḥ // PSBh_3.12:13
children.translated_text: * Even though there is a separate statement, laughing and singing have separate application. // PSBh 3.12:13
* But here, singing and dancing are distinguished. // PSBh 3.12:14
* And so are study and restraint. // PSBh 3.12:15

children.text: * tasmāt pṛthagabhidhānamanurato vā vibhāge bhavatānyadoṣaḥ // PSBh_3.12:16
children.translated_text: * Therefore, whether by a separate statement or by delighting in the distinction — if otherwise, there would be a fault. // PSBh 3.12:16

children.text: * tataḥ krāthanakriyayāvamānādiṣu niṣpanneṣu krāthanādi saṃsṛṣṭaṃ samutsṛjya śīghramutthātavyam // PSBh_3.12:17
children.translated_text: * Then, when the contempt and the like have been accomplished through the snoring practice, one should abandon the snoring and the like, mixed [with other behaviors], and quickly rise up, // PSBh 3.12:17

children.text: * yathā laukikānāṃ sampratyayo bhavati kimapyanena svapnāntare bhayaṃ dṛṣṭamiti // PSBh_3.12:18
children.translated_text: * so that the worldly people believe 'this one has seen something frightening in a dream.' // PSBh 3.12:18
* Therefore, having risen, one should cause some limb — head, hand, or the like — to tremble. // PSBh 3.12:19
* Since he says: // PSBh 3.12:20
Or one should tremble — || PS 3.13 ||
* Here, 'trembling' (<s>spandana</s>) governs knowledge and desire. // PSBh 3.13:1
* Why? // PSBh 3.13:2
* Because the body-parts should be caused to tremble with [prior] knowledge, desire, and effort. // PSBh 3.13:3

children.text: * draṣṭāro hi vāyusaṃsṛṣṭo 'yamiti laukikāḥ pratipadyante paribhavanti ca // PSBh_3.13:4
children.translated_text: * For the onlookers, the worldly people, conclude 'this one is afflicted by wind [disease]' and treat him with contempt. // PSBh 3.13:4

children.text: * anenānṛtābhiyogenāsya tatpuṇyamāgacchati asyāpi ca yat pāpaṃ tān gacchati // PSBh_3.13:5
children.translated_text: * Through this false attribution, their merit comes to him, and whatever sin is his goes to them. // PSBh 3.13:5
* Thus, 'trembling' (<s>spandana</s>) is the practice. // PSBh 3.13:6

children.text: * ita ity abhiyajana ājñāyāṃ niyoge ca // PSBh_3.13:7
children.translated_text: * 'Ita' [indicates] the practice of acquiring [merit], in the sense of command and injunction. // PSBh 3.13:7

children.text: * evamādisādhane sati vā vikalpe raudrībahurūpīvat // PSBh_3.13:8
children.translated_text: * In such initial practices, 'or' indicates an option, like [the choice between] <s>Raudrī</s> and <s>Bahurūpī</s>. // PSBh 3.13:8
* The word 'or' should be understood in the distinction between staying still, snoring, rising, trembling, and the like. // PSBh 3.13:9

children.text: * āha abhiprasthitasya dharmasādhanaṃ kimasti neti // PSBh_3.13:10
children.translated_text: * He asks: For one who has set out, is there a means of acquiring merit or not? // PSBh 3.13:10
* It is said: There is. // PSBh 3.13:11
* Since he says: // PSBh 3.13:12
Or one should limp — || PS 3.14 ||
* 'Or' (<s>vā</s>) governs lameness of the foot. // PSBh 3.14:1

children.text: * maṇṭane ca prayukte vaktāro vadantyupahatam asya pādendriyam // PSBh_3.14:2
children.translated_text: * And when limping is employed, speakers say: 'His foot-faculty is impaired.' // PSBh 3.14:2

children.text: * kṛtsnasyāśubhasya ca vṛttir asmiñcharīre upalabhyate // PSBh_3.14:3
children.translated_text: * 'And the function of all inauspiciousness is perceived in this body.' // PSBh 3.14:3

children.text: * uktaṃ hi / dāridryaṃ vyādhibhūyiṣṭhatā mūrkhatvaṃ cārūpatā bhraṃśatāpi / dehotpattirvarṇahīne kule vā pratyādeśaḥ karmaṇāṃ duṣkṛtānām // PSBh_3.14:4
* draṣṭāro hi upahatapāda iti prapadyante paribhavanti ca // PSBh_3.14:5
children.translated_text: * For the onlookers conclude 'this one has an impaired foot' and treat him with contempt. // PSBh 3.14:5

children.text: * anenānṛtābhiyogena yat teṣāṃ sukṛtaṃ tadasyāgacchati // PSBh_3.14:6
children.translated_text: * Through this false attribution, whatever merit is theirs comes to him. // PSBh 3.14:6

children.text: * asyāpi ca yat pāpaṃ tān gacchati // PSBh_3.14:7
children.translated_text: * And whatever sin is his goes to them. // PSBh 3.14:7
* Thus, 'limping' (<s>maṇṭana</s>) is the practice. // PSBh 3.14:8

children.text: * ita ityabhiyajane ājñāyāṃ niyoge ca // PSBh_3.14:9
children.translated_text: * 'Ita' [indicates] the practice of acquiring [merit], in the sense of command and injunction. // PSBh 3.14:9
* The word 'or' should be understood in the distinction between snoring, trembling, limping, and the like. // PSBh 3.14:10
* He asks: Is there a means of acquiring merit in [the presence of] women? // PSBh 3.14:11
* It is said: There is. // PSBh 3.14:12
* Since he says: // PSBh 3.14:13
* For it has been said: 'Poverty, being prone to illness, stupidity, ugliness, degradation, birth in a low-caste family — [these are] the retribution of evil deeds.' // PSBh 3.14:4
Or one should act amorously — || PS 3.15 ||
* Here, 'amorous behavior' (<s>śṛṅgāraṇa</s>) governs the display of emotional expression. // PSBh 3.15:1
* How? // PSBh 3.15:2

children.text: * strījanasamūhasyānuparodhe nātidūre nātisaṃnikarṣe adhidṛṣṭinipāte sthitvaikāṃ rūpayauvanasampannāṃ striyam adhikṛtyālocanasaṃkalpādhyavasāyābhimānādayaḥ prayoktavyāḥ // PSBh_3.15:3
children.translated_text: * Without obstructing the group of women, not too far and not too near, standing within the range of [their] gaze, one should select a single woman endowed with beauty and youth, and employ glancing, resolve, determination, self-conceit, and the like. // PSBh 3.15:3

children.text: * ayuktā cecchāvaloke hi sati keśasaṃyamanādīni kāmaliṅgāni prayoktavyāni // PSBh_3.15:4
children.translated_text: * And when there is improper desire in the gaze, the signs of passion such as smoothing the hair and the like should be employed. // PSBh 3.15:4

children.text: * tataḥ strīpuṃnapuṃsakādayo vaktāro vadantyabrahmacārī kāmyayamiti // PSBh_3.15:5
children.translated_text: * Then speakers — women, men, and eunuchs — say: 'This one is not a celibate; he desires [that woman].' // PSBh 3.15:5

children.text: * anenānṛtābhiyogenāsya yat teṣāṃ sukṛtaṃ tadāgacchati asyāpi yat pāpaṃ tat teṣāṃ gacchatyeva // PSBh_3.15:6
children.translated_text: * Through this false attribution, whatever merit is theirs comes to him, and whatever sin is his goes to them indeed. // PSBh 3.15:6
* 'Amorous behavior' (<s>śṛṅgāraṇa</s>) is the practice. // PSBh 3.15:7

children.text: * ita ityabhiyajane ājñāyāṃ niyoge ca vāśabdaḥ krāthanaspandanamaṇṭanaśṛṅgāraṇādikriyāntarāṇāṃ vikalpe // PSBh_3.15:8
children.translated_text: * 'Ita' [indicates] the practice of acquiring [merit], in the sense of command and injunction. The word 'or' indicates the option among the various practices — snoring, trembling, limping, amorous behavior, and other practices. // PSBh 3.15:8
* And because the practices are different, this word 'or' is not redundant. // PSBh 3.15:9

children.text: * āha krāthanādikriyācatuṣkaṃ yasya nāsti tasya sāmānyatvāt // PSBh_3.15:10
children.translated_text: * He says: For one who does not have the four practices beginning with snoring, [the merit-transfer operates] in a general way, // PSBh 3.15:10

children.text: * uktaṃ hi / ye hi vai dīkṣitaṃ yajamānaṃ pṛṣṭhato'pavadanti te tasya pāpmānamabhivrajanti // PSBh_3.15:11

children.translated_text: * '[Speaking ill] from behind, from the front, and from the side' should be applied. // PSBh 3.15:12

children.text: * tasmāt krātheta vā spandeta vā maṇṭeta vā śṛṅgāreta vā // PSBh_3.15:13
children.translated_text: * Therefore, one should snore, or tremble, or limp, or act amorously. // PSBh 3.15:13
* Because [these practices] are distinguished by the special [merit of] excessive worship (<s>atiyajana</s>) and the like. // PSBh 3.15:15

* Because of the word of the omniscient one, and because [the teaching] is not inconsistent with [its] purpose — there is no worldly acceptance [of these practices, yet they are valid]. // PSBh 3.15:17
* He asks: Should only these four practices be performed here? // PSBh 3.15:18
* It is said: No. // PSBh 3.15:19
* Since he says: // PSBh 3.15:20
* for it has been said: 'Those who speak ill behind [the back of] a consecrated sacrificer take upon themselves his sin.' // PSBh 3.15:11
One should also do that [improper action] — || PS 3.16 ||
* Here, the word 'also' (<s>api</s>) indicates the accumulation of all practices beginning with snoring. // PSBh 3.16:1
* 'That' (<s>tad</s>) indicates indeterminacy. // PSBh 3.16:2
* 'Should do' (<s>kuryāt</s>) governs the skillful behavior of amusement. // PSBh 3.16:3

children.text: * yamānāmavirodhināṃ śuvirūpakāṇāṃ dravyāṇāṃ kāṣṭhaloṣṭādīnāṃ grahaṇadhāraṇasaṃsparśanādīni kartavyāni // PSBh_3.16:4
children.translated_text: * The grasping, holding, and touching of objects that do not contradict the restraints (<s>yama</s>) — [objects that are] misshapen, deformed — [and of] substances such as sticks, clods of earth, and the like — should be performed. // PSBh 3.16:4

children.text: * tataste vaktāro vadanti asamyakkārī śucyaśucyoḥ kāryākāryayor avibhāgajña iti // PSBh_3.16:5
children.translated_text: * Then those speakers say: 'This one acts improperly, he does not know the difference between pure and impure, between what should and should not be done.' // PSBh 3.16:5
* Through this false attribution, the purification of his <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> through abandonment and acquisition occurs. // PSBh 3.16:6
* He asks: Should only these five practices be performed here? // PSBh 3.16:7
* To that it is said: No. // PSBh 3.16:8
* Since he says: // PSBh 3.16:9
One should also speak that [improper speech] — || PS 3.17 ||
* Here, the word 'also' (<s>api</s>) suggests the possibility of employing the function of all the senses. // PSBh 3.17:1
* 'That' (<s>tad</s>) indicates indeterminacy. // PSBh 3.17:2
* 'Should speak' (<s>bhāṣet</s>) governs the function of speech. // PSBh 3.17:3

children.text: * itpadam apārthakaṃ punaruktaṃ vyāhataṃ bhāṣitavyamiti // PSBh_3.17:4
children.translated_text: * One should speak meaningless, redundant, and contradictory [words]. // PSBh 3.17:4

children.text: * tataste vaktāro vadanti asamyagvādī vācyāvācyayor avibhāgajña iti // PSBh_3.17:5
children.translated_text: * Then those speakers say: 'This one speaks improperly, he does not know the difference between what should and should not be said.' // PSBh 3.17:5
* Through this false attribution, the purification of his <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> through renunciation and acquisition occurs. // PSBh 3.17:6

children.text: * āha kiṃ hasitādivad yathāpāṭhakrameṇaiva krāthanādayaḥ prayoktavyāḥ // PSBh_3.17:7
children.translated_text: * He asks: Should the [practices] beginning with snoring be employed in the order of the text, like laughing and the like? // PSBh 3.17:7
* Or, what is the purpose to be accomplished? // PSBh 3.17:8
* To that it is said: For the purpose of accomplishing contempt and the like. // PSBh 3.17:9
* Since he says: // PSBh 3.17:10
By which one should incur contempt — || PS 3.18 ||

children.text: * atra yacchabdaḥ atikrāntāpekṣaṇe vīpsāyāṃ ca // PSBh_3.18:1
children.translated_text: * Here, the relative pronoun 'which' (<s>yat</s>) refers to the foregoing and [indicates] distribution. // PSBh 3.18:1
* 'Contempt' (<s>paribhava</s>) has been explained above. // PSBh 3.18:2
* 'Should incur' — that is, disgrace, contempt, and verbal abuse should be obtained; this is the meaning. // PSBh 3.18:3

children.text: * evamatra vyaktācārasamāsoktānāṃ krāthanādīnāmācārāṇāṃ vistaravibhāgaviśeṣopasaṃhārādayaś ca vyākhyātā ityarthaḥ // PSBh_3.18:4
children.translated_text: * Thus, here the expansion, distinction, specification, and conclusion of the manifest practices beginning with snoring, described in condensed [sūtra] form, have been explained — this is the meaning. // PSBh 3.18:4

children.text: * āha kiyantaṃ kālaṃ paribhavādayaḥ prāptavyāḥ // PSBh_3.18:5
children.translated_text: * He asks: For how long should contempt and the like be endured? // PSBh 3.18:5
* Or, by what kind [of person]? // PSBh 3.18:6
* To that it is said: // PSBh 3.18:7

children.text: paribhūyamāno hi vidvān kṛtsnatapā bhavati || PS_3.19 ||
children.translated_text: For one who is being treated with contempt, the wise one becomes one of complete austerity (<s>kṛtsnatapas</s>) — || PS 3.19 ||
* Here, 'pari' [indicates] totality on all sides. // PSBh 3.19:1
* 'Being [treated with contempt]' — multiple instances of disgrace and the like should be endured. // PSBh 3.19:2
* 'Honor' (<s>māna</s>) — its meaning has been stated above. // PSBh 3.19:3
* The word 'for' (<s>hi</s>) [indicates] the excellence of complete austerity. // PSBh 3.19:4
* It should be understood as implying excellence. // PSBh 3.19:5

children.text: * vidyā nāma yā granthārthavartipadārthānām abhivyañjikā vipratvalakṣaṇā // PSBh_3.19:6
children.translated_text: * 'Knowledge' (<s>vidyā</s>) is that which illuminates the meanings of the topics that form the content of the text, characterized by <s>vipratva</s> (learned scholarship). // PSBh 3.19:6

children.text: * nyāyāt padārthānām adhigatapratyayo lābhamalopāyābhijñaḥ vidvānityucyate // PSBh_3.19:7
children.translated_text: * One who, through reasoning, has ascertained the meanings of the topics and knows the means of obtaining [merit] and of preventing loss — such a one is called 'learned' (<s>vidvān</s>). // PSBh 3.19:7

children.text: * kṛtsnamiti prayogaprāptau paryāptimadhikurute na tu harṣādiprāptāv ityarthaḥ // PSBh_3.19:8
children.translated_text: * 'Complete' (<s>kṛtsna</s>) governs the sufficiency of application, not [merely] the attainment of joy and the like — this is the meaning. // PSBh 3.19:8
* 'One of complete austerity' (<s>kṛtsnatapas</s>) means one of sufficient austerity, a [fully qualified] practitioner — this is the meaning. // PSBh 3.19:9
* 'Becomes' (<s>bhavati</s>) is a statement of established fact — without doubt. // PSBh 3.19:10

children.text: * yadā yamaniyameṣu dṛḍho bhūtvā krāthanādīn prayuṅkte tadā kṛtsnatapā bhavati // PSBh_3.19:11
children.translated_text: * When, having become firm in the restraints (<s>yama</s>) and observances (<s>niyama</s>), one employs the [practices] beginning with snoring — then one becomes one of complete austerity. // PSBh 3.19:11
* The characteristic of complete austerity is to be known through direct perception of the self (<s>ātmapratyakṣa</s>). // PSBh 3.19:12
* Thus, having concluded the chapter, it is proper to state: // PSBh 3.19:13
Here one should recite this <s>Brahman</s> [mantra] — || PS 3.20 ||
* Thus. // PSBh 3.20:1
* Its meaning has been stated above. // PSBh 3.20:2
* But what then is that <s>Brahman</s>? // PSBh 3.20:3
* To that it is said: // PSBh 3.20:4
From the non-terrible ones (<s>Aghora</s>) — || PS 3.21 ||

children.text: * athavā brahmaṇā saha brahmasambandho bhavati // PSBh_3.21:1
children.translated_text: * Alternatively, through [the mantra] <s>Brahman</s>, connection with <s>Brahman</s> occurs. // PSBh 3.21:1
* How? // PSBh 3.21:2
* By the apprehension of mind, the objects are devoid of form and the like. // PSBh 3.21:3

children.text: * kiṃ tāni surūpāṇi salakṣaṇāni vilakṣaṇāni uta salakṣaṇavilakṣaṇānīti // PSBh_3.21:4
children.translated_text: * Are they beautiful, well-characterized, ill-characterized, or both well- and ill-characterized? // PSBh 3.21:4

children.text: * kiṃ parimitāni uta aparimitāni uta parimitāparimitāni // PSBh_3.21:5
children.translated_text: * Are they finite, or infinite, or both finite and infinite? // PSBh 3.21:5

children.text: * ucyate kāraṇatvabahutvenoktasya bhagavato rūpanānātvaṃ vailakṣaṇyāvailakṣaṇyaṃ parimitāparimitatvaṃ cocyate aghorebhyaḥ // PSBh_3.21:6
children.translated_text: * It is said: Because of the multiplicity of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s causality as previously stated, the diversity of forms, the [quality of being] both distinctive and non-distinctive, and the [quality of being] both finite and infinite is expressed [by the mantra] '<s>Aghora</s>' (from the non-terrible ones). // PSBh 3.21:6
* The prefix 'a' negates the terribleness (<s>ghoratva</s>) of the forms. // PSBh 3.21:7
* '<s>Aghora</s>' means supremely peaceful, bestowing grace — this is the meaning. // PSBh 3.21:8
* 'From these' (<s>ebhyaḥ</s>) means from the innumerable, uncountable [forms] — this is the meaning. // PSBh 3.21:9

children.text: * āha kimetānyeva ebhya eva vā // PSBh_3.21:10
children.translated_text: * He asks: Are these the only ones, or from these only? // PSBh 3.21:10
* To that it is said: No. // PSBh 3.21:11
* Since he says: // PSBh 3.21:12
And from the terrible ones (<s>Ghora</s>) — || PS 3.22 ||

children.text: * atra athaśabdo ghorarūpopādhiko draṣṭavyaḥ ghorāṇi aśivāni aśāntāni ananugrahakārīṇītyarthaḥ // PSBh_3.22:1
children.translated_text: * Here, the word 'now' (<s>atha</s>) should be understood as qualified by the terrible forms (<s>ghorarūpa</s>) — 'terrible' means inauspicious, unpeaceful, not producing grace — this is the meaning. // PSBh 3.22:1
* 'From these' (<s>ebhyaḥ</s>) means from unlimited and uncounted [forms] — this is the meaning. // PSBh 3.22:2

children.text: * āha kimetānyeva dvisaṃsthānasaṃsthebhya eva vā // PSBh_3.22:3
children.translated_text: * He asks: Are these [forms] themselves [in question], or [only those] that are established in [the category of] two configurations? // PSBh 3.22:3
* It is said — because he states: // PSBh 3.22:4
And from those more terrible than the terrible (<s>ghoraghoratara</s>). || PS 3.23 ||

children.text: * atra ghora ityetad bhagavato nāmadheyam // PSBh_3.23:1
children.translated_text: * Here, '<s>Ghora</s>' (the Terrible) is a name of the Blessed Lord. // PSBh 3.23:1
* The second word '<s>ghora</s>' should be understood as applying to the forms. // PSBh 3.23:2
* '<s>Tara</s>' is used in the sense of distinction [i.e., comparative degree]. // PSBh 3.23:3
* Like '<s>śāntatara</s>' (more peaceful) and the like. // PSBh 3.23:4

children.text: * tebhyo ghorebhyo 'ghorebhyaśca yānyanyāni paśūnāṃ sammohakarāṇi tāni ghoratarāṇītyarthaḥ // PSBh_3.23:5
children.translated_text: * From those terrible and non-terrible [forms] — those others that cause delusion (<s>sammoha</s>) in the bound souls (<s>paśu</s>) are called 'more terrible' (<s>ghoratara</s>) — this is the meaning. // PSBh 3.23:5
* 'From these' (<s>ebhyaḥ</s>) means from unlimited and uncounted [forms] — this is the meaning. // PSBh 3.23:6
* The word '<s>ca</s>' (and) should be understood as concluding [the discussion of] the terrible and non-terrible forms. // PSBh 3.23:7
* These forms are of three classes only, not others — this is the meaning. // PSBh 3.23:8
* He asks: From what does he create those forms? // PSBh 3.23:9
* Or where do they abide? // PSBh 3.23:10
* To that it is said: // PSBh 3.23:11
From all [things]. || PS 3.24 ||
* Here, [the word 'all' refers to] those that are the causes of form-creation. // PSBh 3.24:1
* Why 'all-ness'? // PSBh 3.24:2
* Because of the fault that there would be no space anywhere — like two <s>badarī</s>-fruits on the tip of a needle. // PSBh 3.24:3
* Rather, because the power of the cause is unobstructed. // PSBh 3.24:4
* They [exist] everywhere — this is the meaning. // PSBh 3.24:5

children.text: * āha rūpakaraṇe karaṇeṣvasyāpratighāta iti kva siddham // PSBh_3.24:6
children.translated_text: * He asks: Where is it established that his [power] is unobstructed in his instruments for creating forms? // PSBh 3.24:6
* To that it is said: here [in this system]. // PSBh 3.24:7
* Because he states: // PSBh 3.24:8
<s>Śarva</s>, from all [things]. || PS 3.25 ||

children.text: * atra śarva ityetad bhagavato nāmadheyam // PSBh_3.25:1
children.translated_text: * Here, '<s>Śarva</s>' is a name of the Blessed Lord. // PSBh 3.25:1
* Why [is he called] '<s>Śarva</s>'? // PSBh 3.25:2
* Because of being the shelter (<s>śaraṇa</s>) of effects such as knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>) and the like, he is called '<s>Śarva</s>.' // PSBh 3.25:3
* All effects such as knowledge and the like abide in <s>Rudra</s>. // PSBh 3.25:4
* And the Blessed One is the impeller (<s>codaka</s>) in all things, as the cause, everywhere. // PSBh 3.25:5

children.text: * sarvaśabdaḥ trisaṃkhyeṣvapi eṣu niravaśeṣavācī draṣṭavyaḥ // PSBh_3.25:6
children.translated_text: * The word 'all' (<s>sarva</s>) should be understood as a comprehensive term without remainder, applying to these [forms] of three classes as well. // PSBh 3.25:6
* 'From these' (<s>ebhyaḥ</s>) means from unlimited and uncounted [forms] — this is the meaning. // PSBh 3.25:7

children.text: * āha athaitāṃ rūpavibhūtiṃ jñātvā sādhakena kiṃ kartavyam // PSBh_3.25:8
children.translated_text: * He asks: Now, having known this manifestation of forms (<s>rūpavibhūti</s>), what should the practitioner (<s>sādhaka</s>) do? // PSBh 3.25:8
* To that it is said: // PSBh 3.25:9
Obeisance to you, to the forms of <s>Rudra</s>! || PS 3.26 ||

children.text: * atra nama ityātmaprayukta ityarthaḥ te iti kāraṇāpadeśe // PSBh_3.26:1
children.translated_text: * Here, '<s>namas</s>' (obeisance) means 'offered by oneself' — this is the meaning. 'To you' (<s>te</s>) indicates the cause. // PSBh 3.26:1
* 'Obeisance to you' — <s>namaste</s>. // PSBh 3.26:2
* Or alternatively, having offered oneself through obeisance, they desire the acquisition of an accumulation of <s>dharma</s>. // PSBh 3.26:3
* Now, what is this acquisition? // PSBh 3.26:4
* To that it is said: Through the acquisition of the distinguished [Lord]. // PSBh 3.26:5
* To that it is said: here '<s>Rudra</s>' indicates the cause. // PSBh 3.26:6
* The <s>Rudra</s>-nature of <s>Rudra</s> has been stated previously. // PSBh 3.26:7

children.text: * rūpāṇi yāni śarīrāṇyutpādayati tebhyo rūpebhya ityarthaḥ // PSBh_3.26:8
children.translated_text: * The forms (<s>rūpa</s>) that he produces as bodies (<s>śarīra</s>) — 'to those forms' — this is the meaning. // PSBh 3.26:8

children.text: * atra rūpavyapadeśena rūpiṇi namaskāro draṣṭavyaḥ // PSBh_3.26:9
children.translated_text: * Here, through the designation of 'forms,' the obeisance should be understood as directed to the form-possessor (<s>rūpin</s>). // PSBh 3.26:9
* Because of the application of the intention directed toward him. // PSBh 3.26:11
* Like the worship (<s>upasthāna</s>) at [the abode of] <s>Śiva</s>. // PSBh 3.26:12
* 'From these' (<s>ebhyaḥ</s>) — // PSBh 3.26:13
* means from unlimited and uncounted [forms] — this is the meaning. // PSBh 3.26:14

children.text: * rūpanirdeśārthānyatvāc ca punaruktāpunaruktābhyāṃ śabdā draṣṭavyāḥ // PSBh_3.26:15
