children.translated_text: * And because the purpose is to indicate the forms, and because of the difference [in meaning], the words should be understood as both repetition and non-repetition. // PSBh 3.26:15
<s>Pāśupatasūtra</s>, Chapter 4
The concealed knowledge (<s>gūḍhavidyā</s>) shines forth for the infinity of austerity (<s>tapas</s>). || PS 4.1 ||
* '<s>Guhū</s>' [is used] in the sense of protecting. // PSBh 4.1:1
* It should be protected, not revealed — this is the meaning. // PSBh 4.1:2
* Concealment (<s>gopana</s>) means non-revelation. // PSBh 4.1:3
* Knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>), as previously stated, illuminates both oneself and others — like a lamp. // PSBh 4.1:4
* The knowledge established in the practitioner (<s>sādhaka</s>) should be concealed by [external] marks (<s>liṅga</s>) — this is the meaning. // PSBh 4.1:5

children.text: * āha gūḍhavidye sādhake kā kāryaniṣpattiḥ // PSBh_4.1:6
children.translated_text: * He asks: What effect is produced in the practitioner whose knowledge is concealed? // PSBh 4.1:6

children.text: * taducyate tapaānantyāya prakāśate ityeṣa pāṭhaḥ // PSBh_4.1:7
children.translated_text: * To that it is said: 'It shines forth for the infinity of austerity (<s>tapas</s>)' — this is the reading. // PSBh 4.1:7

children.text: * athavā kuravonmahitavat tapo'nantyāya prakāśata ityeṣa vā pāṭhaḥ // PSBh_4.1:8
children.translated_text: * Or alternatively, like [the reading in the] <s>Kuru</s> [recension] with elevation: 'It shines forth for the infinity of austerity' — this is also a [variant] reading. // PSBh 4.1:8
* Therefore, here, austerity (<s>tapas</s>) is the same [as mentioned before]. // PSBh 4.1:9
* Its etymology has been stated previously. // PSBh 4.1:10
* '<s>An</s>' is also understood as a synonym for injunction. // PSBh 4.1:11
* Because of being an effect of austerity (<s>tapas</s>) — like the transcendent attainment (<s>atigati</s>) and union (<s>sāyujya</s>). // PSBh 4.1:12

children.text: * āha kiṃ parimiteṣvartheṣvānantyaśabdaḥ utāparimiteṣu kiṃ vā parimitāparimiteṣviti // PSBh_4.1:13
children.translated_text: * He asks: Does the word 'infinity' (<s>ānantya</s>) apply to limited objects, or to unlimited objects, or to both limited and unlimited objects? // PSBh 4.1:13
* It is said: The word 'infinity' applies to both limited and unlimited objects. // PSBh 4.1:14

children.text: * tatra tāvad īśvarasyaikaikaśaḥ parimiteṣu teṣveva vibhutvād aparimiteṣu tathā parimitāparimiteṣvartheṣu abhivyaktāsya śaktiḥ // PSBh_4.1:15
children.translated_text: * There, first, the power of the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>) is manifest individually in those limited [objects], and because of all-pervasiveness in those same [objects which are thereby] unlimited — thus in both limited and unlimited objects. // PSBh 4.1:15
* The word 'infinity' applies to his [power over] wholesome and unwholesome states. // PSBh 4.1:16

children.text: * yasmāduktaṃ na caitāstanavaḥ kevalaṃ mama iti // PSBh_4.1:17
children.translated_text: * Because it has been said: 'And these are not my bodies alone.' // PSBh 4.1:17

children.text:
* tathā rudraḥ samudro hi ananto bhāskaro nabhaḥ / ātmā brahma ca vāk caiva na śakyaṃ bhedadarśanam // PSBh_4.1:18
* anātmavidbhiradhyastāṃ paṅktiṃ yojanamāyatām / vedavit punate pārtha niyuktaḥ paṅktimūrdhani // PSBh_4.1:19
* tathā ca vedavit paṅktimātmavit punate dvijaḥ / ānantyaṃ punate vidvān nābhātvaṃ yo na paśyati // PSBh_4.1:20
* ānantyāya iti caturthī tasmāt tapa etat na tu vidyā kāryā // PSBh_4.1:21
children.translated_text: * 'For infinity' (<s>ānantyāya</s>) — the dative case [indicates purpose]. Therefore, this is austerity, not knowledge, that should be practised. // PSBh 4.1:21

children.text: * prakāśo nāma bhāvaprakāśyam na tu pradīpavat // PSBh_4.1:22
children.translated_text: * 'Shining forth' (<s>prakāśa</s>) means the illumination of [inner] states (<s>bhāva</s>) — but not like a lamp. // PSBh 4.1:22
* How? // PSBh 4.1:23

children.text: * yogādhikṛtasya pradīpasthānītayamānaijasthānīyam āvārakam abhibhūya prakāśate // PSBh_4.1:24
children.translated_text: * For one established in <s>yoga</s>, like a lamp overcoming darkness — [knowledge], which stands in the place of the radiant [faculty], overpowers the obscuring [factor] and shines forth. // PSBh 4.1:24

children.text: * cakṣuḥsthānīyayā vidyayā kuśalavivekādikāryaṃ māhātmyātigatiprakāśapravṛttismṛtisāyujyasthityādiprakāśanaṃ tapaḥkāryamityarthaḥ evaṃ ca gupte brāhmaṇe tapa ānantyāya prakāśata ityarthaḥ // PSBh_4.1:25
children.translated_text: * Through knowledge, which stands in the place of the eye, the effects such as the discernment of the wholesome and the like — [namely] greatness (<s>māhātmya</s>), transcendent attainment (<s>atigati</s>), illumination (<s>prakāśa</s>), activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>), memory (<s>smṛti</s>), union (<s>sāyujya</s>), stability (<s>sthiti</s>), and the like — are the effect of austerity — this is the meaning. Thus, for the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> in whom [knowledge] is concealed, austerity shines forth unto infinity — this is the meaning. // PSBh 4.1:25

children.text: * āha svabhāvaguptatvād atīndriyātmagatī vidyā gopyeti // PSBh_4.1:26
children.translated_text: * He asks: Since knowledge is by its very nature concealed — being supersensory (<s>atīndriya</s>) and pertaining to the self — knowledge should [naturally] be concealed. // PSBh 4.1:26
* To that it is said: It should be concealed by marks (<s>liṅga</s>) such as the conditions of being unmanifest, appearing dead, and the like — this is the meaning. // PSBh 4.1:27

children.text: * āha kāni punastāni vidyāliṅgāni yair guptair vidyā guptā bhavati // PSBh_4.1:28
children.translated_text: * He asks: What then are those marks of knowledge by which, when concealed, knowledge becomes concealed? // PSBh 4.1:28
* To that it is said: Observances (<s>vrata</s>) and the like. // PSBh 4.1:29
* Because he states: // PSBh 4.1:30

* Likewise: '<s>Rudra</s> is the ocean, infinite, radiant, and the sky; the self (<s>ātman</s>), <s>Brahman</s>, and speech — distinction among them cannot be perceived.' 'A row extending a <s>yojana</s>, superimposed by those who do not know the self — the knower of the <s>Vedas</s>, O <s>Pārtha</s>, purifies [that row] when placed at its head.' 'Likewise, the <s>Veda</s>-knower purifies a row, the self-knower purifies [further], the wise one who does not perceive non-selfhood purifies unto infinity.' // PSBh 4.1:18-20
One whose observance is concealed (<s>gūḍhavrata</s>). || PS 4.2 ||
* Here, 'concealed' (<s>gūḍha</s>) means hidden, covered, unrevealed — this is the meaning. // PSBh 4.2:1

children.text: * vrataṃ nāma yadāyatane snānahasitādyaḥ sādhanavargastad vratam // PSBh_4.2:2
children.translated_text: * 'Observance' (<s>vrata</s>) means the class of practices such as bathing in the sanctuary, laughter, and the like — that is the observance. // PSBh 4.2:2
* Why? // PSBh 4.2:3

children.text: * sākṛtatvād yasmādayaṃ brāhmaṇastathā prayuṅkte yathā laukikānāṃ dharmasādhanabhāvo na vidyata iti ato gūḍhavrata iti // PSBh_4.2:4
children.translated_text: * Because of acting deliberately [in a way that seems contrary]: since this <s>brāhmaṇa</s> conducts himself in such a way that worldly people do not perceive the nature of the <s>dharma</s>-practice — therefore [he is called] 'one whose observance is concealed.' // PSBh 4.2:4
* He objects: Since concealment is already achieved through the conditions of being unmanifest and appearing dead, this is a repetition. // PSBh 4.2:5
* It is said: It is not a repetition, because of the difference in meaning. // PSBh 4.2:6
* There, [in the earlier case,] what is unmanifest is merely the condition [itself]. // PSBh 4.2:7
* But here, [the concealment refers to] the hiding of bathing, laughter, and the like. // PSBh 4.2:8

children.text: * api ca tatra niṣpannaṃ liṅgam avyaktam // PSBh_4.2:9
children.translated_text: * Moreover, there, what is unmanifest is the completed mark (<s>liṅga</s>). // PSBh 4.2:9

children.text: * iha tu niṣpattikāle ca gopanopadeśaḥ // PSBh_4.2:10
children.translated_text: * But here, there is a teaching of concealment even at the time of accomplishment. // PSBh 4.2:10
* Nor is the condition of being unmanifest or appearing dead [itself] a mark of knowledge. // PSBh 4.2:11
* And therefore it is not a repetition. // PSBh 4.2:12

children.text: * tasmād gūḍhavratopadeśāya sthānāpadeśāpavādāya sthāne vastavyam // PSBh_4.2:13
children.translated_text: * Therefore, for the teaching of the concealed observance, and for the refutation of the [false] teaching about the [practice-]stage, one should dwell in the [proper] stage. // PSBh 4.2:13
* And the bathing, laughter, and the like should be performed in a concealed manner. // PSBh 4.2:14
* Thus, knowledge becomes concealed — this is the meaning. // PSBh 4.2:15

children.text: * āha kiṃ vratamevaikaṃ vidyāliṅgaṃ gopyam āhosvid anyadapyasti neti // PSBh_4.2:16
children.translated_text: * He asks: Is only the observance to be concealed as a mark of knowledge, or is there something else as well? // PSBh 4.2:16
* It is said: There is. // PSBh 4.2:17
* Because he states: // PSBh 4.2:18
One whose purified speech is concealed (<s>gūḍhapavitravāṇi</s>). || PS 4.3 ||

children.text: * atra gūḍhā guptā pracchannā aprakāśetyarthaḥ // PSBh_4.3:1
children.translated_text: * Here, 'concealed' (<s>gūḍhā</s>) means protected, hidden, unrevealed — this is the meaning. // PSBh 4.3:1

children.text: * pavitrā nāma satyā saṃskṛtā arghyahetuḥ sampannā na tu viparītetyarthaḥ // PSBh_4.3:2
children.translated_text: * 'Purified' (<s>pavitrā</s>) means truthful, refined, worthy of respect, accomplished — but not the opposite — this is the meaning. // PSBh 4.3:2
* That [speech] should be concealed. // PSBh 4.3:3
* For what purpose? // PSBh 4.3:4
* To that it is said: For the purpose of indicating birth (<s>jāti</s>), knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), austerity (<s>tapas</s>), and praise (<s>stava</s>). // PSBh 4.3:5
* Just as the osprey (<s>kurara</s>) indicates the autumn. // PSBh 4.3:6

children.text:
* uktaṃ hi / śaradaṃ kuraraḥ prāha vasantaṃ prāha kokilaḥ / prāha varṣā mayūraśca vāk pavitrāha brāhmaṇam // PSBh_4.3:7
* tathā / vāgeva hi manuṣyasya śrutamākhyāti bhāṣitā / dīpayantī yathā sarvaṃ prabhā bhānumivāmalā // PSBh_4.3:8

children.translated_text: * Therefore, birth, knowledge, austerity, and praise become [apparent through speech]. // PSBh 4.3:9
* And when one is praised, the increase and decrease of merit and demerit are absent for one who possesses finality [in knowledge] and lack of pride. // PSBh 4.3:10
* Therefore, this is stated: 'One whose purified speech is concealed.' // PSBh 4.3:11

children.text: * āha kiṃ vrataṃ vāṇī ca dvayamevātra gopyam āhosvid anyadapyasti neti // PSBh_4.3:12
children.translated_text: * He asks: Are only the observance and speech — these two — to be concealed here, or is there something else as well? // PSBh 4.3:12
* It is said: There is. // PSBh 4.3:13
* Because he states: // PSBh 4.3:14

* For it has been said: 'The osprey announces the autumn; the cuckoo announces the spring; the peacock announces the rains; and purified speech announces the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>.' Likewise: 'Indeed, it is speech that declares a man's learning when spoken — illuminating everything, like the pure radiance [declares] the sun.' // PSBh 4.3:7-8
Having closed all doors. || PS 4.4 ||
* Thus. // PSBh 4.4:1

children.text: * atra sarvaśabdo dvāraprakṛter niravaśeṣavācī draṣṭavyaḥ // PSBh_4.4:2
children.translated_text: * Here, the word 'all' (<s>sarva</s>) should be understood as a comprehensive term, without remainder, applying to the category of doors. // PSBh 4.4:2
* The doors are snorting and the like. // PSBh 4.4:3
* And why [are they called] doors? // PSBh 4.4:4
* Because they are the causes of income and expenditure of <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit) — [therefore they are called] doors. // PSBh 4.4:5
* 'Doors' in the plural — like the senses [which form part of] the cognitive apparatus (<s>vijñānayantra</s>). // PSBh 4.4:6
* 'Having closed' (<s>pidhāya</s>) takes as its domain the prior application of practices. // PSBh 4.4:7
* How? // PSBh 4.4:8

children.text: * asthānakāladeśakriyāprayogaprayojanāntarāṇi vidhivad vivecya yadā samyaṅ māyayā saṃnādyabhedakrameṇa prayuktāni tadā pihitāni bhavantītyarthaḥ // PSBh_4.4:9
children.translated_text: * Having properly discerned the improper place, time, location, action, application, and purpose — when [the doors] are applied through illusion (<s>māyā</s>), in the order of undivided [awareness], without breaking [that awareness], then they become closed — this is the meaning. // PSBh 4.4:9
* He asks: By what should those [doors] be closed? // PSBh 4.4:10
* To that it is said: // PSBh 4.4:11
By the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>). || PS 4.5 ||

children.text: * yasmādasya śrotrendriyavat pidhāyeti samyag jñānaprayoge sarvajñena bhagavatā vidyānugṛhītayā buddhyā pidhānamuktaṃ tasmādatra karaṇākhyā buddhyeti na jñānākhyā // PSBh_4.5:1
children.translated_text: * Because, like the organ of hearing, 'having closed' refers to the proper application of knowledge — the closure has been stated by the omniscient Blessed Lord through the intellect that is favored by knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>); therefore, here it is the designation of the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) — 'intellect' (<s>buddhi</s>) — and not the designation of knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>). // PSBh 4.5:1
* How is this understood? // PSBh 4.5:2
* Because of the use of the instrumental case with '<s>buddhyā</s>' (by intellect). // PSBh 4.5:3
* Like 'with ash' for bathing. // PSBh 4.5:4
* It is not the designation of knowledge. // PSBh 4.5:5

children.text: * yasya vijñānākhyā buddhirna jñānākhyā kathaṃ gamyate // PSBh_4.5:6
children.translated_text: * [If one asks:] His intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) bears the designation of discernment (<s>vijñāna</s>), not the designation of knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) — how is this understood? // PSBh 4.5:6

children.text: * tasya prāg jñānotpatter acetanapuruṣastasya hy ajñānād asaṃbodhyaḥ syāt // PSBh_4.5:7
children.translated_text: * [It is understood] because prior to the arising of knowledge, the person is unconscious; and because of his ignorance, he would be [spiritually] unawakened. // PSBh 4.5:7

children.text: * tasmādatra trikaṃ cintyate pidhātā pidhānaṃ pidheyamiti tatra pidhātā sādhakaḥ // PSBh_4.5:8
children.translated_text: * Therefore, here the threefold [analysis] is considered: the closer (<s>pidhātā</s>), the closing (<s>pidhāna</s>), and the closable (<s>pidheya</s>). There, the closer is the practitioner (<s>sādhaka</s>). // PSBh 4.5:8
* The closing [instrument] is his intellect favored by knowledge (<s>vidyānugṛhītā buddhi</s>). // PSBh 4.5:9

children.text: * pidheyaṃ vrataṃ vāṇī dvārāṇi ceti // PSBh_4.5:10
children.translated_text: * The closable [objects] are the observance, speech, and the doors. // PSBh 4.5:10

children.text: * kramavṛttitvāc ca buddhereva prayuṅkte śeṣāṇy akartṛtvenaivāprayuktāni // PSBh_4.5:11
children.translated_text: * And because the intellect functions sequentially, it engages only [one faculty at a time]; the remaining ones, not being engaged, are as if inactive. // PSBh 4.5:11
* The meaning is: at that time they become concealed. // PSBh 4.5:12
* Here, the section on <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) and <s>jñāna</s> (cognition) is concluded. // PSBh 4.5:13
* He asks: are only the two states — <s>avyakta</s> (inconspicuous) and <s>preta</s> (ghost-like) — to be practiced here? // PSBh 4.5:14

children.text: * vāgādīni vā gopāyitvā sādhakena kiṃ kartavyam // PSBh_4.5:15
children.translated_text: * Or, having concealed speech and the other [faculties], what should the practitioner do? // PSBh 4.5:15
* It is said: // PSBh 4.5:16
One should wander in the world like a madman. // PS 4.6 //

children.text: * atra buddhyā antaḥkaraṇānāṃ śrotrādīnāṃ ca bāhyānāṃ vṛttivibhramaḥ kartavyo'sati viṣaye viṣayagrahaṇam // PSBh_4.6:1
children.translated_text: * Here, a derangement of the functions of the internal organs — the intellect and the external [senses] such as hearing — is to be produced: apprehending sense-objects where there are no sense-objects. // PSBh 4.6:1

children.text: * atra / pañconmādāḥ samākhyātā vātapittakaphātmakāḥ / caturthaḥ saṃnipātastu abhighātastu pañcamaḥ // PSBh_4.6:2
* evaṃ grahabahutve sati yo 'yaṃ vātapittaśleṣmaṇāṃ samūhaḥ sāṃnipātiko'yaṃ mahāgrahaḥ // PSBh_4.6:3
children.translated_text: * Thus, when there are many [types of] seizure, the combination of <s>vāta</s> (wind), <s>pitta</s> (bile), and <s>śleṣman</s> (phlegm) — this <s>sāṃnipātika</s> (combined) one — is the great seizure. // PSBh 4.6:3
* Thus, the practice of the discipline is to be performed. // PSBh 4.6:4

children.text: * tatra yadi kaścid jñānajijñāsanārthaṃ dayārtham anugrahārthaṃ vā pṛcchati taṃ nivartayitvā brūyāt samayataḥ praviśasveti // PSBh_4.6:5
children.translated_text: * In this regard, if someone asks — for the purpose of inquiring about knowledge, out of compassion, or for the purpose of bestowing grace — one should turn him away and say: "Enter according to the observance." // PSBh 4.6:5

children.text: * tato dvāreṇa praviśya viparītam aviparītaṃ vā yadi kaścid brūyāt ko bhavāniti tato vaktavyaṃ māheśvaro'haṃ kaumāro 'hamiti duratyayaṃ kṛtaṃ ca mamāneneti // PSBh_4.6:6
children.translated_text: * Then, having entered through the door, whether he speaks contrarily or correctly, if someone asks "Who are you?" — then one should say: "I am a devotee of <s>Maheśvara</s>," "I am a devotee of <s>Kumāra</s>," and "Something insurmountable has been done to me by him." // PSBh 4.6:6

children.text: * tato jighāṃsanārthaṃ mayā spṛṣṭo na tu viṣayakrīḍārthaṃ vā // PSBh_4.6:7
children.translated_text: * Then, "He touched me in order to harm, not for the purpose of sensual play." // PSBh 4.6:7

children.text: * tataḥ parivarjayati ityevaṃ laukikaparīkṣakāṇāṃ sammohanārtham uktam unmattavad iti // PSBh_4.6:8
children.translated_text: * Then he avoids [the practitioner]. Thus, for the purpose of deluding worldly examiners, it is said "like a madman." // PSBh 4.6:8
* From "like a madman" and "like a ghost," only the derangement of the functions of the internal organs and the like is to be adopted [as practice]. // PSBh 4.6:9
* "Alone" — solitude without companionship is intended. // PSBh 4.6:10

children.text: * ekenetarebhyo vicchinnenāsahāyenety arthaḥ āha ekena kiṃ kartavyamiti // PSBh_4.6:11
children.translated_text: * The meaning is: alone, separated from others, without a companion. He asks: what should one do alone? // PSBh 4.6:11
* It is said: one should roam about. // PSBh 4.6:12
* Because he says "<s>vicareta</s>" (one should wander). // PSBh 4.6:13
* Here, "<s>vi</s>" [signifies] extension. // PSBh 4.6:14
* "<s>caret</s>" (one should practice) indicates acquisition — in the acquisition of <s>dharma</s> (merit). // PSBh 4.6:15
* "<s>īta</s>" [signifies] command and injunction. // PSBh 4.6:16
* The meaning is: by the injunction of extension, one should roam about particularly. // PSBh 4.6:17
* He asks: where should one roam about? // PSBh 4.6:18
* It is said: in the world. // PSBh 4.6:19

children.text: * trivarṇāśramiṣu lokasaṃjñā na tu brahmalokādiṣu // PSBh_4.6:20
children.translated_text: * The designation "world" [refers to] the three <s>varṇas</s> (social classes) and <s>āśramas</s> (stages of life), not to <s>Brahmaloka</s> (the world of Brahmā) and the like. // PSBh 4.6:20
* Why? // PSBh 4.6:21
* Because it is impossible in the exalted [realms]. // PSBh 4.6:22
* "In the world" indicates proximity and presence. // PSBh 4.6:23
* The meaning is: the other <s>varṇas</s> (social classes) constitute the world; one should roam about in [the presence of] their overseers. // PSBh 4.6:24

children.text: * āha kāṃ vṛttimāsthāya loke vihartavyam sarvabhakṣameva // PSBh_4.6:25
children.translated_text: * He asks: adopting what mode of livelihood should one roam about in the world — eating everything? // PSBh 4.6:25
* It is said: no. // PSBh 4.6:26
* Because he says: // PSBh 4.6:27

* Regarding this: five kinds of madness are declared — those caused by <s>vāta</s> (wind), <s>pitta</s> (bile), and <s>kapha</s> (phlegm); the fourth is <s>saṃnipāta</s> (combination of all three), and the fifth is <s>abhighāta</s> (injury). // PSBh 4.6:2
One should take up prepared food that has been discarded. // PS 4.7 //
* Here, by the word "prepared" (<s>kṛta</s>), there is a prohibition of unprepared things such as seeds, stalks, fruits, and the like. // PSBh 4.7:1

children.text: * kṛtaṃ bhinnodbhinnādyaṃ tad bhaikṣam utsṛṣṭaṃ yathālabdhaṃ vidhinā prāptamupayojyam // PSBh_4.7:2
children.translated_text: * "Prepared" means split, sprouted, and the like — that is alms-food; "discarded" (<s>utsṛṣṭa</s>) means obtained as it comes, received according to rule, and to be consumed. // PSBh 4.7:2

children.text: * atra kṛtagrahaṇādakṛtapratiṣedhaḥ akṛtapratiṣedhāc ca kṛtsnā hiṃsā tantre pratiṣiddhā draṣṭavyā // PSBh_4.7:3
children.translated_text: * Here, by the word "prepared," there is a prohibition of the unprepared; and by the prohibition of the unprepared, all <s>hiṃsā</s> (violence) should be seen as prohibited in the system. // PSBh 4.7:3

children.text: * āha kiṃ tat kṛtaṃ nāma buddhighaṭādyam // PSBh_4.7:4
children.translated_text: * He asks: what is this "prepared" — things produced by the intellect, such as pots? // PSBh 4.7:4
* To that it is said: no. // PSBh 4.7:5
* Because he says "food" (<s>anna</s>). // PSBh 4.7:6
* There, by the word "food," there is a prohibition of what is not food. // PSBh 4.7:7

children.text: * tac ca dviyoni indrābhiṣiktam indriyābhiṣiktaṃ ca tatrendrābhiṣiktaṃ vrīhiyavādyam // PSBh_4.7:8
children.translated_text: * And that [food] is of two origins: consecrated by <s>Indra</s> and consecrated by the senses. Of these, what is consecrated by <s>Indra</s> is rice, barley, and the like. // PSBh 4.7:8
* What is consecrated by the senses, however, is meat. // PSBh 4.7:9

children.text: * tat pañcavidham bhakṣyaṃ bhojyaṃ lehyaṃ peyaṃ coṣyamiti // PSBh_4.7:10
children.translated_text: * That is of five kinds: <s>bhakṣya</s> (edible solids), <s>bhojya</s> (foods to be eaten), <s>lehya</s> (foods to be licked), <s>peya</s> (beverages), and <s>coṣya</s> (foods to be sucked). // PSBh 4.7:10
* Likewise, it has six tastes: sweet, sour, salty, bitter, pungent, and astringent. // PSBh 4.7:11

children.text: * āha tasya kṛtānnasyārjanaṃ kutaḥ kartavyam // PSBh_4.7:12
children.translated_text: * He asks: from where should the acquisition of that prepared food be done? // PSBh 4.7:12
* To that it is said: [from what is] discarded. // PSBh 4.7:13
* Here, by the word "discarded" (<s>utsṛṣṭa</s>), there is a prohibition of begged food and food obtained as it comes. // PSBh 4.7:14
* For what reason? // PSBh 4.7:15
* Because of the purpose of avoiding faults such as [those arising from] the slaughterhouse and the like, and because of the faults of theft, receiving gifts, and the like. // PSBh 4.7:16
* And that discarded [food] is of three kinds. // PSBh 4.7:17

children.text: * tad yathā nisṛṣṭaṃ visṛṣṭam atisṛṣṭamiti // PSBh_4.7:18
children.translated_text: * They are as follows: <s>nisṛṣṭa</s> (released), <s>visṛṣṭa</s> (given away), and <s>atisṛṣṭa</s> (abandoned). // PSBh 4.7:18

children.text: * tatra sanimittaṃ parityaktamannaṃ pānaṃ vā tan nisṛṣṭam // PSBh_4.7:19
children.translated_text: * Of these, food or drink abandoned with a specific cause is <s>nisṛṣṭa</s> (released). // PSBh 4.7:19
* That which is given up for the sake of cows, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, and the like is <s>visṛṣṭa</s> (given away). // PSBh 4.7:20
* <s>Atisṛṣṭa</s> (abandoned) is that which is discarded from some other [motive]. // PSBh 4.7:21

children.text: * dayārtham ānṛśaṃsārthaṃ vā yadi kaścid dadyāt tadapi grāhyameva // PSBh_4.7:22
children.translated_text: * If someone gives out of compassion or kindness, that too is certainly to be accepted. // PSBh 4.7:22

children.text: * āha anena sādhakena kiṃ kartavyamiti // PSBh_4.7:23
children.translated_text: * He asks: what should this practitioner do [with it]? // PSBh 4.7:23
* It is said: it should be consumed. // PSBh 4.7:24
* Because he says "<s>upādadīta</s>" (one should take up). Here, "<s>upa</s>" [signifies] acceptance. // PSBh 4.7:25
* The meaning is: by one who stands in the restraint of complete <s>asanmāna</s> (dishonor). // PSBh 4.7:26

children.text: * ādadīta ityupayoge grahaṇe ca vivakṣitasūtragrahaṇe tvāvad bhavati // PSBh_4.7:27
children.translated_text: * "<s>Ādadīta</s>" (one should take) is intended for consumption and taking up; but in the taking up of the [words of the] <s>sūtra</s> as intended, it stands [as follows]. // PSBh 4.7:27

children.text: * taduktam / saṃcitvā naramevainaṃ kāmānāmavitṛptikam / vyāghraḥ paśumivādāya mṛtyurādāya gacchati // PSBh_4.7:28

children.translated_text: * Thus. // PSBh 4.7:29
* Even in consumption, [one should] not [be] like <s>Nātha</s> and <s>Kaṇāda</s>. // PSBh 4.7:30
* Therefore, it should be consumed. // PSBh 4.7:31
* "<s>Īta</s>" [signifies] command and injunction. // PSBh 4.7:32
* That discarded [food], obtained according to rule, should be consumed. // PSBh 4.7:33

children.text: * anyathā hi vidhivyapetena krameṇa vṛttyarjanaṃ na kartavyamityarthaḥ // PSBh_4.7:34
children.translated_text: * The meaning is: otherwise, acquisition of livelihood by a method departing from the rule should not be done. // PSBh 4.7:34

children.text: * āha vratādīni gopayitvā samyaksādhanaprayoge utsṛṣṭopayoge ca vartataḥ ke vārthā niṣpadyante // PSBh_4.7:35
children.translated_text: * He asks: having concealed the vows and the like, when one is engaged in the proper practice of the discipline and in the consumption of discarded [food], what benefits are accomplished? // PSBh 4.7:35

children.text: * asanmānaprakaraṇasya vā parisamāptiḥ kimasti neti // PSBh_4.7:36
children.translated_text: * Or, is there a conclusion to the section on <s>asanmāna</s> (dishonor), or not? // PSBh 4.7:36
* It is said: there is. // PSBh 4.7:37
* Because he says: // PSBh 4.7:38
* Thus it has been said: "Having stalked this man who is insatiable in his desires, death seizes him and carries him away, like a tiger seizing an animal." // PSBh 4.7:28

children.text: unmatto mūḍha ityevaṃ manyante itare janāḥ || PS_4.8 ||
children.translated_text: Other people consider [him] thus: "He is mad, he is deluded." // PS 4.8 //
* Here, "madman" refers to that same [practitioner]. // PSBh 4.8:1
* Its etymology has been stated previously. "Deluded" (<s>mūḍha</s>) — // PSBh 4.8:2
* The root "<s>muhu</s>" [means] non-recognition. // PSBh 4.8:3

children.text: * avyakto'yaṃ preto'yam unmatto'yaṃ mūḍho'yaṃ mūrkho'yamiti vaktāro vadantītyarthaḥ // PSBh_4.8:4
children.translated_text: * The meaning is: speakers say "this one is inconspicuous," "this one is a ghost," "this one is mad," "this one is deluded," "this one is a fool." // PSBh 4.8:4
* The word "<s>iti</s>" (thus), because of its function of expressing meanings, serves to conclude the section. // PSBh 4.8:5
* Thus, because the [topics of] state, time, place, action, practice, purpose, concealment, dwelling, meaning, and all austerities have been explained — // PSBh 4.8:6
* "<s>Evam</s>" (thus) [is used] in reference to what has passed. // PSBh 4.8:7
* "<s>Manyate</s>" (they consider) [is used] in the sense of firm conviction. // PSBh 4.8:8
* "Others" (<s>itare</s>) refers to householders, celibate students, forest-dwellers, mendicants, and heretics — those qualified for <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate discipline). // PSBh 4.8:9
* "People" (<s>janāḥ</s>) — // PSBh 4.8:10
* The root "<s>janī</s>" [means] coming into being. // PSBh 4.8:11

children.text: * janā iti varṇāśramiṇāṃ janānām adhikṛtānāṃ grahaṇam uktaṃ hi / janena hi jano jātaḥ janaṃ janayase jana / janaṃ śocasi nātmānaṃ mātmānaṃ śoca mā janam // PSBh_4.8:12

children.translated_text: * The meaning is: thus the speakers speak. // PSBh 4.8:13
* Here, the principal section on the practice of <s>asanmāna</s> (dishonor) is concluded. // PSBh 4.8:14

children.text: * āha vratādīni gopayitvā samyaksādhanaprayoge utsṛṣṭopayoge ca tataḥ ko guṇaḥ yaṃ guṇaṃ jñātvā avyaktapretonmattādyā vādā niṣpādyā iti // PSBh_4.8:15
children.translated_text: * He asks: having concealed the vows and the like, when one is engaged in the proper practice of the discipline and in the consumption of discarded [food], what is the benefit — knowing which benefit the practices of behaving as inconspicuous, ghost-like, mad, and the like are to be accomplished? // PSBh 4.8:15

children.text: * taducyate taṃ guṇaṃ jñātvā vakṣyāmaḥ // PSBh_4.8:16
children.translated_text: * To that it is said: knowing that benefit, we shall explain [it]. // PSBh 4.8:16

children.text: * api ca avyaktapretonmattādyaṃ brāhmaṇakarmaviruddhaṃ kramaṃ dṛṣṭvā yāvadayaṃ śiṣyaḥ enamarthaṃ na bravīti tattasya hṛdistham aśaṅkitam upalabhyottaraṃ brūma iti kṛtvā bhagavānidaṃ sūtramuvāca // PSBh_4.8:17
children.translated_text: * Moreover, having observed the conduct of behaving as inconspicuous, ghost-like, mad, and the like — which is contrary to the conduct of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> — until this disciple does not speak of this matter, [the teacher], having ascertained that it is fixed in his heart without doubt, says "we shall state the answer" — thinking thus, the Blessed Lord spoke this <s>sūtra</s>: // PSBh 4.8:17

* "People" (<s>janāḥ</s>) refers to those of the <s>varṇas</s> and <s>āśramas</s>, the qualified people. For it has been said: "By people indeed a person is born; you produce people, O person; you grieve for people, not for yourself — do not grieve for yourself, do not [grieve for] people." // PSBh 4.8:12

children.text: asanmāno hi yantrāṇāṃ sarveṣāmuttamaḥ smṛtaḥ || PS_4.9 ||
children.translated_text: For <s>asanmāna</s> (dishonor) is remembered as the supreme among all restraints. // PS 4.9 //
* Here, the "a" prefix [in <s>asanmāna</s>] serves to negate <s>māna</s> (pride/honor). // PSBh 4.9:1
* <s>Māna</s> (pride) here is of two kinds. // PSBh 4.9:2
* Pride of birth (<s>jātyabhimāna</s>) and pride of being a householder (<s>gṛhasthābhimāna</s>). // PSBh 4.9:3
* Of these, pride of birth is [the thought] "I am a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>." // PSBh 4.9:4

children.text: * pūjyatvād ūrdhvagamanādīnāṃ kāryāṇām ucchritatvāt trayāṇāmapi varṇānāmupadeśena gurutvād yajñakartṛtvāt trailokyasthitihetoḥ brāhmaṇo'hamiti prathamo māno jātyutkarṣāt // PSBh_4.9:5
children.translated_text: * Because of being worthy of worship, because of the elevation of duties such as going upward, because of being a teacher to all three <s>varṇas</s> through instruction, because of being a performer of <s>yajña</s> (sacrifice), and because of being the cause of the stability of the three worlds — "I am a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>" — this is the first pride, arising from the excellence of birth. // PSBh 4.9:5

children.text: * tathā brāhmaṇānāmapi gṛhasthādīnāṃ pūjyatvāt tatkṛtamānaśca // PSBh_4.9:6
children.translated_text: * Likewise, even among <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, because householders and the like are worthy of worship, pride produced by that [status] also [exists]. // PSBh 4.9:6
* And this twofold pride is prohibited by the injunction of inconspicuous conduct. // PSBh 4.9:7

children.text: * tathā vittaṃ bandhuryaśaḥ karma vidyā bhavati pañcamī / etāni mānyasthānāni garīyo yadyaduttaram // PSBh_4.9:8
* etāni caikavāsaḥpretācaraṇagūḍhavratopadeśinā sūtrataḥ pratiṣiddhānītyato māno na kartavyaḥ // PSBh_4.9:9
children.translated_text: * And these are prohibited by the <s>sūtra</s> through the instruction of the hidden vow of wearing a single garment and behaving like a ghost; therefore, pride should not be cultivated. // PSBh 4.9:9
* "<s>San</s>" [is used] in the sense of praise and in [the sense of] existence. // PSBh 4.9:10
* And further, [it is] distinguished by the section on the practice of <s>asanmāna</s> (dishonor). // PSBh 4.9:11
* The word "<s>hi</s>" (for/indeed) should be seen as implying the excellence of the supreme. // PSBh 4.9:12

children.text: * yantrāṇi agniṣṭomādīni māsopavāsādīni ca gṛhasthādīnāṃ śuddhivṛddhikarāṇi // PSBh_4.9:13
children.translated_text: * <s>Yantras</s> (restraints) are [rituals] such as <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> and the like, monthly fasts and the like, which produce purification and spiritual growth for householders and the like. // PSBh 4.9:13
* And why [are they called] <s>yantras</s> (restraints)? // PSBh 4.9:14
* A <s>yantra</s> (restraint) is ritual action and the like. // PSBh 4.9:15

children.text: * yasmād ayantrā laukikā amaryādāvasthā bhavantītyato yantrāṇām // PSBh_4.9:16
children.translated_text: * Because without restraints, worldly people would be in a state without boundaries; therefore, [they are called] restraints. // PSBh 4.9:16
* "Of restraints" (<s>yantrāṇām</s>) is genitive plural. // PSBh 4.9:17

children.text: * āha bahuvacanaprayogāt saṃdehaḥ atha kiyatāṃ yantrāṇām // PSBh_4.9:18
children.translated_text: * He asks: because of the use of the plural, there is doubt — of how many restraints [is it the supreme]? // PSBh 4.9:18
* To that it is said: of all. // PSBh 4.9:19
* Here, "of all" means without exception. // PSBh 4.9:20
* "Of all" (<s>sarveṣām</s>) is genitive plural. // PSBh 4.9:21
* He asks: because the genitive requires [completion], there is doubt. // PSBh 4.9:22
* Of those, the essential natures stand [as causes]. // PSBh 4.9:23
* To that it is said: the supreme. // PSBh 4.9:24
* Here, "supreme" (<s>uttama</s>) [is used] in the sense of excellence, [implying] the highest purity, renunciation, acquisition, disposition, and the like. // PSBh 4.9:25

children.text: * uktaṃ hi / vareṇyaḥ sattamo mukhyo variṣṭhaḥ śobhano'thavā / uttamaścāparārdhaśca svarthaḥ śreṣṭhārthavācakāḥ // PSBh_4.9:26
children.translated_text: * For it has been said: "<s>Vareṇya</s>, <s>sattama</s>, <s>mukhya</s>, <s>variṣṭha</s>, <s>śobhana</s>, or <s>uttama</s> and <s>aparārdha</s> — these are synonyms expressing the meaning of 'best.'" // PSBh 4.9:26
* [That is,] the best. // PSBh 4.9:27
* And here it is said: "supreme" (<s>uttama</s>). // PSBh 4.9:28

children.text: * āha asanmānaḥ sarvayantrāṇāmuttama iti kva siddham // PSBh_4.9:29
children.translated_text: * He asks: where is it established that <s>asanmāna</s> (dishonor) is the supreme among all restraints? // PSBh 4.9:29
* It is said: here [in this teaching]. // PSBh 4.9:30
* Because he says "<s>smṛtaḥ</s>" (remembered/declared). // PSBh 4.9:31

children.text: * atra smṛta ityuktaparyāyaḥ maheśvareṇoktaṃ proktaṃ kathitaṃ varṇitamityarthaḥ // PSBh_4.9:32
children.translated_text: * Here, "remembered" (<s>smṛta</s>) is a synonym for "spoken" — the meaning is: spoken, proclaimed, told, described by <s>Maheśvara</s>. // PSBh 4.9:32
* Why is it distinguished? // PSBh 4.9:33
* Because of the word of the omniscient one, and because it is not contradictory. // PSBh 4.9:34
* The meaning is: for the words of those who see directly are never contradictory. // PSBh 4.9:35

children.text: * āha asmin krame uttamatvena vyākhyāyamānaṃ ka ādyaḥ śodhakaḥ // PSBh_4.9:36
children.translated_text: * He asks: in this progression being explained as the highest, who was the first purifier? [PSBh 4.9:36]

children.text: * kena vā idaṃ vidhānaṃ cīrṇam // PSBh_4.9:37
children.translated_text: * And by whom was this method practiced? [PSBh 4.9:37]

children.text: * ācaratā vā kiṃ phalaṃ prāptam // PSBh_4.9:38
children.translated_text: * And what fruit was obtained by the one who practiced it? [PSBh 4.9:38]
* That should be stated for the purpose of our conviction. [PSBh 4.9:39]
* That is stated: [PSBh 4.9:40]
* Likewise: "Wealth, kinsmen, fame, action, and learning is the fifth — these are the grounds of honor; each succeeding one is weightier [than the preceding]." // PSBh 4.9:8

children.text: indro vā agre asureṣu pāśupatamacarat || PS_4.10 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s>, or [others], in the beginning, practiced the <s>Pāśupata</s> [observance] among the <s>asuras</s>. [PS 4.10]
* Here, <s>Indra</s> is the king of the gods. [PSBh 4.10:1]
* How is this known? From the statement of practicing among the <s>asuras</s>. [PSBh 4.10:2]
* And this <s>Indra</s> is a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, the foremost. [PSBh 4.10:3]
* Because of the mention of <s>brāhmaṇa</s> in the <s>sūtra</s> and the prohibition against <s>śūdras</s>. [PSBh 4.10:4]
* The root <s>idi</s> means 'supreme sovereignty' — from that [comes] <s>Indra</s>. [PSBh 4.10:5]

children.text: * indra utkṛṣṭaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ devagandharvayakṣarākṣasapitṛpiśācādīnāṃ śreṣṭho na tu brahmādīnām // PSBh_4.10:6
children.translated_text: * <s>Indra</s> is the exalted, foremost one — foremost among gods, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, <s>pitṛs</s>, <s>piśācas</s>, and such — but not of <s>Brahmā</s> and others. [PSBh 4.10:6]

children.text: * kiṃ tu svargiṇāṃ madhye aiśvaryeṇa vidyayā ājñayā cety ataḥ śreṣṭhatvād indraḥ // PSBh_4.10:7
children.translated_text: * Rather, among the celestial beings, he is foremost by sovereignty, knowledge, and command — therefore [he is called] <s>Indra</s>. [PSBh 4.10:7]
* The word <s>vā</s> is in the sense of honoring. [PSBh 4.10:8]
* This method was also practiced by other foremost gods. [PSBh 4.10:9]
* How much more then for you and others, who are mere humans? [PSBh 4.10:10]
* Therefore this matter should be honored. [PSBh 4.10:11]
* He asks: when was it practiced? [PSBh 4.10:12]
* The answer is: 'in the beginning' (<s>agre</s>). [PSBh 4.10:13]
* Here <s>agra</s> refers to a former time. [PSBh 4.10:14]
* Before the connection of <s>Kuśika</s> and <s>Īśāna</s>. [PSBh 4.10:15]
* First it was practiced by the immortals. [PSBh 4.10:16]
* In the <s>Kṛta</s>, <s>Tretā</s>, <s>Dvāpara</s>, and other ages — this is the meaning. [PSBh 4.10:17]
* He asks: among whom was it practiced? [PSBh 4.10:18]
* The answer is: among the <s>asuras</s>. [PSBh 4.10:19]
* Here <s>asuras</s> means those other than the gods (<s>suras</s>), endowed with thievery. [PSBh 4.10:20]

children.text: * prāṇāpaharaṇād vā asurāḥ prajāpatiputrā vijñeyāḥ // PSBh_4.10:21
children.translated_text: * Or <s>asuras</s> should be understood as the sons of <s>Prajāpati</s>, from [their] taking away life-breaths. [PSBh 4.10:21]
* 'Among the <s>asuras</s>' indicates proximate presence. [PSBh 4.10:22]
* In the proximity of the <s>asuras</s>, in the vicinity of the <s>asuras</s>, in the presence of the <s>asuras</s> — this is the meaning. [PSBh 4.10:23]
* He asks: what is that [which he practiced]? [PSBh 4.10:24]
* The answer is: the <s>Pāśupata</s> [observance]. [PSBh 4.10:25]

children.text: * atra paśupatinoktaparigrahādhikāreṣu vartata iti pāśupatam // PSBh_4.10:26
children.translated_text: * Here, because it operates within the authority of what has been spoken and accepted by <s>Paśupati</s>, it is [called] <s>Pāśupata</s>. [PSBh 4.10:26]
* Or because <s>Paśupati</s> is contemplated in it, it is <s>Pāśupata</s>. [PSBh 4.10:27]
* Or because it leads to <s>Paśupati</s>, it is <s>Pāśupata</s>. [PSBh 4.10:28]

children.text: * pāśupatamiti samastasya sampūrṇasya vidhānasyaitad grahaṇam // PSBh_4.10:29
children.translated_text: * '<s>Pāśupata</s>' — this is a designation for the entire, complete method. [PSBh 4.10:29]
* Because the sequence of the unmanifest and so forth is preceded by the manifest mark. [PSBh 4.10:31]

children.text: * tasmāt kṛtsnamidameva vidhānamācīrṇamindreṇa duḥkhāntārthinā śuddhivṛddhyartham // PSBh_4.10:32
children.translated_text: * Therefore, this entire method was practiced by <s>Indra</s>, who desired the end of suffering, for the purpose of purification and growth [of merit]. [PSBh 4.10:32]
* Because of the abundance of <s>dharma</s> among the gods, it was practiced on earth. [PSBh 4.10:33]
* 'Practiced' (<s>acarad</s>) — this is the past tense. [PSBh 4.10:34]
* In past time, he practiced — this is the meaning. [PSBh 4.10:35]

children.text: * āha indreṇāsureṣvācaratā kiṃ phalaṃ prāptam // PSBh_4.10:36
children.translated_text: * He asks: what fruit was obtained by <s>Indra</s> when he practiced among the <s>asuras</s>? [PSBh 4.10:36]
* That is stated: [PSBh 4.10:37]
He took their <s>iṣṭāpūrta</s> (sacrificial and meritorious works). [PS 4.11]
* 'He' (<s>sa</s>) refers to <s>Indra</s>; 'of them' (<s>teṣām</s>) refers to the <s>asuras</s>. [PSBh 4.11:1]
* <s>Iṣṭāpūrtam</s> is a <s>dvandva</s> compound. [PSBh 4.11:2]

children.text: * iṣṭaṃ ca pūrtaṃ ceṣṭāpūrtam tatra yan mantrapūrvakeṇa vidhinā dattaṃ hutaṃ stutyādiniṣpannaṃ sukṛtaṃ tad iṣṭam // PSBh_4.11:3
children.translated_text: * <s>Iṣṭa</s> and <s>pūrta</s> together make <s>iṣṭāpūrta</s>. There, whatever merit is given, offered, or accomplished through hymns and such by a procedure preceded by mantras — that is <s>iṣṭa</s> (sacrificial merit). [PSBh 4.11:3]
* Whatever [is done] without being preceded by mantras — that is <s>pūrta</s> (meritorious works). [PSBh 4.11:4]
* By what means did <s>Indra</s> take [it] from the <s>asuras</s>? [PSBh 4.11:5]
* The answer is: [PSBh 4.11:6]
By well-employed deception (<s>māyā</s>), he obtained [it]. [PS 4.12]

children.text: * krāthanaspandanādiprayogaiḥ dhikkṛtasya nidrāviṣṭo vāyusaṃspṛṣṭo mandakārī asamyakkārī asamyagvādīti yo 'yaṃ duṣṭaśabdo 'bhiyogaśabdaśca niṣpadyate tasminn anṛte māyāsaṃjñā // PSBh_4.12:1
children.translated_text: * When one is despised through the employment of snoring, trembling, and such [behaviors], and the abusive words arise — 'he is overcome by sleep, touched by wind, a slow worker, a wrong-doer, a wrong-speaker' — in that falsehood the designation <s>māyā</s> (deception) [is used]. [PSBh 4.12:1]
* And in mental and physical abuse. [PSBh 4.12:2]
* 'By <s>māyā</s>' — [this is] an instrumental case. [PSBh 4.12:3]
* 'Well-employed' (<s>sukṛtayā</s>) — [PSBh 4.12:4]

children.text: * su praśaṃsāyām tayā sukṛtayā samyak prayuktayeti sādhakasādhanaprādhānyam // PSBh_4.12:5
children.translated_text: * <s>Su</s> is in the sense of praise; 'by that well-employed, properly applied [deception]' — the emphasis is on the practitioner's means. [PSBh 4.12:5]

children.text: * avindata iti prāptau prādhānye ca // PSBh_4.12:6
children.translated_text: * 'He obtained' (<s>avindata</s>) — in the sense of attainment and supremacy. [PSBh 4.12:6]
* 'He took their sacrificial and meritorious works.' [PSBh 4.12:7]

children.text: * uktaṃ hi / ākrośamāno nākrośenmanyureva titikṣati / sa teṣāṃ duṣkṛtaṃ dattvā sukṛtaṃ cāsya vindati // PSBh_4.12:8

children.translated_text: * He objects: <s>Indra</s> is the supreme [example]. [PSBh 4.12:9]

children.text: * sa teṣāmiṣṭāpūrtam ityukte parāpadeśenāsya vṛttir nirguṇīkṛtā // PSBh_4.12:10
children.translated_text: * When it is said 'he took their sacrificial and meritorious works,' this practice has been made valuable by reference to another [i.e., <s>Indra</s>]. [PSBh 4.12:10]
* Now, is there also a self-reference here, or not? [PSBh 4.12:11]
* The answer is: there is. [PSBh 4.12:12]
* Because [the sūtra] states: [PSBh 4.12:13]
* For it has been said: 'When being reviled, one should not revile back; one should endure anger with forbearance. He gives his sin to them and obtains their merit.' [PSBh 4.12:8]
For this censure is [in fact] non-censure; therefore — [PS 4.13]
* Here, dishonor, abuse, and such constitute censure (<s>nindā</s>). [PSBh 4.13:1]
* Contempt, reproach — this is the meaning. [PSBh 4.13:2]
* The word [<s>nindā</s>] should be understood as introducing the excellence and superiority of the highest [practice]. [PSBh 4.13:3]
* This is understood from the context of the highest [practice]. [PSBh 4.13:4]
* 'This' (<s>eṣā</s>) — in reference to what has gone before. [PSBh 4.13:5]
* The meaning is: the censure consisting of dishonor, abuse, reviling, and such. [PSBh 4.13:6]
* 'Non-censure' (<s>anindā</s>) — the prefix 'a-' negates the state of being censured. [PSBh 4.13:7]
* Non-censure, non-contempt, non-reproach — this is the meaning. [PSBh 4.13:8]
* Here the word 'therefore' (<s>tasmāt</s>) refers to both what precedes and what follows. [PSBh 4.13:9]

children.text: * tatra pūrvākāṅkṣāyāṃ tāvat kṛtsnā nindāprakaraṇaguṇavacane // PSBh_4.13:10
children.translated_text: * There, in the forward reference first: all censure is a statement of the quality of the subject matter. [PSBh 4.13:10]

children.text: * yasmād indrasyāpi śuddhivṛddhikāriṇī ātmāpadeśena parāpadeśena ca bhagavatā asanmānacarir guṇīkṛtā tasmādityarthaḥ // PSBh_4.13:11
children.translated_text: * Because even for <s>Indra</s>, the conduct of dishonor has been made valuable — as producing purification and growth — by the Blessed One through both self-reference and reference to another; therefore — this is the meaning. [PSBh 4.13:11]

children.text: * āha nirākāṅkṣānirdeśāt saṃdeho yathā yathā varṇitaṃ tathā tathā ca vyākhyātam // PSBh_4.13:12
children.translated_text: * He says: from the instruction that is free of expectation, the doubt has been resolved — as it was described, so it has been explained. [PSBh 4.13:12]

children.text: * nindāyā aninditatvaṃ guṇaṃ jñātvā sādhakena kiṃ kartavyam // PSBh_4.13:13
children.translated_text: * Having known the quality that censure is [actually] non-censure, what should the practitioner do? [PSBh 4.13:13]
* That is stated: [PSBh 4.13:14]
Being censured, one should wander about. [PS 4.14]
* Here censure (<s>nindā</s>) is as previously stated. [PSBh 4.14:1]
* 'Being censured' — at the present time of censure; this is the meaning. [PSBh 4.14:2]
* 'One should wander' (<s>caret</s>) refers to acquiring. [PSBh 4.14:3]
* In the injunction for acquiring <s>dharma</s>. [PSBh 4.14:4]
* And because of the difference in context, the word <s>cari</s> (wander) should be understood as non-repetitive. [PSBh 4.14:5]
* Here this incidental section on the practice of the path of dishonor is completed. [PSBh 4.14:6]

children.text: * āha nindyamānaś caredityuktvā ādyaṃ vidhānamācarataḥ ko 'rtho niṣpadyate // PSBh_4.14:7
children.translated_text: * He asks: having said 'being censured, one should wander about,' what result is accomplished by one practicing the first method? [PSBh 4.14:7]
* Or how is it designated when accomplished? [PSBh 4.14:8]
* That is stated: [PSBh 4.14:9]
One whose action is unblemished. [PS 4.15]

children.text: * atra caryottarasambandhād gamyate yadetadaninditaṃ karma dharmaḥ sa eva nindyamānasyācarato niṣpadyate // PSBh_4.15:1
children.translated_text: * Here, from the connection with what follows the [mention of] conduct, it is understood that this unblemished action — <s>dharma</s> — is accomplished for one who wanders about while being censured. [PSBh 4.15:1]
* Therefore he becomes one 'whose action is unblemished' — this is the meaning. [PSBh 4.15:2]

children.text: * āha nindyamānasyācarato 'ninditaṃ karma bhavatīti kva siddham // PSBh_4.15:3
children.translated_text: * He asks: where is it established that unblemished action arises for one who wanders about while being censured? [PSBh 4.15:3]
* The answer is: here, because [the sūtra] states: [PSBh 4.15:4]
This path is distinguished from all [others]. [PS 4.16]
* Here 'this' (<s>ayam</s>) is in the sense of what is directly present. [PSBh 4.16:1]
* Just as 'this person.' [PSBh 4.16:2]

children.text: * yathāvidhiś caririti yāḥ kriyāḥ atrādhikṛtasyāninditaṃ karma bhavatītyāha bhagavān // PSBh_4.16:3
children.translated_text: * The Blessed One says: the practices of one who follows the method as prescribed, and of the one who is qualified here — his action becomes unblemished. [PSBh 4.16:3]
The true path. [PS 4.17]
* And because of the undiminished power to lead to non-return. [PSBh 4.17:2]

children.text: * tasmāt sarvajñavacanāvisaṃvāditvāc cāyaṃ satpatha ityarthaḥ // PSBh_4.17:3
children.translated_text: * Therefore, because the word of the omniscient one is unfailing, this is the true path (<s>satpatha</s>) — this is the meaning. [PSBh 4.17:3]

children.text: * āha kimanyatra panthāno na santi iti // PSBh_4.17:4
children.translated_text: * He asks: do paths not exist elsewhere? [PSBh 4.17:4]
* The answer is: they exist. [PSBh 4.17:5]
* But — [PSBh 4.17:6]
* Why? Because of the power to lead to the proximity of <s>Rudra</s>. [PSBh 4.17:1]
The others are false paths. [PS 4.18]
* Here <s>ku</s> is in the sense of contempt. [PSBh 4.18:1]
* Why? [PSBh 4.18:2]
* This is understood from the use of the word <s>ku</s>. [PSBh 4.18:3]
* Like <s>kupuruṣa</s> (contemptible person). [PSBh 4.18:4]
* 'Paths' means methods, means — this is the meaning. [PSBh 4.18:5]
* The word <s>tu</s> ('but') is in the sense of the excellence of non-return. [PSBh 4.18:6]
* 'Others' (<s>anye</s>) — [PSBh 4.18:7]
* the paths of householders, celibate students, forest-dwellers, mendicants, and sectarians. [PSBh 4.18:8]
* They are false paths. [PSBh 4.18:9]
* No [they are not entirely false]. [PSBh 4.18:10]

children.text: * āha ayameva satpathaḥ śeṣāḥ kupathā iti kva siddham // PSBh_4.18:11
children.translated_text: * He asks: where is it established that this alone is the true path and the rest are false paths? [PSBh 4.18:11]
* Or what makes this a true path? [PSBh 4.18:12]
* And why are the rest false paths? [PSBh 4.18:13]
* The answer is: here. [PSBh 4.18:14]
* Because [the sūtra] states: [PSBh 4.18:15]
Having gone to the proximity of <s>Rudra</s> by this method — [PS 4.19]

children.text: * atra anena ity anapekṣaṇe / vidhinā bhasmasnānakrāthanādinopāyenety arthaḥ // PSBh_4.19:1

children.translated_text: * 'By the method' (<s>vidhinā</s>) — [this is] an instrumental case. [PSBh 4.19:2]
* '<s>Rudra</s>' is stated as a teaching about the time [of attainment]. [PSBh 4.19:3]
* The nature of <s>Rudra</s>'s <s>Rudra</s>-hood has been previously stated. [PSBh 4.19:4]
* 'Proximity' (<s>samīpa</s>) is a synonym for <s>yoga</s> (union). [PSBh 4.19:5]
* How is this understood? [PSBh 4.19:6]
* Because it is stated immediately after the method. [PSBh 4.19:7]

children.text: * sati vidhiviṣayatve puruṣeśvarayor viṣayādhikārakṛtaṃ viyogaṃ dṛṣṭvā jñānaparidṛṣṭena vidhinādhyayanadhyānādhikṛto viśuddhabhāvaḥ samīpastha ityarthaḥ // PSBh_4.19:8
children.translated_text: * When the method applies, having seen the separation between <s>puruṣa</s> (person) and <s>Īśvara</s> (Lord) caused by the difference in their domains — one who is purified in nature, qualified for study and meditation through a method guided by knowledge, stands in proximity [to <s>Rudra</s>]; this is the meaning. [PSBh 4.19:8]
* 'Going' (<s>gati</s>) means the attainment of [this] state — this is the meaning. [PSBh 4.19:9]
* <s>Tvā</s> indicates the completion of the action of the method. [PSBh 4.19:10]

children.text: * āha atraivaṃ vidhyācaraṇaṃ samīpagamanaṃ ca kasyopadiśyate // PSBh_4.19:11
children.translated_text: * He asks: here, for whom is the practice of this method and the approach to proximity taught? [PSBh 4.19:11]
* The answer is: not for everyone, like the <s>dharma</s> of pilgrimage and such. [PSBh 4.19:12]
* Rather, like consecration (<s>saṃskāra</s>), for a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> alone. [PSBh 4.19:13]
* Because [the sūtra] states: [PSBh 4.19:14]
* Here 'by this' (<s>anena</s>) is in the sense of exclusivity; 'by the method' — by the means of ash-bathing, snoring, and so forth; this is the meaning. [PSBh 4.19:1]
No <s>brāhmaṇa</s> whatsoever returns again. [PS 4.20]
* Here the teaching of the negative (<s>na</s>) is for the purpose of prohibiting the adoption of other practices. [PSBh 4.20:1]
* 'Whatsoever' (<s>kaścit</s>) — a householder and such. [PSBh 4.20:2]
* The word 'whatsoever' applies only among <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, from the observation of the distinction of station alone. [PSBh 4.20:3]

children.text: * gṛhastho brahmacārī vānaprastho bhikṣur ekavedo dvivedas trivedaś caturvedo gāyatrīmātrasāro vānena vidhinā rudrasamīpaṃ prāptaḥ san na kaścid brāhmaṇaḥ punarāvartata ityarthaḥ // PSBh_4.20:4
children.translated_text: * A householder, a celibate student, a forest-dweller, a mendicant — whether knowing one <s>Veda</s>, two <s>Vedas</s>, three <s>Vedas</s>, or four <s>Vedas</s>, or one whose essence is merely the <s>Gāyatrī</s> [mantra] — having attained the proximity of <s>Rudra</s> by this method, no <s>brāhmaṇa</s> whatsoever returns again; this is the meaning. [PSBh 4.20:4]

children.text: * brāhmaṇagrahaṇaṃ brāhmaṇyāvadhāraṇārthaṃ brāhmaṇa eva nānya ityarthaḥ // PSBh_4.20:5
children.translated_text: * The mention of '<s>brāhmaṇa</s>' is for the purpose of restricting [this] to a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> alone — 'a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> only, not another'; this is the meaning. [PSBh 4.20:5]
* And the designation '<s>brāhmaṇa</s>' [applies] also to the knower of the field (<s>kṣetrajña</s>). [PSBh 4.20:6]
* Why? [PSBh 4.20:7]

children.text: * upacayajanmayogāt saṃskārayogāt śrutayogāc ca brāhmaṇaḥ // PSBh_4.20:8
children.translated_text: * Because of the connection with accumulation, birth, and <s>yoga</s>, and because of the connection with consecration (<s>saṃskāra</s>) and learning (<s>śruta</s>), he is a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. [PSBh 4.20:8]
* The word 'again' (<s>punaḥ</s>) serves to negate re-return. [PSBh 4.20:9]

children.text: * yathā pūrvasaṃjñānādibhir gatvā āvartate punaḥ punaḥ tathānena vidhinā rudrasamīpaṃ gatvā na sakṛdāvartate // PSBh_4.20:10
children.translated_text: * Just as previously, through innate knowledge and such, having gone [into saṃsāra], one returns again and again — so, having gone to the proximity of <s>Rudra</s> by this method, one does not return even once. [PSBh 4.20:10]

children.text: * punaḥ punaḥ sarvathāpi nāvartata ityarthaḥ // PSBh_4.20:11
children.translated_text: * Again and again, in every way, [the impurity] does not return — this is the meaning. // PSBh 4.20:11

children.text: * āṅ iti svaśāstroktamaryādām adhikurute abhividhyarthaṃ ca // PSBh_4.20:12
children.translated_text: * 'Ā' governs the limit prescribed by one's own scripture, and [indicates] pervasion. // PSBh 4.20:12

children.text: * ye cānena vidhinākṣapitājñānakaluṣapāpamāyādayaḥ kṣīṇāḥ te punaḥ punarāvartante // PSBh_4.20:13
children.translated_text: * And those — ignorance, impurity, sin, illusion (<s>māyā</s>), and the like — which have been destroyed by this method, do not return again and again. // PSBh 4.20:13

children.text: * na taiḥ saha saṃyogo bhavati // PSBh_4.20:14
children.translated_text: * There is no conjunction with them. // PSBh 4.20:14

children.text: * na cāparaṃ janma pratipadyata ityarthaḥ // PSBh_4.20:15
children.translated_text: * And [the practitioner] does not undergo another birth — this is the meaning. // PSBh 4.20:15

children.text: * evam adhyāyaparisamāptiṃ kṛtvā yuktaṃ vaktum // PSBh_4.20:16
children.translated_text: * Thus, having concluded the chapter, it is proper to state: // PSBh 4.20:16
Here one should recite this <s>Brahman</s> [mantra] — || PS 4.21 ||
* Its meaning has been stated above. // PSBh 4.21:1
* He asks: But what then is that <s>Brahman</s>? // PSBh 4.21:2

children.text: * tad ucyate kāraṇādibhāvenoktasya bhagavata ekatvaṃ sādhako jñātvā tatsādhanam ārabhate // PSBh_4.21:3
children.translated_text: * To that it is said: Having known the oneness of the <s>Bhagavān</s> who has been described as the cause and in his various aspects, the practitioner commences [reciting] that which is the means [of attaining him]. // PSBh 4.21:3
We know that <s>Tatpuruṣa</s> (Supreme Person) — || PS 4.22 ||

children.text: * atra pūrvaṃ kāraṇatvabahutvanānātvenopadiṣṭasya parāmarśaḥ tad iti // PSBh_4.22:1
children.translated_text: * Here, 'that' (<s>tat</s>) is a reference back to what was previously taught as the cause in its multiplicity and diversity. // PSBh 4.22:1

children.text: * puruṣa iti pauruṣyānupūraṇāc ca puruṣaḥ // PSBh_4.22:2
children.translated_text: * '<s>Puruṣa</s>' (person) — because of filling with manliness, [he is called] <s>Puruṣa</s>. // PSBh 4.22:2
* His manliness consists in his abiding in many forms. // PSBh 4.22:3
* The forms abiding therein are <s>Aghora</s> and the like. // PSBh 4.22:4
* '<s>Tatpuruṣāya</s>' is a dative case. // PSBh 4.22:5

children.text: * yathā grāmāya tattvaṃ jñātumicchati tathā puruṣāya tattvaṃ jñātumicchati // PSBh_4.22:6
children.translated_text: * Just as [one might say] 'he wishes to know the truth about the village,' so too 'he wishes to know the truth about the <s>Puruṣa</s>.' // PSBh 4.22:6
* 'We know' (<s>vidmahe</s>) — // PSBh 4.22:7
* '<s>Vid</s>' [means] 'to know.' // PSBh 4.22:8
* 'We know, we understand, we perceive' — this is the meaning. // PSBh 4.22:9
* He objects: Because of the multiplicity of <s>puruṣas</s> (persons), there is doubt. // PSBh 4.22:10
* Now, to which <s>Puruṣa</s>? // PSBh 4.22:11
* To that it is said: // PSBh 4.22:12
We meditate on <s>Mahādeva</s> (the Great God) — || PS 4.23 ||

children.text: * atra mahādevatvaṃ ca pūrvoktam mahādevāyeti caturthī // PSBh_4.23:1
children.translated_text: * Here, his <s>Mahādevatva</s> (great-godhood) has been stated above. '<s>Mahādevāya</s>' is a dative case. // PSBh 4.23:1
* 'We meditate' (<s>dhīmahi</s>) — // PSBh 4.23:2
* '<s>Dhī</s>' [means] 'to merge, to unite.' // PSBh 4.23:3

children.text: * dhyāyemahi līyāmahe jñānakriyāśaktibhyāṃ saṃyujyāmaha ityarthaḥ // PSBh_4.23:4
children.translated_text: * 'May we meditate, may we dissolve [into him], may we be united with the powers of knowledge and action' — this is the meaning. // PSBh 4.23:4
* Here, '<s>dhī</s>' is a synonym for the power of knowledge (<s>jñānaśakti</s>). // PSBh 4.23:5

children.text: * yayā sarvapadārthānāṃ tattvamadhigacchati sā jñānaśaktiḥ // PSBh_4.23:6
children.translated_text: * That by which one ascertains the true nature of all objects — that is the power of knowledge. // PSBh 4.23:6
* '<s>Mahi</s>' is a synonym for the power of action (<s>kriyāśakti</s>). // PSBh 4.23:7

children.text: * yayā vidhiyogācaraṇasamartho bhavati sā kriyāśaktirityarthaḥ // PSBh_4.23:8
children.translated_text: * That by which one becomes capable of performing the prescribed <s>yoga</s> practices — that is the power of action; this is the meaning. // PSBh 4.23:8

children.text: * āha athaite dṛkkriyāśaktī mahādevāt sādhakaḥ kiṃ svaśaktita āsādayati āhosvit paraśaktitaḥ utobhayaśaktitaḥ // PSBh_4.23:9
children.translated_text: * He asks: Now, does the practitioner attain these powers of perception and action from <s>Mahādeva</s> through his own power, or through the other's power, or through both powers? // PSBh 4.23:9
* To that it is said: Through the other's power. // PSBh 4.23:10
* Since he says: // PSBh 4.23:11
May <s>Rudra</s> impel us to that — || PS 4.24 ||
* 'That' (<s>tad</s>) refers to the powers of perception and action. // PSBh 4.24:1
* 'Us' (<s>naḥ</s>) designates the self. // PSBh 4.24:2
* 'Of us' — this is the meaning. // PSBh 4.24:3
* '<s>Rudra</s>' designates the cause. // PSBh 4.24:4
* The <s>Rudratva</s> (nature of <s>Rudra</s>) has been stated above. // PSBh 4.24:5
* 'Pra' [indicates] the initial action. // PSBh 4.24:6
* '<s>Cud</s>' [means] 'to impel.' // PSBh 4.24:7
* 'Impelling' (<s>codana</s>) means the conjunction with the powers of knowledge and action. // PSBh 4.24:8
* 'Yāt' [indicates] desire [to obtain]. // PSBh 4.24:9
* 'Unite me [with those powers]' — this is the meaning. // PSBh 4.24:10

children.text: * uktaṃ hi rudrasyecchāpūrvako yo yogo jñānakriyāśaktibhyāṃ paśvādiṣu sambhavaḥ taccodanam āhur ācāryāḥ // PSBh_4.24:11
children.translated_text: * For it has been said: The teachers say that <s>Rudra</s>'s conjunction — preceded by [his] will — with the individual souls and the like through the powers of knowledge and action, that is 'impelling' (<s>codana</s>). // PSBh 4.24:11
<s>Pāśupatasūtra</s>, 5
Non-attachment (<s>asaṅga</s>) — || PS 5.1 ||
* Here, the prefix 'a' negates attachment (<s>saṅga</s>). // PSBh 5.1:1

children.text: * atra saṅgo nāma yadetat puruṣe viṣayitvam // PSBh_5.1:2
children.translated_text: * Here, attachment (<s>saṅga</s>) is that which is the object-directedness in a person. // PSBh 5.1:2

children.text: * tena viṣayitvena yogādadharmeṇa cāyaṃ puruṣo yadā adhyayanadhyānādibhyaścyavati // PSBh_5.1:3
children.translated_text: * When, through this object-directedness and through <s>adharma</s> (demerit), this person falls from study, meditation, and the like [of yoga] — // PSBh 5.1:3

children.text: * dṛṣṭāntaśravaṇaprekṣaṇalakṣaṇo vanagajavat traikālyam ity arthaḥ // PSBh_5.1:4
children.translated_text: * [This is] characterized by seeing, hearing, and observing [sense-objects] — like a wild elephant, throughout the three times; this is the meaning. // PSBh 5.1:4

children.text: * asaṅgitvam apy atītānāgatavartamānānāṃ viṣayāṇāmanucintanaṃ bhikṣuvat // PSBh_5.1:5
children.translated_text: * Non-attachment means also the non-rumination upon objects of the past, future, and present — like a mendicant (<s>bhikṣu</s>). // PSBh 5.1:5
* Thus, the abiding of the mental state in <s>Maheśvara</s> — that is non-attachment; this is the meaning. // PSBh 5.1:6

children.text: * āha kim asaṅgitvam evaikamuktaṃ nānyal lakṣaṇam // PSBh_5.1:7
children.translated_text: * He asks: Is non-attachment alone stated as the single [characteristic], or is there another characteristic? // PSBh 5.1:7
* It is said: Since he says — // PSBh 5.1:8
A <s>yogin</s> — || PS 5.2 ||
* Thus. // PSBh 5.2:1

children.text: * atra yogo nāmātmeśvarasaṃyogo yogaḥ pratyetavyaḥ // PSBh_5.2:2
children.translated_text: * Here, <s>yoga</s> should be understood as the union of the self (<s>ātman</s>) with the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>). // PSBh 5.2:2

children.text: * uktaṃ hi / śaṅkhadundubhinirghoṣair vividhair gativāditaiḥ / kriyamāṇairna budhyeta etad yuktasya lakṣaṇam // PSBh_5.2:3

children.translated_text: * Thus. // PSBh 5.2:4
* He asks: Are only two characteristics of the one absorbed [in yoga] stated here? // PSBh 5.2:5
* No. // PSBh 5.2:6
* Since he says: // PSBh 5.2:7

* For it has been said: 'When sounds of conches, drums, various musical instruments and songs are being produced, [yet] one is not aware [of them] — this is the characteristic of the one absorbed [in yoga].' // PSBh 5.2:3
Of eternal self (<s>nityātman</s>) — || PS 5.3 ||
* Here, by the qualification 'eternal,' impermanence is negated. // PSBh 5.3:1

children.text: * nityatvaṃ nāma sati vibhutve puruṣeśvarayor manasā saha gatasyātmatābhāvasya vṛttyākārasya viṣayaṃ prati kramo 'kṣopo 'vasthānaṃ vṛkṣaśakunivat // PSBh_5.3:2
children.translated_text: * 'Permanence' (<s>nityatva</s>) means: when omnipresence obtains in the <s>puruṣa</s> and <s>Īśvara</s>, together with the mind — the non-disturbance, the stable abiding of the mode of self-nature (<s>ātmatābhāva</s>) that has gone [toward objects] with regard to the object — like a bird on a tree. // PSBh 5.3:2

children.text: * tasmin nirvṛtte maheśvare yukto nitya ityucyate // PSBh_5.3:3
children.translated_text: * When that has ceased [and rests] in <s>Maheśvara</s>, the one absorbed [in yoga] is called 'eternal' (<s>nitya</s>). // PSBh 5.3:3
* '<s>Ātmā</s>' (self) refers to the knower-of-the-field (<s>kṣetrajña</s>). // PSBh 5.3:4
* How is this understood? // PSBh 5.3:5

children.text: * cittasthityupadeśād yogārthaṃ vidyācaraṇopadeśād asaṅgayogiyuktātmājamaitrādīnāṃ cetane sambhavāt na tv acetaneṣu kāryakaraṇapradhānādiṣu // PSBh_5.3:6
children.translated_text: * From the teaching of the stability of the mind, from the teaching of knowledge and conduct for the purpose of <s>yoga</s>, [and] because non-attachment, [being a] <s>yogin</s>, [having an] absorbed self, [being] unborn, friendly, and the like are possible in a conscious [entity], but not in unconscious things such as effects, instruments, or <s>pradhāna</s>. // PSBh 5.3:6
* In that conscious [entity], the word '<s>ātman</s>' (self) [is applied]. // PSBh 5.3:7
* And why [is it called] <s>ātman</s>? // PSBh 5.3:8
* Because it pervades (<s>atati</s>) — [it is called] <s>ātman</s>. // PSBh 5.3:9

children.text: * āpūrya kāryakaraṇaṃ viṣayāṃś cetayatīty ātmā // PSBh_5.3:10
children.translated_text: * Pervading the instruments and effects, it makes the objects conscious — [therefore it is called] <s>ātman</s>. // PSBh 5.3:10

children.text: * uktaṃ hi / yad āpnoti yad ādatte yac cātti viṣayān punaḥ / yac cāsya satataṃ bhāvaḥ tasmādātmeti saṃjñitaḥ // PSBh_5.3:11
* sa ca śrotā spraṣṭā draṣṭā rasayitā ghrātā mantā vaktā boddhā ityevamādiḥ // PSBh_5.3:12
children.translated_text: * And it is the hearer, the toucher, the seer, the taster, the smeller, the thinker, the speaker, the knower — and so forth. // PSBh 5.3:12

children.text:
* uktaṃ hi / puruṣaś cetano bhoktā kṣetrajñaḥ pudgalo janaḥ / aṇur vedo 'mṛtaḥ sākṣī jīvātmā paribhūḥ paraḥ // PSBh_5.3:13
* iti / tasya sukhaduḥkhecchādveṣaprayatnacaitanyādibhir liṅgair adhigamaḥ kriyata ityarthaḥ // PSBh_5.3:14
children.translated_text: * For it has been said: '<s>Puruṣa</s> (person), conscious one, enjoyer, knower-of-the-field (<s>kṣetrajña</s>), individual (<s>pudgala</s>), being, atom, knower, immortal one, witness, <s>jīvātman</s> (living self), all-pervading one, the supreme one' — thus. Its apprehension is accomplished through [its] marks such as pleasure, pain, desire, aversion, effort, consciousness, and the like; this is the meaning. // PSBh 5.3:13-14
* He asks: Are only three characteristics of the one absorbed [in yoga] stated? // PSBh 5.3:15
* No, since he says: // PSBh 5.3:16
* For it has been said: 'That which attains, that which takes, that which again consumes the objects, and that which is its constant state — therefore it is designated <s>ātman</s>.' // PSBh 5.3:11
Unborn (<s>aja</s>) — || PS 5.4 ||
* Here, 'unborn' (<s>aja</s>) denotes the negation of the manifestation of other [mental] objects. // PSBh 5.4:1

* Here, 'other objects' means [objects] other [than the Lord] — sounds, touches, forms, tastes, and smells — [as well as activities such as] study, meditation, recollection, and the like. // PSBh 5.4:2

children.text: * teṣu na jāyata iti ajaḥ // PSBh_5.4:3
children.translated_text: * In them he is not born — therefore [he is called] 'unborn' (<s>aja</s>). // PSBh 5.4:3
* He asks: Are only four characteristics of the one absorbed [in yoga] stated? // PSBh 5.4:4
* No. // PSBh 5.4:5
* Since he says: // PSBh 5.4:6
Friendly (<s>maitra</s>) — || PS 5.5 ||

children.text: * atra maitra iti samatāyāṃ bhavati // PSBh_5.5:1
children.translated_text: * Here, 'friendly' (<s>maitra</s>) indicates impartiality (<s>samatā</s>). // PSBh 5.5:1
* As [for example], the sun is friendly [to all]. // PSBh 5.5:2

children.text: * sarvabhūtasthite ca maheśvare sthitacittaḥ icchādveṣavinivṛtto 'pravṛttimān maitra ityucyate // PSBh_5.5:3
children.translated_text: * And with the mind fixed on <s>Maheśvara</s> who abides in all beings, free from desire and aversion, without [further] activity — [such a one] is called 'friendly' (<s>maitra</s>). // PSBh 5.5:3

children.text: * tasmāt kāryakaraṇavān eva cittasthitisamakālam evāsaṅgādibhāvena jāyate // PSBh_5.5:4
children.translated_text: * Therefore, while still possessing instruments and effects, simultaneously with the stability of the mind, [the practitioner] is born in the state of non-attachment and the like. // PSBh 5.5:4

children.text: * āha atha kathaṃ punaretad gamyate // PSBh_5.5:5
children.translated_text: * He asks: Now, how is this understood — // PSBh 5.5:5

children.text: * yathā kāryakaraṇavān eva cittasthitisamakālam evāsaṅgādibhāvena jāyate // PSBh_5.5:6
children.translated_text: * that while still possessing instruments and effects, simultaneously with the stability of the mind, [one] is born in the state of non-attachment and the like? // PSBh 5.5:6
* It is said: It is understood. // PSBh 5.5:7
* Since he says: // PSBh 5.5:8
Is born [in that state] (<s>abhijāyate</s>) — || PS 5.6 ||
* Here, the prefix 'abhi' [indicates] specification. // PSBh 5.6:1
* What specification? one might ask. // PSBh 5.6:2
* To that it is said: // PSBh 5.6:3

children.text: * yasmādayaṃ saṅgī ayogī anityātmā anajo 'maitraś ca bhūtvā asaṅgādibhāvena jāyata ityeṣa viśeṣaḥ // PSBh_5.6:4
children.translated_text: * Because this one, having been attached, not a <s>yogin</s>, of non-eternal self, not unborn, and not friendly — [now] is born in the state of non-attachment and the like; this is the specification. // PSBh 5.6:4
* 'Is born' (<s>jāyate</s>) — // PSBh 5.6:5
* '<s>Janī</s>' [means] 'to manifest.' // PSBh 5.6:6

children.text: * tasmāt kāryakaraṇavān eva cittasthitisamakālam evāsaṅgādibhāvena yugapaj jāyate avaśyādivad ityarthaḥ // PSBh_5.6:7
children.translated_text: * Therefore, while still possessing instruments and effects, simultaneously with the stability of the mind, [the practitioner] is born in the state of non-attachment and the like all at once — like [the onset of] dew; this is the meaning. // PSBh 5.6:7

children.text: * asaṅgādibhāve ko 'sāv abhyupāyo yena jāyate // PSBh_5.6:8
children.translated_text: * What is the means by which one is born in the state of non-attachment and the like? // PSBh 5.6:8
* It is said: // PSBh 5.6:9
Through the conquest of the senses — || PS 5.7 ||
* Here, the state of being conquered is the conquest (<s>jaya</s>). // PSBh 5.7:1
* Therefore, from that conquest, non-attachment and the like arise. // PSBh 5.7:2

children.text: * atra parigrahatayeśvarāṇi indriyāṇi buddhyādīni vāgantāni trayodaśa karaṇāni // PSBh_5.7:3
children.translated_text: * Here, 'senses' (<s>indriyāṇi</s>) means the thirteen instruments (<s>karaṇa</s>) — from <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) down to speech — which belong [to the Lord] by way of possession. // PSBh 5.7:3
* Through their conquest — this is the meaning. // PSBh 5.7:4
* He asks: How is [the existence of] <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) established? // PSBh 5.7:5
* To that it is said: Because it is established [by evidence]. // PSBh 5.7:6

children.text: * atra matibuddhipidhānasthāpanoddeśād ghaṭapaṭavat siddhatvāc ca buddhiḥ siddhā tathā paropadeśāt svātmaparātmaprativibhāgadarśanāt suro'haṃ naro'hamiti bhinnavṛttitvāc cāhaṃkāraḥ siddhaḥ // PSBh_5.7:7
children.translated_text: * Here, from the teaching of 'mind' (<s>mati</s>), 'intellect' (<s>buddhi</s>), 'covering,' 'establishing,' and 'indicating' — like a pot or a cloth, <s>buddhi</s> is established because it is [thus] demonstrated. Likewise, from the teaching of others and from the observation of the distinction between one's own self and another's self — 'I am a god,' 'I am a man' — <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego) is established because of having differentiated functions. // PSBh 5.7:7

children.text: * tathā manaḥ pravartate manojavī mano'mana iti saṃkalpavikalpavṛttinānātvaṃ ca siddham // PSBh_5.7:8
children.translated_text: * Likewise, [from the expressions] 'the mind operates,' 'swift as mind,' 'mind [is] not-mind' — the diversity of the functions of resolve and doubt [shows that] <s>manas</s> (mind) is established. // PSBh 5.7:8
* Thus the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) of the <s>puruṣa</s>, functioning in the three times, has been explained. // PSBh 5.7:9
* Likewise, among the cognitive senses (<s>buddhīndriya</s>), hearing (<s>śrotra</s>) has been explained: // PSBh 5.7:10

children.text: * paraparivādādivacanād uccairubhayathā pramukhe dvir adhiṣṭhāne saṃniviṣṭaṃ sāmantācchabdavyañjanasamarthaṃ siddham // PSBh_5.7:11
children.translated_text: * From the teaching of speaking ill of others, [hearing] in both ways [positive and negative], loudly, in the front, situated in two locations, in the vicinity — capable of apprehending sound and syllable — it is established. // PSBh 5.7:11

children.text: * tathātitapopadeśāt tvag antarbahiśca śarīraṃ vyāpya saṃniviṣṭā sparśavyañjanasamarthā siddhā // PSBh_5.7:12
children.translated_text: * Likewise, from the teaching of extreme austerity, the skin (<s>tvak</s>), pervading the body internally and externally, situated [throughout], capable of apprehending touch — is established. // PSBh 5.7:12

children.text: * tathā mūtrapurīṣadarśanapratiṣedhāt kṛtānnādivacanāc ca cakṣuḥ uccair ubhayathā pramukhe dvir adhiṣṭhāne saṃniviṣṭaṃ ghaṭarūpādi vyañjanasamarthaṃ siddham // PSBh_5.7:13
children.translated_text: * Likewise, from the prohibition of seeing excrement and urine, and from the statement about prepared food and the like, the eye (<s>cakṣus</s>), in both ways, loudly, in the front, situated in two locations — capable of apprehending the form of pots and the like — is established. // PSBh 5.7:13

children.text: * tathā māṃsalavaṇopadeśāj jihvā tanmukhe māṃsapeśyāṃ saṃniviṣṭā rasajñānajananasamarthā siddhā // PSBh_5.7:14
children.translated_text: * Likewise, from the teaching about meat and salt, the tongue (<s>jihvā</s>), situated in the mouth, on the fleshy mass — capable of generating the knowledge of taste — is established. // PSBh 5.7:14

children.text: * tathā prāṇāyāmopadeśād ghrāṇaṃ pramukhe uccairubhayathā dvir adhiṣṭhāne saṃniviṣṭaṃ gandhagrahaṇasamarthaṃ siddham // PSBh_5.7:15
children.translated_text: * Likewise, from the teaching of <s>prāṇāyāma</s>, the nose (<s>ghrāṇa</s>), in the front, in both ways, loudly, situated in two locations — capable of apprehending smell — is established. // PSBh 5.7:15

children.text: * evamadhikārivṛttibhirbudhyaty ebhiḥ puruṣa iti buddhīndriyāṇi // PSBh_5.7:16
children.translated_text: * Thus, the <s>puruṣa</s> cognizes by these [senses] with their authoritative functions — therefore they are called cognitive senses (<s>buddhīndriya</s>). // PSBh 5.7:16
* Likewise, the action senses (<s>karmendriya</s>): // PSBh 5.7:17

children.text: * maṇṭanaviharaṇopadeśāt pādendriyam adhastād dvir adhiṣṭhāne saṃniviṣṭaṃ gamanakriyāsamarthaṃ siddham // PSBh_5.7:18
children.translated_text: * From the teaching of limping and moving about, the foot-faculty (<s>pādendriya</s>), below, situated in two locations — capable of the action of locomotion — is established. // PSBh 5.7:18

children.text: * tathā mūtrapurīṣadarśanapratiṣedhāt pāyvindriyaṃ guhyapradeśe saṃniviṣṭam utsargakriyāsamarthaṃ siddham // PSBh_5.7:19
children.translated_text: * Likewise, from the prohibition of seeing excrement and urine, the excretory faculty (<s>pāyvindriya</s>), situated in the private region — capable of the action of elimination — is established. // PSBh 5.7:19

children.text: * tathā strīpratiṣedhād upasthendriyaṃ trivalīguhyapradeśasaṃniviṣṭam ānandakriyāsamarthaṃ siddham // PSBh_5.7:20
children.translated_text: * Likewise, from the prohibition of women, the generative faculty (<s>upasthendriya</s>), situated in the private region of the three folds — capable of the action of pleasure — is established. // PSBh 5.7:20

children.text: * tathā api tatkarmopadeśāt hastendriyam uccairubhayathā dvir adhiṣṭhāne bhujāntardeśe saṃniviṣṭam ādānakriyāsamarthaṃ siddham // PSBh_5.7:21
children.translated_text: * Likewise, from the teaching of 'also that action,' the hand-faculty (<s>hastendriya</s>), in both ways, loudly, situated in two locations in the region between the arms — capable of the action of grasping — is established. // PSBh 5.7:21

children.text: * tathā api tadbhāṣaṇopadeśād vāgindriyaṃ vāktālujihvādiṣu sthāneṣu saṃniviṣṭaṃ vacanakriyāsamarthaṃ siddham // PSBh_5.7:22
children.translated_text: * Likewise, from the teaching of 'also that speech,' the speech-faculty (<s>vāgindriya</s>), situated in the locations of the palate, tongue, and the like — capable of the action of speaking — is established. // PSBh 5.7:22

children.text: * atra vikāratadvṛttibhiḥ karmotpattiḥ puruṣe iti karmendriyāṇi evametāni trayodaśa karaṇānīndriyāṇi sūtrato vyākhyātāni // PSBh_5.7:23
children.translated_text: * Here, through the modifications and their activities, action arises in the person — thus these thirteen instruments (<s>karaṇa</s>) are the senses (<s>indriya</s>), explained from the <s>sūtra</s>. // PSBh 5.7:23
* Why? // PSBh 5.7:24

children.text: * indriyāṇāmiti sāmānyagrahaṇād vikaraṇavat sāmānyapratiṣedhāc ca // PSBh_5.7:25
children.translated_text: * Because of the general reference 'of the senses,' and because of the general negation like [that of] dissolution (<s>vikaraṇa</s>). // PSBh 5.7:25
* 'Of the senses' (<s>indriyāṇām</s>) is a genitive plural. // PSBh 5.7:26

children.text: * uktaṃ hi / ādānād grahaṇāt tyāgād raṅgaṇād gamanāt tathā / iṅganādravaṇāc caiva tasmād indriyamucyate // PSBh_5.7:27

children.translated_text: * 'Through conquest' (<s>abhijayāt</s>) — // PSBh 5.7:28
* The prefix '<s>abhi</s>' is used in the sense of complete victory and subjugation. // PSBh 5.7:29
* [The senses] are to be overcome and subjugated. // PSBh 5.7:30
* Like wind, desire, anger, and <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>. // PSBh 5.7:31

children.text: * tasmād akuśalebhyo vyāvartayitvā kāmataḥ kuśalaṃ yojitāni tadā jitāni bhavanti // PSBh_5.7:32
children.translated_text: * Therefore, having turned [them] away from the unwholesome (<s>akuśala</s>) and having at will yoked them to the wholesome (<s>kuśala</s>) — then they become conquered. // PSBh 5.7:32

children.text: * tasmād uktam indriyāṇām abhijayāditi asaṅgādijanmanimittatvāt pañcamī draṣṭavyā // PSBh_5.7:33
children.translated_text: * Therefore it is said: 'Through the conquest of the senses.' The fifth [case ending, ablative] should be understood as indicating the cause, [namely] non-attachment and the like. // PSBh 5.7:33

children.text: * āha anyatra sāṃkhyayogādīnām asaṅgādiyuktāḥ muktāḥ śāntiṃ prāptāḥ // PSBh_5.7:34
children.translated_text: * He objects: Elsewhere, in <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, <s>Yoga</s>, and other [systems], those endowed with non-attachment and the like are [considered] liberated, having attained peace. // PSBh 5.7:34

children.text: * nirabhilapyā muktā ityucyante mukta eva na yukta iti kva siddham // PSBh_5.7:35
children.translated_text: * They are said to be liberated — indescribable, liberated — that they are only liberated, not [still] yoked [in union] — where is this established? // PSBh 5.7:35
* To that it is said: here — because he states: // PSBh 5.7:36
* For it has been said: 'Because of taking, grasping, abandoning, delighting, going, moving, and flowing — therefore it is called a sense (<s>indriya</s>).' // PSBh 5.7:27
<s>Rudra</s> has thus declared. || PS 5.8 ||
* There, '<s>Rudra</s>' indicates the cause. // PSBh 5.8:1
* The <s>Rudra</s>-nature [of <s>Rudra</s>] has been previously stated. // PSBh 5.8:2
* The prefix '<s>pra</s>' is used in the sense of clarity of expression. // PSBh 5.8:3
* Like 'clear-sensed' (<s>prasannendriya</s>). // PSBh 5.8:4
* '<s>Vaca</s>' [is used] in the sense of manifest speech. // PSBh 5.8:5
* 'He declared' (<s>provāca</s>). // PSBh 5.8:6

children.text: * evaṃ yat sāṃkhyaṃ yogaśca varṇayati asaṅgādiyuktāḥ muktāḥ śāntiṃ prāptā iti tadaviśuddhaṃ teṣāṃ darśanam // PSBh_5.8:7
children.translated_text: * Thus, what <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and <s>Yoga</s> describe — that those endowed with non-attachment and the like are liberated and have attained peace — that is an impure view of theirs. // PSBh 5.8:7
* Like the vision of one afflicted with an eye-disease seeing [multiple] moons. // PSBh 5.8:8

children.text: * ayaṃ tu yukta eva na mukta iti viśuddhametaddarśanaṃ draṣṭavyam // PSBh_5.8:9
children.translated_text: * But this [Pāśupata view] — that he is still yoked [in union], not liberated — this should be regarded as the pure view. // PSBh 5.8:9
* Why? // PSBh 5.8:10
* This is understood from the word of the omniscient one, and because it is non-contradictory. // PSBh 5.8:11
* It is so, not otherwise — this is the meaning. // PSBh 5.8:12

children.text: * kiṃcānyad idam athaśabdādi śivāntaṃ pravacanaṃ rudraproktaṃ tāvat sarvatantrāṇāṃ śreṣṭham // PSBh_5.8:13
children.translated_text: * Moreover, this teaching (<s>pravacana</s>), beginning with the word '<s>atha</s>' and ending with '<s>Śiva</s>,' spoken by <s>Rudra</s>, is the most excellent of all treatises (<s>tantra</s>). // PSBh 5.8:13
