* Therefore, the supreme authoritativeness of both the cause and the treatise is to be firmly ascertained — this is the meaning. // PSBh 5.8:14
* Here [follows] a verse of explanation. // PSBh 5.8:15

children.text: * āha kim etānīndriyāṇi parijñānamātrād eva jitāni bhavanti pradhānavat // PSBh_5.8:16
children.translated_text: * He asks: Are these senses conquered merely through complete knowledge, like <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter [in <s>Sāṃkhya</s>])? // PSBh 5.8:16

children.text: * taducyate na jñānena vacanādibhireṣāṃ jayaḥ kartavyaḥ yasmādeṣāṃ jaye bhagavatā vasatyarthavṛttibalakriyālābhāya vasatā ityatas tajjaye vasatyartha eva tāvad ucyate // PSBh_5.8:17
children.translated_text: * To that it is said: The conquest of these [senses] is not to be accomplished by knowledge or speech and the like; because, for their conquest, the Blessed One has [prescribed] dwelling — for the purpose of obtaining the activity of strength and meaning in dwelling — and thus dwelling itself is the first [requirement] for their conquest. // PSBh 5.8:17
* Because he states: // PSBh 5.8:18
One who dwells in an empty house or a cave (<s>śūnyāgāraguhāvāsī</s>). || PS 5.9 ||
* Thus. // PSBh 5.9:1
* Here, an empty house itself is the '<s>śūnyāgāra</s>.' // PSBh 5.9:2
* 'Empty' (<s>śūnya</s>) means solitary, deserted, without people — this is the meaning. // PSBh 5.9:3

children.text: * āgāram iti gṛhaparyāyaḥ āgāraṃ gṛhaṃ veśma sadanamiti paryāyaḥ // PSBh_5.9:4
children.translated_text: * '<s>Āgāra</s>' is a synonym for house — '<s>āgāra</s>,' '<s>gṛha</s>,' '<s>veśma</s>,' '<s>sadana</s>' are synonyms. // PSBh 5.9:4
* '<s>Guhū</s>' [is used] in the sense of covering. // PSBh 5.9:5

children.text: * praviṣṭaṃ sādhakam āvarayati gopayatīti guhā // PSBh_5.9:6
children.translated_text: * A cave (<s>guhā</s>) is that which covers and conceals the practitioner who has entered [it]. // PSBh 5.9:6

children.text: * āha āvarakatvāviśeṣāc chūnyāgāraguhayor aviśeṣa iti cet taducyate mṛttṛṇakāṣṭhādikṛtam agāraṃ parvataguhādyā guhā // PSBh_5.9:7
children.translated_text: * He objects: Since there is no difference in the covering function between an empty house and a cave — to that it is said: A house is made of clay, grass, wood, and the like; a cave is a mountain cave and the like. // PSBh 5.9:7
* Therefore, there is no non-distinction. // PSBh 5.9:8

children.text: * yathā sati vibhutve jñatvaṃ sādharmyaṃ puruṣeśvarayoḥ sarvajñatvato viśeṣaḥ // PSBh_5.9:9
children.translated_text: * Just as, when all-pervasiveness exists, the person and the Lord share the similarity of being knowers, [but] omniscience is the distinction. // PSBh 5.9:9

children.text: * tasmād āyatane 'viviktadoṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā śūnyāgāre guhāyāṃ vā yathopapattito vicārya viviktaṃ vivecya yanmātrasthānāsanaśayanādibhir upajīvati tanmātraṃ saṃskaraṇamaryādayopayogakriyābhiniviṣṭena vastavyam // PSBh_5.9:10
children.translated_text: * Therefore, having observed the defect of non-solitude in the sanctuary, and having deliberated according to circumstances, whether in an empty house or a cave — with just as much as is needed for standing, sitting, lying down, and the like — one should dwell, absorbed in the activities of purification, in accordance with the boundary of consecration. // PSBh 5.9:10
* Through conjunction with dwelling, one becomes a cave-dweller (<s>guhāvāsī</s>). // PSBh 5.9:11
* Like a sandbank-dweller (<s>pulinavāsin</s>). // PSBh 5.9:12

children.text: * āha tat kathaṃ jñeyaṃ yathā jitānīndriyāṇi // PSBh_5.9:13
children.translated_text: * He asks: How is it to be known that the senses are conquered? // PSBh 5.9:13

children.text: * teṣāṃ jitānāṃ vā kiṃ lakṣaṇam // PSBh_5.9:14
children.translated_text: * Or what is the mark of those [senses] being conquered? // PSBh 5.9:14
* To that it is said: // PSBh 5.9:15
Constant [union] with the deity (<s>devanitya</s>). || PS 5.10 ||
* Here, the 'god' (<s>deva</s>) is the Blessed Lord. // PSBh 5.10:1

children.text: * tatra yadāsya bhagavati deve nityatā katham // PSBh_5.10:2
children.translated_text: * There, when he has constancy (<s>nityatā</s>) in the Blessed Lord — how [is this achieved]? // PSBh 5.10:2

children.text: * adhyayanadhyānābhyāṃ deve 'dhikṛtasya prādhānyena niścalatā vartate // PSBh_5.10:3
children.translated_text: * Through study (<s>adhyayana</s>) and meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), for one who is primarily established in the deity, unwavering stability prevails. // PSBh 5.10:3
* Even with the slightest interruption, through the continuous attainment of intensive <s>yoga</s> practice — // PSBh 5.10:4
* memory (<s>smṛti</s>) is the [meaning of] 'constant [union] with the deity' — this is the meaning. // PSBh 5.10:5
* He asks: What is the mark of constancy with the deity? // PSBh 5.10:6
* To that it is said: Mastery of the senses (<s>jitendriyatva</s>). // PSBh 5.10:7
* Because he states: // PSBh 5.10:8
One who has conquered the senses (<s>jitendriya</s>). || PS 5.11 ||
* Here, mastery of the senses (<s>jitendriyatva</s>) means the capacity for both releasing and restraining [them]. // PSBh 5.11:1

children.text: * indriyāṇi buddhyādīni vāgantāni trayodaśa karaṇāni pūrvoktāni // PSBh_5.11:2
children.translated_text: * The senses — the thirteen instruments beginning with intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) and ending with speech — have been previously stated. // PSBh 5.11:2

children.text: * tāni yadā akuśalebhyo vyāvartayitvā kāmataḥ kuśale yojitāni hataviṣadarvīkaravad avasthitāni bhavanti tadā devanityo jitendriya ityarthaḥ // PSBh_5.11:3
children.translated_text: * When [the senses] have been turned away from the unwholesome and at will yoked to the wholesome, and stand like a snake whose venom has been extracted — then one is 'constant with the deity' and 'one who has conquered the senses' — this is the meaning. // PSBh 5.11:3

children.text: * āha kiṃ devanityataivāsya paro niṣṭhāyogaḥ // PSBh_5.11:4
children.translated_text: * He asks: Is constancy with the deity his final and supreme <s>yoga</s>? // PSBh 5.11:4
* It is said: No. // PSBh 5.11:5
* Because he states: // PSBh 5.11:6
For one constantly yoked for six months — || PS 5.12 ||
* Or alternatively, [this sūtra has] a different, remote connection. // PSBh 5.12:1

children.text: * yasmāduktam / yasya yenārthasambandho dūrasthamapi tena hi / arthato 'nyasamānānām ānantarye 'pyasaṃgatiḥ // PSBh_5.12:2

children.translated_text: * Thus, here too there is a remote connection. Why? // PSBh 5.12:3

children.text: * iha purastāduktaṃ vijñānāni cāsya pravartante iti etair guṇair yukta iti ca // PSBh_5.12:4
children.translated_text: * Here it was previously stated: 'His discernments arise' and 'endowed with these qualities.' // PSBh 5.12:4

children.text: * kiyatā kālenāsya te guṇāḥ pravartante // PSBh_5.12:5
children.translated_text: * In what length of time do those qualities arise for him? // PSBh 5.12:5

children.text: * kiṃ yuktasya kiṃ viyuktasya kiṃ yugapat kramaśo vā kiṃ sakalasya niṣkalasya veti // PSBh_5.12:6
children.translated_text: * [Questions:] For one who is yoked or unyoked? All at once or sequentially? For one who is complete (<s>sakala</s>) or incomplete (<s>niṣkala</s>)? // PSBh 5.12:6
* For the purpose of explaining these unexplained matters, this [sūtra] is commenced. // PSBh 5.12:7
* Because he states: 'For one constantly yoked for six months.' // PSBh 5.12:8

children.text: * atra ṣaḍ iti saṃkhyā māsān iti kālanirdeśaḥ // PSBh_5.12:9
children.translated_text: * Here, 'six' (<s>ṣaḍ</s>) is a number; 'months' (<s>māsān</s>) is a designation of time. // PSBh 5.12:9
* By human reckoning, a month is thirty days. // PSBh 5.12:10
* Twelve months make a year. // PSBh 5.12:11
* Twelve fortnights make a half-year. // PSBh 5.12:12
* 'Six months' (<s>ṣaṇmāsān</s>). // PSBh 5.12:13
* Therefore, within [the period] between the sixth and first months. // PSBh 5.12:14
* 'For one constantly yoked' (<s>nityayuktasya</s>) — // PSBh 5.12:15
* means continuously, without interruption — this is the meaning. // PSBh 5.12:16
* 'Yoked' (<s>yukta</s>) — // PSBh 5.12:17
* <s>yoga</s> is the union of the self (<s>ātman</s>) and the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>). // PSBh 5.12:18
* 'Of one constantly yoked' (<s>nityayuktasya</s>) — [this is] a genitive [case]. // PSBh 5.12:19

children.text: * āha asya yuktasya kiṃ bhavati // PSBh_5.12:20
children.translated_text: * He asks: What happens for this one who is yoked? // PSBh 5.12:20
* To that it is said: // PSBh 5.12:21

* Because it has been said: 'For one whose purpose is connected with something, even if remote — the arising of that purpose is the same. For those of a different nature though equal in proximity, there is no connection.' // PSBh 5.12:2
[The qualities] arise abundantly (<s>bhūyiṣṭham</s>). || PS 5.13 ||

children.text: * atra bhūyiṣṭham iti krame prāye ca bhavati // PSBh_5.13:1
children.translated_text: * Here, 'abundantly' (<s>bhūyiṣṭham</s>) is used in the sense of sequence and preponderance. // PSBh 5.13:1

children.text: * yathā kramaśo dadāti ādityo vā gato bhūyiṣṭham // PSBh_5.13:2
children.translated_text: * As one gives sequentially — or like the sun that has risen [gradually spreading light] abundantly. // PSBh 5.13:2

children.text: * tasmāt sūcyagreṇotpalapattraśatabhedanakramavat kramād dūradarśanādayaḥ pravartanta ityarthaḥ // PSBh_5.13:3
children.translated_text: * Therefore, like the sequential piercing of a hundred lotus petals with the tip of a needle — far-seeing (<s>dūradarśana</s>) and the other [powers] arise sequentially — this is the meaning. // PSBh 5.13:3
* '<s>Sam</s>' is used in the sense of unification. // PSBh 5.13:4
* [This means:] for one who is incomplete (<s>niṣkala</s>), free from effects and instruments — this is the meaning. // PSBh 5.13:5
* '<s>Pra</s>' is used in the sense of initial action, [indicating] commencement. // PSBh 5.13:6

children.text: * yuktottare prabhāvād guṇāḥ pravartante ityarthaḥ // PSBh_5.13:7
children.translated_text: * Combined with the preceding [discussion], the qualities arise through power — this is the meaning. // PSBh 5.13:7
* In what [do they] operate? // PSBh 5.13:8
* Seeing [operates] in the visible; hearing and the rest in the audible and the rest — this is the meaning. // PSBh 5.13:9

children.text: * tasmāt ṣaṣṭhaprathamamāsayorabhyantare nityayuktasya kramaśo guṇāḥ sampravartante // PSBh_5.13:10
children.translated_text: * Therefore, within [the period] between the sixth and first months, for one who is constantly yoked, the qualities arise sequentially. // PSBh 5.13:10
* From what [source do they arise]? // PSBh 5.13:11
* From the grace of <s>Maheśvara</s>. // PSBh 5.13:12

children.text: * aśivatvasaṃjñake vinivṛtte śivatvaprasādābhyāṃ guṇāḥ pravartante // PSBh_5.13:13
children.translated_text: * When the state of non-auspiciousness (<s>aśivatva</s>) has ceased, the qualities arise through auspiciousness (<s>śivatva</s>) and grace (<s>prasāda</s>). // PSBh 5.13:13
* The word 'qualities' (<s>guṇa</s>) refers to far-seeing (<s>dūradarśana</s>) and the like. // PSBh 5.13:14

children.text: * āha kāṃ vṛttimāsthāya śūnyāgāre guhāyāṃ vāsaḥ kāryaḥ // PSBh_5.13:15
children.translated_text: * He asks: Adopting what mode of livelihood should one dwell in an empty house or cave? // PSBh 5.13:15
* To that it is said: // PSBh 5.13:16
Alms-food (<s>bhaikṣya</s>). || PS 5.14 ||
* A collection of alms (<s>bhikṣā</s>) is alms-food (<s>bhaikṣya</s>) — like the pigeon manner (<s>kāpota</s>). // PSBh 5.14:1

children.text: * tac ca nagaragrāmādibhyo gṛhād gṛhaṃ paryaṭato bhakṣyabhojyādīnām anyatamaṃ yat prāpyate kṛtānnādivacanād bhaikṣyam // PSBh_5.14:2
children.translated_text: * And that [alms-food] is any of the edible, eatable, and other [kinds of food] that is obtained while wandering from house to house in towns, villages, and the like — because of the mention of prepared food and the like — that is alms-food (<s>bhaikṣya</s>). // PSBh 5.14:2
* Because of destroying fear (<s>bhayakṣapaṇa</s>), it is called alms-food (<s>bhaikṣya</s>). // PSBh 5.14:3
* Because of the mention of alms (<s>bhikṣā</s>), non-alms is prohibited. // PSBh 5.14:4

children.text: * āha ādhārāttu kṛtvā saṃdehaḥ atha kutra tad bhaikṣyaṃ grāhyam // PSBh_5.14:5
children.translated_text: * He asks: As to the vessel — since there is doubt — where should that alms-food be received? // PSBh 5.14:5
* To that it is said: In a vessel (<s>pātra</s>). // PSBh 5.14:6
* Because he states: // PSBh 5.14:7
Received in a vessel (<s>pātrāgatam</s>). || PS 5.15 ||
* Here, like alms-food, the vessel (<s>pātra</s>) is well known. // PSBh 5.14:1

children.text: * alābudāruvastrādīnām anyatamaṃ yat prāpyate tat khalu hiṃsāsteyādirahitena krameṇāhāre yatparyāptaṃ grāhyam // PSBh_5.15:2
children.translated_text: * Whatever vessel is obtained — whether of gourd, wood, cloth, or the like — one should take [only] what is sufficient for food, through a process free from violence (<s>hiṃsā</s>) and theft (<s>steya</s>) and the like. // PSBh 5.15:2

children.text: * tasmin tadaphalake pātre āgataṃ pātrāgatamityarthaḥ // PSBh_5.15:3
children.translated_text: * 'Received in the vessel' (<s>pātrāgatam</s>) means that which has arrived in that fruitless [i.e., simple] vessel — this is the meaning. // PSBh 5.15:3
* He objects: In the manner of a celibate student, [one should avoid] honey, meat, and salt. // PSBh 5.15:4

children.text: * tat kiṃ madhumāṃsādīny ekāntenaiva duṣṭānīti // PSBh_5.15:5
children.translated_text: * Is it that honey, meat, and the like are absolutely prohibited? // PSBh 5.15:5
* To that it is said: No. // PSBh 5.15:6
* Because he states: // PSBh 5.15:7
Meat is not blameworthy, nor [food taken] with salt. || PS 5.16 ||
* There, meat (<s>māṃsa</s>) is well known, like alms-food. // PSBh 5.16:1

children.text: * yasya māhiṣavārāhādīnām anyatamaṃ yat prāpyate tat khalu hiṃsāsteyarahitatvāt // PSBh_5.16:2
children.translated_text: * Whatever meat is obtained — whether of buffalo, boar, or the like — that is [acceptable] because it is free from violence and theft. // PSBh 5.16:2
* 'Or with salt' (<s>lavaṇena vā</s>) — // PSBh 5.16:3

children.text: * atra lavaṇaṃ nāma saindhavasauvarcalādyaṃ māṃsavat prasiddham // PSBh_5.16:4
children.translated_text: * Here, salt (<s>lavaṇa</s>) means rock salt (<s>saindhava</s>), <s>sauvarcala</s> salt, and the like — well known like meat. // PSBh 5.16:4

children.text: * tad etan māṃsasamasaṃsṛṣṭaṃ vā bhaikṣyavidhinā prāptam // PSBh_5.16:5
children.translated_text: * That [food], whether mixed with meat or combined [with salt], obtained according to the rule of alms-food — // PSBh 5.16:5
* is 'not blameworthy' (<s>aduṣya</s>) — not contemptible, not censurable — this is the meaning. // PSBh 5.16:6
* '<s>Vā</s>' (or) is used in the sense of an alternative. // PSBh 5.16:7

children.text: * māṃsena vā lavaṇena vā ubhābhyāmapi sākṣādvā aduṣyam ityarthaḥ // PSBh_5.16:8
children.translated_text: * With meat or with salt or with both, or directly — it is not blameworthy — this is the meaning. // PSBh 5.16:8

children.text: * āha bhaikṣyālābhakāle aparyāptikāle vā kimanena kartavyam // PSBh_5.16:9
children.translated_text: * He asks: At the time when alms-food is not obtained, or when it is insufficient — what should one do? // PSBh 5.16:9
* To that it is said: One should drink water and remain. // PSBh 5.16:10
* Because he states: // PSBh 5.16:11
Or one should eat water at the proper time, in due order. || PS 5.17 ||
* Here, '<s>āṇ</s>' [yields] waters (<s>āpaḥ</s>). // PSBh 5.17:1

children.text: * āṅ iti atra saṃvṛtaparipūtādimaryādām adhikurute kṛtānnotsṛṣṭavad apadāntaritatvāt // PSBh_5.17:2
children.translated_text: * The prefix '<s>āṅ</s>' here governs the boundary of [water that is] covered, purified, and the like — because it is not separated from [the condition of] prepared food, like [food that has been] properly set aside. // PSBh 5.17:2
* The nominative case should be understood in place of the accusative. // PSBh 5.17:3
* Water (<s>āpaḥ</s>) here is well known in worldly usage and the like. // PSBh 5.17:4
* Water that is free from grass and the like — this is the meaning. // PSBh 5.17:5
* '<s>Vā</s>' (or) is used in the sense of distinction. // PSBh 5.17:6

children.text: * anyad bhaikṣyam anyā āpa iti // PSBh_5.17:7
children.translated_text: * Alms-food is one thing, water is another. [PSBh 5.17:7]
* The word <s>api</s> ('even') is in the sense of honoring. [PSBh 5.17:8]

children.text: * apy apaḥ pītvā stheyaṃ na tu śāstravyapetena krameṇa vṛttyarjanaṃ kartavyamityarthaḥ // PSBh_5.17:9
children.translated_text: * Even having drunk water, one should remain — but one should not seek livelihood by a method contrary to the scripture; this is the meaning. [PSBh 5.17:9]
* The word <s>yathā</s> ('just as') is in the sense of equivalence. [PSBh 5.17:10]

children.text: * yathā bhaikṣyopadeśaṃ kṛtvā yogakarmaṇyudyamaḥ kartavya iti vyākhyātaṃ tathā apaḥ pītveti // PSBh_5.17:11
children.translated_text: * Just as it has been explained that, having given the teaching on alms, effort in the practice of <s>yoga</s> should be made — so too with 'having drunk water.' [PSBh 5.17:11]
* The time here is of two kinds: the time of non-obtainment and the time of insufficiency. [PSBh 5.17:12]

children.text: * tatra yadā grāmaṃ nagaraṃ vā kṛtsnamaṭitvā na kiṃcidāsādayati saḥ alābhakālaḥ aparyāptikālo nāma yadā bhikṣāṃ bhikṣādvayaṃ vā āsādayati tadā apaḥ pītvāpi stheyam // PSBh_5.17:13
children.translated_text: * There, when having wandered through an entire village or city one obtains nothing — that is the time of non-obtainment. The time of insufficiency is when one obtains one or two alms-portions — then one should remain even having drunk water. [PSBh 5.17:13]

children.text: * āha evaṃ sthitena kimanena kartavyam // PSBh_5.17:14
children.translated_text: * He asks: what should be done by one who remains thus? [PSBh 5.17:14]
* The answer is: one should consume [food]. [PSBh 5.17:15]
* Because [the sūtra] states: 'one should eat in proper sequence.' [PSBh 5.17:16]
* 'One should eat' — this refers to the limit of lightness in food without obstruction to the practice of <s>yoga</s>. [PSBh 5.17:17]
* <s>Aśa</s> [is the root meaning] 'to eat.' [PSBh 5.17:18]
* One should eat in proper sequence. [PSBh 5.17:19]
* <s>Anu</s> [is used] in the sense of subsequent action. [PSBh 5.17:20]

children.text: * anupūrvaśa iti atikrāntāpekṣaṇe prakāravacane ca // PSBh_5.17:21
children.translated_text: * 'In proper sequence' (<s>anupūrvaśaḥ</s>) — in reference to what has gone before, and in the sense of manner. [PSBh 5.17:21]

children.text: * yathāpūrvaṃ grāmādi praviśya bhaikṣyārjanaṃ kṛtvālābhakāle aparyāptikāle vā tadanu paścād apaḥ pītvā stheyamiti kṛtvā bhagavatā etaduktam aśnīyādanupūrvaśa iti // PSBh_5.17:22
children.translated_text: * Having first entered a village and such and collected alms, in the time of non-obtainment or insufficiency, subsequently, having drunk water and remained — with this understanding, the Blessed One stated: 'one should eat in proper sequence.' [PSBh 5.17:22]
* Here a verse is given as explanation. [PSBh 5.17:23]

children.text: * āha śūnyāgāraguhāvasthasyendriyajayena vartato'sya balaṃ kiṃ cintyate kimakaluṣatvameva // PSBh_5.17:24
children.translated_text: * He asks: for one dwelling in an empty house or cave, engaged in the conquest of the senses — is only strength to be considered, or is freedom from impurity [also to be considered]? [PSBh 5.17:24]
* The answer is: no [not strength alone]. [PSBh 5.17:25]
* Because [the sūtra] states: [PSBh 5.17:26]
Having the nature of a cow, or having the nature of a deer. [PS 5.18]

children.text: * atra gaur lokādiprasiddho mṛgavat khurakakudaviṣāṇasāsnādimān iti // PSBh_5.18:1
children.translated_text: * Here a cow is well-known in the world and tradition, like a deer, having hooves, hump, horns, dewlap, and so forth. [PSBh 5.18:1]

children.text: * tathā mṛgo'pi godravyaval lokādiprasiddhaḥ kṛṣṇamṛgādīnām anyatamaḥ // PSBh_5.18:2
children.translated_text: * Likewise, a deer too, like a cow's characteristics, is well-known in the world and tradition — being any one of the black antelope and others. [PSBh 5.18:2]

children.text: * tayostu sati dharmabahutve samāno dharmo gṛhyate ādhyātmikādidvaṃdvasahiṣṇutvam // PSBh_5.18:3
children.translated_text: * Of the two, though having many qualities, the common quality adopted is: endurance of the pairs of opposites — <s>ādhyātmika</s> (relating to the self) and others. [PSBh 5.18:3]
* We shall explain that further below. [PSBh 5.18:4]
* The mention of the qualities of cow and deer is for the purpose of mutually qualifying [each other]. [PSBh 5.18:5]
* The word <s>vā</s> is in the sense of option. [PSBh 5.18:6]

children.text: * kriyāsāmānyadṛṣṭyā raudrībahurūpīvad ekadharmeṇa caikadharmeṇa vā stheyamityarthaḥ // PSBh_5.18:7
children.translated_text: * From the perspective of commonality of action, like <s>Raudrī</s> and <s>Bahurūpī</s> — one should remain with one quality or with [another] one quality; this is the meaning. [PSBh 5.18:7]
* He asks: by what strength is the result accomplished for him? [PSBh 5.18:8]
* That is stated: [PSBh 5.18:9]
One becomes pure by water alone. [PS 5.19]

children.text: * atra adbhiḥ āṅ iva adbhireva āpo jalamityādiprasiddhāḥ pūrvoktāḥ // PSBh_5.19:1
children.translated_text: * Here, 'by water' (<s>adbhiḥ</s>) — the prefix <s>ā</s>, as it were, 'by water indeed' — water, liquid, and such are well-known, as previously stated. [PSBh 5.19:1]
* 'By water' — [this is] an instrumental case. [PSBh 5.19:2]
* The prefix <s>ā</s> indicates the limit of the previously established measure and so forth. [PSBh 5.19:3]
* And in the limit of enduring the pairs of opposites, like a cow or deer. [PSBh 5.19:4]
* <s>Iva</s> is in the sense of comparison. [PSBh 5.19:5]

children.text: * yathā adbhiśca mṛdbhiśca prakṣālitāni vastrādīni śuddhāni bhavanti tadvat // PSBh_5.19:6
children.translated_text: * Just as garments and such become clean when washed with water and earth — so too. [PSBh 5.19:6]
* Through the strength of having the nature of cow or deer, one becomes pure. [PSBh 5.19:7]
* The answer is: no [it is not so simple]. [PSBh 5.19:8]

children.text: * yasmādāha gomṛgayor akuśaladharmapratiṣedhaṃ kuśaladharme ca niyogaṃ siddhaśaktipraśaṃsayā asiddhaśaktipratiṣedhaṃ ca vakṣyāmaḥ // PSBh_5.19:9
children.translated_text: * Because [the sūtra] states — we shall explain the prohibition of unwholesome qualities and the injunction of wholesome qualities for the cow and deer, with praise of the power of the perfected and prohibition of [the conduct of] one not yet perfected. [PSBh 5.19:9]
* He states: [PSBh 5.19:10]

children.text: siddhayogī na lipyate karmaṇā pātakena vā || PS_5.20 ||
children.translated_text: A perfected <s>yogī</s> is not tainted by action or by sin. [PS 5.20]

children.text: * asiddhastu sarvathāpi vartamāno lipyata ityarthaḥ // PSBh_5.20:1
children.translated_text: * But one who is not perfected, even while proceeding in every way, is tainted — this is the meaning. [PSBh 5.20:1]

children.text: * ato yogī siddha ityevaṃ prāpte sukhamukhoccāraṇārtham uktaṃ siddhayogī iti // PSBh_5.20:2
children.translated_text: * Therefore, when 'a <s>yogī</s> [who is] perfected' is the established [meaning], the expression <s>siddhayogī</s> is used for ease of pronunciation. [PSBh 5.20:2]
* Here: [PSBh 5.20:3]
* <s>Yoga</s> means the union of the self and the Lord. [PSBh 5.20:4]
* By that [union], this one is a <s>yogī</s>. [PSBh 5.20:5]
* 'Perfected' (<s>siddha</s>) means one who has attained sovereignty beginning with [supernatural] vision. [PSBh 5.20:6]
* He is indeed skilled in controlling, entering, governing, and so forth. [PSBh 5.20:7]

children.text: * na lipyate na saṃyujyata ityarthaḥ // PSBh_5.20:8
children.translated_text: * 'Is not tainted' means is not conjoined [with sin] — this is the meaning. [PSBh 5.20:8]
* He asks: by what is he not tainted? [PSBh 5.20:9]
* The answer is: by action (<s>karma</s>). [PSBh 5.20:10]
* Here 'by action' is stated. [PSBh 5.20:11]
* Because of its being produced. [PSBh 5.20:13]
* 'By action' — [this is] an instrumental case. [PSBh 5.20:14]

children.text: * iṣṭasthānaśarīrendriyaviṣayasambandhakṛtena karmaṇā na lipyate na saṃyujyata ityarthaḥ // PSBh_5.20:15
children.translated_text: * He is not tainted, not conjoined, by action that produces the connection with desired places, bodies, senses, and objects — this is the meaning. [PSBh 5.20:15]

children.text: * āha aninditena śubhena karmaṇā na saṃyujyata ityucyate āho atha kimaśubhena karmaṇā lipyate neti // PSBh_5.20:16
children.translated_text: * He asks: is it said that he is not conjoined with unblemished, auspicious action? Or is he also not tainted by inauspicious action? [PSBh 5.20:16]
* The answer is: no [he is not tainted by either]. [PSBh 5.20:17]
* Because [the sūtra] states: 'by sin' (<s>pātakena</s>). [PSBh 5.20:18]

children.text: * atra pāpākhyena pātakena vāniṣṭasthānaśarīrendriyaviṣayagato 'śubhaṃ bhuṅkte tenāpyaśubhena karmaṇā na lipyate na yujyata ityarthaḥ // PSBh_5.20:19
children.translated_text: * Here, by sin designated as <s>pāpa</s> — that which leads to undesired places, bodies, senses, and objects and [makes one] experience the inauspicious — by that inauspicious action too he is not tainted, not conjoined; this is the meaning. [PSBh 5.20:19]
* <s>Vā</s> is in the sense of threefold option. [PSBh 5.20:20]

children.text: * pātakena vā apātakena vā samastābhyāṃ vā vaśīkaraṇāveśanapālanādiṣu pravartamāno na lipyate na saṃyujyata ityarthaḥ // PSBh_5.20:21
children.translated_text: * By sin, or by non-sin, or by both — while engaging in controlling, entering, governing, and so forth, he is not tainted, not conjoined; this is the meaning. [PSBh 5.20:21]
* Because of the power of perfection (<s>siddhi</s>). [PSBh 5.20:23]

children.text: * asiddhaścāyaṃ yogī brāhmaṇo gomṛgadharmāvastho yadi sarvathāpi gomṛgavat pravartate tato lipyate // PSBh_5.20:24
children.translated_text: * But if this <s>yogī</s> <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, while in the state of cow-nature or deer-nature, is not yet perfected and proceeds in every way like a cow or deer, then he is tainted. [PSBh 5.20:24]

children.text: * tasmād gomṛgayor akuśaladharmo na grāhyaḥ // PSBh_5.20:25
children.translated_text: * Therefore, the unwholesome quality of the cow and deer should not be adopted. [PSBh 5.20:25]
* And the wholesome quality — namely, endurance of the pairs of opposites relating to the self and such — is to be adopted. [PSBh 5.20:26]
* By that, this one becomes pure. [PSBh 5.20:27]
* He asks: what is his impurity? [PSBh 5.20:28]

children.text: * taducyate dvaṃdvair yogavyāsaṅgakaraiḥ kāmakrodhaśirorogādinimittaiḥ śītādibhiranyairvā // PSBh_5.20:29
children.translated_text: * The answer is: by the pairs of opposites that obstruct <s>yoga</s> — having causes such as desire, anger, headache, and so forth — by cold and such, or by other [afflictions]. [PSBh 5.20:29]

children.text: * na lipyate na saṃyujyata ityarthaḥ // PSBh_5.20:30
children.translated_text: * He is not tainted, not conjoined — this is the meaning. [PSBh 5.20:30]
* Because he has attained strength — this is the meaning. [PSBh 5.20:32]
* Here a verse is given as explanation. [PSBh 5.20:33]

children.text: * āha śūnyāgāraguhāvasthasyendriyajaye vartataḥ kāḥ kriyāḥ kartavyāḥ // PSBh_5.20:34
children.translated_text: * He asks: for one dwelling in an empty house or cave, engaged in the conquest of the senses — what practices should be performed? [PSBh 5.20:34]
* Are they bathing, laughing, and such? Or snoring, trembling, staggering, and such? [PSBh 5.20:35]
* The answer is: no [neither of those]. [PSBh 5.20:36]
* Because [the sūtra] states: [PSBh 5.20:37]
One should study the desired <s>ṛc</s> (verse), the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, with self-restraint. [PS 5.21]
* Here, <s>ṛcam</s> or <s>ṛcām</s> — both readings are acceptable. [PSBh 5.21:1]
* Here, the <s>ṛc</s> (verse) is [the mantra of] <s>Aghora</s>. [PSBh 5.21:2]
* How is this known? [PSBh 5.21:3]
* From the middle of the <s>ṛṅ</s> [group of five mantras]. [PSBh 5.21:4]
* Like <s>Sadyojāta</s>, <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>, and <s>Īśāna</s> — [the five are] <s>arci</s>, <s>varca</s>, <s>gāḥ</s> [etc.]. [PSBh 5.21:5]

children.text: * iṣṭā ceyaṃ tatra tatra japtavyatvena guṇīkṛtatvāt // PSBh_5.21:6
children.translated_text: * And this is 'desired' (<s>iṣṭā</s>) because it has been made valuable here and there as something to be recited. [PSBh 5.21:6]

children.text: * pūrvottarasūtreṣu japtavyatvena gāyatryā sahādhyānād āśubhāvasamādhyāsādanāc ca iṣṭā // PSBh_5.21:7
children.translated_text: * In the previous and subsequent <s>sūtras</s>, because of being something to be recited together with the <s>Gāyatrī</s> in meditation, and because of the attainment of rapid realization (<s>āśubhāvasamādhi</s>), it is desired. [PSBh 5.21:7]
* 'Study' (<s>adhyayana</s>) is a synonym for recitation (<s>japya</s>). [PSBh 5.21:8]
* <s>Īta</s> is in the sense of command and injunction. [PSBh 5.21:9]
* The meaning is: one should study mentally. [PSBh 5.21:10]
* He asks: should only the <s>ṛc</s> (verse) alone be studied? [PSBh 5.21:11]
* The answer is: no. [PSBh 5.21:12]
* Because [the sūtra] says <s>Gāyatrī</s>. [PSBh 5.21:13]
* The <s>Gāyatrī</s> is [the mantra of] <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>. [PSBh 5.21:14]
* Its etymology has been previously stated. [PSBh 5.21:15]
* The meaning is: one should study mentally. [PSBh 5.21:16]
* He asks: in what manner should one study? [PSBh 5.21:17]
* The answer is: with self-restraint (<s>ātmayantrita</s>). [PSBh 5.21:18]
* Self-restraint (<s>ātmayantraṇa</s>) is a synonym for <s>pratyāhāra</s> (withdrawal of the senses). [PSBh 5.21:19]
* 'Self' (<s>ātmā</s>) here means the knower of the field (<s>kṣetrajña</s>). [PSBh 5.21:20]
* Its selfhood is consciousness (<s>caitanya</s>). [PSBh 5.21:21]
* What is to be attained is: the effect, the instrument, and the objects. [PSBh 5.21:22]
* 'Self-restraint' — here, given the triad [of effect, instrument, objects], [the term] applies. [PSBh 5.21:23]

children.text: * yantraṇaṃ nāma yathāyam ātmabhāvo brahmaṇy akṣarapadapaṅktyāṃ yukto vartate tadātmā yantrito bhavati // PSBh_5.21:24
children.translated_text: * Restraint (<s>yantraṇa</s>) means: when this self-nature is engaged in <s>Brahman</s>, in the series of imperishable syllables — then the self is restrained. [PSBh 5.21:24]
* By the analogy of a mind absorbed in dance. Why? [PSBh 5.21:26]
* Because of the non-severance of the self and its self-nature. [PSBh 5.21:27]
* Between quality and qualified too, there is likewise simultaneous existence. [PSBh 5.21:28]

children.text: * yaṣṭuṃ pravṛtto yantrayituṃ ca pravṛtta eva bhavati // PSBh_5.21:30
children.translated_text: * One who has set out to recite has also set out to restrain. [PSBh 5.21:30]
* Like a mendicant. [PSBh 5.21:31]
* Therefore, this restraint itself is <s>pratyāhāra</s> (withdrawal of senses). [PSBh 5.21:32]
* He objects: here, because of the multiplicity of <s>Gāyatrīs</s>, there is doubt. [PSBh 5.21:33]

children.text: * kathamavagamyate ṛcā aghoreṇa vā tatpuruṣeṇeti // PSBh_5.21:34
children.translated_text: * How is it determined [whether it is] the <s>ṛc</s> [of] <s>Aghora</s> or [of] <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>? [PSBh 5.21:34]
* The answer is: it is determined. [PSBh 5.21:35]
* Because [the sūtra] states: [PSBh 5.21:36]
The <s>Raudrī</s> or the <s>Bahurūpī</s>. [PS 5.22]
* Here <s>Raudrī</s> is [the <s>Gāyatrī</s> of] <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>. [PSBh 5.22:1]
* Its etymology has been previously stated. [PSBh 5.22:2]
* The word <s>vā</s> should be understood as distributing between <s>Raudrī</s> and <s>Bahurūpī</s>. [PSBh 5.22:3]
* <s>Bahurūpī</s> is [the <s>Gāyatrī</s> of] <s>Aghora</s>. [PSBh 5.22:4]
* <s>Vā</s> is in the sense of option. [PSBh 5.22:5]
* Because of the equality of fruit. [PSBh 5.22:6]
* By <s>vā</s> — one or the other. [PSBh 5.22:7]
* With self-restraint one should study — this is the meaning. [PSBh 5.22:8]
* He asks: what result is accomplished for one who studies with self-restraint? [PSBh 5.22:9]
* That is stated: [PSBh 5.22:10]
From this, <s>yoga</s> proceeds. [PS 5.23]
* Here <s>ataḥ</s> ('from this') is in the sense of indicating a cause. [PSBh 5.23:1]
* The meaning is: 'with self-restraint one should study.' [PSBh 5.23:2]
* From that cause, reason, occasion — this is the meaning. [PSBh 5.23:3]
* The union of the self and the Lord is to be understood as <s>yoga</s>. [PSBh 5.23:5]
* <s>Pra</s> is in the sense of initial action. [PSBh 5.23:6]
* 'Proceeds' (<s>pravartate</s>) — its meaning has been previously stated. [PSBh 5.23:7]
* Here a verse is given as explanation. [PSBh 5.23:8]

children.text: * āha ṛcam adhīyatā brahmaṇyakṣarapadapaṅktyāṃ kiṃ yuktenaiva stheyam // PSBh_5.23:9
children.translated_text: * He asks: for one studying the <s>ṛc</s> (verse), engaged in <s>Brahman</s>, in the series of imperishable syllables — should one simply remain engaged? [PSBh 5.23:9]

children.text: * āhosvid dṛṣṭā asyānyā sūkṣmatarā upāsanā kriyādhyānanamaḥstavyam // PSBh_5.23:10
children.translated_text: * Or is there observed for him another, subtler form of meditation — practice, meditation, homage, and hymn? [PSBh 5.23:10]
* The answer is: it is observed. [PSBh 5.23:11]
* Because [the sūtra] states: [PSBh 5.23:12]
One should meditate on <s>Oṃkāra</s>. [PS 5.24]

children.text: * atra oṃ ityeṣa japyaparyāyo vāmadevādivat // PSBh_5.24:1
children.translated_text: * Here <s>Oṃ</s> is a synonym for recitation, like <s>Vāmadeva</s> and such. [PSBh 5.24:1]
* The word <s>kāra</s> should be understood as restrictive. [PSBh 5.24:2]
* For what reason? [PSBh 5.24:3]

children.text: * uktaṃ hi / praṇave nityayuktasya vyāhṛtiṣu ca saptasu / tripadāyāṃ ca gāyatryāṃ na mṛtyurvindate param // PSBh_5.24:4
* ityata oṃkāra evāvadhāryate dhyeyatvena na tu gāyatryādayaḥ // PSBh_5.24:5
children.translated_text: * Therefore, <s>Oṃkāra</s> alone is determined as the object of meditation, not the <s>Gāyatrī</s> and others. [PSBh 5.24:5]
* <s>Abhi</s> is in the sense of repetition/practice. [PSBh 5.24:6]
* One should have a mind closely applied to <s>Oṃkāra</s>. [PSBh 5.24:7]
* <s>Dhyai</s> [is the root meaning] 'to contemplate.' [PSBh 5.24:8]
* <s>Dhyāna</s> (meditation) means contemplation — this is the meaning. // PSBh 5.24:9

children.text: * uktaṃ hi / dhyai cintālakṣaṇaṃ dhyānaṃ brahma cauṃkāralakṣaṇam / dhīyate līyate vāpi tasmād dhyānamiti smṛtam // PSBh_5.24:10
children.translated_text: * For it has been stated: "<s>Dhyai</s> — meditation is characterized by contemplation, and <s>Brahman</s> is characterized by <s>Oṃkāra</s> (the syllable Oṃ); it is held (<s>dhīyate</s>) or dissolved (<s>līyate</s>), therefore it is called <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation)." // PSBh 5.24:10

children.text: * muhūrtārdhaṃ muhūrtaṃ vā prāṇāyāmāntare'pi vā // PSBh_5.24:11
children.translated_text: * For half a <s>muhūrta</s> (moment), or for a <s>muhūrta</s>, or even during the interval of <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control), // PSBh 5.24:11

children.text: * dhyeyaṃ cintayamānastu pāpaṃ kṣapayate naraḥ // PSBh_5.24:12
children.translated_text: * a person who contemplates the object of meditation destroys his sin. // PSBh 5.24:12
* The suffix <s>īta</s> is used in the sense of command and injunction. // PSBh 5.24:13

children.text: * oṃkāra eva dhyeyo nānya ityarthaḥ / āha oṃkāro dhyeyaḥ // PSBh_5.24:14
children.translated_text: * <s>Oṃkāra</s> (the syllable Oṃ) alone is to be meditated upon, nothing else — this is the meaning. He says: <s>Oṃkāra</s> is the object of meditation. // PSBh 5.24:14
* What then is the place of meditation? // PSBh 5.24:15

children.text: * kasmin vā deśe dhāraṇā kartavyā // PSBh_5.24:16
children.translated_text: * In what place should <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration) be practiced? // PSBh 5.24:16
* Or what should be done by one who is meditating? // PSBh 5.24:17
* That is stated: // PSBh 5.24:18

* For it has been said: 'For one who is constantly engaged in <s>Praṇava</s> (Oṃ), in the seven <s>Vyāhṛtis</s>, and in the three-footed <s>Gāyatrī</s> — death does not find [him who practices] the supreme.' [PSBh 5.24:4]
One should practice <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration) in the heart. // PS 5.25 //
* Here, "in the heart" (<s>hṛdi</s>) is a synonym for the self (<s>ātman</s>). // PSBh 5.25:1
* Why? // PSBh 5.25:2
* Because of the force of what precedes and what follows. // PSBh 5.25:3

children.text: * yo 'rtho yatra milati sa tatra sthāpayitavyaḥ sa evārtho dhārayitavyaḥ // PSBh_5.25:4
children.translated_text: * Whatever meaning converges in a given place, that should be established there; that very meaning should be held firm. // PSBh 5.25:4

children.text:
* kiṃca vedaprāmāṇyāduktam / aṅgādaṅgāt sambhavasi hṛdayād adhijāyase / ātmā vai putranāmāsi sa jīva śaradaḥ śatam // PSBh_5.25:5
* anyatrāpi ātmā vijāyate putra ātmā vai ātmanaḥ pitā / ātmaprajo bhaviṣyāmi paramaṃ hṛdayaṃ hi saḥ // PSBh_5.25:6

children.translated_text: * Therefore it is said that the heart means the self. // PSBh 5.25:7
* The intellect produces a state of determined conviction. // PSBh 5.25:8

children.text: * hṛdayaṃ priyāpriye vetti trividhā karaṇasthitiḥ // PSBh_5.25:9
children.translated_text: * The heart knows what is pleasant and unpleasant — such is the threefold condition of the instrument. // PSBh 5.25:9

children.text: * tathā loke'pi santi vaktāro hṛdayaṃ te jñāsyati // PSBh_5.25:10
children.translated_text: * Likewise, in common usage too there are speakers who say "your heart will know," // PSBh 5.25:10
* What is meant by this? // PSBh 5.25:11
* "Your self will know" — this is the meaning. // PSBh 5.25:12
* From this it is understood that "in the heart" (<s>hṛdi</s>) is a synonym for the self. // PSBh 5.25:13
* "In the heart" indicates proximity by way of connection (<s>aupaśleṣika</s>). // PSBh 5.25:14

children.text: * atra tu oṃkāro dhāryo nātmā kiṃtu ya evātmanyātmabhāvaḥ // PSBh_5.25:15
children.translated_text: * But here it is <s>Oṃkāra</s> that is to be held, not the self; rather, that which is the self's own nature within the self. // PSBh 5.25:15

children.text: * tasyoṃkārāt pracyutasya viṣayebhyo vṛttivikāramātreṇa gatasya pratyānayanaṃ pratyāhāraḥ // PSBh_5.25:16
children.translated_text: * <s>Pratyāhāra</s> (withdrawal) is the bringing back of that [<s>Oṃkāra</s>] which, having fallen away from <s>Oṃkāra</s>, has gone toward sense-objects through mere modification of mental activity. // PSBh 5.25:16
* Having withdrawn it, <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration) should be practiced in the heart. // PSBh 5.25:17
* And what is to be held is the continuous contemplation of <s>Oṃkāra</s>. // PSBh 5.25:18
* Remaining there for a very long time is <s>adhyayana</s> (study/practice). // PSBh 5.25:19
* The supreme <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) is that which is established through <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration). // PSBh 5.25:20
* The final yoga, however, we shall explain as "having established." // PSBh 5.25:21
* Regarding "<s>kurvīta</s>" (one should do): // PSBh 5.25:22
* The root <s>ḍukṛñ</s> means "doing." // PSBh 5.25:23
* Its locative ending yields the form <s>kurvīta</s> (one should do). // PSBh 5.25:24
* <s>Dhāraṇā</s> (concentration) should be practiced in the heart. // PSBh 5.25:25
* The suffix <s>īta</s> is used in the sense of command and injunction. // PSBh 5.25:26
* The injunction serves to prohibit <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration) being practiced in other locations such as the foot, knee, spine, nose, and so forth. // PSBh 5.25:27
* It should be held in the heart, not elsewhere — this is the meaning. // PSBh 5.25:28

children.text: * āha oṃkāraḥ kiṃ parapa viṣṇurumā kumāraśca catasro 'rdhamātrā vā // PSBh_5.25:29
children.translated_text: * He asks: Is <s>Oṃkāra</s> identical with <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Umā</s>, <s>Kumāra</s>, or the four half-measures (<s>ardhamātrā</s>)? // PSBh 5.25:29
* Or is it an ordinary person (<s>samānapuruṣa</s>)? // PSBh 5.25:30
* It is said: No. // PSBh 5.25:31
* Because he states: // PSBh 5.25:32

* Moreover, on the authority of the <s>Veda</s>, it has been stated: "From limb after limb you are born, from the heart you are produced; you are the self named 'son' — live a hundred autumns." // PSBh 5.25:5
* And elsewhere too: "The self is born as a son; the self indeed is one's own father; you will become one whose progeny is the self — for he is the supreme heart." // PSBh 5.25:6
He is the <s>Ṛṣi</s> (seer), the <s>Vipra</s> (wise one), the great one. // PS 5.26 //

children.text: * atra ṛṣiḥ ityetad bhagavatā nāmadheyam // PSBh_5.26:1
children.translated_text: * Here, "<s>Ṛṣi</s>" (seer) is a name of the Lord. // PSBh 5.26:1
* Why is he called <s>Ṛṣi</s>? // PSBh 5.26:2
* The root <s>ṛṣi</s> denotes action (<s>kriyā</s>). // PSBh 5.26:3
* <s>Ṛṣitva</s> (seer-hood) means he is called <s>Ṛṣi</s> because of his proclamation of creative action. // PSBh 5.26:4

children.text: * tathā kṛtsnaṃ kāryaṃ vidyādyamīśata ityataḥ ṛṣiḥ // PSBh_5.26:5
children.translated_text: * Likewise, because he rules over (<s>īśate</s>) the entire domain of action and knowledge, therefore he is <s>Ṛṣi</s>. // PSBh 5.26:5

children.text: * tathā vipra ityetadapi bhagavato nāma // PSBh_5.26:6
children.translated_text: * Likewise, "<s>Vipra</s>" (wise one) is also a name of the Lord. // PSBh 5.26:6
* Why is he called <s>Vipra</s>? // PSBh 5.26:7
* The root <s>vida</s> means "knowing." // PSBh 5.26:8
* <s>Vipratva</s> (wisdom) means the power of knowledge. // PSBh 5.26:9

children.text: * vyāptamanena bhagavatā jñānaśaktyā kṛtsnaṃ jñeyamityato vipra iti // PSBh_5.26:10
children.translated_text: * Because this Lord has pervaded the entire knowable through his power of knowledge, therefore he is called <s>Vipra</s>. // PSBh 5.26:10
* Likewise, "<s>Mahān</s>" (great) denotes surpassing excellence. // PSBh 5.26:11

children.text: * yadetad dṛkkriyālakṣaṇamasti anāgantukam akṛtakamaiśvaryaṃ tadguṇasadbhāvaḥ satattvaṃ tattvadharmaḥ tadakṛtakaṃ puruṣacaitanyavat tan nānyasyetyato 'bhyadhikaḥ utkṛṣṭo'tiriktaśceti mahān // PSBh_5.26:12
children.translated_text: * That sovereignty characterized by vision and creative action, which is beginningless, uncreated — the real existence of that quality, its true nature, its essential attribute — that is uncreated, like the consciousness of a <s>puruṣa</s> (person/soul); it belongs to no other — therefore he is surpassing, exalted, and exceeding, hence "<s>Mahān</s>" (great). // PSBh 5.26:12
* "<s>Eṣa</s>" (this) is used in the sense of direct perception. // PSBh 5.26:13

children.text: * eṣa yo mayā pūrvam oṃ iti śrotrapratyakṣīkṛto 'rthaḥ asau viṣṇūmākumārādīnām anyatamo na bhavati // PSBh_5.26:14
children.translated_text: * This meaning which was previously made perceptible to the ear by me through the syllable <s>Oṃ</s> — that is not any one among <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Umā</s>, <s>Kumāra</s>, and others. // PSBh 5.26:14
* Because of his <s>ṛṣitva</s> (seer-hood), <s>vipratva</s> (wisdom), and <s>mahattva</s> (greatness) — this is the meaning. // PSBh 5.26:16

children.text: * āha ṛṣitvaṃ vipratvaṃ ca kīdṛśe maheśvare cintanīyam // PSBh_5.26:17
children.translated_text: * He asks: In what kind of <s>Maheśvara</s> should <s>ṛṣitva</s> (seer-hood) and <s>vipratva</s> (wisdom) be contemplated? // PSBh 5.26:17
* Or what kind of <s>Oṃkāra</s> should be meditated upon? // PSBh 5.26:18
* That is stated: // PSBh 5.26:19
<s>Vāgviśuddha</s> (pure of speech). // PS 5.27 //

children.text: * atrāpi vāgviśuddha ityapi bhagavato nāmadheyam // PSBh_5.27:1
children.translated_text: * Here too, "<s>Vāgviśuddha</s>" (pure of speech) is a name of the Lord. // PSBh 5.27:1
* It is not as though these [names] refer to another Lord. // PSBh 5.27:2

children.text: * sa yathā hy atho hitvā vāṇīṃ manasā saha rūparasagandhavidyāpuruṣādiparo niṣkalo dhyeyaḥ // PSBh_5.27:3
children.translated_text: * Just as, having abandoned speech together with the mind, he is to be meditated upon as <s>niṣkala</s> (without parts/formless), beyond form, taste, smell, knowledge, <s>puruṣa</s>, and so forth. // PSBh 5.27:3

children.text: * yasmāduktam / ākṛtimapi parihṛtya dhyānaṃ nityaṃ pare rudre / yena prāptaṃ yoge muhūrtamapi tat paro yogaḥ // PSBh_5.27:4

children.translated_text: * "Supreme yoga" — this is the meaning. // PSBh 5.27:5

children.text: * āha atha yathāyaṃ bālavan niṣkalastathā kiṃ samānapuruṣaḥ // PSBh_5.27:6
children.translated_text: * He asks: Since he is <s>niṣkala</s> (formless) like an infant, is he then an ordinary person (<s>samānapuruṣa</s>)? // PSBh 5.27:6
* That is answered: No. // PSBh 5.27:7
* Because he states: "Even then, this one is..." // PSBh 5.27:8

* Because it has been stated: "Having set aside even form, one should constantly meditate on the supreme <s>Rudra</s>; that by which even a moment's yoga is attained — that is the supreme yoga." // PSBh 5.27:4
<s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord). // PS 5.28 //

children.text: * atrānādyajñānadyatinā ṛṣitvavipratvasaṃjñakena mahatā aiśvaryeṇa maheśvara iti siddham iha tu yadāyaṃ vāgviśuddho niṣkalastadā kiṃ samānapuruṣavad anīśvara ityasya saṃśayasya saṃvyudāsārtham ucyate maheśvara iti // PSBh_5.28:1
children.translated_text: * Here, the name "<s>Maheśvara</s>" is established through the great sovereignty designated as <s>ṛṣitva</s> (seer-hood) and <s>vipratva</s> (wisdom), with the beginningless [quality that transcends] ignorance. But here, the doubt is: when he is <s>vāgviśuddha</s> (pure of speech) and <s>niṣkala</s> (formless), is he then without sovereignty like an ordinary person? To dispel this doubt, it is said "<s>Maheśvara</s>." // PSBh 5.28:1

children.text: * yasmād asyaiśvaryaṃ niṣkalasyāpi svaguṇasadbhāvaḥ satattvaṃ tattvadharmaḥ // PSBh_5.28:2
children.translated_text: * Because his sovereignty — the real existence of his own qualities, their true nature, their essential attribute — persists even when he is <s>niṣkala</s> (formless). // PSBh 5.28:2
* Its uncreatedness is like the consciousness of a <s>puruṣa</s> (person/soul). // PSBh 5.28:3
* Therefore, even then, this one is indeed great and sovereign — <s>Maheśvara</s>. // PSBh 5.28:4

children.text: * tasmādakṛtaka eva mahacchabda ityato maheśvara iti // PSBh_5.28:5
children.translated_text: * Therefore, the word "<s>mahat</s>" (great) is itself uncreated, and hence he is <s>Maheśvara</s>. // PSBh 5.28:5
* Thus "<s>Oṃkāra</s>" has been stated as the object of meditation. // PSBh 5.28:6

children.text: * dhyeyaguṇīkaraṇamuktam ṛṣir vipro mahāneṣa iti // PSBh_5.28:7
children.translated_text: * The qualification of the object of meditation has been stated as "the <s>Ṛṣi</s>, the <s>Vipra</s>, the great one." // PSBh 5.28:7
* The determination of the object of meditation has been stated as "<s>Vāgviśuddha</s>, <s>niṣkala</s> (formless)." // PSBh 5.28:8
* And the praise of the power of the object of meditation has been stated as "<s>Maheśvara</s>." // PSBh 5.28:9

children.text: * evaṃ yasmādindriyajaye vartate ato vasatyarthavṛttibalakriyālābhādayaśca vyākhyātā iti // PSBh_5.28:10
children.translated_text: * Thus, since he abides in the mastery of the senses, therefore the dwelling-place, livelihood, strength, practices, attainments, and so forth have been explained. // PSBh 5.28:10
* Therefore it is appropriate to state here: // PSBh 5.28:11
* The section on the empty dwelling and cave (<s>śūnyāgāra-guhā</s>) is concluded. // PSBh 5.28:12

children.text: * āha śūnyāgāraguhāyāṃ yadā jitānīndriyāṇi devanityatā ca prāptā bhavati tadā kiṃ tadeva bhaikṣyaṃ vṛttimāsthāya tatraivānena duḥkhāntaprāpteḥ stheyam // PSBh_5.28:13
children.translated_text: * He asks: When in the empty dwelling and cave the senses have been conquered and the state of being established with the gods (<s>devanityatā</s>) has been attained, then should one remain there itself, relying on that same livelihood of begging (<s>bhaikṣya</s>), until the end of suffering is reached? // PSBh 5.28:13
* Or does this [stage] too have a prescribed dwelling-place, livelihood, strength, practices, and attainments? // PSBh 5.28:14
* It is said: It does. // PSBh 5.28:15
* Because he states: // PSBh 5.28:16

children.text: * āha śūnyāgāraguhām utsṛjya prayojanābhāvāt śmaśāne saṃkrāntirayukteti cet // PSBh_5.29:1
children.translated_text: * He asks: Is it not inappropriate to abandon the empty dwelling and cave and move to the <s>śmaśāna</s> (cremation ground), since there is no purpose? // PSBh 5.29:1
* That is answered: No. // PSBh 5.29:2
* Because it serves to remove attachment to yoga [practice in one place]. // PSBh 5.29:3

children.text: * ihāvasthānād avasthānaṃ prāpya brāhmaṇasya sarvatra vasatyarthavṛttibalakriyālābhādayo 'yutasiddhā vaktavyāḥ // PSBh_5.29:4
children.translated_text: * Having reached each successive stage of abiding from this abiding, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>'s dwelling-place, livelihood, strength, practices, attainments, and so forth are to be explained as inherently established everywhere. // PSBh 5.29:4

children.text: * tatrādidharmā apyasya tāvadāyatane vasatyarthaḥ vṛttirbhaikṣyaṃ balamaṣṭāṅgaṃ brahmacaryaṃ kriyāḥ sthānahasitādyāḥ snānaṃ kaluṣāpohaḥ śuddhiḥ jñānāvāptiḥ akaluṣatvaṃ ca lābhā iti // PSBh_5.29:5
children.translated_text: * There, his initial <s>dharmas</s> (stages) are as follows: in the temple, the dwelling-place; the livelihood is begging (<s>bhaikṣya</s>); the strength is the eightfold <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy); the practices are standing, laughing, and so forth; bathing is the removal of impurity; purification is the attainment of knowledge; freedom from impurity; and these are the attainments. // PSBh 5.29:5

children.text: * tathā asanmānaparibhavopadeśād āyatane vasatyarthaḥ vṛttirutsṛṣṭaṃ balamakaluṣatvam indriyadvārapidhānaṃ ca kriyā indriyāṇi pidhāya unmattavadavasthānaṃ pāpakṣayāc chuddhiḥ lābhastu kṛtsno dharmastulyendriyajaye vartate // PSBh_5.29:6
children.translated_text: * Likewise, from the instruction regarding dishonor and reproach: in the temple the dwelling-place; the livelihood is what has been abandoned [by others]; the strength is freedom from impurity and the closing of the sense-doors; the practice is abiding like a madman having closed the senses; purification comes from the destruction of sin; and the attainment is the entire <s>dharma</s>, which is operative in the mastery of the senses equally. // PSBh 5.29:6

children.text: * tathā vasatyarthaḥ śūnyāgāraguhā vṛttirbhaikṣyaṃ balaṃ gomṛgayoḥ sahadharmitvaṃ kriyā adhyayanadhyānādyā ajitendriyavṛttitāpohaḥ śuddhiḥ lābhastu devanityatā jitendriyatvaṃ ceti // PSBh_5.29:7
children.translated_text: * Likewise, the dwelling-place is the empty dwelling and cave; the livelihood is begging (<s>bhaikṣya</s>); the strength is sharing the nature of a cow and a deer; the practices are study, meditation, and so forth; purification is the removal of uncontrolled sensory activity; and the attainments are the state of being established with the gods (<s>devanityatā</s>) and mastery of the senses. // PSBh 5.29:7

children.text: * tathehāpi śmaśāne vasatyarthaḥ vasan dharmātmā // PSBh_5.29:8
children.translated_text: * Likewise, here too, in the <s>śmaśāna</s> (cremation ground) is the dwelling-place — dwelling there, one becomes a <s>dharmātmā</s> (one whose self is dharma). // PSBh 5.29:8

children.text: * yathālabdhamiti vṛttiḥ kriyā smṛtiḥ asmṛtyapohaḥ śuddhiḥ lābhastu sāyujyam // PSBh_5.29:9
children.translated_text: * "Whatever is obtained" — this is the livelihood; the practice is <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness); purification is the removal of forgetfulness; and the attainment is <s>sāyujya</s> (union [with the Lord]). // PSBh 5.29:9

children.text: * tathottaratra ṛṣir iti vasatyarthaḥ balamapramādaḥ prasāda upāyaḥ duḥkhāpohaḥ śuddhiḥ guṇāvāptiśca lābha iti // PSBh_5.29:10
children.translated_text: * Likewise, beyond that: "<s>Ṛṣi</s>" is the dwelling-place; the strength is vigilance (<s>apramāda</s>); grace (<s>prasāda</s>) is the means; purification is the removal of suffering; and the attainment of qualities is the gain. // PSBh 5.29:10

children.text:
* tathoktaṃ ca / pañca lābhān malān pañca pañcopāyān viśeṣataḥ / yastu budhyati pañcārthe sa vidvān nātra saṃśayaḥ // PSBh_5.29:11
* prathamo vidyālābhastapaso lābho'tha devanityatvam / yogo guṇapravṛttirlābhāḥ pañceha vijñeyāḥ // PSBh_5.29:12
* ajñānamadharmaśca viṣayābhyāsaḥ sthiteralābhaśca / anaiśvaryaṃ ca malā vijñeyāḥ pañca pañcārthe // PSBh_5.29:13
* vāso dhyānam akhilakaraṇanirodhastathā smṛtiścaiva / prasāda iti copāyā vijñeyāḥ pañca pañcārthe // PSBh_5.29:14
* vāsārtho lokaśca śūnyāgāraṃ tathā śmaśānaṃ ca / rudraśca pañca deśā niyataṃ siddhyarthamākhyātāḥ // PSBh_5.29:15

children.translated_text: * Therefore, what has been stated is appropriate. // PSBh 5.29:16

children.text: * sa eva prāguktaḥ sambandhaḥ śmaśānavāsī iti // PSBh_5.29:17
children.translated_text: * The connection previously mentioned is the same — that is, "dweller in the <s>śmaśāna</s> (cremation ground)." // PSBh 5.29:17

children.text: * atra śmaśānaṃ nāma yad etal lokādiprasiddhaṃ laukikānāṃ mṛtāni śavāni parityajanti tat // PSBh_5.29:18
children.translated_text: * Here, "<s>śmaśāna</s>" (cremation ground) refers to that which is well-known in the world from common convention — where worldly people abandon their dead corpses. // PSBh 5.29:18

children.text: * śavasambandhāt śmaśānam tasminn ākāśe vṛkṣamūle yathānabhiṣvaṅgamaryādayā jitadvaṃdvena smṛtikriyāniviṣṭena vastavyam // PSBh_5.29:19
children.translated_text: * Because of its connection with corpses (<s>śava</s>), it is called <s>śmaśāna</s>. In that open space, at the root of a tree, one should dwell without attachment, with proper discipline, having conquered the pairs of opposites, absorbed in the practice of <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness). // PSBh 5.29:19

children.text: * vasatisaṃyogāt śmaśānavāsī bhavati pulinavāsivad ityarthaḥ // PSBh_5.29:20
children.translated_text: * Through the connection of dwelling, one becomes a "dweller in the <s>śmaśāna</s>" (cremation ground), just as one who dwells on a sandbank is called a sandbank-dweller — this is the meaning. // PSBh 5.29:20

children.text: * āha kimasya gomṛgayoḥ sahadharmitvameva balam // PSBh_5.29:21
children.translated_text: * He asks: Is this one's strength only the sharing of nature with the cow and the deer? // PSBh 5.29:21
* That is answered: No. // PSBh 5.29:22
* Because he states: // PSBh 5.29:23

* And thus it has been stated: "He who understands the five attainments, the five impurities, and the five means in the <s>Pañcārtha</s> (five topics) in detail — he is truly learned, there is no doubt." // PSBh 5.29:11
* "The first is the attainment of knowledge; then the attainment of <s>tapas</s> (austerity); then the state of being established with the gods; yoga; and the arising of [divine] qualities — these are to be known as the five attainments herein." // PSBh 5.29:12
* "Ignorance, <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness), attachment to sense-objects, failure to attain stability, and lack of sovereignty — these five are to be known as the impurities in the <s>Pañcārtha</s>." // PSBh 5.29:13
* "Dwelling, meditation, the complete restraint of all instruments [of cognition], <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness), and <s>prasāda</s> (grace) — these five are to be known as the means in the <s>Pañcārtha</s>." // PSBh 5.29:14
* "The community, the empty dwelling, the <s>śmaśāna</s> (cremation ground), <s>Rudra</s> — these are the five places taught as fixed for the purpose of attainment." // PSBh 5.29:15
Dweller in the <s>śmaśāna</s> (cremation ground). // PS 5.30 //

children.text: * atra dharmo nāma ya eṣa yamaniyamapūrvako 'bhivyakto māhātmyādidharmaḥ sa pūrvoktaḥ // PSBh_5.30:1
children.translated_text: * Here, <s>dharma</s> refers to that which is the <s>dharma</s> of greatness and so forth, manifested through the preliminary practices of <s>yama</s> (restraints) and <s>niyama</s> (observances) — that has been previously stated. // PSBh 5.30:1
* That has been accumulated in his self. // PSBh 5.30:2
* Through that <s>dharma</s>, he becomes a <s>dharmātmā</s> (one whose self is dharma) — this is the meaning. // PSBh 5.30:3
* He asks: Is his livelihood only begging? // PSBh 5.30:4
* It is said: No. // PSBh 5.30:5
* Because he states: // PSBh 5.30:6
<s>Dharmātmā</s> (one whose self is dharma). // PS 5.31 //

children.text: * atra yathā iti samānārthe amlādiṣu jitendriyatvāt // PSBh_5.31:1
children.translated_text: * Here, "<s>yathā</s>" (as it comes) means in the sense of "whatever" — because of mastery of the senses with respect to sour and other [tastes]. // PSBh 5.31:1
* <s>Labdha</s> means obtained, come upon, without having sought — this is the meaning. // PSBh_5.31:2
* <s>Upa</s> is used in the sense of proximity, sustaining nearby. // PSBh_5.31:3

children.text: * tad yathālabdhamannapānaṃ śmaśānādanirgacchatā divase divase jīvanāya sthityarthaṃ tadupajīvan yathālabdhopajīvako bhavatītyarthaḥ // PSBh_5.31:4
children.translated_text: * That is to say, living on whatever food and drink is obtained, without leaving the cremation ground, day after day, subsisting on that for the sake of maintaining life — thus one becomes a <s>yathālabdhopajīvaka</s> (one who lives on whatever is obtained). This is the meaning. // PSBh_5.31:4

children.text: * āha kiṃ jīvanameva paro lābha iti // PSBh_5.31:5
children.translated_text: * He asks: Is mere living itself the highest gain? // PSBh_5.31:5
* It is said: No. // PSBh_5.31:6
* Because he says: // PSBh_5.31:7
The one who lives on whatever is obtained attains union with <s>Rudra</s>. // PS_5.32 //

children.text: * atra labhate vindate āsādayatītyarthaḥ rudra iti kāraṇāpadeśe // PSBh_5.32:1
children.translated_text: * Here <s>labhate</s> means obtains, finds, attains — this is the meaning. <s>Rudra</s> is a designation of the Cause (<s>kāraṇa</s>). // PSBh_5.32:1
* The <s>Rudra</s>-nature of <s>Rudra</s> has been stated previously. // PSBh_5.32:2

children.text: * sākṣād rudreṇa saha saṃyogaḥ sāyujyam // PSBh_5.32:3
children.translated_text: * <s>Sāyujya</s> (union) is direct conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>) with <s>Rudra</s> himself. // PSBh_5.32:3
* The use of <s>bhāva</s> (abstract state) is for the purpose of excluding anything other than the self and the Lord. // PSBh_5.32:4
* The perfection (<s>samyaktva</s>) of <s>yoga</s> is <s>sāyujya</s> — thus it is understood as a synonym of <s>yoga</s>. // PSBh_5.32:5
* From the word pertaining to the nature of <s>dharma</s> and the self, the meaning is: like the transcendence of states and infinity. // PSBh_5.32:6
* He asks: By what means does one attain that? // PSBh_5.32:7
* Is it by study and teaching alone? // PSBh_5.32:8
* To that it is said: No. // PSBh_5.32:9
* Because he says: // PSBh_5.32:10
One should constantly remember <s>Rudra</s>. // PS_5.33 //

children.text: * atra sadā nityaṃ satatamavyucchinnamiti rudramiti kāraṇāpadeśe // PSBh_5.33:1
children.translated_text: * Here <s>sadā</s> means always, perpetually, continuously, without interruption. <s>Rudra</s> is a designation of the Cause (<s>kāraṇa</s>). // PSBh_5.33:1
* The <s>Rudra</s>-nature of <s>Rudra</s> has been stated previously. // PSBh_5.33:2
* <s>Rudram</s> is in the accusative case, denoting the object of action. // PSBh_5.33:3
* <s>Anu</s> is used in the sense of repeated or subsequent action. // PSBh_5.33:4

children.text: * pūrvokto dhyeyo'rthaḥ satatam anusmartavyaḥ / smṛtiḥ cintāyām // PSBh_5.33:5
* ūṣmavadavasthitasya karmaṇaścyutihetoḥ kṣapaṇārthaṃ satatam anusmartavyaḥ // PSBh_5.33:6
children.translated_text: * For the purpose of exhausting <s>karma</s> which remains like residual heat and is the cause of falling, one should constantly remember [<s>Rudra</s>]. // PSBh_5.33:6
* But remembrance (<s>smṛti</s>) means constant devotion to the deity — this is the meaning. // PSBh_5.33:7

children.text: * tataḥ kṣīṇe karmaṇi taddoṣahetujālamūlaviśiṣṭasya pratyāsaikanimittābhāvāt sāyujyaprāptau na punaḥ saṃsāraḥ // PSBh_5.33:8
children.translated_text: * Then, when <s>karma</s> is exhausted, because there is no cause for re-approach for one who is distinguished by the severance of the root of the net of causes of those defects, upon attaining union (<s>sāyujya</s>), there is no further <s>saṃsāra</s> (cycle of rebirth). // PSBh_5.33:8
* Here is a verse with etymological explanation. // PSBh_5.33:9
* He asks: Because of the possibility of the spread of the connection with ignorance, impurity, sin, latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), and so forth, there is doubt: // PSBh_5.33:10

children.text: * sūkṣmavadavasthite karmaṇi kṣīṇe 'tyantaviśuddhaḥ sāyujyamāsādayati āhosvid aviśuddha iti // PSBh_5.33:11
children.translated_text: * When <s>karma</s> that remains in a subtle state is exhausted, does one attain union (<s>sāyujya</s>) in a state of complete purity, or in an impure state? // PSBh_5.33:11
* It is said: In a pure state. // PSBh_5.33:12
* Because he says: // PSBh_5.33:13
* The previously stated object of meditation is to be constantly remembered (<s>anusmartavya</s>). <s>Smṛti</s> (remembrance) here means contemplation (<s>cintā</s>). // PSBh_5.33:5
Having cut the root of the net of causes of defects — // PS_5.34 //

children.text: * atra vyutkramābhidhānāc chedaḥ kramaśo yojanīyaḥ // PSBh_5.34:1
children.translated_text: * Here, because of the inverted order of expression, the cutting should be understood sequentially. // PSBh_5.34:1
* The cutting should be understood as consisting of restraint (<s>yantraṇa</s>) and concentration (<s>dhāraṇā</s>). // PSBh_5.34:2
* For what purpose? // PSBh_5.34:3
* For the purpose of destroying <s>karma</s> that remains in a subtle state, because the instruction concerns the meaning of dwelling and so forth. // PSBh_5.34:4

children.text: * kiṃca arthānām anirvacanārthatvāt tatra japa eva kevalo'bhihitaḥ // PSBh_5.34:5
children.translated_text: * Moreover, because the meaning of the objects is inexpressible, there only <s>japa</s> (recitation) alone was taught. // PSBh_5.34:5

children.text: * iha tu yata indriyāṇi jetavyāni yo jetā yayā jetavyāni yathā jetavyāni yatprayojanaṃ jetavyāni yasmiṃśca jite jitāni bhavanti tad vakṣyāmaḥ // PSBh_5.34:6
children.translated_text: * But here we shall explain: why the senses are to be conquered, who is the conqueror, by what means they are to be conquered, how they are to be conquered, for what purpose they are to be conquered, and upon conquering which one all are conquered. // PSBh_5.34:6

children.text: * tathā yasyātmavṛttir adhyayanadhyānasmaraṇādi ca vakṣyāmaḥ // PSBh_5.34:7
children.translated_text: * Likewise we shall explain the conduct of the self, including study, meditation, remembrance, and so forth. // PSBh_5.34:7

children.text: * tathā yata ātmā chettavyaḥ chettāraṃ chedakaraṇaṃ chedaprayojanaṃ chedyaṃ chittiṃ yasmin chinne chinnaṃ bhavati tad vakṣyāmaḥ // PSBh_5.34:8
children.translated_text: * Likewise we shall explain: why the self is to be cut off, the cutter, the instrument of cutting, the purpose of cutting, what is to be cut, the cutting itself, and upon cutting which one all is cut. // PSBh_5.34:8
* To that it is said: 'having cut' (<s>chittvā</s>). // PSBh_5.34:9
* Here, cutting means merely the separation from the condition of selfhood (<s>ātmabhāva</s>). // PSBh_5.34:10
* This is understood from the word denoting severance. // PSBh_5.34:11
* From the suffix <s>tvā</s>, it is understood that [this involves] study, meditation, concentration, restraint, and so forth, for one dwelling in an empty house or cave. // PSBh_5.34:12
* He asks: What is that? // PSBh_5.34:13
* And from what is one to be cut off? // PSBh_5.34:14

children.text: * taducyate doṣāṇāṃ hetujālasya mūlam iti // PSBh_5.34:15
children.translated_text: * To that it is said: 'the root of the net of causes of defects.' // PSBh_5.34:15
* Here, the defects (<s>doṣa</s>) are sound, touch, form, taste, and smell. // PSBh_5.34:16
* Because they are rooted in desire (<s>kāma</s>), acquisition (<s>arjana</s>), and so forth. // PSBh_5.34:18

children.text: * yasmāduktam / kāmaḥ krodhastathā lobho bhayaṃ svapnaśca pañcamaḥ / rāgo dveṣaśca mohaśca // PSBh_5.34:19

children.translated_text: * Likewise, acquisition (<s>arjana</s>), protection (<s>rakṣaṇa</s>), loss (<s>kṣaya</s>), attachment (<s>saṅga</s>), violence (<s>hiṃsā</s>), and so forth are the defects. // PSBh_5.34:20

children.text: * arjanaṃ nāma pratigrahajayakrayavikrayanirveśyādiṣu varṇināṃ viṣayārjanopāyāḥ // PSBh_5.34:21
children.translated_text: * <s>Arjana</s> (acquisition) means: the methods of acquiring sense objects for [people of different] <s>varṇas</s> through accepting gifts, conquest, buying, selling, wages, and so forth. // PSBh_5.34:21

children.text: * eteṣu ca viṣayāṇāmarjane vartatātmapīḍā parapīḍā vā avarjanīye bhavataḥ // PSBh_5.34:22
children.translated_text: * And in the acquisition of sense objects through these means, self-affliction or affliction of others is unavoidable for one who is engaged [in them]. // PSBh_5.34:22

children.text: * tatra yadyātmānaṃ pīḍayati tena ihaiva loke duḥkhī bhavati // PSBh_5.34:23
children.translated_text: * In that regard, if one afflicts oneself, by that one becomes miserable in this very world. // PSBh_5.34:23

children.text: * syāt paraṃ pīḍayati tatrāpyasyādharmo duḥkhādiphalaḥ saṃcīyate // PSBh_5.34:24
children.translated_text: * If one afflicts others, in that case too <s>adharma</s> (demerit), bearing fruit as suffering and so forth, is accumulated. // PSBh_5.34:24

children.text: * tac ca duḥkhaṃ nānyo'nubhavati kartaivānubhavati // PSBh_5.34:25
children.translated_text: * And that suffering is experienced by no other — only the doer himself experiences it. // PSBh_5.34:25
* Moreover, sense objects are like the <s>kimpāka</s> fruit. // PSBh_5.34:26

children.text: * tadyathā śrūyate lavaṇasāgarasaṃnikarṣe kālayavanadvīpe kimpākā nāma viṣavṛkṣāḥ // PSBh_5.34:27
children.translated_text: * As is heard: near the salt ocean, on the island of <s>Kālayavana</s>, there are poisonous trees called <s>kimpāka</s>. // PSBh_5.34:27

children.text: * tatphalāny āsvādenāmṛtopamāni ca kecidajñānād guḍavad bhakṣayanti // PSBh_5.34:28
children.translated_text: * Their fruits are like <s>amṛta</s> (nectar) in taste, and some, out of ignorance, eat them as if they were <s>guḍa</s> (jaggery). // PSBh_5.34:28

children.text: * bhakṣitāni ca tāni mūrchāṃ chardiṃ ca janayanti // PSBh_5.34:29
children.translated_text: * And when eaten, they produce stupor and vomiting. // PSBh_5.34:29
* Overwhelmed by that intense suffering, they perish. // PSBh_5.34:30

children.text: * śrutvā tu suhṛdāṃ vākyaṃ yo naro hy avamanyate / sa dahyate vipākānte kimpākairiva bhakṣitaiḥ // PSBh_5.34:31
children.translated_text: * 'The man who, having heard the words of well-wishers, disregards them — he is burned at the time of fruition, like one who has eaten <s>kimpāka</s> fruits.' // PSBh_5.34:31

children.text: * evaṃ kimpākaphalopamā viṣayāḥ sevyamānāḥ sukhaṃ janayanti // PSBh_5.34:32
children.translated_text: * Thus, sense objects, which are like <s>kimpāka</s> fruits, produce pleasure when enjoyed, // PSBh_5.34:32

children.text: * pariṇāme saṃsāre janmanimittatvād duḥkhāni pratipadyante // PSBh_5.34:33
children.translated_text: * but in their ripening, in <s>saṃsāra</s>, because they are the cause of [further] birth, they lead to sufferings. // PSBh_5.34:33

children.text: * ityevaṃ viṣayāṇāmarjane doṣaṃ jñātvā virajyate śatānāṃ sahasrāṇāṃ vā yadi kaścit // PSBh_5.34:34
children.translated_text: * Thus, knowing this defect in the acquisition of sense objects, among hundreds or thousands, perhaps one becomes dispassionate. // PSBh_5.34:34
* Then another [asks]: How so? // PSBh_5.34:35
* Let this defect in the acquisition of sense objects be granted. // PSBh_5.34:36
* Let that be their [problem]. // PSBh_5.34:37
* We do not deny that. // PSBh_5.34:38

children.text: * ayaṃ tv anyaḥ kaṣṭo viṣayadoṣaḥ // PSBh_5.34:39
children.translated_text: * But this other defect of sense objects is grievous. // PSBh_5.34:39
* And what is that? // PSBh_5.34:40
* It is said: the defect of protection (<s>rakṣaṇa</s>). // PSBh_5.34:41

children.text: * arjitānām apyeṣām avaśyam evodyatāyudhena rakṣā vidhātavyā // PSBh_5.34:42
children.translated_text: * Even after these [sense objects] have been acquired, protection must necessarily be maintained with weapon in hand. // PSBh_5.34:42
* Because they are subject to [loss through] kings, fire, thieves, heirs, and shared ownership. // PSBh_5.34:44
* In that there is self-affliction. // PSBh_5.34:45
* And regarding the affliction of others, it is as stated [before]. // PSBh_5.34:46

children.text:
* uktaṃ hi / svadravyaṃ puruṣaṃ corāḥ svamāṃsaṃ piśitāśinaḥ / kleśayanti yathā ghorās tathāhi viṣayā naram // PSBh_5.34:47
* kleśaṃ samanubhuṅkte ca viṣayāṇāṃ parigrahāt / teṣāmeva parityāgāt sarvakleśakṣayo bhavet // PSBh_5.34:48
* ātmaduḥkhopaghātārthaṃ tyāgadharmaṃ samācaret / nāparityajya viṣayān viṣayī sukhamedhate // PSBh_5.34:49
children.translated_text:
* For it has been said: 'Just as thieves torment a man for his property, and flesh-eaters for his own flesh, so indeed do sense objects torment a person grievously. // PSBh_5.34:47
* One experiences suffering from the possession of sense objects; from their complete renunciation, the destruction of all suffering would occur. // PSBh_5.34:48
* For the purpose of warding off one's own suffering, one should practice the <s>dharma</s> of renunciation. Without abandoning sense objects, the sensualist does not flourish in happiness.' // PSBh_5.34:49

children.text: * viṣayāṇāmarjanādau doṣaṃ jñātvā virajyate śatānāṃ sahasrāṇāṃ vā yadi kaścit // PSBh_5.34:50
children.translated_text: * Knowing the defect in acquisition and so forth of sense objects, among hundreds or thousands, perhaps one becomes dispassionate. // PSBh_5.34:50
* Then another [asks]: How so? // PSBh_5.34:51

children.text: * astveṣa viṣayāṇām arjanarakṣaṇādau doṣau bhavatasteṣām // PSBh_5.34:52
children.translated_text: * Let these two defects of sense objects — acquisition, protection, and so forth — be granted as belonging to them. // PSBh_5.34:52
* We do not deny those two. // PSBh_5.34:53

children.text: * ayaṃ tv anyaḥ kaṣṭataro viṣayāṇāṃ doṣaḥ // PSBh_5.34:54
children.translated_text: * But this other defect of sense objects is more grievous. // PSBh_5.34:54
* And what is that? // PSBh_5.34:55
* It is said: the defect of loss (<s>kṣaya</s>). // PSBh_5.34:56

children.text: * arjitānāṃ surakṣitānām apyeṣām avaśyam evābhyupagantavyaḥ // PSBh_5.34:57
children.translated_text: * Even when these have been acquired and well-protected, [loss] must inevitably be accepted. // PSBh_5.34:57
* And upon the loss of sense objects, intense suffering manifests for the sensualists. // PSBh_5.34:58

children.text: * matsyādivad yathodakakṣaye nadīnāṃ tadvat tasmād aśobhanam // PSBh_5.34:59
children.translated_text: * Like fish and such creatures when the water of rivers dries up — likewise, therefore it is not good. // PSBh_5.34:59

children.text:
* uktaṃ hi / traya eva hradā durgāḥ sarvabhūtāpahāriṇaḥ / striyo 'nnapānam aiśvaryaṃ teṣu jāgratha brāhmaṇāḥ // PSBh_5.34:60
* nāsti jñānasamaṃ cakṣurnāsti krodhasamo ripuḥ / nāsti lobhasamaṃ duḥkhaṃ nāsti tyāgāt paraṃ sukham // PSBh_5.34:61
children.translated_text:
* For it has been said: 'There are only three dangerous pools that carry away all beings: women, food and drink, and sovereignty — be vigilant regarding these, O <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>! // PSBh_5.34:60
* There is no eye equal to knowledge, no enemy equal to anger, no suffering equal to greed, no happiness greater than renunciation.' // PSBh_5.34:61
* Thus. // PSBh_5.34:62

children.text: * evaṃ viṣayāṇāṃ kṣayadoṣaṃ jñātvā virajyate śatānāṃ sahasrāṇāṃ vā yadi kaścit // PSBh_5.34:63
children.translated_text: * Thus, knowing the defect of loss in sense objects, among hundreds or thousands, perhaps one becomes dispassionate. // PSBh_5.34:63
* Then another [asks]: How so? // PSBh_5.34:64
* Let these defects of sense objects — acquisition and so forth — be granted. // PSBh_5.34:65

children.text: * ayamanyataraḥ kaṣṭataro doṣaḥ kaścāsāv iti // PSBh_5.34:66
children.translated_text: * This other is the most grievous defect. And what is that? // PSBh_5.34:66
* It is said: the defect of attachment (<s>saṅga</s>). // PSBh_5.34:67

children.text: * yadi tāvad arjanaṃ kriyate rakṣaṇaṃ ca kṣaye ca punaḥ punararjanaṃ kriyate rakṣaṇaṃ ca // PSBh_5.34:68
children.translated_text: * Even if acquisition is performed, and protection, and upon loss, acquisition and protection are performed again and again — // PSBh_5.34:68
* if only the defect of attachment did not exist! // PSBh_5.34:69
* How so? // PSBh_5.34:70

children.text: * yāvad ayam indriyayukto viṣayān abhilaṣati tāvadasya tṛptirupaśāntirautsukyavinivṛttiśca na bhavati // PSBh_5.34:71
children.translated_text: * As long as this person, endowed with senses, craves sense objects, so long there is no satisfaction, no peace, no cessation of restless longing for him. // PSBh_5.34:71

children.text: * bhūya eva viṣayān anveṣṭum ārabhate // PSBh_5.34:72
children.translated_text: * He begins to seek sense objects yet again. // PSBh_5.34:72
* Then again dissatisfaction and the rest arise, just as before. // PSBh_5.34:73
* Therefore it is not good. // PSBh_5.34:74

children.text:
* uktaṃ hi / na jātu kāmaḥ kāmānām upabhogena śāmyati / haviṣā kṛṣṇavartmeva bhūya evābhivardhate // PSBh_5.34:75
* yat pṛthivyāṃ vrīhiyavaṃ hiraṇyaṃ paśavaḥ striyaḥ / nālamekasya tat tṛptyai tasmād vidvān śamaṃ vrajet // PSBh_5.34:76
children.translated_text:
* For it has been said: 'Desire is never quenched by the enjoyment of desires; like fire [fed] with oblations, it only grows ever more. // PSBh_5.34:75
* All the rice, barley, gold, cattle, and women on earth are not enough to satisfy one person — therefore the wise one should seek peace.' // PSBh_5.34:76
* Thus. // PSBh_5.34:77

children.text: * evaṃ viṣayāṇāṃ saṅgadoṣaṃ jñātvā virajyate śatānāṃ sahasrāṇāṃ vā yadi kaścit // PSBh_5.34:78
children.translated_text: * Thus, knowing the defect of attachment in sense objects, among hundreds or thousands, perhaps one becomes dispassionate. // PSBh_5.34:78
* Then another [asks]: How so? // PSBh_5.34:79
* Let these defects of sense objects — acquisition and so forth — be granted. // PSBh_5.34:80
* Let those be their [problem]. // PSBh_5.34:81
* We do not deny those. // PSBh_5.34:82

children.text: * ayaṃ tv anyaḥ kaṣṭatamo viṣayāṇāṃ doṣaḥ // PSBh_5.34:83
children.translated_text: * But this other defect of sense objects is the most grievous. // PSBh_5.34:83
* And what is that? // PSBh_5.34:84
* It is said: the defect of violence (<s>hiṃsā</s>). // PSBh_5.34:85

children.text: * śakyameteṣāṃ viṣayāṇām arjanādi kartum indriyalaulyadoṣo'pi bhavatu // PSBh_5.34:86
children.translated_text: * It may be possible to perform acquisition and so forth of these sense objects; let the defect of sensory restlessness also exist — // PSBh_5.34:86
* if only the defect of violence did not exist! // PSBh_5.34:87
* How so? // PSBh_5.34:88

children.text: * eteṣāmeva viṣayāṇāmupabhoge vartatā avaśyameva hiṃsādidoṣāḥ kartavyāḥ // PSBh_5.34:89
children.translated_text: * For one engaged in the enjoyment of these very sense objects, defects such as violence and the rest must inevitably be committed. // PSBh_5.34:89

children.text: * nānupahatya bhūtāni viṣayopabhogaḥ śakyate kartum // PSBh_5.34:91
children.translated_text: * Because enjoyment of sense objects cannot be accomplished without harming beings. // PSBh_5.34:91
* In that regard, first, this [harm] is committed on account of sound. // PSBh_5.34:92

children.text: * tadyathā vīṇānimittaṃ khadirādīn chidyamānān dṛṣṭvā tantrīnimittaṃ vā kāṃściddhiṃsyamānān dṛṣṭvā yadi kaścid brūyād aśobhano'yaṃ bhūtavadhaḥ kriyate kadanaṃ karma kriyate sa vaktavyo'tra te na śobhano'yam // PSBh_5.34:93
children.translated_text: * For example: upon seeing <s>khadira</s> trees and such being cut down for the sake of a <s>vīṇā</s>, or upon seeing certain creatures being killed for the sake of strings — if someone were to say, 'This killing of creatures that is being done is not good; a cruel deed is being done,' he should be told: 'This is not good for you either — // PSBh_5.34:93

children.text: * yadā bhikṣāpradagṛheṣu ramyān śabdān śroṣyasi tatra paraḥ paritoṣo bhaviṣyati // PSBh_5.34:94
children.translated_text: * when you will hear delightful sounds in the houses of alms-givers, there you will take great pleasure in them.' // PSBh_5.34:94

children.text: * tathā sūtrādinimittaṃ tāvad bhūtavadhaḥ kriyate // PSBh_5.34:95
children.translated_text: * Likewise, for the sake of thread and the like, killing of beings is carried out. // PSBh 5.34:95

children.text: * tadyathā kośakārādīn vadhyamānān dṛṣṭvā yadi kaścid brūyād aśobhano'yaṃ bhūtavadhaḥ kadanaṃ karma kriyate // PSBh_5.34:96
children.translated_text: * For example, having seen silkworms and the like being killed, if someone were to say, 'This killing of beings is unseemly; a destructive act is being performed' — // PSBh 5.34:96

children.text: * sa vaktavyo'tra te na śobhano'yam yadā bhikṣadagṛheṣu mṛdutarasparśāni vāsāṃsi prāpsyasi tatra te paraḥ paritoṣo bhaviṣyati // PSBh_5.34:97
children.translated_text: * he should be told: 'You do not find this unseemly; when in beggars' houses you will obtain garments of the softest touch — there your supreme satisfaction will arise.' // PSBh 5.34:97

children.text: * tathā rūpanimittaṃ tāvad bhūtavadhaḥ kriyate // PSBh_5.34:98
children.translated_text: * Likewise, for the sake of form, killing of beings is carried out. // PSBh 5.34:98

children.text: * tadyathā aśokādīn vṛkṣān chidyamānāndṛṣṭvā hastinaśca dantanimittaṃ vadhyamānān dṛṣṭvā yadi kaścid brūyād aśobhano 'yaṃ bhūtavadhaḥ kadanaṃ karma kriyate sa vaktavyo'tra te na śobhano'yam // PSBh_5.34:99
children.translated_text: * For example, having seen <s>aśoka</s> trees and the like being cut down, and elephants being killed for the sake of their tusks — if someone were to say, 'This killing of beings is unseemly; a destructive act is being performed' — he should be told: 'You do not find this unseemly; // PSBh 5.34:99

children.text: * yadā bhikṣadagṛham alaṃkṛtakavāṭagopuraṃ drakṣyasi tatra te paraḥ paritoṣo bhaviṣyati // PSBh_5.34:100
children.translated_text: * when you will see beggars' houses adorned with decorated doors and gate-towers — there your supreme satisfaction will arise.' // PSBh 5.34:100

children.text: * tathā rasanimittaṃ tāvad bhūtavadhaḥ kriyate // PSBh_5.34:101
children.translated_text: * Likewise, for the sake of taste, killing of beings is carried out. // PSBh 5.34:101

children.text: * tadyathā tittirimayūravarāhādīn vadhyamānān dṛṣṭvā yadi kaścid brūyād aśobhano 'yaṃ bhūtavadhaḥ kriyate // PSBh_5.34:102
children.translated_text: * For example, having seen partridges, peacocks, boars, and the like being killed — if someone were to say, 'This killing of beings is unseemly; [a destructive act] is being performed' — // PSBh 5.34:102

children.text: * sa vaktavyo'tra te na śobhano'yam // PSBh_5.34:103
children.translated_text: * he should be told: 'You do not find this unseemly; // PSBh 5.34:103

children.text: * yadā bhikṣadagṛheṣu ṣaḍrasamāṃsaprakārair bhokṣyase tatra te paraḥ paritoṣo bhaviṣyati // PSBh_5.34:104
children.translated_text: * when in beggars' houses you will eat [dishes prepared] with six tastes and varieties of meat — there your supreme satisfaction will arise.' // PSBh 5.34:104

children.text: * tathā gandhanimittaṃ tāvad bhūtavadhaḥ kriyate / tadyathā pañcanakhādīn vadhyamānān dṛṣṭvā yadi kaścid brūyād aśobhano'yaṃ bhūtavadhaḥ kadanaṃ karma kriyate // PSBh_5.34:105
