children.translated_text: * Likewise, for the sake of smell, killing of beings is carried out. For example, having seen five-clawed animals and the like being killed — if someone were to say, 'This killing of beings is unseemly; a destructive act is being performed' — // PSBh 5.34:105

children.text: * sa vaktavyo'tra te na śobhano'yam // PSBh_5.34:106
children.translated_text: * he should be told: 'You do not find this unseemly; // PSBh 5.34:106

children.text: * yadā bhikṣadagṛheṣu sugandhān gandhān prāpsyasi tatra te paritoṣo bhaviṣyati // PSBh_5.34:107
children.translated_text: * when in beggars' houses you will obtain fragrant perfumes — there your satisfaction will arise.' // PSBh 5.34:107

children.text: * evam / kāmaḥ krodhaśca lobhaśca bhayaṃ svapnaśca pañcamaḥ / rāgo dveṣaśca mohaśca / iti // PSBh_5.34:108
children.translated_text: * Thus: 'Desire, anger, greed, fear, and sleep as the fifth; passion, aversion, and delusion' — thus. // PSBh 5.34:108

children.text: * arjanarakṣaṇakṣayasaṅgahiṃsādimūlatvād ato'tra śabdādayo viṣayā doṣāḥ // PSBh_5.34:109
children.translated_text: * Because [sense-objects] are the root of acquisition, protection, loss, attachment, violence, and the like — therefore here sound and the other sense-objects are faults (<s>doṣa</s>). // PSBh 5.34:109
* And how are they faults? // PSBh 5.34:110
* In the distraction of the mind. // PSBh 5.34:111
* They corrupt (<s>dūṣayanti</s>) — therefore they are faults (<s>doṣa</s>). // PSBh 5.34:112

children.text: * dūṣayanti yasmād adhyayanadhyānādiniṣṭhaṃ sādhakaṃ vicittaṃ kurvantīti doṣāḥ // PSBh_5.34:113
children.translated_text: * Because they corrupt — since they disturb the practitioner who is devoted to study, meditation, and the like — they are faults. // PSBh 5.34:113
* 'Of the faults' (<s>doṣāṇām</s>) is genitive plural. // PSBh 5.34:114

children.text: * āha kiṃ doṣāṇāmeva doṣebhya eva vā chettavyamuktam // PSBh_5.34:115
children.translated_text: * He asks: Is it stated that the faults alone or [something arising] from the faults should be cut? // PSBh 5.34:115
* Since he says: The cause (<s>hetu</s>). // PSBh 5.34:117
* Here, the cause is <s>adharma</s> (demerit). // PSBh 5.34:118

children.text: * cittacyutihetutvāt yasmāt tenāviṣṭaḥ sādhako 'dhyayanasmaraṇādibhyaś cyavatītyato 'trādharmo hetuḥ dharmastu sthityādihetuḥ // PSBh_5.34:120
children.translated_text: * Because it is the cause of the mind's falling away; since the practitioner, possessed by it, falls away from study, recollection, and the like — therefore here <s>adharma</s> is the cause. But <s>dharma</s> (merit) is the cause of stability and the like. // PSBh 5.34:120
* He asks: Of what is this the cause? // PSBh 5.34:121
* It is said: Of the net (<s>jāla</s>). // PSBh 5.34:122

children.text: * atra yadā adharmaḥ kūṭastho 'nārabdhakāryas tadā heturityucyate // PSBh_5.34:123
children.translated_text: * Here, when <s>adharma</s> remains fixed (<s>kūṭastha</s>) with its effects not yet begun, it is called 'the cause.' // PSBh 5.34:123

children.text: * yadā tv ajñānavāsanāvaśāddhṛtyā sthityādibhāvam āpannastadā jālākhyāṃ labhate // PSBh_5.34:124
children.translated_text: * But when, through the force of the impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) of ignorance, it has attained the state of stability and the like through perseverance (<s>dhṛti</s>), then it obtains the designation 'net' (<s>jāla</s>). // PSBh 5.34:124
* Because, like a net and the like, [it catches] the aggregate — this is the meaning. // PSBh 5.34:126
* Because there is no other cause of that nature. // PSBh 5.34:127
* 'Of the net' (<s>jālasya</s>) — the genitive is construed with 'cutting.' // PSBh 5.34:128
* Therefore it is indeed cut. // PSBh 5.34:129
* Because both the cause and the net arise from the conjunction of faults and mind. // PSBh 5.34:131

children.text: * āha kiṃ pratisambandhi doṣahetujālasaṃśliṣṭaṃ bhavati // PSBh_5.34:132
children.translated_text: * He asks: Is that which is associated with the faults, cause, and net a correlate? // PSBh 5.34:132
* Then how is it expressed? // PSBh 5.34:133
* To that it is said: The root (<s>mūla</s>). // PSBh 5.34:134
* Here, when 'root' is said, [the question arises:] of what? // PSBh 5.34:135

* Since the cause and the net arise from the conjunction of faults and mind — from [their] activity — therefore it is understood that the root here is precisely the root of conjunction (<s>saṃyogamūla</s>). // PSBh 5.34:136

children.text: * āha kenāyaṃ chettā mūlacchedaṃ karoti // PSBh_5.34:137
children.translated_text: * He asks: By what means does this cutter perform the cutting of the root? // PSBh 5.34:137
* To that it is said: // PSBh 5.34:138
* As it has been said: 'Desire, anger, greed, fear, and sleep as the fifth; passion, hatred, and delusion —' // PSBh_5.34:19
By the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) — || PS 5.35 ||
* The <s>buddhi</s> called the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) has been spoken of. // PSBh 5.35:1

children.text: * tayā dharmasmṛticodanādisahitayā vidyāgṛhītayā buddhyā chedyaṃ sthāpyaṃ cetyarthaḥ // PSBh_5.35:2
children.translated_text: * By that <s>buddhi</s>, accompanied by the remembrance of <s>dharma</s>, impulse, and the like, and grasped by knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>) — [the net] should be cut and [the mind] should be established; this is the meaning. // PSBh 5.35:2

children.text: * āha kiṃ doṣādisahagatavadhādiviśliṣṭamapi tat paratantramucyate // PSBh_5.35:3
children.translated_text: * He asks: Is that which is separated from the killing of [faults] accompanied by faults and the like still called dependent? // PSBh 5.35:3
* Since he says: When the [entity] designated as 'root' has ceased — // PSBh 5.35:5
The collected mind (<s>saṃcitta</s>) — || PS 5.36 ||

children.text: * atra sam iti doṣādiviśliṣṭaṃ svayameva svaguṇatvena parigṛhyate agnyuṣṇatvavadity ānubandhitvāc cetyarthaḥ // PSBh_5.36:1
children.translated_text: * Here, 'sam' [indicates that], separated from faults and the like, [the mind] itself is appropriated by its own quality — like the heat of fire; and because of its inherent connection; this is the meaning. // PSBh 5.36:1
* He asks: What is that? // PSBh 5.36:2
* It is said: The mind (<s>citta</s>). // PSBh 5.36:3

children.text: * atra citī saṃjñāne cetayati cinoti vā aneneti cittam // PSBh_5.36:4
children.translated_text: * Here, '<s>cit</s>' [means] 'to cognize'; it cognizes (<s>cetayati</s>) or it accumulates (<s>cinoti</s>) by this — therefore [it is called] <s>citta</s> (mind). // PSBh 5.36:4

children.text: * cetayati sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ padārthān cinoti dharmādharmau arjayatītyataḥ cetayati cinoti vā aneneti cittam // PSBh_5.36:5
children.translated_text: * It cognizes pleasure and pain and objects; it accumulates <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, it earns [them] — therefore it cognizes or accumulates by this; hence [it is called] <s>citta</s>. // PSBh 5.36:5
* <s>Citta</s> (mind), <s>manas</s> (mind), and <s>antaḥkaraṇa</s> (inner organ) [are synonyms] — this is the meaning. // PSBh 5.36:6

children.text: * atra tv etebhyo doṣahetutvādibhyo yugapac chettavyaṃ vidyamānebhyastu kramaśaḥ kṣapaṇamiti // PSBh_5.36:7
children.translated_text: * Here, however, from these — the faults, cause, and the like — [the net] should be cut simultaneously from all present [ones]; but the destruction should proceed gradually. // PSBh 5.36:7

children.text: * āha chittvā tac cittaṃ kiṃ kartavyam // PSBh_5.36:8
children.translated_text: * He asks: Having cut that mind, what should be done? // PSBh 5.36:8
* It is said: [It should be] established in <s>Rudra</s>. // PSBh 5.36:9
* Since he says: // PSBh 5.36:10
And having established [the mind] in <s>Rudra</s> — || PS 5.37 ||
* Here, '<s>sthā</s>' (to stand) [means] the cessation of movement. // PSBh 5.37:1
* The non-interruption of the mind from <s>Rudra</s> is called 'stability' (<s>sthiti</s>). // PSBh 5.37:2

children.text: * vā iti śmaśānādyavasthasya smṛtikarmaṇo niṣṭhā // PSBh_5.37:3
children.translated_text: * 'Or' (<s>vā</s>) indicates the completion of the practice of recollection in the state of the cremation-ground and the like. // PSBh 5.37:3
* The word 'and' (<s>ca</s>) indicates conjunction. // PSBh 5.37:4

children.text: * na kevalaṃ chittvā stheyaṃ kiṃtu sthāpayitavyaṃ cetyarthaḥ // PSBh_5.37:5
children.translated_text: * Not only should [the net] be cut, but [the mind] should be established [in Rudra] as well — this is the meaning. // PSBh 5.37:5
* 'In <s>Rudra</s>' designates the cause. // PSBh 5.37:6

children.text: * rudrasya rudratvaṃ pūrvoktam rudra ityaupaśleṣikaṃ saṃnidhānam // PSBh_5.37:7
children.translated_text: * The <s>Rudratva</s> of <s>Rudra</s> has been stated above. 'In <s>Rudra</s>' indicates proximity and close connection. // PSBh 5.37:7

children.text: * rudre cittam upaśleṣayitavyaṃ nānyatrety arthaḥ // PSBh_5.37:8
children.translated_text: * The mind should be brought into close connection with <s>Rudra</s>, not elsewhere — this is the meaning. // PSBh 5.37:8

children.text: * evaṃ viṣayebhya indriyāṇāṃ jayaḥ kartavyaḥ // PSBh_5.37:9
children.translated_text: * Thus, the conquest of the senses from [attachment to] sense-objects should be performed. // PSBh 5.37:9
* Here, the conqueror is the self (<s>ātman</s>). // PSBh 5.37:10
* That by which [the senses] are to be conquered is the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>). // PSBh 5.37:11
* How they are to be conquered — gradually. // PSBh 5.37:12
* For what purpose they are to be conquered — for the purpose of the stability of the mind (<s>cittasthiti</s>). // PSBh 5.37:13

children.text: * yasmiṃśca jite jitāni bhavanti cittam ityetadapi vyākhyātam // PSBh_5.37:14
children.translated_text: * And in what [once] conquered, [all else] becomes conquered — the mind (<s>citta</s>); this too has been explained. // PSBh 5.37:14
* Thus, [this] should also be applied to recitation (<s>japa</s>), restraint (<s>yantraṇa</s>), concentration (<s>dhāraṇā</s>), the essential cutting, and the like. // PSBh 5.37:15

children.text: * tathāntaḥkaraṇavṛttim āsthāya kālaviśeṣanimittaraśmimaṇidīpavat tathātmavṛttiradhyayanadhyānasmaraṇādīni cittasthitiśca vyākhyātā // PSBh_5.37:16
children.translated_text: * Likewise, having recourse to the function of the inner organ, [the process is] like a ray, a jewel, or a lamp conditioned by a particular time; and thus the self's functions — study, meditation, recollection, and the like — and the stability of the mind have been explained. // PSBh 5.37:16
* [This] verse is self-explanatory. // PSBh 5.37:17

children.text: * āha kāryakaraṇaṃ ca tac cittasthitisamakālam eva rudre sthitāni tāni yuktāni // PSBh_5.37:18
children.translated_text: * He says: And those instruments and effects — simultaneously with the stability of the mind — are established in <s>Rudra</s>, and are thereby absorbed [in yoga]. // PSBh 5.37:18

children.text: * atha kiṃ tānyeva yuktasya lakṣaṇāni iti // PSBh_5.37:19
children.translated_text: * Now, are these alone the characteristics of the one absorbed [in yoga]? // PSBh 5.37:19
* It is said: No. // PSBh 5.37:20
* Since he says: // PSBh 5.37:21
Alone, secure, being [free], beyond sorrow — || PS 5.38 ||

children.text: * atra dharmādharmayor vṛttyoruparame avasitaprayojanatvāt pakvaphalavat sarpakañcukavad gataprāyeṣu kāryakaraṇeṣu rudre sthitacitto niṣkala eka ityabhidhīyate // PSBh_5.38:1
children.translated_text: * Here, when the two functions of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> have ceased — since the purpose has been accomplished, like a ripe fruit, like a snake's sloughed skin — when the instruments and effects have mostly departed, [the practitioner] with mind established in <s>Rudra</s>, without parts (<s>niṣkala</s>), is designated 'alone' (<s>eka</s>). // PSBh 5.38:1

children.text: * tathā yogavyāsaṅgakare 'dharme nivṛtte doṣādiviśliṣṭo nistīrṇakāntāravad avasthito rudre sthitacittaḥ kṣemī ityabhidhīyate // PSBh_5.38:2
children.translated_text: * Likewise, when the <s>adharma</s> that causes obstruction to <s>yoga</s> has ceased, separated from faults and the like, abiding like one who has crossed a wilderness, with mind established in <s>Rudra</s> — [such a one] is designated 'secure' (<s>kṣemin</s>). // PSBh 5.38:2

children.text: * tathā sūkṣmasthūlasabāhyābhyantarasalakṣaṇavilakṣaṇāsu kriyāsu vinivṛttāsu rudre sthitacitto niṣkriyaḥ san ityabhidhīyate // PSBh_5.38:3
children.translated_text: * Likewise, when all activities — subtle and gross, external and internal, well-characterized and ill-characterized — have ceased, with mind established in <s>Rudra</s>, without activity, [such a one] is designated as 'being' (<s>san</s>). // PSBh 5.38:3
* He asks: Now, how is it understood that this one is without activity? // PSBh 5.38:4
* And are only three characteristics of the one absorbed [in yoga stated] here? // PSBh 5.38:5
* It is said: No. // PSBh 5.38:6
* Since he says: 'Beyond sorrow' (<s>vītaśoka</s>). // PSBh 5.38:7
* Here, 'sorrow' (<s>śoka</s>) and 'thought' (<s>cintā</s>) are not different in meaning. // PSBh 5.38:8

children.text: * sā ca cintā dvividhā bhavati // PSBh_5.38:9
children.translated_text: * And that thought is twofold: // PSBh 5.38:9
* Wholesome (<s>kuśala</s>) and unwholesome (<s>akuśala</s>). // PSBh 5.38:10
* There, wholesome [thought] means study, meditation, recollection, and the like. // PSBh 5.38:11
* Unwholesome [thought] means non-study, non-meditation, non-recollection, and the like. // PSBh 5.38:12

children.text: * evaṃ japayantraṇadhāraṇādīṃśca kariṣyāmi na kariṣyāmītyevam anekavidhāyāmapi cintāyāṃ vinivṛttāyāṃ vyapagataśoko vītaśoka ityabhidhīyate // PSBh_5.38:13
children.translated_text: * Thus, when all thought of manifold kinds — such as 'I will perform recitation, restraint, concentration, and the like' or 'I will not perform [them]' — has ceased, one who has gone beyond sorrow is designated 'beyond sorrow' (<s>vītaśoka</s>). // PSBh 5.38:13
* Thus, here the topic of <s>yoga</s> is concluded. // PSBh 5.38:14
* Because the meanings have been etymologically explained. // PSBh 5.38:16

children.text: * yasmād asyādhyāyasyādāv uddiṣṭā ye padārthāste doṣacchedāsaṅgasthityādiṣu vyākhyātāḥ // PSBh_5.38:17
children.translated_text: * Since the topics enumerated at the beginning of this chapter have been explained in [the sections on] the cutting of faults, non-attachment, stability, and the like. // PSBh 5.38:17

children.text: * evamanena yuktena brahmādayo devā viśeṣitā bhavanti // PSBh_5.38:18
children.translated_text: * Thus, by this one absorbed [in yoga], <s>Brahmā</s> and the other gods are surpassed. // PSBh 5.38:18
* Because of the statement of non-attachment and the like [applying to him]. // PSBh 5.38:19

children.text: * āha atha sāṃkhyayogamuktāḥ kiṃ na viśeṣitāḥ // PSBh_5.38:20
children.translated_text: * He asks: Now, are those liberated through <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and <s>Yoga</s> [also] not surpassed? // PSBh 5.38:20
* It is said: They are surpassed. // PSBh 5.38:21
* Because of the superiority of that [Pāśupata] knowledge. // PSBh 5.38:23

children.text: * sāṃkhyayogamuktāḥ kaivalyagatāḥ svātmaparātmajñānarahitāḥ saṃmūrchitavat sthitāḥ // PSBh_5.38:25
children.translated_text: * Those liberated through <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and <s>Yoga</s>, having gone to the state of <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation), stand devoid of knowledge of one's own self and another's self, as if in a state of unconsciousness. // PSBh 5.38:25
* But this one [the Pāśupata yogin] has knowledge. // PSBh 5.38:26
* Since he says: // PSBh 5.38:27
Vigilant, [he] should reach the end of sufferings, through the grace of the Lord (<s>Īśa</s>) — || PS 5.39 ||
* Thus. // PSBh 5.39:1
* Acting thus, the omniscient one demonstrates to him his freedom from delusion (<s>asaṃmoha</s>). // PSBh 5.39:2

children.text: * uktam / kāryakaraṇāñjanebhyo nirañjanebhyaśca sarvapuruṣebhyaḥ / aprāptāntaṃ puruṣaṃ yo 'bhyadhikaṃ varṇayet sa budhaḥ // PSBh_5.39:3

children.translated_text: * He says: What was to be reached has been reached. // PSBh 5.39:4
* Now, is this merely figurative? // PSBh 5.39:5
* It is said: No. // PSBh 5.39:6
* Because of [our] incomplete knowledge, our system does not culminate merely in <s>yoga</s>. // PSBh 5.39:7
* Rather, even beyond that <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation), the omniscient one speaks. // PSBh 5.39:8
* 'Vigilant (<s>apramādin</s>), [one] should reach the end of sufferings, through the grace of the Lord.' // PSBh 5.39:9

children.text: * atra pramādaśabdo 'nāgatānavadhānagatatvaṃ pāratantryaṃ ca khyāpayatītyarthaḥ // PSBh_5.39:10
children.translated_text: * Here, the word 'carelessness' (<s>pramāda</s>) indicates inattention to the future and the state of dependence — this is the meaning. // PSBh 5.39:10

children.text: * tadaṅkuraparirakṣaṇavad anāgatakālapratīkārakaraṇena caivāyam apramādīśabdo draṣṭavyaḥ // PSBh_5.39:11
children.translated_text: * Like the protection of a sprout, and by making provision for the future — thus this word 'vigilant' (<s>apramādin</s>) should be understood. // PSBh 5.39:11
* Therefore, one should remain vigilant and absorbed [in yoga]. // PSBh 5.39:12
* Likewise, for one who thus conducts himself, the sovereign power of <s>Maheśvara</s> has indeed been attained — this has been stated. // PSBh 5.39:13
* 'Should reach' (<s>gacchet</s>) — 'going' (<s>gati</s>) means attainment. // PSBh 5.39:14
* The roots <s>gam</s> and <s>sṛp</s> mean 'to go.' [PSBh 5.39:15]
* He 'attains' — thus [he is called] the self; like the yellowing of leaves and the ripening of fruit. [PSBh 5.39:16]

children.text: * tasminneva pravartato yo 'yaṃ duḥkhāpoho guṇastatreyaṃ gatiriti saṃjñā kriyata ityarthaḥ // PSBh_5.39:18
children.translated_text: * For one who proceeds in that very [state], this quality of the removal of suffering — therein the designation 'going' (<s>gati</s>) is applied; this is the meaning. [PSBh 5.39:18]

* 'Of sufferings' — here the well-known sufferings are <s>ādhyātmika</s> (relating to the self), <s>ādhibhautika</s> (relating to beings), and <s>ādhidaivika</s> (relating to the gods). [PSBh 5.39:19]

children.text: * tatrādhyātmikaṃ dvividhaṃ duḥkhaṃ śārīraṃ mānasaṃ ca // PSBh_5.39:20
children.translated_text: * Of these, <s>ādhyātmika</s> suffering is twofold: bodily and mental. [PSBh 5.39:20]

children.text: * tatra manasi bhavaṃ mānasaṃ krodhalobhamohabhayaviṣāderṣyāsūyādveṣamadamānamātsaryāratyādyaviśeṣadarśanādinimittaṃ tad duḥkham // PSBh_5.39:21
children.translated_text: * Mental suffering is that arising in the mind — caused by anger, greed, delusion, fear, poison, jealousy, envy, hatred, intoxication, pride, selfishness, dissatisfaction, failure to perceive distinctions, and so forth. [PSBh 5.39:21]

* Likewise, bodily suffering too is that produced from causes such as headache, toothache, eye disease, fever, indigestion, dysentery, cough, breathing difficulties, abdominal ailments, and so forth. [PSBh 5.39:22]
* Likewise, there is another fivefold suffering. [PSBh 5.39:23]
* Namely: [suffering of the] womb, birth, ignorance, old age, and death. [PSBh 5.39:24]

children.text: * tatra garbhe tāvad yadāyaṃ puruṣo māturudare nyastagātraḥ khaṇḍaśakaṭastha iva pumān niyamaśramam anubhavamāno 'vakāśarahitaḥ ākuñcanaprasāraṇādiṣv aparyāptāvakāśaḥ sarvakriyāsu niruddha ityevam advārake andhatamasi mūḍho bandhanastha iva pumān avaśyaṃ samanubhavati // PSBh_5.39:25
children.translated_text: * Of these, first in the womb: when this <s>puruṣa</s> (person), with limbs deposited in the mother's belly, like a person lying in a broken cart, experiencing the toil of confinement, without space, with insufficient room for contracting, extending, and so forth, obstructed in all activities — thus in a doorless pitch-darkness, the person, bewildered as if bound in prison, necessarily experiences [this suffering]. [PSBh 5.39:25]

children.text: * cetanatvād bhoktṛtvāt tanmayatvāc ca na tu kāryakaraṇāni // PSBh_5.39:27
children.translated_text: * Because of being conscious, because of being an experiencer, and because of being pervaded by it — but not the effects and instruments [body and senses]. [PSBh 5.39:27]
* Because of being unconscious, because of being non-experiencers, and because of not being pervaded by it. [PSBh 5.39:29]
* Likewise, the suffering of birth too: [PSBh 5.39:30]

children.text: * yadāyaṃ puruṣo jāyamānaḥ purīṣapaṅkamagnavadano mūtradhārābhir abhiṣicyamāno dehe saṃvṛtadvārake yoniniḥsaraṇasaṃkaṭe 'tyarthaṃ pīḍyamāno 'sthimarmabandhanaiḥ praghṛṣyamāṇo vikrośan ninadaṃś ca jāyate // PSBh_5.39:31
children.translated_text: * When this <s>puruṣa</s>, being born, with face submerged as if in a mire of feces, being sprinkled by streams of urine, in a body whose openings are enclosed, being intensely pressed in the narrow passage of exit from the womb, being scraped by the bones, vital points, and ligaments, crying out and wailing — [thus] he is born. [PSBh 5.39:31]

children.text: * paścāt punastasyānucitena bāhyena vāyunā jananāvartena spṛṣṭasya tīvraṃ duḥkhamabhivyajyate // PSBh_5.39:32
children.translated_text: * Afterwards again, when he is touched by the unfamiliar external wind and the whirlpool of birth, intense suffering manifests for him. [PSBh 5.39:32]
* Like one raised by a king [being suddenly exposed to hardship]. [PSBh 5.39:33]
* And by that, the impressions (<s>saṃskāras</s>) that are the cause of memory from previous births are destroyed for him. [PSBh 5.39:34]
* Thus, the suffering of birth is experienced by the <s>puruṣa</s> alone. [PSBh 5.39:35]
* Because of being conscious, because of being an experiencer, and because of being pervaded by it. [PSBh 5.39:37]
* But not the effects and instruments. [PSBh 5.39:38]
* Because of being unconscious, because of being non-experiencers, and because of not being pervaded by it. [PSBh 5.39:40]

children.text: * tathā ajñānaduḥkhamapi ahaṃkārasatkṛtagātro na jānan ko 'haṃ kuto'haṃ kasyāhaṃ kena vā bandhanena baddho'hamiti kiṃ kāraṇaṃ kimakāraṇaṃ kiṃ bhakṣyaṃ kimabhakṣyaṃ kiṃ peyaṃ kimapeyaṃ kiṃ satyaṃ kimasatyaṃ kim jñānaṃ kimajñānam ityajñānaduḥkhaṃ puruṣa evānubhavati // PSBh_5.39:41
children.translated_text: * Likewise, the suffering of ignorance too: with a body honored by egoism (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>), not knowing — 'Who am I? From where am I? Whose am I? By what bond am I bound? What is the cause? What is not the cause? What is to be eaten? What is not to be eaten? What is to be drunk? What is not to be drunk? What is true? What is false? What is knowledge? What is ignorance?' — thus the suffering of ignorance is experienced by the <s>puruṣa</s> alone. [PSBh 5.39:41]
* Because of being conscious, because of being an experiencer, and because of being pervaded by it. [PSBh 5.39:43]
* But not the effects and instruments. [PSBh 5.39:44]
* Because of being unconscious, because of being non-experiencers, and because of not being pervaded by it. [PSBh 5.39:46]
* Likewise, the suffering of old age too: [PSBh 5.39:47]

children.text: * yadāyaṃ puruṣo jarājarjaritaḥ kṛśaśarīraḥ śithilīkṛtanayanakapolanāsikābhrūdaśanāvaraṇaḥ krauñcajānuriva nirviṇṇo 'kṣidūṣikādiṣvapakarṣaṇādiṣv asamartho vihaṃga iva lūnapakṣo laṅghanaplavanadhāvanādiṣv asamarthaḥ pūrvātītāni bhogavyāyāmaśilpakarmāṇy anusmaramāṇaḥ smṛtivaikalyam āpanno 'vaśyaṃ kleśamanubhavati // PSBh_5.39:48
children.translated_text: * When this <s>puruṣa</s>, worn out by old age, with an emaciated body, with loosened eyes, cheeks, nose, eyebrows, teeth, and coverings, dejected like a crane-kneed [bird], unable to remove eye-discharge and such, like a bird with clipped wings, unable to leap, jump, run, and so forth, remembering past enjoyments, exercises, and craft-works, having arrived at the failure of memory — he necessarily experiences affliction. [PSBh 5.39:48]
* Because of being conscious, because of being an experiencer, and because of being pervaded by it. [PSBh 5.39:50]
* But not the effects and instruments. [PSBh 5.39:51]
* Because of being unconscious, because of being non-experiencers, and because of not being pervaded by it. [PSBh 5.39:53]
* Likewise, the suffering of death too: [PSBh 5.39:54]

children.text: * yadāyaṃ puruṣo maraṇasamaye ślathakaraṇaḥ śirodharam avalambamānaḥ śvāsanocchvasanatatparaḥ khurukhurāyamāṇakaṇṭhaḥ svopārjitamaṇikanakadhanadhānyapatnīputrapaśusaṃghātaḥ kasya bhaviṣyatīty anutapyamānaḥ viṣayānanu dodūyamānaḥ salilādi yācamāno viraktavadano marmabhiś chidyamānair avaśyaṃ kleśamanubhavati // PSBh_5.39:55
children.translated_text: * When this <s>puruṣa</s>, at the time of dying, with loosened instruments [senses], hanging his head, intent on breathing in and breathing out, with throat rattling, agonizing over 'to whom will my self-acquired jewels, gold, wealth, grain, wife, sons, and herds of animals belong?', shuddering after the sense-objects, begging for water and such, with a pallid face, being cut at the vital points — he necessarily experiences affliction. [PSBh 5.39:55]
* Because of being conscious, because of being an experiencer, and because of being pervaded by it. [PSBh 5.39:57]
* But not the effects and instruments. [PSBh 5.39:58]
* Because of being unconscious, because of being non-experiencers, and because of not being pervaded by it. [PSBh 5.39:60]

children.text: * uktaṃ hi / garbhe praviśan duḥkhaṃ nivasan duḥkhaṃ viniṣkraman duḥkham / jātaśca duḥkham ṛcchati tasmādapunarbhavaḥ śreyān // PSBh_5.39:61
children.translated_text: * For it has been said: 'Entering the womb is suffering, dwelling [therein] is suffering, coming out is suffering; and once born, one encounters suffering. Therefore, non-return to existence is better.' [PSBh 5.39:61]
* Thus. [PSBh 5.39:62]
* Likewise, there is another fivefold suffering. [PSBh 5.39:63]

children.text: * tadyathā ihalokabhayaṃ paralokabhayam ahitasaṃprayogaḥ hitaviprayogaḥ icchāvyāghātaśceti // PSBh_5.39:64
children.translated_text: * Namely: fear of this world, fear of the next world, conjunction with the undesirable, separation from the desirable, and frustration of desire. [PSBh 5.39:64]
* Likewise, there is another threefold suffering. [PSBh 5.39:65]

children.text: * ādhyātmikamajñānaṃ puruṣe ādhibhautikaṃ viṣayitvam ādhidaivikaṃ ca paśutvaṃ trividham aparaṃ prāhuḥ // PSBh_5.39:66
children.translated_text: * They speak of another threefold [suffering]: <s>ādhyātmika</s> is ignorance in the <s>puruṣa</s>, <s>ādhibhautika</s> is being subject to sense-objects, and <s>ādhidaivika</s> is the state of being a <s>paśu</s> (bound soul). [PSBh 5.39:66]

children.text: * ityevamādīni bādhanāyā aprītiphalāyā janmanimittatvād duḥkhānītyupacaryante // PSBh_5.39:67
children.translated_text: * Thus such [conditions] and others — because they are the cause of affliction resulting in displeasure, and because of being the cause of birth — are figuratively called 'sufferings.' [PSBh 5.39:67]

children.text: * āha caraṇādhikāre 'natiprasādād aśivatvasaṃjñake sarvāṇy anatiprasādabījatvāt kuto nātyantanivṛttāni bhavanti // PSBh_5.39:68
children.translated_text: * He asks: in the domain of practice, designated as the state of non-supreme-grace, as inauspiciousness — since all [sufferings] are seeds of non-supreme-grace, why are they not completely and permanently removed? [PSBh 5.39:68]

children.text: * saṃhāraṃ prāptasya nigaḍamuktādhikāravan muktāv atiśayitaguṇaprāptyartham ucyate gacched duḥkhānāmantam // PSBh_5.39:70
children.translated_text: * For one who has reached the dissolution — like the condition of one released from fetters, for the purpose of attaining surpassingly excellent qualities in liberation — it is said: 'one should go to the end of sufferings.' [PSBh 5.39:70]

children.text: * duḥkhānām atyantaṃ paramāpoho guṇāvāptiśca paraṃ bhavatīti // PSBh_5.39:71
children.translated_text: * The absolute removal of sufferings and the attainment of qualities is the supreme [state]. [PSBh 5.39:71]
* Both of these come from this [practice] alone. [PSBh 5.39:72]
* Therefore it says: 'by the grace of <s>Īśa</s> (the Lord).' [PSBh 5.39:73]
* Here '<s>Īśa</s>' is this name of the Blessed One. [PSBh 5.39:74]
* Why [is he called] <s>Īśa</s>? [PSBh 5.39:75]
* Because of ruling (<s>īśana</s>) over the effect beginning with knowledge — [he is] <s>Īśa</s>. [PSBh 5.39:76]
* Grace (<s>prasāda</s>) means the wish to bestow. [PSBh 5.39:77]

children.text: * tasmāt prasādāt sarvaduḥkhāpoho guṇāvāptiś cadim upādhyantarāt paraparivādādivacanāt śuddhiriva yugapadityarthaḥ // PSBh_5.39:78
children.translated_text: * Therefore, from that grace, the removal of all sufferings and the attainment of qualities [occur] — from the intermediate teacher and from the words of others' reviling and such — purification, as it were, simultaneously; this is the meaning. [PSBh 5.39:78]
* Thus this word <s>atha</s>. [PSBh 5.39:79]

children.text: * paśupater ityuddiṣṭayor duḥkhāntaprasādayor gacched duḥkhānām antamīśaprasādāditi duḥkhāntaṃ parisamāptamiti // PSBh_5.39:80
children.translated_text: * Of the 'end of suffering' and 'grace' that were enumerated [with the words] 'of <s>Paśupati</s>' — 'one should go to the end of sufferings by the grace of <s>Īśa</s>' — the [discussion of the] end of suffering is completed. [PSBh 5.39:80]
* Having thus completed the chapter, it is proper to state: [PSBh 5.39:81]

* It has been said: 'That wise one who would describe the person (<s>puruṣa</s>) as surpassing the effects, instruments, and coloring [of the senses], as well as all persons who are stainless and have not reached the end [of suffering].' // PSBh 5.39:3
Here one should recite this <s>Brahman</s> [mantra]. [PS 5.40]
* Thus: [PSBh 5.40:1]
* Its meaning has been previously stated. [PSBh 5.40:2]
* By the method — by the previously stated method — one should recite. [PSBh 5.40:3]
* But not by one who has reached the end of suffering, like a chief of <s>gaṇas</s>; this is the meaning. [PSBh 5.40:4]

children.text: * āha kāmitvāt kṛpayā bhagavatā duḥkhānto dattaḥ svecchayaiva na punaraduḥkhāntaṃ kariṣyati // PSBh_5.40:5
children.translated_text: * He objects: because of [the Lord's] power of will (<s>kāmitva</s>), the end of suffering has been given by the Blessed One out of compassion, by his own will alone — will he not [then] reverse it to non-end-of-suffering? [PSBh 5.40:5]

children.text: * athāśaktas tathāpyasya śaktivyāghātaḥ pācakavad akarmāpekṣatvaṃ cocyate // PSBh_5.40:6
children.translated_text: * If he is unable [to reverse it], then even so, his power would be obstructed — and it is said that, like a cook, [grace] is dependent on action. [PSBh 5.40:6]

children.text: * atra yathā nityo duḥkhāntastathā vakṣyāmaḥ // PSBh_5.40:7
children.translated_text: * Here, just as the end of suffering is eternal, so we shall explain. [PSBh 5.40:7]

children.text: * yathā ca kāṅkṣato lipsataś ca sādhakādhikāranivṛttistathā vakṣyāmaḥ // PSBh_5.40:8
children.translated_text: * And just as the cessation of the practitioner's qualification [occurs] for one who desires and wishes [liberation], so we shall explain. [PSBh 5.40:8]
* And it is stated for the purpose of concluding the [discussion of] categories: [PSBh 5.40:9]
<s>Īśāna</s> (the Ruler) of all knowledges. [PS 5.41]
* Here, from 'ruling' (<s>īśana</s>), [he is] <s>Īśāna</s>. [PSBh 5.41:1]
* Here, 'from ruling, <s>Īśāna</s>' — this has been stated as the reason. [PSBh 5.41:2]
* <s>Īśāna</s> means the lord, the sustainer — this is the meaning. [PSBh 5.41:3]
* He asks: of what is he the <s>Īśāna</s>? [PSBh 5.41:4]

children.text: * taducyate sarvasyeśānaḥ / sarvaśabdo vidyāprakṛter niravaśeṣavācī draṣṭavyaḥ // PSBh_5.41:5
* vidyānāṃ dharmārthakāmakaivalyatatsādhanaparāṇām īśānaḥ vidyānāmiti ṣaṣṭhībahuvacanam // PSBh_5.41:6
children.translated_text: * <s>Īśāna</s> of knowledges — of those devoted to <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, <s>kāma</s>, <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation), and their means. 'Of knowledges' — genitive plural. [PSBh 5.41:6]

children.text: * āha kiṃ vidyānāmeveśānaḥ na tu vidyābhirye vidanti // PSBh_5.41:7
children.translated_text: * He asks: is he <s>Īśāna</s> only of knowledges, but not of those who know by means of knowledges? [PSBh 5.41:7]
* The answer is: [PSBh 5.41:8]
* The answer is: <s>Īśāna</s> of everything. The word 'all' (<s>sarva</s>) should be understood as referring exhaustively to those of the nature of knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>). [PSBh 5.41:5]
Lord of all beings. [PS 5.42]
* Here, by unsurpassed sovereignty, he is the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>). [PSBh 5.42:1]
* The <s>puruṣa</s>, like consciousness — this is the meaning. [PSBh 5.42:2]
* He asks: of what is he the Lord? [PSBh 5.42:3]

children.text: * taducyate sarvabhūtānām / atra cetanācetaneṣu sarvaśabdaḥ na kevalaṃ pṛthivyādiṣu kiṃtu siddheśvaravarjaṃ cetaneṣveva sarvabhūtaprakṛterniravaśeṣavācī sarvaśabdo draṣṭavyaḥ // PSBh_5.42:4

children.translated_text: * Why [are they called] 'beings' (<s>bhūtas</s>)? [PSBh 5.42:5]
* Because of being brought into existence (<s>bhāvana</s>), they are called 'beings.' 'Of beings' — genitive plural. [PSBh 5.42:6]

children.text: * āha atra kecid vidyābhūtavyatiriktaṃ brahmāṇamicchanti // PSBh_5.42:7
children.translated_text: * He objects: here some desire a <s>Brahmā</s> who is distinct from knowledges and beings. [PSBh 5.42:7]
* Is this one the lord of him too, or not? [PSBh 5.42:8]
* The answer is: he is the lord. [PSBh 5.42:9]
* Because [the sūtra] states: [PSBh 5.42:10]

* The answer is: of all beings. Here, among the conscious and unconscious, the word 'all' — not only among earth and such, but exclusively among conscious beings except the perfected lords — the word 'all' should be understood as exhaustively referring to those of the nature of beings. [PSBh 5.42:4]
Overlord of <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>. [PS 5.43]

children.text: * atra yo 'yaṃ viriñciḥ paramaḥ patiḥ sarvacetanavyatiriktaḥ kṣetrajñaḥ tasmin brahmasaṃjñā // PSBh_5.43:1
children.translated_text: * Here, this <s>Viriñci</s> (Brahmā) who is the supreme lord, distinct from all conscious beings, the knower of the field (<s>kṣetrajña</s>) — in him the designation <s>Brahman</s> [applies]. [PSBh 5.43:1]
* But not in <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) and such. [PSBh 5.43:2]
* Why? [PSBh 5.43:3]
* Because it would contradict the statement of 'overlord.' [PSBh 5.43:4]
* And why [is he called] <s>Brahmā</s>? [PSBh 5.43:5]
* Because of expanding (<s>bṛṃhaṇa</s>) and because of being great (<s>bṛhat</s>), he is <s>Brahmā</s>. [PSBh 5.43:6]

children.text: * bṛṃhayate yasmād vidyākalābhūtāni bṛhac ca tebhya ityato 'dhipatirbrahmā // PSBh_5.43:7
children.translated_text: * Because he expands the beings [consisting of] knowledge and faculties, and because he is great beyond them — therefore he is the overlord, <s>Brahmā</s>. [PSBh 5.43:7]
* 'Of <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>brahmaṇaḥ</s>) — [this is] a genitive case. [PSBh 5.43:8]
* <s>Adhi</s> [is used] in the sense of being the presider. [PSBh 5.43:9]

children.text: * tatsvābhāvyāt saṃhṛte cāsaṃhṛte ca kārya ityarthaḥ // PSBh_5.43:10
children.translated_text: * Because of its intrinsic nature, [he presides] over the effect both when it is dissolved and when it is not dissolved — this is the meaning. [PSBh 5.43:10]
* The lord of the lord (<s>pati</s>) is the overlord (<s>adhipati</s>). [PSBh 5.43:11]
* Like 'king of kings.' [PSBh 5.43:12]

children.text: * patiḥ pālane patirdarśane bhoge ca // PSBh_5.43:13
children.translated_text: * <s>Pati</s> [means] in the sense of protecting; <s>pati</s> [also means] in the sense of seeing and enjoying. [PSBh 5.43:13]
* Because he protects <s>Brahmā</s> and others, he is the Lord. [PSBh 5.43:14]
* The overlord is the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>). [PSBh 5.43:16]

children.text: * evaṃ bṛṃhayate yasmād vidyādikāryaṃ bṛhac ca tebhya ityato 'dhipatirbrahmā bhagavāniti // PSBh_5.43:17
children.translated_text: * Thus, because he expands the effect beginning with knowledge, and because he is great beyond them — therefore the Blessed One is the overlord, <s>Brahmā</s>. [PSBh 5.43:17]

children.text: * āha atra kāryakaraṇamahābhāgyam evātra brahmaṇi cintyate na tu sādhakasya lipsā lābho veti // PSBh_5.43:18
children.translated_text: * He objects: here, is only the great fortune of the effect and instruments contemplated in this <s>Brahman</s>, but not the desire or attainment of the practitioner? [PSBh 5.43:18]
* The answer is: no [it is not only that]. [PSBh 5.43:19]
* Because [the sūtra] states: [PSBh 5.43:20]
* He protects the effect [beginning with] <s>Brahmā</s>. The overlord is <s>Brahmā</s>. [PSBh 5.43:15]
May <s>Śiva</s> (the Auspicious One) be [gracious] to me. [PS 5.44]

children.text: * atra yeṣāṃ sādhikāratvād anatiprasannas teṣāmaśivatvaṃ dṛṣṭvā duḥkhāntaṃ gateṣu ca śivatvaṃ dṛṣṭvā āha śivo me astu iti // PSBh_5.44:1
children.translated_text: * Here, seeing the inauspiciousness (<s>aśivatva</s>) of those who still have [worldly] duties and [for whom divine grace is] not fully bestowed, and seeing the auspiciousness (<s>śivatva</s>) in those who have reached the end of suffering — he says: 'May <s>Śiva</s> be for me.' // PSBh 5.44:1
* 'For me' (<s>me</s>) is a self-reference — 'for myself' is the meaning. // PSBh 5.44:2
* 'May [it] be' (<s>astu</s>) expresses a wish. // PSBh 5.44:3
* He wishes, desires, seeks — this is the meaning. // PSBh 5.44:4

children.text: * āha kiyantaṃ kālaṃ bhagavānasya śivo bhavati // PSBh_5.44:5
children.translated_text: * He asks: For how long does the Blessed Lord become <s>Śiva</s> (auspicious) for him? // PSBh 5.44:5
* To that it is said: Eternally (<s>nityam</s>). // PSBh 5.44:6
* Because he states: // PSBh 5.44:7
Always (<s>sadā</s>). || PS 5.45 ||

children.text: * atra sadā nityaṃ saṃtatam avyucchinnamityarthaḥ // PSBh_5.45:1
children.translated_text: * Here, 'always' (<s>sadā</s>) means eternally (<s>nityam</s>), continuously (<s>saṃtatam</s>), without interruption (<s>avyucchinnam</s>) — this is the meaning. // PSBh 5.45:1
* He asks: To whom does he say this? // PSBh 5.45:2
* Or who becomes <s>Śiva</s> (auspicious) for him? // PSBh 5.45:3
* It is said: // PSBh 5.45:4

children.text: * atra śiva ityetadapi bhagavato nāma // PSBh_5.46:1
children.translated_text: * Here, '<s>Śiva</s>' — this too is a name of the Blessed Lord. // PSBh 5.46:1
* Why [is he called] '<s>Śiva</s>'? // PSBh 5.46:2
* Because of being completely full (<s>paripūrṇa</s>) and completely satisfied (<s>paritṛpta</s>), he is '<s>Śiva</s>' (auspicious). // PSBh 5.46:3
* Therefore, from the teaching of 'eternally auspicious' (<s>sadāśiva</s>), the end of suffering is eternal. // PSBh 5.46:4
* The cessation of the authority of the cause (<s>kāraṇādhikāra</s>) [occurs]. // PSBh 5.46:5

children.text: * tadarthaṃ nityo duḥkhānta iti siddham // PSBh_5.46:6
children.translated_text: * For that purpose, the end of suffering is eternal — this is established. // PSBh 5.46:6

children.text: * evamete pañca padārthāḥ kāryakāraṇayogavidhiduḥkhāntāḥ samāsavistaravibhāgaviśeṣopasaṃhāranigamanataś ca vyākhyātāḥ // PSBh_5.46:7
children.translated_text: * Thus, these five categories (<s>padārtha</s>) — effect (<s>kārya</s>), cause (<s>kāraṇa</s>), <s>yoga</s> (union), rule (<s>vidhi</s>), and end of suffering (<s>duḥkhānta</s>) — have been explained through summary (<s>samāsa</s>), elaboration (<s>vistara</s>), division (<s>vibhāga</s>), distinction (<s>viśeṣa</s>), conclusion (<s>upasaṃhāra</s>), and recapitulation (<s>nigamana</s>). // PSBh 5.46:7
* For it has been said: // PSBh 5.46:8

children.text: * ādau yad bhavati samāsoktaṃ madhye tasya vistarataś ca vibhāgataś copanayanigamanena satāmapyeṣa niścayaḥ // PSBh_5.46:9
children.translated_text: * 'That which is stated in summary at the beginning, and then in the middle through elaboration, division, and through approach and recapitulation — this is the determination even for the virtuous.' // PSBh 5.46:9
* Thus. // PSBh 5.46:10

children.text: * atra tāvat patiriti kāraṇapadārthasyopadeśaḥ samāsena // PSBh_5.46:11
children.translated_text: * Here, first, '<s>Pati</s>' (Lord) is the teaching of the category of cause (<s>kāraṇa</s>) in summary. // PSBh 5.46:11

children.text: * vistarastu vāmo devo jyeṣṭho rudraḥ kāmaḥ śaṃkaraḥ kālaḥ kalavikaraṇo balavikaraṇo'ghoro ghorataraḥ sarvaḥ śarva tatpuruṣo mahādeva oṃkāra ṛṣir vipro mahānīśa īśāna īśvaro 'dhipatirbrahmā śiva ityevamādyo vistaraḥ // PSBh_5.46:12
children.translated_text: * The elaboration is: <s>Vāma</s>, <s>Deva</s>, <s>Jyeṣṭha</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Kāma</s>, <s>Śaṃkara</s>, <s>Kāla</s>, <s>Kalavikaraṇa</s>, <s>Balavikaraṇa</s>, <s>Aghora</s>, <s>Ghoratara</s>, <s>Sarva</s>, <s>Śarva</s>, <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>, <s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Oṃkāra</s>, <s>Ṛṣi</s>, <s>Vipra</s>, <s>Mahān</s>, <s>Īśa</s>, <s>Īśāna</s>, <s>Īśvara</s>, <s>Adhipati</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Śiva</s> — and so on is the elaboration. // PSBh 5.46:12

children.text: * vibhāgo'pi anyat patitvam anyad ajātatvam anyad bhavodbhavatvamityādyo vibhāgaḥ // PSBh_5.46:13
children.translated_text: * The division is also: lordship (<s>patitva</s>) is one thing, unborn nature (<s>ajātatva</s>) is another, being the source of existence (<s>bhavodbhavatva</s>) is another — and so on is the division. // PSBh 5.46:13

children.text: * viśeṣaḥ anyeṣāṃ pradhānādīni asmākaṃ tadvyatirikto bhagavānīśvaraḥ // PSBh_5.46:14
children.translated_text: * The distinction is: For the others [i.e., other systems], <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) and the like [are the causes]; for us, the Blessed Lord <s>Īśvara</s>, who is different from those, [is the cause]. // PSBh 5.46:14
* Regarding the authority of the cause — because he states: '<s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) of all beings.' // PSBh 5.46:15
* This conclusion (<s>upasaṃhāra</s>) is called '<s>sārvakāmika</s>' (fulfilling all desires). // PSBh 5.46:16

children.text: * nigamanam īśa īśāna īśvaro'dhipatirbrahmā śiva iti // PSBh_5.46:17
children.translated_text: * The recapitulation (<s>nigamana</s>): '<s>Īśa</s>, <s>Īśāna</s>, <s>Īśvara</s>, <s>Adhipati</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Śiva</s>.' // PSBh 5.46:17
* Likewise, '<s>Paśu</s>' (bound soul) is the introduction of the category of effect (<s>kārya</s>). // PSBh 5.46:18

children.text: * tasya vistaro vidyā kalā paśavaḥ // PSBh_5.46:19
children.translated_text: * Its elaboration is: knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>), parts (<s>kalā</s>), and bound souls (<s>paśu</s>). // PSBh 5.46:19

children.text: * utpādyā anugrāhyās tirobhāvyakālpyavikāryam aspadasya bodhyadhiṣṭheyatve cetyevam ādyaḥ sūtravidyādharmārthakāmair bhedair duḥkhāntaḥ vidyā // PSBh_5.46:20
children.translated_text: * [Effects are:] what is to be produced, graced, concealed, created, and transformed; the non-abode; and what is to be awakened and presided over — thus, through differentiations of <s>sūtra</s>, knowledge, <s>dharma</s>, wealth (<s>artha</s>), and desire (<s>kāma</s>), the end of suffering — [this is] knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>). // PSBh 5.46:20
* The parts (<s>kalā</s>) are twofold. // PSBh 5.46:21
* Those designated as effects (<s>kārya</s>) and those designated as instruments (<s>karaṇa</s>). // PSBh 5.46:22
* Among them, those designated as effects are earth (<s>pṛthivī</s>) and the rest. // PSBh 5.46:23
* Those designated as instruments are intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) and the rest. // PSBh 5.46:24
* And the bound souls (<s>paśu</s>) are threefold. // PSBh 5.46:25
* Gods (<s>deva</s>), humans (<s>manuṣya</s>), and animals (<s>tiryañc</s>). // PSBh 5.46:26
* Among them, the gods are eightfold, beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>. // PSBh 5.46:27
* And the human [category] is manifold, beginning with <s>brāhmaṇas</s>. // PSBh 5.46:28
* And the animal birth is fivefold, beginning with domestic animals and wild animals. // PSBh 5.46:29
* The bound souls are both tainted (<s>sāñjana</s>) and untainted (<s>nirañjana</s>). // PSBh 5.46:30
* Such is the elaboration. // PSBh 5.46:31

children.text: * vibhāgo'pi anyā vidyā anyāḥ kalāḥ anye ca paśava ityevamādyo vibhāgaḥ // PSBh_5.46:32
children.translated_text: * The division is also: knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>) is one thing, the parts (<s>kalā</s>) are another, and the bound souls (<s>paśu</s>) are yet another — thus is the division. // PSBh 5.46:32

children.text: * viśeṣaḥ anyeṣāṃ pradhānādīni kāraṇāni tānīha śāstre kāryatvena vyākhyātāni // PSBh_5.46:33
children.translated_text: * The distinction is: For the others, <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) and the like are the causes; those are explained in this treatise as effects (<s>kārya</s>). // PSBh 5.46:33

children.text: * tatra pradhānaṃ kāraṇam anyeṣāṃ tadiha śāstre paśyanāt pāśakatvāt kāryatvena vyākhyātam // PSBh_5.46:34
children.translated_text: * There, <s>Pradhāna</s> is the cause according to the others; here in this treatise, because of being seen [as dependent] and because of being a fetter (<s>pāśa</s>), it is explained as an effect. // PSBh 5.46:34

children.text: * tathā puruṣaḥ kāraṇamanyatra iha śāstre paśutvāt kāryatvena vyākhyātaḥ // PSBh_5.46:35
children.translated_text: * Likewise, <s>puruṣa</s> (person/soul) is the cause elsewhere; here in this treatise, because of being a bound soul (<s>paśu</s>), it is explained as an effect. // PSBh 5.46:35

children.text: * tathā karmamadhyatvāt kālaḥ svabhāvaḥ upasaṃhāravat // PSBh_5.46:36
children.translated_text: * Likewise, because of being intermediate to action, time (<s>kāla</s>) and inherent nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) [are effects] — like in the conclusion. // PSBh 5.46:36
* The elements (<s>bhūta</s>), because of being transformable, are explained as effects. // PSBh 5.46:37
* This is the distinction. // PSBh 5.46:38
* The conclusion (<s>upasaṃhāra</s>) is called '<s>sārvakāmika</s>' — this is the meaning. // PSBh 5.46:39
* The recapitulation: 'Knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>), parts (<s>kalā</s>), and elements (<s>bhūta</s>) — [these are] <s>Brahman</s>.' // PSBh 5.46:40
* Likewise, '<s>yoga</s>' is the introduction of the category of <s>yoga</s> (union). // PSBh 5.46:41

children.text: * tasyaivaṃ carataḥ yogaḥ pravartate ubhayathā yaṣṭavyaḥ atyāgatiṃ gamayate nānyabhaktistu śaṃkare evaṃ devanityatānityayuktatā adhyayanaṃ dhyānaṃ smaraṇaṃ nityasāyujyamiti vistaraḥ vibhāgaḥ kriyālakṣaṇaṃ kriyoparamalakṣaṇaṃ dūradarśanaśravaṇamananavijñānāni gaṇapatiḥ bhūyiṣṭhaṃ sampravartate siddhaḥ gacched duḥkhānāmantam ityevamādyo vibhāgaḥ // PSBh_5.46:42
children.translated_text: * Its [elaboration]: 'For one practising thus, <s>yoga</s> proceeds'; 'He should be worshipped in both ways'; 'It leads to the transcendent attainment (<s>atyāgati</s>)'; 'But devotion to none other than <s>Śaṃkara</s>'; thus — constant [union] with the deity (<s>devanityatā</s>), being constantly yoked (<s>nityayuktatā</s>), study (<s>adhyayana</s>), meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), remembrance (<s>smaraṇa</s>), eternal union (<s>nityasāyujya</s>) — this is the elaboration. The division: characterized by action, characterized by cessation of action, far-seeing (<s>dūradarśana</s>), hearing (<s>śravaṇa</s>), thinking (<s>manana</s>), discernment (<s>vijñāna</s>), <s>Gaṇapati</s> (lord of the hosts), '[the qualities] arise abundantly,' 'the perfected one attains the end of sufferings' — such is the division. // PSBh 5.46:42
* The power of knowledge (<s>jñānaśakti</s>) and the power of action (<s>kriyāśakti</s>). // PSBh 5.46:43
* There, the power of knowledge begins with hearing (<s>śravaṇa</s>) and the rest. // PSBh 5.46:44
* The power of action begins with the speed of mind (<s>manojavitva</s>) and the rest. // PSBh 5.46:45
* Such is the division. // PSBh 5.46:46

children.text: * viśeṣaḥ anyeṣāṃ kaivalyam iha tu viśeṣo vikaraṇamiti // PSBh_5.46:47
children.translated_text: * The distinction: For the others, <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation) [is the goal]; but here, the distinction is <s>vikaraṇa</s> (dissolution of instruments). // PSBh 5.46:47

children.text: * pratikaraṇa iti kaivalyadharmātiśaktir niṣkalam aiśvaryamityeṣa viśeṣaḥ // PSBh_5.46:48
children.translated_text: * '<s>Pratikaraṇa</s>' (counter-instrument) means a power transcending the nature of <s>kaivalya</s> — [namely] sovereignty (<s>aiśvarya</s>) without parts (<s>niṣkala</s>) — this is the distinction. // PSBh 5.46:48

children.text: * upasaṃhāraḥ ity ebhir guṇairyukta iti // PSBh_5.46:49
children.translated_text: * The conclusion: 'Thus endowed with these qualities.' // PSBh 5.46:49

children.text: * ato yāvanti vākyaviśeṣāṇi saṃnikṛṣṭaviprakṛṣṭāni nirvacanāni tāni ca sarvanirvacanānīti kṛtvā yuktamuktam // PSBh_5.46:50
children.translated_text: * Therefore, however many particular statements, whether proximate or remote, and however many explanations — taking all explanations together, what has been stated is fitting. // PSBh 5.46:50

children.text: * evamatra śrībhagavatkauṇḍinyaviracite śrīmadyogapāśupataśāstrasūtravyākhyāne pañcārthabhāṣye pañcamo'dhyāyaḥ saha brahmaṇā granthato 'rthataśca parisamāpta iti // PSBh_5.46:51
children.translated_text: * Thus, in the commentary on the <s>sūtras</s> of the blessed <s>Yoga-Pāśupata</s> treatise, composed by the blessed <s>Bhagavat Kauṇḍinya</s> — in the <s>Pañcārthabhāṣya</s> (Commentary on the Five Topics) — the fifth chapter, together with the <s>Brahman</s> [sections], in both text and meaning, is hereby concluded. // PSBh 5.46:51
* Auspicious! (<s>Śubham</s>) // PSBh 5.46:52
